author: amazeamazing
body:
…ll evaluators

- Add dry_run=True parameter to InspectAIEvaluator and MultiTurnRLEvaluator (Benchmark, CustomScorer, LLMAsJudge already had it)
- Add verify_evaluation_caller_permissions() to validate the caller's identity has the pipeline-orchestration permissions before submitting
- Define EVALUATION_CALLER_ACTIONS constant with the set of 22 IAM actions needed by whoever calls evaluator.evaluate()
- Fix bug: LLMAsJudge InspectAI code path was missing the dry_run check
- Wire dry_run through _get_aws_execution_context() for all evaluators
- Add unit tests covering dry_run behavior across all evaluator types

*Issue #, if available:*

*Description of changes:*

## Summary

Adds `dry_run` support to all evaluators and introduces caller-side IAM permission validation for the evaluate module's Pipeline-based execution model.

## Problem

The SDK's evaluate module uses SageMaker Pipelines under the hood to orchestrate evaluation jobs. This means the **caller** (notebook user, Lambda, CI role) needs ~22 IAM permissions to create/start/describe pipelines — separate from the **execution role** that the pipeline assumes to run training jobs.

Previously:
- `InspectAIEvaluator` and `MultiTurnRLEvaluator` had no `dry_run` parameter
- No validation existed for the caller's pipeline permissions — users got opaque `AccessDenied` errors from `CreatePipeline`
- `LLMAsJudgeEvaluator`'s InspectAI code path skipped the `dry_run` check entirely (bug)

## Changes

### New: `verify_evaluation_caller_permissions()` (`sagemaker-core`)
- Simulates `EVALUATION_CALLER_ACTIONS` against the caller's identity via `iam:SimulatePrincipalPolicy`
- Raises `RoleValidationError` when permissions are definitively denied
- Returns `None` gracefully when the caller can't self-simulate (common Studio/notebook case)

### New: `EVALUATION_CALLER_ACTIONS` constant
Complete set of caller permissions needed for `evaluator.evaluate()`:
- Pipeline orchestration (12 actions)
- Hub model resolution (4 actions)
- Lineage artifact management (3 actions)
- S3 access for config/benchmark upload (3 actions)

### Updated: All evaluators
- `InspectAIEvaluator.evaluate(dry_run=False)` — new parameter
- `MultiTurnRLEvaluator.evaluate(dry_run=False)` — new parameter
- `BaseEvaluator._get_aws_execution_context()` — now calls `verify_evaluation_caller_permissions()` (always raises on denied)

### Bug fix: LLMAsJudge InspectAI path
The InspectAI code path in `LLMAsJudgeEvaluator.evaluate()` had its own `return self._start_execution(...)` that bypassed the `dry_run` check. Fixed by adding the check before submission.

## Testing

- **Unit tests**: 10 new tests in `test_evaluator_dry_run.py` covering all 5 evaluator types + both LLMAsJudge paths
- **Integration tests**: Validated with scoped IAM role (`nilis-0121`) against real AWS — both InspectAI (Nova Lite/Bedrock) and Benchmark (OSS/MMLU) pipelines start successfully with least-privilege caller permissions

## IAM Permission Summary

| Category | Actions | Used by |
|----------|---------|---------|
| Pipeline orchestration | CreatePipeline, UpdatePipeline, DescribePipeline, ListPipelines, StartPipelineExecution, DescribePipelineExecution, ListPipelineExecutionSteps, StopPipelineExecution, ListTags, AddTags, DescribeTrainingJob, iam:PassRole | Caller |
| Hub model resolution | DescribeHubContent, ListHubContents, DescribeHub, ListHubs | Caller (construction time) |
| Lineage | CreateArtifact, ListArtifacts, DescribeArtifact | Caller (before pipeline start) |
| S3 | PutObject, GetObject, ListBucket | Caller (config/benchmark upload) |

author: steipete
body:
## What Problem This Solves

The observer HUD (#112260) shows what the session is doing; this PR makes it answerable. The expanded card gains a question input — "why is it rerunning that test?" — answered by the same utility model from the observer's existing digest and sanitized note context, without touching the main agent run.

## Why This Change Was Made

- New read-scoped RPC `sessions.observer.ask`: params validated by protocol schema; the observer answers from a snapshot of its latest digest plus the already-sanitized bounded note buffer (never raw transcripts), falling back to the persisted entry digest for unobserved sessions.
- Guardrails inherit the digest discipline wholesale: requester must be a session-message subscriber of that session; observer must be enabled and the utility model resolved (never the primary model); one in-flight ask per session with typed busy errors; sliding-window rate limits per connection and global; 10s timeout; answers redacted and truncated; stale-snapshot rejection; nothing persisted or broadcast — the answer returns only to the caller.
- Card UI: Enter-submitted input, ephemeral per-session Q&A thread (last six exchanges, cleared on session switch), pending/busy/unavailable states as muted hints, aria-live polite answers. Lazy chunk (3.02 KiB gzip), startup budgets untouched.
- Mock harness answers asks with a canned response so the flow is demoable end to end.

## User Impact

Operators can interrogate a running session from the HUD card without interrupting it or spending primary-model tokens. With the observer disabled or no utility model resolved, the input reports unavailable and nothing else changes.

## Evidence

- 154 focused test assertions across gateway (subscriber/enabled gating, busy, rate limits, unobserved fallback, sanitized-notes-only, truncation, utility-only) and UI (ask-flow state machine, session-switch clearing, RPC payload) suites; e2e screenshots and video captured via the mock harness.
- New RPC registered with method descriptors + since-train entry; protocol regenerated (ts/swift/kotlin) with generated models in-tree; no new WS event; knip lanes clean.
- Structured autoreview (gpt-5.6-sol, high): clean on the first round — the guard set was specced from the digest pipeline's thirteen prior accepted findings.

body:
The `_get_detector_for_group` function in `sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py` was using `logger.exception` within an `except DetectorGroup.DoesNotExist` block. This caused an error to be reported to Sentry every time a `DetectorGroup` record was not found for a given group, even though this is an expected and gracefully handled fallback scenario.

This change downgrades the log level from `logger.exception` to `logger.info` for this specific case. This prevents Sentry from being spammed with non-exceptional `DetectorGroup.DoesNotExist` errors, while still retaining a log entry for diagnostic purposes. The redundant `pass` statement has also been removed.

body:
#### 1665f4bc90084a86cd9463d60553211b8a79a77b 
[GFC][Cleanup] Remove some code duplication for resolving margins
https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=319942
rdar://problem/182860702

Reviewed by Cole Carley.

After track sizing is finished, we attempt to resolve the margins for
grid items in two different places: once during the final sizing of the
item and then when we want to align them. The logic to do this is
exactly the same and we do it in two different ways in both scenarios
when we do not need to. Instead, let's just use the static helper
function that we already have during item sizing and remove the lambdas
that were basically just duplicate code.

This change requires us to compute a list of the margins for each grid
item rather than resolve the margins one at a time, but this is
basically just a matter of plumbing the values to the right place.

* Source/WebCore/layout/formattingContexts/grid/GridLayout.cpp:
Remove the local UsedMargins definition now that it lives in
GridLayoutUtils.h.

(WebCore::Layout::GridLayout::layoutGridItems const):
Resolve each grid item's used margins with computeMarginsForAxis and pass
them into the sizing functions.

* Source/WebCore/layout/formattingContexts/grid/GridLayoutUtils.cpp:
(WebCore::Layout::GridLayoutUtils::stretchFitSize):
(WebCore::Layout::GridLayoutUtils::inlinePreferredSize):
(WebCore::Layout::GridLayoutUtils::blockPreferredSize):
(WebCore::Layout::GridLayoutUtils::inlineUsedSize):
(WebCore::Layout::GridLayoutUtils::blockUsedSize):
Aforementioned plumbing from GridLayout::layoutGridItems to the spots
where we were manually resolving them in the lambdas.

author: psaab
body:
## Summary

- **#5482 remaining gap (BACKUP side).** `becomeMaster` was already fail-closed by **#5082** — it refuses to publish MASTER when the VIP add fails (rolls back, reverts to `StateBackup`, returns `false`). The **symmetric BACKUP hazard remained unfixed**: `becomeBackup` (and the run-startup BACKUP entry) called the **void** `removeVIPs` and then `emitEvent` **unconditionally**.
- The daemon consumes the BACKUP event to inject blackhole routes and clear `rg_active` (`pkg/daemon/daemon_ha.go`), so a swallowed netlink removal failure left this now-BACKUP node **still answering ARP for a VIP it no longer owns** — a duplicate-address hazard against the new master and a silent control-plane/kernel divergence.
- `removeVIPs`/`removeVIPsLocked` now **return** the first genuine `AddrDel` failure. Benign cases stay non-errors: an unresolvable interface (address gone with the link) and a `not found`/`no such` delete (already absent) leave no stale VIP, so only an `AddrDel` failing against a **resolvable** interface is reported.
- `becomeBackup` and the run-startup entry route the result through the new `surfaceStaleVIP`: bump a monotonic `vipRemoveFailures` counter, set `vipDiverged`, log at **Error**, and `scheduleVIPRemoveReconcile` — a bounded async retry (5 attempts, per-instance backoff, stops on re-promotion to MASTER or shutdown) that clears the stale VIP and resets `vipDiverged`.

## Failure policy (the crux)

BACKUP is **still emitted** — we ARE stepping down, and withholding the event would risk split-brain / a no-master gap, which is worse than a transient stale VIP. The fix makes the divergence **loud and self-healing** instead of silent, without changing the ~60ms failover path (the `vipMu` lock is uncontended on the clean path, and the reconcile is async). This mirrors the #5082 MASTER-side policy from the opposite direction: MASTER refuses to publish an ownership it can't back; BACKUP publishes the honest step-down but never silently strands the VIP.

## Test plan

- [x] `pkg/vrrp/vip_backup_verify_5482_test.go`:
  - `TestBecomeBackupSurfacesVIPRemoveFailure_5482` (**fail-on-revert**) — rigs the netlink `AddrDel` seam to fail; asserts BACKUP is still emitted **and** the failure is surfaced (`vipRemoveFailures == 1`, `vipDiverged` set).
  - `TestBecomeBackupCleanRemovalNoDivergence_5482` — non-tautological control: on a clean removal the counter/flag stay at zero.
  - `TestBackupStaleVIPReconcileSelfHeals_5482` — first delete fails, later succeeds; the async reconcile clears `vipDiverged`.
- [x] `go build ./...`, `go vet ./pkg/vrrp/`, `go test -race ./pkg/vrrp/...` — all pass.
- [ ] **Loss-cluster failover smoke** (`make test-failover` / `test-ha-crash`) — VRRP/HA path; to be batched by the reviewer/lead.

**Parent RED-on-revert:** replace `vi.surfaceStaleVIP(vi.removeVIPs(), "becomeBackup")` in `becomeBackup` with the pre-fix `vi.removeVIPs()` (discarding the error) → still compiles → `TestBecomeBackupSurfacesVIPRemoveFailure_5482` fails on `vipRemoveFailures = 0, want 1` (clean assertion, not a build break).

## Docs

`pkg/vrrp/README.md` — added a "Verified role publication (#5082 MASTER, #5482 BACKUP)" bullet documenting the role/VIP-agreement contract on both transition sides.

## Refs

Closes #5482 · symmetric to #5082 (MASTER-side fail-closed) · consumer: `pkg/daemon/daemon_ha.go` MASTER/BACKUP event handling

author: dfrisone
body:
## Summary
Bug report: with the raid/party Power Bar section **unsynced**, power bars turned **off for raid** but **on for party**, the party power bars stop updating while in combat. Syncing the section makes them work again.

**Root cause:** `UpdatePowerEventRegistration` gated each unit tracker's `UNIT_POWER_UPDATE` registration on the raid profile's "Show Power Bar For" role flags only. The per-unit event trackers are shared by raid and party frames (the `player`/`party1-4` tokens drive the party buttons), so with the raid role flags all off it unregistered the event for every unit, including the party's. The party bars still rendered a correct snapshot on full-update paths (roster changes etc.), but received no live power events, so they sat frozen mid-combat.

## Fix
- `UpdatePowerEventRegistration` now also consults the party settings proxy for units the party frames can display: `player`/`partyN` tokens, plus any unit currently mapped to a party button (covers arena, where the party header binds `raid1-5`). This mirrors how `UpdateCombatEventRegistration` already handles the raid/party split for `UNIT_FLAGS`.
- `ReloadPartyFrames` now re-runs `UpdatePowerEventRegistration()` after its temp-swap restore, so syncing/unsyncing the Power Bar section (or editing party-side role filters) takes effect immediately instead of waiting for the next roster change. Same reasoning as the existing `UpdateCombatEventRegistration` call at its top.

Event (un)registration is combat-safe; no secure-frame code is touched.

## Testing
- Repro setup (Power Bar section unsynced, raid power off, party power on): party power bars now update live in combat. Confirmed in-game by the reporting tester.
- Synced behaviour unchanged (party reads raid flags, exactly as before).
- Raid-on/party-off still hides the party power bars.
- Flipping the Power Bar sync checkbox mid-session now re-registers events without a reload.

body:
The 'Search events by date' card on event nodes stacked **two** 'View more events from this day' links, the birthday summary **and** its open picker form with its own heading - four doors to the same place.

### Causes and fixes
1. **JS force-show**: `tdih-interactive.js` unconditionally showed `.tdih-today-history-wrapper`, defeating the template's `show_today_history` hiding and leaking the wrapper's view-more link. Removed - the day/month form renders results into its own container.
2. **Disclosure open-heuristic too broad**: the picker opened whenever the ledger was hidden (designed for /this-day-in-history where the form IS the page). New `picker_open` theme variable (default NULL keeps the heuristic) lets the event embed close it.
3. **Event embed config**: now passes `show_more_link: FALSE` + `picker_open: FALSE` - exactly one view-more link remains.

### Bonus root-cause
`tdih_library_info_build()` re-defined `tdih-interactive` in PHP (v1.0, missing `core/once`), silently clobbering `tdih.libraries.yml` - version bumps there were no-ops so browsers kept stale JS. Hook deleted; both libraries consolidated in YAML at v1.1 (busts every client cache).

### Verified (Playwright)
- Event card: header + closed 'What happened on your birthday?' line + one link
- Picker AJAX: 16 June → 18 events rendered in-card
- No regression: front page ledger + lead image intact; /this-day-in-history keeps open form with default today results
- Console: only pre-existing noise (CSP report-only, one unrelated 404 derivative)

author: ecv
body:
## Summary

One tenant's broken login policy can black out the shared gateway for every tenant on it. A tenant OIDC `SecurityPolicy` pointing at a missing secret gets pushed to the shared proxy. The running proxy masks the damage by holding its last-good config, but the next restart reloads from scratch and comes up serving nothing, taking every neighbour down.

This adds the e2e test that locks in the containment: one tenant's mistake stays on its own route, even across a proxy restart. It rests on a reusable proxy-restart step. Without a forced restart the test would pass on a broken build.

**Arm 1: bad policy never reaches the shared proxy.** OIDC policy whose secret is never created is held back (`Accepted=False, reason=PendingSecret`), nothing projected downstream, neighbour keeps serving.

**Arm 2: from-scratch reload stays healthy.** Bad config forced directly onto the shared gateway, proxy restarted; afterwards the neighbour still serves, the bad route fails alone, listeners come up intact.

It also guards upgrades: passes on pinned Envoy Gateway v1.7.4 plus the #304 hold, goes red only if Envoy Gateway is bumped back into the still-open upstream bug. The scenario and README say so, so a green run is never misread as "upstream fixed".

> [!NOTE]
> Root cause is an open upstream Envoy Gateway bug (envoyproxy/gateway#6123). This test does not fix it. It stops a silent re-upgrade into it and proves the #304 hold works.

## Test plan

e2e-edge suite against the real shared data plane; not runnable in envtest or locally.

- [ ] `oidc-missing-secret-isolation` passes on pinned Envoy Gateway v1.7.4
- [ ] Arm 1: policy held, nothing projected downstream, neighbour serving
- [ ] Arm 2: after restart, neighbour serving, bad route fails alone, listeners intact

Related to #194

author: jwindhager
body:
# References and relevant issues

<!--
What relevant resources were used in the creation of this PR?
If this PR addresses an existing issue on the repo, please link to that issue here as "Closes #(issue-number)".
If this PR depends on another PR (even in another repo), please link to it with "Depends on #(PR-number)" or "Depends on org/repo#(PR-number)".
-->

None.

# Type of change

<!-- If "Other", please specify. -->

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [x] Improvement (non-breaking change which modifies an existing feature)
- [x] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) — packages are now ESM-only (see below)
- [x] Other — large internal refactor / code reorganization

# List of changes made

<!-- Specify what changes have been made and why. -->

The bulk of this PR is a refactor, but it also carries deliberate functional changes — see
the dedicated section below. Structural changes:

- **Extracted rendering into a new `@tissuumaps/render` package.** All WebGL and SVG
  rendering, previously living in `@tissuumaps/core` (and partly in the viewer), now has a
  dedicated home with a clear public surface (see `packages/@tissuumaps-render/src/index.ts`).
  This keeps `core` free of rendering/OpenSeadragon concerns.
- **Renamed the "Controller" abstraction to "Renderer" and restructured it.** The old
  `core/src/controllers/*` (`OpenSeadragonController`, `WebGLController`,
  `WebGLPointsController`, `WebGLShapesController`, `WebGLControllerBase`) are gone, replaced
  by renderers under `@tissuumaps-render`: `WebGLPointsRenderer`, `WebGLShapesRenderer`,
  `WebGLRendererBase`, `OpenSeadragonImageRenderer`, `OpenSeadragonLabelsRenderer`,
  `OpenSeadragonRendererBase`, plus new `WebGLContext`/`OpenSeadragonContext` and
  `WebGLOptions`/`OpenSeadragonOptions` option types. `WebGLControllerBase` became
  `webgl/WebGLUtils`.
- **Moved the per-attribute data resolvers** out of `core/src/utils/data/*DataUtils.ts` into
  `@tissuumaps-render/src/webgl/resolvers/*Resolver.ts` (`Color`, `Marker`, `Opacity`, `Size`,
  `Visibility`, and `DataUtilsBase` → `ResolverBase`), matching their renderer-facing role.
- **Added a `WebGLShapesRasterizer`** (with tests) to encapsulate shape rasterization.
- **Reorganized `@tissuumaps/core` types.** `src/types.ts` and `model/types.ts` were split into
  focused modules: `types/arrays.ts`, `types/callbacks.ts`, `types/geometry.ts`,
  `types/legacy.ts`, and `model/primitives.ts`. Added `GeometryUtils` (with tests).
- **Build/tooling housekeeping:** introduced per-package `tsconfig.src.json`, renamed
  `tsconfig.dts.json` → `tsconfig.ts59.json`, updated `vite.config.ts` files and root tsconfig
  project references, and regenerated `pnpm-lock.yaml` for the new package.

# Functional changes (not pure restructuring)

- **Dropped non-ESM (CommonJS/UMD) build output — packages are now ESM-only.** Every package
  (`core`, `storage`, `viewer`, `plugins`, and the new `render`) now builds with Vite
  `formats: ["es"]` only; the `"umd"`/`"cjs"` lib formats and UMD global names were removed.
  Correspondingly, `package.json` drops the top-level `main`/`module`/`types` fields and the
  `require` export condition (replaced by `"default": "./dist/*.js"`). **This breaks any
  downstream consumer relying on `require()` / CommonJS / a UMD global** — consumers must now
  use ESM `import`.
- **Restructured the OpenSeadragon rendering strategy into two anchored renderers.** The single
  `OpenSeadragonController` was split into `OpenSeadragonImageRenderer` and
  `OpenSeadragonLabelsRenderer` (both extending `OpenSeadragonRendererBase`). Each renderer owns
  a transparent, zero-opacity *anchor* tiled image placed at a fixed z-index (`anchorIndex`);
  the renderer's object tiled images then occupy the contiguous "tiled-image band" of indices
  immediately after their anchor. `cleanRenderedObjects` enforces this band — each surviving
  object must sit at the expected consecutive index (`anchorIndex + 1 + n`), otherwise it is
  removed and recreated — and the anchor is continuously resized to the bounding box of its band
  (`updateBounds`). This gives images and labels independent, stable slices of the OSD world
  z-order that cannot interfere with one another. Relatedly, the old polled "dummy bounds"
  fallback was replaced by a push model: the WebGL renderers now return their rendered bounds
  from `synchronize()`, which `Viewer` feeds into the OSD renderers via `setExtraBounds` so the
  world/home bounds extend to cover off-image points/shapes.
- **Serialized OpenSeadragon world-item mutations (fixes HMR).** `OpenSeadragonContext` now
  funnels every mutation of the viewer world — `addTiledImage`, `removeTiledImage`,
  `getTiledImageIndex`, `updateBounds` — through a single FIFO promise chain
  (`_enqueueItemsMutation` / `_itemsMutationPromise`), and `destroy()` awaits any pending
  mutation before tearing the viewer down. Because OSD's `addTiledImage` is asynchronous and
  FIFO, previously the rapid effect teardown/re-init during hot module replacement could
  interleave add/remove operations and leave the world in a corrupt state (orphaned/duplicate
  tiled images, wrong ordering); serializing them makes HMR reliable.
- **WebGL context-loss handling and forced GPU-resource release.** `useWebGL` now listens for
  `webglcontextlost`/`webglcontextrestored` and stops/restarts the renderers, and
  `WebGLContext.destroy()` force-loses the context via the `WEBGL_lose_context` extension to
  immediately free GPU resources — so repeated remounts under React StrictMode/HMR don't exhaust
  the browser's live-WebGL-context cap. This is the WebGL counterpart to the OSD
  mutation-serialization fix above.
- **Reworked the viewer overlay hooks (`useSVG`, `useWebGL`, `useOpenSeadragon`) and `Viewer`.**
  Initialization moved from a `parent` + `initialViewport` effect to a callback-ref pattern
  (e.g. `initSVG`), and the hooks now reactively sync live `viewport`, `containerSize`, and
  interaction-mode changes to the underlying controller/renderer instead of re-initializing.
  The `OpenSeadragonController` context/provider was also renamed to `OpenSeadragonContext`.
  This changes the overlay lifecycle and update timing.
- **Adopted a "callee owns the abort signal" convention.** Redundant `signal.throwIfAborted()`
  calls in promise success handlers and after worker round-trips were removed (e.g. in
  `ParquetTableData.loadValues`/`loadValueRange`); remaining checks were kept and commented
  where they guard subsequent O(n) work. This changes where/when aborts are detected at runtime.
- **Normalized async signatures** (e.g. `GeoJSONShapesData.loadGeometry` and the parquet
  worker's `slice` are now `async`; sync-body `return await Promise.resolve(x)` simplified to
  `return Promise.resolve(x)`) — behavior-neutral, but part of the same async harmonization.

author: p3nj
body:
## Summary
Makes page teardown actually run on all navigation, and fixes two router hash-dedupe bugs.

> **Stacked on #61** (base branch `pr2-date-timezone`). Merge #60 → #61 → this in order.

## The core bug
Live-poll timers (execution 3s, instances 5s) and Chart.js instances were only cleaned up via `Router.beforeNavigate`, which runs **only inside `Router.navigate()`**. But navbar links are plain `#<hash>` anchors that fire `hashchange`, and Back/Forward fire `popstate` — neither path goes through `navigate()`. So leaving a page via the navbar or the back button left pollers running forever (2–3 API calls every tick, mutating now-hidden DOM) and leaked charts.

## Changes
**`router.js`**
- New **`Router.onRouteChange(cb)`** teardown registry, invoked from `handleRouteChange` on *every* real route change (hashchange/popstate/navigate), after the dedupe check.
- `navigate()`: clear `lastRenderedHash` before the forced same-target `handleRouteChange()` — otherwise the dedupe short-circuits and the intended forced re-run never happens.
- `replaceState()`: update `lastRenderedHash` to the newly-written hash, so a later `navigate()` back to the previous hash isn't dropped as a "same hash" no-op (this is exactly the in-page filter-sync → navigate-back path).

**`app.js`**
- Move poll teardown into `Router.onRouteChange` and also call `AnalysisPage.cleanup()` there (stops auto-refresh + destroys charts), so it runs for navbar/back navigation too. `beforeNavigate` now only does the auth check.
- Null-guard the navbar-collapse click handler.

## Verification
- `node --check` on both files.
- In-browser: `Router.onRouteChange` is a function; navigating `instances → integrations → analysis` runs the teardown hook with no JS errors.

author: sheahawkins
body:
The problem is basically this:

Under `LanguageModel`'s previous contract, it was streaming a TokenStream up out out to `LmStage`. If we do that, that means that `LmStage` needs to know how to parse the tokens for tool calls -- which is model and harness-specific. `LanguageModel` [knows](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bZe5J8SVCYQ) how to parse its tool calls, regardless of whether it's a RigAgent, Vertex, or whatever.

Therefore, the contract is updated so that `LanguageModel` provides `ModelDelta` to `LmStage`. `ModelDelta` can be a Transcript partial, or it can be complete `ToolCall`. `serde` is used to ensure that tool calls are valid json before they get passed downstream.

author: depfu[bot]
body:
🚨 Your current dependencies have known security vulnerabilities 🚨 This dependency update fixes known security vulnerabilities. Please see the details below and assess their impact carefully. We recommend to merge and deploy this as soon as possible!
Here is everything you need to know about this update. Please take a good look at what changed and the test results before merging this pull request. ### What changed? #### ↗️ loofah (_indirect_, 2.19.1 → 2.25.2) · [Repo](https://github.com/flavorjones/loofah) · [Changelog](https://github.com/flavorjones/loofah/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
Security Advisories 🚨

🚨 Loofah `allowed_uri?` does not detect `javascript:` URIs split by named whitespace character references

Summary

Loofah::HTML5::Scrub.allowed_uri? does not correctly reject javascript: URIs when the scheme is split or prefixed by the HTML5 named character references 	 (tab) or 
 (line feed).

This is a bypass of the fix for GHSA-46fp-8f5p-pf2m, which handled the equivalent numeric character references (	, 
, ) but did not cover the named forms.

Details

allowed_uri? decodes HTML entities with CGI.unescapeHTML, which handles numeric character references but not HTML5 named character references. Payloads like java	script:alert(1) are therefore left intact, so the method does not recognize the javascript: scheme and returns true. A browser, however, decodes 	 and 
 to tab and line feed and strips them from the URL during parsing, producing javascript:alert(1).

	 and 
 are the only relevant named character references: across the HTML5 named-character table, they are the only two that decode to characters the WHATWG URL parser strips from a URL (U+0009 and U+000A; there is no named reference for U+000D).   /   decode to U+00A0, which browsers do not strip, so they aren't usable for this bypass.

Note that Loofah's default sanitize() path is not affected, because Nokogiri decodes or entity-escapes HTML entities during parsing before Loofah evaluates the URI protocol. This issue only affects callers of the public allowed_uri? string-level helper that pass it HTML-encoded strings.

Impact

Callers that validate a user-controlled URL with Loofah::HTML5::Scrub.allowed_uri? and then render the approved value into an href or other browser-interpreted URI attribute may be vulnerable to cross-site scripting (XSS). This includes applications that call allowed_uri? directly, as well as higher-level features built on top of it, such as Action Text 8.2's markdown link validation.

Mitigation

Upgrade to Loofah >= 2.25.2.

Credit

Responsibly reported by GitHub user @connorshea.

🚨 Loofah: SVG `href` attribute bypasses local-reference restriction

Summary

Loofah's HTML5 sanitizer restricted only the xlink:href attribute on certain SVG elements to local, same-document references. Browsers also accept a plain href attribute as an alternative to the deprecated xlink:href per the SVG 2 spec, but Loofah did not apply the same restriction to it, allowing those elements to reference arbitrary external documents.

Impact

SVG <use> can load and render external SVG content by reference. If the referenced external SVG is same-origin and contains scripts or other dangerous content, it could execute in the context of the sanitized document. <feImage> can load external images, which can be used for tracking. Modern browsers restrict cross-origin <use> fetches, which limits but does not eliminate the risk.

Applications that sanitize user-supplied SVG (directly, or as part of HTML) with Loofah's default allowlist are affected.

Mitigation

Upgrade to Loofah >= 2.25.2.

Credit

Found by the maintainer, Mike Dalessio, during a security audit.

🚨 Loofah `allowed_uri?` does not detect `javascript:` URIs split by numeric character references without semicolons

Summary

Loofah::HTML5::Scrub.allowed_uri? does not correctly reject javascript: or vbscript: URIs when the scheme is split by a numeric character reference that has no trailing semicolon. A browser decodes such references and resolves the URL to an executable javascript: scheme, while allowed_uri? reports it safe.

This is a bypass of the fix for GHSA-46fp-8f5p-pf2m, which handled numeric character references with a trailing ; (	, 
, ) but did not cover the forms without semicolons.

Details

allowed_uri? decodes HTML entities with CGI.unescapeHTML, which decodes numeric character references only when they carry a trailing ;. A reference without a semicolon such as &#58 (colon) or &#9 (tab) is left literal, so the scheme-detection check finds no scheme, and the method falls through to its scheme-less path and returns true.

A browser, however, decodes numeric character references even without a trailing semicolon. An encoded colon such as &#58 becomes the : scheme separator, so javascript&#58alert(1) resolves to javascript:alert(1). Encoded whitespace such as &#9 (tab) is decoded

<!--
Please submit this PR as a draft initially.
Do not mark it as "Ready for review" until the template has been completely filled out, and PR status checks have passed at least once.
-->

## **Description**

A set of low-risk, no-behavior-change cleanups to the GitHub Actions workflows. These were identified as part of a broader workflow optimization audit; a follow-up PR (pt 2) will tackle the more structural changes (artifact sharing, Storybook workflow consolidation).

Changes:

- **Remove single-value `node-version` matrices** from `lint-build-test.yml` and `chromatic.yml`. A matrix with one entry still pays the scheduling/fanout overhead with zero parallelism benefit. `cache-node-modules` in the `prepare` job was updated from the now-removed `matrix.node-version == '24.x'` condition to a plain `true`.
- **Extract `yarn test:scripts` into its own job** (`test-scripts`) so it runs once instead of once per workspace package in the `test` matrix.
- **Remove `action-checkout-and-setup` from the label-check workflow.** The `github-script` action reads labels directly from `context.payload.pull_request.labels`, which is always present in `pull_request` events — no local checkout is needed.
- **Run `analyse-code` in parallel with `check-workflows`** by removing the `needs: check-workflows` dependency. The security scanner has no dependency on workflow file validation and was being blocked unnecessarily.

## **Expected CI impact**

This PR delivers real efficiency gains, but **don't expect a dramatic drop in overall Main workflow wall-clock time**. Comparing recent runs on this branch vs main, total time was within normal variance (~217s vs ~221s).

### What we gain

- **Less duplicate work:** `yarn test:scripts` previously ran 6× (once per package matrix job); it now runs once in a dedicated `test-scripts` job (~40–50s of redundant runner time removed per PR).
- **Faster package test jobs:** Removing `test:scripts` from each matrix leg trimmed the slowest jobs by ~9–18s (e.g. react-native ~104s → ~95s, react ~93s → ~75s).
- **Parallel security scan:** `analyse-code` no longer waits for `check-workflows` (~7s earlier start on a ~3 min job).
- **Minor trims:** Single-entry matrix removal and dropping checkout from the label-check workflow reduce scheduling/checkout overhead (seconds, not minutes).

### Why total time barely changes (for now)

The Main workflow critical path is still dominated by jobs this PR doesn't shorten:

- Code scanner (~3 min)
- Slowest package test (~1.5 min + prepare), still running a full `yarn build` per matrix job
- Chromatic and Storybook accessibility tests

Pt 1 removes wasted repetition and starts the scanner slightly sooner, but **does not** address the structural cost drivers (duplicate builds across jobs, lack of artifact sharing, no changed-path package filtering).

### Pt 2 (follow-up)

The next workflow cleanup PR will tackle those structural changes — artifact sharing between jobs, Storybook workflow consolidation, and related optimizations — where the meaningful wall-clock improvements should show up.

## **Related issues**

Fixes:

## **Manual testing steps**

1. Verify CI passes on this PR — all jobs in the `Main` workflow should complete successfully.
2. Confirm the `test-scripts` job appears as a distinct job in the workflow run (not grouped inside the `test` matrix).
3. Confirm `ensure-blocking-pr-labels-absent` still correctly fails when the `DO-NOT-MERGE` label is applied.
4. Confirm `analyse-code` and `check-workflows` now start simultaneously in the workflow graph.

author: jason-easyazz
body: Operator decision 2026-07-22: **everything local**. ## The problem `dist/chat.html` loaded **9** libraries from jsDelivr/unpkg, the two journal pages loaded FilePond + 6 plugins from unpkg, and the two developer pages `@import`ed Google Fonts. This breaks Zoe's local-first doctrine (`docs/VISION.md`), leaks a page view to a third party on every load, and is an availability bug — no internet means no markdown rendering, no HTML sanitization, no highlighting, no charts, no maps, no photo upload. It has already bitten us: routing those cross-origin requests through the SW's NetworkFirst strategy handed workbox an **opaque** response it could not read, and all 9 assets failed `net::ERR_FAILED` on every SW-controlled reload. The fix at the time was to leave cross-origin *unrouted*; this PR removes the cross-origin part entirely. Same rationale as #1371 (Workbox), applied to the pages. ## Inventory (every external origin in `dist/**`, before this PR) | Page | Asset | Version in URL | |---|---|---| | `chat.html`, `touch/chat.html` | `cdn.jsdelivr.net` marked | `@15` (floating) | | | `cdn.jsdelivr.net` dompurify | `@3` (floating) | | | `cdn.jsdelivr.net` prismjs theme + core + autoloader + `components/` | `@1.29.0` | | | `cdn.jsdelivr.net` qrcode | `@1.4.4` | | | `unpkg.com` leaflet css + js | `@1.9.4` | | | `cdn.jsdelivr.net` chart.js | `@4.4.4` | | `journal.html` | `unpkg.com` filepond css + js | **unversioned = latest** | | | `unpkg.com` filepond plugins ×5 (image-preview css+js, image-resize, image-transform, file-validate-size, file-validate-type) | **unversioned = latest** | | | `cdn.jsdelivr.net` browser-image-compression | `@2.0.2` | | `touch/journal.html` | `unpkg.com` filepond css + js, image-preview css + js | **unversioned = latest** | | `developer/index.html`, `developer/zoe_dashboard_demo.html` | `fonts.googleapis.com` Inter | — | Also present but **out of scope** (not libraries, and left alone): OpenStreetMap tile template + Nominatim geocoder (runtime data APIs in JS), `t.me/BotFather` hyperlinks, 3 decorative `images.unsplash.com` placeholders in `journal.html`'s static demo timeline. `dist/css/**` and `dist/js/**` were clean. ## What was vendored Under `dist/lib/`, the existing convention (pinned, tracked in git, nothing builds it). Fetched as **official npm registry tarballs, each verified against the registry's `dist.integrity` (sha512) before extraction** — stronger than a bare CDN fetch, and none of the current tags carry an SRI attribute to check against. `marked` 15.0.12 · `dompurify` 3.4.12 · `prismjs` 1.29.0 (core, autoloader, tomorrow theme, 16 language components) · `qrcode` 1.4.4 · `leaflet` 1.9.4 (js + css + `images/`) · `chart.js` 4.4.4 · `filepond` 4.32.12 + 5 plugins · `browser-image-compression` 2.0.2 Load order and every `defer`/`async` attribute preserved verbatim; only the URLs changed. ### Three traps found on the way (now recorded in `services/zoe-ui/AGENTS.md`) 1. **Do not curl the CDN path.** jsDelivr *generates* `.min.js` on demand for files npm does not ship — `prismjs@1.29.0/prism.min.js` and `chart.js@4.4.4/dist/chart.umd.min.js` do not exist in either package. Vendored as `prism.js` / `chart.umd.js`, which is what the packages actually contain (chart.js's UMD dist is already minified). 2. **Leaflet's CSS references `images/` relatively.** Vendoring only the css+js yields a working map with invisible markers. 3. **The FilePond URLs carried no version at all** — "whatever unpkg serves today". Resolved and pinned. The Prism autoloader still fetches one component per code block, but now **same-origin** from `/lib/prism/components/`. A language outside the vendored set renders unhighlighted instead of reaching the internet; `use_minified` defaults true, so a new language means committing `prism-.min.js` plus its `require`. The Google Fonts `@import` is **deleted, not vendored**: nginx's CSP allows neither `fonts.googleapis.com` in `style-src` nor a non-`'self'` `font-src`, so it has never actually loaded. Both pages already fall back to the system UI stack. ## SW_VERSION `4.69.2` → **`4.70.0`**. `chat.html` is in `precacheAndRoute`, so without the bump every existing client keeps serving the precached CDN-referencing copy forever — the #1 documented "my changes aren't showing up" gotcha. The vendored files are deliberately **not** added to `precacheAndRoute`: they are same-origin now, so the generic same-origin script/style routes already cache them on first use, and precaching ~800 KB of libraries would re-download the lot on every future `SW_VERSION` bump. (Offline resilience does not depend on the SW here anyway — nginx serves `/lib/` off local disk.) ## Test + falsification New `services/zoe-data/tests/test_ui_no_external_assets_scan.py` (`pytestmark = pytest.mark.ci_safe`, pure stdlib `re`, sibling of `test_write_path_exception_scan.py`). It asserts: - no `

author: romeovs
body:
Seven fixes to the react-router v7 facade, all landing with the flag still **off**, so v7 stays dormant and nothing here changes behaviour on the shipped v3 engine.

Follow-up to #78103 (merged). Each fix restores a v3 behaviour the v7 shim did not yet reproduce.

## The fixes

1. **A `<Link>` with an empty `to` is a button, not a navigation.** `UndoButton` (the undo toast, including its "Add this to a dashboard" action) renders `<Link to="" onClick=...>`. On v7 the link also navigated, resolving `""` to `/` from the toast's portal, which unmounted the page underneath. Now an absent or empty `to` renders a plain anchor, matching v3 where `router.push("")` was a no-op.
2. **A `replace` to the current URL is a no-op.** history@3 did not notify listeners when replacing the location it already had, so URL-sync effects settled. v7's `v5Compat` history notifies on every replace, which looped `useLocationSync` and crashed the dashboard.
3. **`router.listen` exists on v7, and the router shim is stable.** `use-dashboard-url-query` calls `router.listen`, which the shim lacked, so `<DashboardApp>` threw and the dashboard never rendered. The shim is now memoised once and reads `navigate` through a ref, because v7's `navigate` changes identity per navigation and was tearing down every consumer effect keyed on `router`.
4. **A v3 `query` object is serialised into the search string.** `toNavigateArgs` mapped only `pathname`/`search`/`hash`, so `push({ ...location, query })` silently dropped its params. `query` takes precedence over `search`, matching history@3, because call sites spread a location whose `search` is stale.
5. **The matched-route branch is stable across renders.** react-router returns a fresh `matches` array every render, so `route` was a new object each time and the leave-confirm modal, which resets itself when `route` changes, closed itself mid-interaction.
6. **v7's splat param is republished as v3's `splat`.** v3 exposed a wildcard match as `params.splat`, v7 names it `*`. `AutomaticDashboardApp` builds x-ray URLs from `params.splat`, so on v7 it requested `/auto/dashboard/undefined` and rendered an empty dashboard with no error.
7. **Lint and type cleanups** in the shim.

## Verification

Measured locally by running each spec on both engines and diffing, so pre-existing failures are not counted as v7 regressions:

- `question/new`: v7 **18/18** (was 14/18), matching v3.
- `dashboard/dashboard-back-navigation`: v7 **10/10** (was 7/10), matching v3.
- `collections/collection-pinned-overview`: 13/13. `question/notebook-data-source`: 12/13, its one failure also fails on v3.

Router unit suites pass on both engines, including new regression tests for the empty `to`, the same-URL replace, `router.listen`, and the query serialisation.

author: except-pass
body:
## The Slate — per-run A2UI surfaces

A new region of the run workspace card where an agent, the user, or any local process paints small interactive A2UI surfaces scoped to one run — an open-points list, diagram surfaces with per-surface threads, and live progress cards. Authored **file-in** (`.tinstar/slate/*.json` → watcher → projection), answered **HTTP-out** (persist-then-deliver to the run's agent). Points, threads, and lifecycle are store-backed; the file owns only a surface's A2UI body.

Origin: `docs/brainstorms/2026-07-21-the-slate-requirements.md` · Plan: `docs/plans/2026-07-21-001-feat-the-slate-plan.md`

### What's here (10 units)
- **U1** Promote the A2UI renderer to a shared `src/a2ui/` (reused by Roundup + the Slate).
- **U2** `RunData.slate` projection through the 3-place contract + guard tests.
- **U3** Store-backed points with merge-by-id (a file re-projection never clobbers a store-owned thread/status — KTD1).
- **bridge** Points → `run.slate` as the single render channel.
- **U4** `SlateWatcher`: fs-watch + poll backstop, validate, retain-last-valid, atomic-clear semantics.
- **U5** The Slate as an additive run-workspace column (`data-scrollable`, per-surface error boundaries).
- **U6/U8** The two hero surfaces: open-points list (state track, thread, resolve, add) and diagram surfaces (body + per-surface thread).
- **U7** Run-scoped endpoints (`/api/runs/:id/slate/…`), persist-then-deliver, anchored-regex routing, user-point reconciliation.
- **U9** `bin/tinstar-run` self-reporting wrapper + a server-side stalled-surface sweep.
- **U10** Agent authoring skill + `docs/the-slate.md`.

Also lands a standalone `fix(roundup): mouse wheel scrolls the widget` (the original request that kicked this off).

### Verification
- **2277 unit tests pass** (298 files), full `npm run typecheck` (3 tsconfigs) clean, `npm run lint` clean, both bundles build (`vite` client + `esbuild` server).
- Multi-agent code review ran (correctness, adversarial, api-contract, reliability, frontend-races); four fixes applied in `fix(review):`. No P0/P1 blockers.

### Residual Review Findings (follow-up, not blockers)
- **P2 — Completed `tinstar-run` surfaces get mislabeled "stalled" after ~10 min** (cross-reviewer). `finalize()` writes a terminal ✓/✗ card but doesn't resolve the point, so the staleness sweep re-marks it. Needs a terminal-card concept the sweep excludes.
- **P2 — id-less file surface can lose its thread on a body edit.** `synthesizeId` hashes headline+content, so editing a body re-hashes the id → old point (with the thread) retracted, new empty one created. `bin/tinstar-run` is safe (explicit `id`); hand/skill-authored id-less files are at risk. The skill already recommends stable ids — consider enforcing (reject id-less amend).
- **P3 — Control "answered" state is client-only / non-idempotent.** A widget remount re-arms a control; `/answer` has no already-answered guard, permitting a duplicate answer + second delivery.
- **P3 — Per-pid surface files are never pruned + the 3s poll re-reads the whole dir.** A run that shells hundreds of commands accumulates terminal cards and per-tick read work.
- **Release gate — `@tinstar/plugin-api` `Reply.author` widened to include `'process'`.** Backward-compatible (additive union member; no in-repo exhaustive switch), but the separately-published package needs a version bump + release note; `docs/releasing.md`'s republish diff-gate will fire.
- **Minor:** multi-line reply text still passes into delivered prompts (left intentionally — legitimate multi-line replies); a few unguarded setState-after-unmount paths (store-backed, no data loss); new routes not in `openapi.ts` (matches the pre-existing notices-routes gap).
- **Flaky:** `slate-watcher.test.ts` timing flaked once under heavy parallel load, passed on every clean re-run — watch in CI.

body:
Part of #508

## Summary

Repairs the three shipped .dsp files the `shippedDspCompile` census (#551) proved broken (ledger rows 19+20). **All three repaired in place** — each was a small break with complete descriptors/UI, not unfinished design, so nothing was removed from templates or descriptors.

| File | Failure (app's `@grame/faustwasm` path) | Repair |
|---|---|---|
| `noise-gate.dsp` | `undefined symbol : gate_stereo` | This toolchain's compressors.lib has **no** gate/expander symbols (probed: `gate_stereo`, `gate_mono`, `noise_gate`, `expander*` all undefined; `compressor_mono/stereo` exist). Rebuilt as a linked stereo gate from an AR envelope follower (`en.ar`) using the four declared sliders |
| `de-esser.dsp` | sequential-composition arity ×2 | `max()` envelope composition dropped a bus → fanned-out attack/release envelope; `select2` fed mismatched branches → `select2(listen, gain*dry, sidechain)` |
| `stereo-widener.dsp` | sequential-composition arity | Final `+`/`-` applied to single buses (each output needs both M and S) and the bass-duck envelope applied to nothing → inlined M/S processing; duck envelope now tracks the side signal |

## Compile evidence (all 17 shipped .dsp, same path as the app: `-I libraries/`)

- **Before:** `ERROR noise-gate.dsp :: undefined symbol : gate_stereo`; `ERROR de-esser.dsp :: sequential composition A:B (outputs [1] of A vs inputs [2] of B)`; `ERROR stereo-widener.dsp :: sequential composition A:B (outputs [2] of A vs inputs [4] of B)`
- **After:** `ALL 17 DSP FILES COMPILE`
- Param exposure from each compiled node's JSON UI tree (matches `builtinDSP.ts` descriptors, like spring-reverb in #551):
  - noise-gate → `/noise-gate/{attack,hold,release,threshold}`
  - de-esser → `/de-esser/{bandwidth,frequency,listen,ratio,threshold}`
  - stereo-widener → `/stereo-widener/{mono_bass,width}`

## Verification

- Census baseline now **empty** (goal of the item); the exact-set mechanism stays so any new failure fails CI
- `pnpm test:run shippedDspCompile.spec.ts` → 5 passed (5), exit 0; against the pre-fix DSPs → **4 failed | 1 passed**
- `pnpm test:run src/modules/PluginHost` → 105 passed (105), exit 0
- `pnpm exec eslint shippedDspCompile.spec.ts` → 0 problems, exit 0
- `pnpm typecheck` → exit 0; `pnpm typecheck:test` → exit 0; `pnpm deps:validate` → 0 baseline rows, exit 0

## Notes

The hand-rolled gate semantics are textbook (threshold detector → hold-extended open target → attack/release smoothing); `hold` acts as extra close delay, which is the honest mapping of the four sliders without `co.gate_stereo`'s exact (unavailable) implementation. The de-esser bass-duck curve keeps the author's `1 - envelope` shape; only the disconnected wiring was repaired.

Please take a good look at what changed and the test results before merging this pull request. ### What changed? #### ↗️ loofah (_indirect_, 2.24.1 → 2.25.2) · [Repo](https://github.com/flavorjones/loofah) · [Changelog](https://github.com/flavorjones/loofah/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
Security Advisories 🚨

🚨 Loofah `allowed_uri?` does not detect `javascript:` URIs split by named whitespace character references

Summary

Loofah::HTML5::Scrub.allowed_uri? does not correctly reject javascript: URIs when the scheme is split or prefixed by the HTML5 named character references 	 (tab) or 
 (line feed).

This is a bypass of the fix for GHSA-46fp-8f5p-pf2m, which handled the equivalent numeric character references (	, 
, ) but did not cover the named forms.

Details

allowed_uri? decodes HTML entities with CGI.unescapeHTML, which handles numeric character references but not HTML5 named character references. Payloads like java	script:alert(1) are therefore left intact, so the method does not recognize the javascript: scheme and returns true. A browser, however, decodes 	 and 
 to tab and line feed and strips them from the URL during parsing, producing javascript:alert(1).

	 and 
 are the only relevant named character references: across the HTML5 named-character table, they are the only two that decode to characters the WHATWG URL parser strips from a URL (U+0009 and U+000A; there is no named reference for U+000D).   /   decode to U+00A0, which browsers do not strip, so they aren't usable for this bypass.

Note that Loofah's default sanitize() path is not affected, because Nokogiri decodes or entity-escapes HTML entities during parsing before Loofah evaluates the URI protocol. This issue only affects callers of the public allowed_uri? string-level helper that pass it HTML-encoded strings.

Impact

Callers that validate a user-controlled URL with Loofah::HTML5::Scrub.allowed_uri? and then render the approved value into an href or other browser-interpreted URI attribute may be vulnerable to cross-site scripting (XSS). This includes applications that call allowed_uri? directly, as well as higher-level features built on top of it, such as Action Text 8.2's markdown link validation.

Mitigation

Upgrade to Loofah >= 2.25.2.

Credit

Responsibly reported by GitHub user @connorshea.

🚨 Loofah: SVG `href` attribute bypasses local-reference restriction

Summary

Loofah's HTML5 sanitizer restricted only the xlink:href attribute on certain SVG elements to local, same-document references. Browsers also accept a plain href attribute as an alternative to the deprecated xlink:href per the SVG 2 spec, but Loofah did not apply the same restriction to it, allowing those elements to reference arbitrary external documents.

Impact

SVG <use> can load and render external SVG content by reference. If the referenced external SVG is same-origin and contains scripts or other dangerous content, it could execute in the context of the sanitized document. <feImage> can load external images, which can be used for tracking. Modern browsers restrict cross-origin <use> fetches, which limits but does not eliminate the risk.

Applications that sanitize user-supplied SVG (directly, or as part of HTML) with Loofah's default allowlist are affected.

Mitigation

Upgrade to Loofah >= 2.25.2.

Credit

Found by the maintainer, Mike Dalessio, during a security audit.

🚨 Loofah `allowed_uri?` does not detect `javascript:` URIs split by numeric character references without semicolons

Summary

Loofah::HTML5::Scrub.allowed_uri? does not correctly reject javascript: or vbscript: URIs when the scheme is split by a numeric character reference that has no trailing semicolon. A browser decodes such references and resolves the URL to an executable javascript: scheme, while allowed_uri? reports it safe.

This is a bypass of the fix for GHSA-46fp-8f5p-pf2m, which handled numeric character references with a trailing ; (	, 
, ) but did not cover the forms without semicolons.

Details

allowed_uri? decodes HTML entities with CGI.unescapeHTML, which decodes numeric character references only when they carry a trailing ;. A reference without a semicolon such as &#58 (colon) or &#9 (tab) is left literal, so the scheme-detection check finds no scheme, and the method falls through to its scheme-less path and returns true.

A browser, however, decodes numeric character references even without a trailing semicolon. An encoded colon such as &#58 becomes the : scheme separator, so javascript&#58alert(1) resolves to javascript:alert(1). Encoded whitespace such as &#9 (tab) is decoded

author: copilot
body:
This updates color switching so the browser/UI theme color is applied after the `#content` animation completes, preventing stale `meta[name="theme-color"]` values. It also rolls the service worker cache to `v3` and removes legacy caches during activation to avoid serving outdated assets.

- **Color transition + theme metadata synchronization**
  - Updated `switchColor` in `js/color.js` to set `meta[name="theme-color"]` in the `animate(..., complete)` callback using the active palette entry.

- **Service worker cache versioning + cleanup**
  - Bumped `CACHE_NAME` in `sw.js` from `qset-cache-v2` to `qset-cache-v3`.
  - Added an `activate` handler that deletes all cache buckets except the current version.

```js
$('#content').animate(
  { color: colors[color].fg, backgroundColor: colors[color].bg },
  150,
  'swing',
  () => {
    document
      .querySelector('meta[name="theme-color"]')
      ?.setAttribute('content', colors[color].bg)
  }
)

self.addEventListener('activate', event =>
  event.waitUntil(
    caches.keys().then(names =>
      Promise.all(names.filter(name => name !== CACHE_NAME).map(name => caches.delete(name)))
    )
  )
)
```

author: copilot
body:
The `Lint & Test 🧪` job failed because `flutter analyze` could not resolve `lib/firebase_options.dart` (`DefaultFirebaseOptions` undefined). The QA workflow now guarantees that file exists in both secret-available and secret-unavailable CI contexts.

- **Root cause**
  - `qa` job ran analysis/tests without generating `lib/firebase_options.dart`, while other jobs injected it.

- **Workflow change (`.github/workflows/main.yml`)**
  - Added a **Provide Firebase Options** step to `qa` before dependency install/analyze/test.
  - Behavior:
    - Use `secrets.FIREBASE_OPTIONS` when present.
    - Otherwise generate a minimal fallback `lib/firebase_options.dart` with `DefaultFirebaseOptions.currentPlatform`.

- **Why this is scoped**
  - No app/runtime source changes; only QA job setup was adjusted to unblock lint/test compilation.

```yaml
- name: Provide Firebase Options
  run: |
    if [ -n "${{ secrets.FIREBASE_OPTIONS }}" ]; then
      echo "${{ secrets.FIREBASE_OPTIONS }}" > lib/firebase_options.dart
    else
      cat > lib/firebase_options.dart <<'EOF'
      import 'package:firebase_core/firebase_core.dart';

      class DefaultFirebaseOptions {
        static FirebaseOptions get currentPlatform => const FirebaseOptions(
              apiKey: 'test-api-key',
              appId: '1:1234567890:web:test',
              messagingSenderId: '1234567890',
              projectId: 'test-project-id',
            );
      }
      EOF
    fi
```

author: paulnsorensen
body:
Fixes the three open cheese-factory defects surfaced by run `wf_415200d0-47b` (sorensen-labs/tdbr, spec `match-length-target`).

## #489 — bare-string `args` silently dropped → candidates mode
- A non-JSON string arg is now treated as the spec itself (`{spec: args.trim()}`); a JSON-quoted string likewise; object JSON unchanged. The harness invoke hint passes slash arguments as bare strings, so `/cheese-factory <path>` now resolves directly.
- `SPEC_ARG_RE` accepts absolute and `~/` paths (secondary defect); `..` traversal is still rejected by the separate check, and the allowed charset stays shell-metacharacter-free (the arg is interpolated unquoted into the resolver's Bash command, where a word-initial `~/` tilde-expands).

Closes #489

## #492 — decomposer over-splits a coupled feature, no dependency graph
- The decomposer now emits optional `depends_on` edges and carries explicit splitting rules: split only where curds build/test from `origin/main` alone; a spec-declared multi-site contract is one indivisible curd.
- `mergeCoupledCurds` (extends ADR-005's file-overlap merge) collapses groups coupled by shared files **or** a `depends_on` edge, transitively; if merging leaves one curd, the run degrades to single-pass.
- Merge-over-topological-ordering rationale recorded in **ADR-008** (dependent curds serialize either way; stacked-branch bookkeeping and reviewing A's unreviewed work inside B's taste gate weren't worth the nominal fan-out).

Closes #492

## #493 — `blocked: out of context` cook is terminal, partial work reaped
- `NO_CHAIN_DIRECTIVE` now requires write-phase agents to commit WIP locally before writing a partial `halt` slug — partial work survives worktree reaping regardless of orchestration.
- A cook status matching `/^(blocked|halt)\b/i` with a `worktree_path` gets up to 2 **fresh** coder continuations (never resuming the exhausted agent): each re-enters the curd branch, commits remaining partial work as its first action, orients from `git diff origin/main...<branch>` + the partial slug, and finishes only the remaining criteria. Terminal failure after the cap notes the branch may carry committed WIP. Rationale in **ADR-009**.

Closes #493

## Tests & verification
- 8 new/rewritten cases in `tests/workflows/cheese-factory.test.mjs`: bare/JSON-quoted string args, absolute + `~/` path validation, `..` rejection, 2-curd and 3-curd `depends_on` merge scenarios, continuation exhaustion / mid-chain success / no-worktree skip.
- `./tests/workflows-test.sh` 151/151 · bats 1206/1206 · `just check` exit 0.
- Amusing field note: the coder agent writing these tests itself drowned mid-task and was completed by a fresh continuation seeded from its handback note — the exact #493 recovery pattern, exercised manually.

| Field | Value |

| **Current-state verdict** | STILL BROKEN → fixed here |
| **Tests / hard gates** | `npm test` 6145 pass / 0 fail · authority/banned/allowlist/ladder/paper-weight/wiring guards pass · lint 0 errors · secret scan OK |

| **Owner authorization required** | No |
| **Live validation** | Post-deploy owner app-test steps listed below |
| **Merge authority** | Claude merges the exact passing head under standing authority once all GitHub checks are green |

---

### Concern

For active-session plan explanations/corrections, answer only the requested discrepancy from relevant facts, and never claim a completed plan write without verified proof — response grounding only.

### Exact production failures

Both turns correctly reached `/api/coach/chat` (source: Gemini) after PR #1121; the routing was right, the responses were not.

**Failure 1 — unrelated exercise contamination.** The athlete asked only about Seated Row. Atlas answered:

> "Bench Press has come in below your recent benchmark 5 of the last 5 sessions. What's going on there — the load feels off, recovery, or just not feeling it lately?
>
> For Seated Rows, the plan calls for 200 for 10 reps at 1 RIR to increase the load from the 195 logged in your last session."

The Seated Row half was fine; the Bench Press paragraph was unrelated. Turn id: `turn:2026-07-21T23:36:33.850Z_6_vu0gue`.

**Failure 2 — unsupported completed-mutation claim.** The athlete said "That isn't what you planned. You planned 3 sets at 8 reps." Atlas answered:

> "The plan was updated. It now calls for 3 sets of 10 reps at 200, aiming for 1 RIR."

`/api/coach/chat` is read-only; no trusted plan-write proof accompanied the turn (`Coach_Shadow.trace_missing` includes `write_proof`), no `Session_Plans` event and no `Log_Cleaned` entry were created. Turn id: `turn:2026-07-21T23:36:58.255Z_7_hjnefu`.

### Root cause — the unrelated Bench Press paragraph

`buildChatContext` (routes/coachOps.js) passes all-lift diagnostics to the model: `stalls` (every stalled lift) and `memory_patterns` (up to 5 lifts). `deriveChatCoachMode` sets `coach_mode` to `"challenge"` from **any** `memory_patterns` entry, and the CHALLENGE-MODE prompt (`services/coach.js`) instructs the model to proactively name that pattern and ask one question — the exact "below your recent benchmark 5 of 5 — what's going on?" shape. Nothing narrowed the diagnostics to the exercise the athlete asked about, so the Bench Press pattern was surfaced during a Seated Row question.

### Root cause — the false "plan was updated" claim

Nothing deterministically prevented a completed-write claim on the read-only route. The register guard (`findRegisterViolations`) covers only profanity and PR/celebration vocabulary; the prompt's "you never save/change anything" rule is advisory and the model violated it. The route treated the model prose as safe once it passed the register guard.

### Selected implementation approach

A new pure module `services/coachResponseGrounding.js` (no I/O, no LLM, no clock), wired into `/api/coach/chat`:

- **Context narrowing before generation** (`narrowContextToPlanTurn`): for an active plan explanation/dispute/correction, filter `stalls` + `memory_patterns` to the exercise(s) the turn is about (named in the message, else the active plan lift), drop `muscle_gaps`, and **recompute `coach_mode` from the narrowed patterns** so a challenge can only ever name the target lift itself. A broad-session review is left untouched. Applied **after** the drift shadow / recovery routing, so observability sees the unmodified context.
- **Deterministic response validation + grounded fallback** (`detectUnsupportedMutationClaim` + `buildGroundedPlanStatement`): a state-aware detector flags completed-mutation prose; on this read-only route (no write proof, ever) a flagged reply is replaced with a truthful statement of what the current plan shows plus that nothing changed, and any proposal is dropped.

No prompt rewrite — the deterministic guards do the enforcement.

### Relevance contract

An active-plan explanation/correction answer may discuss the asked exercise, its current prescribed sets/reps/weight/RIR, its directly relevant history, and its rationale. It must not introduce unrelated exercise diagnostics unless the athlete asks for a broad-session review (kept unnarrowed) or the issue is safety-critical. For the production Seated Row turn, Seated Row is allowed; Bench Press commentary is not.

### Mutation / write-proof contract

The response distinguishes: (1) what the current plan says; (2) what the athlete claims; (3) an unapproved proposed change; (4) an approved write with proof; (5) insufficient evidence. Completed-mutation language ("updated", "changed", "switched", "adjusted", "saved", "it now calls for…") is allowed only in state 4. `/api/coach/chat` can never receive verified write proof, so **completed-mutation language is always prohibited on this route**; the detector is state-aware, so proposals ("I can propose…"), questions ("want me to update?"), athlete quotations ("you said the plan was updated"), and negations ("I haven't changed it") pass through. A proposed plan edit still flows through the existing consent/approval mechanism and never mutates the plan by itself.

### Tests and evidence

- **`test/coachResponseGrounding.test.js`** (pure): mutation-claim state-awareness (all completed forms flagged; proposals/questions/quotations/negations/present-state not); relevance filtering including the Bench-vs-Seated **Test 6** control (target lift kept, others dropped) and the broad-review **Test 5** control (unchanged); grounded statement incl. **Test 7** uncertainty with no plan in view.
- **`test/coachChatGrounding.test.js`** (live `/api/coach/chat`): **Failure 2** end-to-end (grounded to the current plan, false prose never shown, proposal dropped, no write — `appendRows` throws if hit); **Failure 1** narrowing wired (the Bench stall is filtered from the model context; the broad-review control keeps it); **Test 3** genuine proposal preserved; **Test 7** ambiguous evidence → uncertainty; **Test 8** one correlated Coach_Shadow/Coach_Response pair storing the exact final text; plus a **regression** that the acceptable present-state explanation is not rewritten.
- Verified failing-first against the pre-fix route (the four new-behavior tests fail without the wiring; the three unchanged-behavior tests pass).
- Gates: `npm test` 6145 pass / 0 fail; all six drift guards pass; lint 0 errors; secret scan OK.

### Trust / scope safety

- [x] Routing remains on `/api/coach/chat` — PR #1121 routing untouched
- [x] No plan or workout data mutated (read-only route; grounded path returns via the standard success helper, no writes; `Session_Plans`/`Session_Plan_Sets`/`Log_Cleaned`/`Effort`/notes/constraints untouched)
- [x] Coach_Shadow and Coach_Response schemas, telemetry writers, and `turn_id` unchanged; one turn still yields one correlated pair
- [x] Phase 4 not started; CoachTurnPacket not made authoritative
- [x] Preview→approve→write trust boundary and the existing proposal/approval flow unchanged
- [x] Recommendation mathematics unchanged;

author: fsantibanezleal
body:
## What

Four things, all verified against the engine rather than assumed.

### 1. The case-source selector was dead UI
`Prebaked` and `Pretrained` loaded the same artifact and rendered the same tabs, differing by one sentence of copy. The axis was also wrong: prebaked-vs-pretrained is a METHOD distinction, which is exactly what the tabs already do.

The source now selects the DATA: **Real samples / Synthetic / Upload**. The synthetic_battery artifact had been baked since v0.03 and left unused behind a literal `void SYNTH_SLUG`.

### 2. New Degradation tab
F1@2px vs crack width (9 px down to 2 px, contrast and angle fixed) for the whole classical ladder. Exact generated ground truth means a drop measures the METHOD, not the labelling. The panel names the two things a reader would otherwise read as bugs: the ordering inverts (Otsu/Sauvola pinned at 1.0, minimal-path and RF fusion below), and fewer curves show than methods because L3 and L4 coincide when there is no gap to bridge.

### 3. dacl10k metric was not benchmark-comparable
`_macro_iou` averaged a per-batch IoU; the benchmark pools intersection and union over the whole split and divides once. So the shipped "0.117 vs 0.424" was never like-for-like.

| protocol | mIoU |
|---|---|
| batch-averaged (old) | 0.0912 |
| pooled @ 0.50 untuned | 0.1441 |
| pooled @ 0.20 val-tuned | 0.1685 |

New `eval_dacl10k.py` recomputes pooled from a saved checkpoint in one pass, sweeps the threshold, and states the tuned-on-val caveat next to the untuned column.

Per-class breakdown is the real story: 10 of 19 classes average 0.3201 IoU, 9 sit at exactly 0, and those 9 are the rarest (ExposedRebars 0.48% of pixels, Crack 1.37%). Unweighted-BCE collapse, not a capacity limit. Fixed with `--pos-weight` using sqrt(neg/pos) on a cached TRAIN-split sample (never val).

### 4. SAC foundation-adapter scaffold
SAM ViT-B, norm-only tuning (36.9K of 93.7M + 388K head), gradient-checkpointed for 8 GB. CPU-smoke-validated. Training queued behind the GPU serialization.

## Verification
Browser-verified both themes: tab sets, thumbnail counts, chart pixels drawn, no console errors. Caught a uPlot default-time-scale bug rendering crack widths as clock times.

author: buremba
body: ## The bug `create_version` decided whether to re-derive `sources` from the prompt's `@`-chips using only `args.prompt !== undefined`. So **any** prompt edit took the derive branch — including a plain-text one. For a chip-free prompt `extractSourcesFromPromptTokens` returns `[]`, so rewording a prompt **silently deleted every source**. No error, no warning, `health` stays green — the Behavior just runs forever against no data. Found by probing production directly: ``` createVersion({ behavior_id, prompt: "Summarize {{src}} differently." }) → { source_count: 0, removed_sources: ["src"] } ``` The behavior had one working source before that call and none after, from an edit that never mentioned sources. ## The fix Derive only when the prompt actually **carries** chips — or when the previous prompt did, so removing the last chip still clears its source. A chip-free prompt edit is a metadata edit and inherits stored sources, matching the `omitted → inherit` intent already documented for metadata bumps. Explicit `sources` still replace (including `[]` to clear), so #2048 semantics are untouched. ## Evidence red→green on the final code, verified by reverting just the guard to `promptEdited`: - with guard → **15/15 pass** - without guard → **3 fail** (`preserves stored sources when only plain prompt text changes` + 2 others) Wider regression run: **198/198 across 26 files** (`integration/watchers`, `integration/behaviors`, source-validation, health-surfacing, approval-e2e). `make pre-pr` clean. Three cases are pinned so the derive path isn't weakened: chip-free edit inherits, chip-removal still clears, explicit sources still replace. --- Need help on this PR? Tag /codesmith with what you need. Autofix is enabled.

author: oxenjo30
body:
## What & why

Google Play flagged two policy warnings under **Policy status → App updates with these issues will be rejected** (deadline **Aug 31, 2026**):

1. **App must target Android 16 (API level 36) or higher**
2. **App must use Google Play Billing Library version 8.0.0 or later**

Both are now fixed.

## Changes (config/dependency only — no runtime behavior change)

| Warning | Change | From → To |
|---|---|---|
| Target API 36 | `compileSdk` / `targetSdk` | 35 → **36** |
| (needed for SDK 36) | AGP | 8.7.3 → **8.13.0** (first 8.x AGP supporting API 36) |
| (needed for AGP 8.13) | Gradle wrapper | 8.10.2 → **8.13** |
| Billing 8 | `com.android.billingclient:billing-ktx` | 7.1.1 → **8.0.0** |
| Release | `versionCode` / `versionName` | 46 → **47** / **0.1.47** |

JDK stays 17.

## Billing 8.0 migration: zero source changes

`BillingRepository.kt` already targeted the 8.0 API surface, so bumping the dependency was sufficient:
- ✅ `enablePendingPurchases(PendingPurchasesParams.newBuilder()...)` — the new required form (parameterless overload was removed in 8.0)
- ✅ `queryPurchasesAsync(QueryPurchasesParams, ...)` — the new form (String-skuType overload removed)
- ✅ KTX `queryProductDetails(QueryProductDetailsParams)` suspend fn — `result.billingResult` / `result.productDetailsList` still resolve
- ✅ Uses **none** of 8.0's removed methods (`querySkuDetailsAsync`, `queryPurchaseHistory`)
- ✅ `WalletScreen`'s `oneTimePurchaseOfferDetails.formattedPrice` unchanged in 8.0

Diamond top-up remains **dark** (`DIAMOND_TOPUP_ENABLED` off), so this touches no live purchase flow.

## Verification

`./gradlew :app:compileReleaseKotlin` → **BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 4m 1s** against compileSdk 36 + AGP 8.13 + Gradle 8.13 + billing 8.0.0. Only pre-existing deprecation warnings (EncryptedSharedPreferences, `Icons.Filled.ReceiptLong`), no errors, none introduced by this change.

## Follow-up (owner)
After merge + CI: build the signed v47 AAB and upload to Play, then re-check **Policy status** — both warnings should clear.

author: alenlukic
body:
## Summary

Building sets and exploring transitions now takes fewer detours across the client. The matches quadrant can accept dropped tracks, filter by candidate track attributes, and stay responsive with large result sets, so it behaves more like the rest of the workspace. The explorer canvas also becomes more direct to manipulate with drag-to-add, multi-select deletion and undo, and persistent zoom controls, while shared table chrome is updated to support the new interactions.

## Changelist

- Standardize a `Pre.` preview column across the configurable tables and teach saved table preferences to insert newly introduced columns in their intended positions instead of appending them.
- Expand the shared filter model to support select-style value filters, enabling candidate key/BPM/genre filtering in matches and Camelot key filtering in the set pool without confusing track attributes with compatibility scores.
- Let dropped browse, tracklist, and pool rows become the active match source, clearing the current transition chain and highlighting the matches quadrant as a valid drop target.
- Virtualize the matches result list so large match sets stay responsive during re-renders, filtering, and column-size or preference changes.
- Rework the explorer canvas around direct manipulation: drop tracks onto open space or an existing node to add roots or children, marquee-select nodes with Ctrl/Cmd-drag, and manage zoom from persistent on-canvas controls.
- Replace explorer delete confirmation flows with immediate deletion plus undo support, including batched restoration of deleted nodes and reconnection of surviving edges when possible.
- Polish the shared table and set header controls with icon-based sort/filter actions, a left-pinned header action slot, earlier set-delete placement, and expanded Vitest coverage for the new drag/drop, filtering, and explorer behaviors.
