author: lobinuxsoft
body:
`ome_sdf` held two unrelated things behind one name, and only one of them is dead.

| | What it was | Fate |
|---|---|---|
| `SDF_PRIMITIVES_WGSL` + shaders | CSG primitive library for the ray-marching renderer | **Deleted** — that renderer went in the 2026-05-02 pivot; nothing has consumed this since |
| `sparse/` | Chunk-local sparse voxel storage with LOD (#136) | **Moved to `ome_world::voxel`** |

The `sparse` module is the substrate Phase 2.5 extracts meshes from (#393, #397, #398), and it is the shape of data rapier 0.34's voxel collider consumes. Deleting it would have meant rewriting it. It now sits next to the rest of the streaming code, with its eight shaders and its WGSL validation tests (which brought `naga` + `pollster` dev-deps along).

## Also removed

- The seven `Sdf*` brush components from `ome_ecs`. Unlike the crate these were **not** opt-in: `ome_ecs` is core, so they compiled into every build and `EcsPlugin` registered all of them — describing geometry for a renderer that no longer exists.
- Their "SDF Shapes" spawn submenu in the editor.
- `ome_gravity`'s dependency on `ome_sdf`, which its code never referenced.

## Two different things called SDF

Worth stating, since the name is doing double duty and this PR only kills one of them:

- **SDF as a rendering/authoring technique** — CSG brushes, raymarching. Dead since the pivot; this PR removes the remains.
- **SDF as a data format** — a voxel storing a signed distance. Alive and load-bearing: dual contouring extracts meshes from exactly that, and rapier's voxel collider reads it directly, which is *better* than the SDF broadphase #42 proposed (closed as superseded).

`ome_bvh::SdfPrimitive` is untouched for the same reason: despite the name it is the current chunk-content representation for world streaming (`ome_world::content`, `content_sources/city`), not a brush.

## Migration

Scenes carrying `Sdf*` components still load — unknown components park in `DynamicComponents` instead of failing the load, so `TestEngine2.0`'s scenes survive. Before that landed this removal would have emptied them.

`docs/MEMORY.md` is updated: it claimed `ome_sdf` survived the pivot as authoring brushes, which is what this PR retires.

**1055 tests pass** (down from 1072 — the deleted crate's own tests).

author: jordypirata
body:
## Summary

Adds `scripts/update.sh`, a self-contained updater that replaces the currently
installed **phoenixd**, **Ambrosia server** (jar), and **Ambrosia client**
(Next.js build) with the latest GitHub release, following the same conventions
as `scripts/install.sh`. Also consolidates CI so the same workflow that
validates `install.sh` now also validates `update.sh` end-to-end.

## What's included

### `scripts/update.sh`
- Resolves the latest release tag for both `olympus-btc/ambrosia` and
  `ACINQ/phoenixd` (pinnable via `AMBROSIA_TAG` / `PHOENIXD_TAG`).
- Skips components already at the latest version (override with `--force`).
- Verifies the phoenixd package via the ACINQ PGP key + SHA256SUMS before
  installing.
- Detects installed versions from the jar manifest, the client
  `.ambrosia-version` marker, and `phoenixd --version`.
- Handles systemd services gracefully (stops before update, restarts if they
  were active) and self-heals the client wrapper script/symlink.
- Non-interactive via `--yes`; safe cleanup of temp dirs on exit.

### CI: `Test Install & Update Scripts` (`.github/workflows/test_install.yml`)
Consolidated into the existing install workflow so install + update are covered
together (update depends on a prior install):

- **`lint-scripts`** (ubuntu): `shellcheck` + `bash -n` on `install.sh` and
  `update.sh` — fast, no network.
- **`install-and-update`** (matrix: ubuntu + macOS):
  1. Installs a pinned **older** baseline (`v0.7.0-beta`) via `install.sh`.
  2. Verifies the baseline (symlinks, jar, client deps, exact versions).
  3. Runs `update.sh --yes`.
  4. Verifies server, client, and phoenixd were actually updated to the
     dynamically-resolved latest release, and symlinks remain valid.
  5. **Significance guard**: fails loudly if the pinned baseline ever equals the
     latest release (which would make the update a no-op), prompting a bump of
     `BASELINE_AMBROSIA_TAG`.

## How to test

Locally:
```bash
shellcheck scripts/update.sh
bash -n scripts/update.sh
```

The `install-and-update` job exercises the real path in CI:
`v0.7.0-beta → latest` for server/client and `0.7.2 → latest` for phoenixd on
both Linux and macOS.

## Checklist

- [x] Code follows style guidelines (conventional commits, shellcheck-clean)
- [x] CI validates the change on Linux and macOS

author: kmay89
body:
## What Changed

The last of the four world-class hardening items: **opt-in hardware root of trust + attestation** — delivered as a **design RFC for your sign-off**, not code. (Secure Boot / flash encryption burn irreversible eFuses and directly trade against the flasher's "you can't brick it" promise, so this is a decision doc, not a merge of lockdown code.)

The repo already has the *ingredients* — a self-provisioned Ed25519 device identity, Ed25519-signed OTA, and a **prepared-but-unenabled** Secure Boot / flash-encryption kit in `firmware/provisioning/` ([`secure_provisioning.md`](../blob/claude/hardware-root-of-trust-rfc/docs/secure_provisioning.md)). What's missing is the **decision layer**, which [`docs/design/hardware_root_of_trust.md`](../blob/claude/hardware-root-of-trust-rfc/docs/design/hardware_root_of_trust.md) supplies:

- **Reconciles the root of trust with "you cannot brick your Canary."** An opt-in **tier ladder** (0 = default, un-brickable → 4 = irreversible Secure Boot + flash encryption + JTAG-off). Tiers 1–2 are pure-software, reversible, and should become universal (anti-rollback, boot safe-mode, attestation, flasher-awareness); Tiers 3–4 knowingly trade the un-brickable guarantee for tamper-*resistance*, gated behind an explicit ceremony. Locked devices recover via **signed OTA + A/B + boot safe-mode** instead of USB reflash — the RFC specifies that the safety net lands *before* any tier removes the USB net.
- **An offline-verifiable attestation protocol** (`securacv.attest/v1`): a nonce-bound challenge-response over the pinned identity key + a firmware measurement, extending the existing `securacv.canary.manifest/v1` self-manifest from "says it's healthy" to "proves it, freshly, un-replayably." No cloud in the trust path.
- **Hardware-bound keys** via the ESP32-S3 DS peripheral (Tier 3+), honest about the Ed25519-vs-DS-RSA wrinkle and about what flash encryption does and doesn't defend (key-at-rest, not a decapping lab).
- **Principle preservation** (2/4/10): the default Canary stays un-brickable and sovereign, the **owner** holds the Secure Boot key (the project never does), and attestation verifies offline.

§7 phases the work (reversible value first); **§8 is the open-decisions list for you to sign off** before any irreversible tier becomes code.

## Checklist

### Required
- [x] Firmware compiles in **both** Arduino IDE and PlatformIO — *N/A: documentation only (`docs/design/hardware_root_of_trust.md` + its index entry). No code, no firmware, no eFuse operations.*
- [x] `regression_check.sh` passes — *N/A. Ran `scripts/lint_docs_index.py` (OK, 162 docs, all reachable, no dead links).*
- [x] No new hardcoded secrets or default passwords — *none; it's a design doc.*
- [x] All new UI buttons have working API endpoints — *N/A.*
- [x] All new API endpoints return proper JSON — *N/A.*

### Security Review
- [x] No new cryptographic primitives / custom crypto **introduced** — *this is a *proposal*; it specifies protocols (attestation challenge-response, DS-bound keys) for review, and implements nothing. Any crypto lands in a later, separately-reviewed PR.*
- [x] No key material in logs/exports/API — *N/A (doc).*
- [x] No downgrade paths (signed → unsigned) — *the RFC *adds* a boot-chain trust layer and is explicit that the default posture is unchanged until a tier is opted into.*
- [x] No new outbound connections (Principle 2) — *the proposed attestation is offline-verifiable by design; no cloud in the trust path.*
- [x] No new trust assumptions introduced by this PR — *doc only; the design explicitly keeps the owner (not the project) holding the Secure Boot key.*
- [x] Device still functions fully offline; user retains sovereignty (Principles 4, 10) — *the RFC's central constraint: the default Canary stays Tier 0, un-brickable and recoverable; irreversible lockdown is opt-in only.*
- [x] No new compile-time features / network services / production interfaces / dependencies — *N/A: no code.*

### Lessons Learned
- [x] New pattern documented — the RFC follows the repo's design-RFC format (mirrors [`design/vault_operator_ux_v1_1.md`](../blob/claude/hardware-root-of-trust-rfc/docs/design/vault_operator_ux_v1_1.md)) and is indexed in `docs/README.md`; it names its open decisions explicitly for sign-off rather than presuming them.

> Note: as with the other open PRs, CI's "page logic tests" is currently red on `main` from a pre-existing `vision.test.js` drift (unrelated to this docs-only change).

body:
## What

Two dead e2e specs were poisoning the local `test:e2e` gate with 8 guaranteed
failures:

1. **`e2e/oauth-google.spec.ts`** — gated behind a module-level
   `test.skip(process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_OAUTH_GOOGLE_ENABLED !== "true", ...)`,
   mirroring `account-set-password.spec.ts`'s existing skip pattern. Google
   OAuth is parked (#232) and the flag is `false` everywhere, so all 8 tests
   in this spec now skip cleanly instead of failing.
2. **`e2e/login-magic-link.spec.ts`** — the happy-path test asserted a
   `getByRole('button', { name: /send the link/i })` control that no longer
   exists; `/login` defaults to the password/OTP flow post-M5. Rewrote it to
   drive the real UI (email → Continue → "Email me a code instead") against
   the seeded deterministic test user, added a single-project guard so
   `chromium` and `mobile-safari` don't both fire a real OTP request for the
   same seeded email inside the same `AUTH_OTP_VERIFY` rate-limit window, and
   sourced the success copy from `AUTH_COPY.codeSentHelper` instead of a
   hardcoded string duplicate. The passing `?error=` test is untouched.

Zero app/source code changed — e2e specs only.

Closes #455, Closes #456.

## Why

Local `pnpm test:e2e` is the mandatory e2e gate for this repo (CI doesn't
run e2e). Two permanently-broken specs meant every contributor had to
mentally subtract 8 known-bad failures from the gate output to find real
regressions — that's exactly the kind of gate poison that lets a real
regression hide in the noise.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm typecheck` — 0 errors
- [x] `pnpm lint` — 0 errors, 12 pre-existing warnings in unrelated files
      (react-hook-form `watch()` memoization notes, a few unused-var
      warnings) — none in the files touched here
- [x] `pnpm test` — 162 test files, 2090 tests, all passing
- [x] `pnpm exec playwright test e2e/oauth-google.spec.ts` — 8/8 skipped,
      0 failures (`NEXT_PUBLIC_OAUTH_GOOGLE_ENABLED` unset)
- [x] `pnpm exec playwright test e2e/login-magic-link.spec.ts` — both
      chromium tests pass; mobile-safari's OTP-request test self-skips per
      its documented single-project guard, its error-param test passes
- [x] **Full local gate** — `pnpm exec playwright test` run twice against an
      isolated local dev server on the local Supabase CLI stack (see
      Notes): once at default parallelism (140 passed / 65 skipped / 14
      failed) and once with `--workers=1` to rule out cross-spec rate-limit
      collisions (148 passed / 65 skipped / **6 failed**). In both runs,
      **zero** failures came from `oauth-google.spec.ts` or
      `login-magic-link.spec.ts` — this PR's target class drops from 8
      failed (2026-07-15 baseline: 153 passed/58 skipped/8 failed) to 0.
      The residual 6 failures (`m3-golden-path.spec.ts`,
      `invite-instant-signup.spec.ts`, `login-flow.spec.ts`, all
      mobile-safari) are pre-existing and unrelated to this diff — out of
      scope for this PR.

## Non-goals (explicit, per plan)

- No refactor of `SUCCESS_COPY`'s home beyond importing the existing
  `AUTH_COPY.codeSentHelper` — no new copy token added.
- No expansion of `oauth-google.spec.ts` coverage; it stays skipped until
  #232 lands.
- No fix for the 6 unrelated pre-existing mobile-safari failures surfaced
  by the full-suite run — filing a follow-up separately if not already
  tracked.

## Notes

**Environment note (flagging for visibility, no code impact):** this
worktree's `.env.local` points `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` /
`SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` at the project's only Supabase instance
(also serving prod), not a local stack. To run the e2e gate without
touching that project, I started an isolated `next dev -p 3100` process
with `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` / `ANON_KEY` / `SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`
shell-overridden to the local Supabase CLI stack (`127.0.0.1:54321`,
standard local demo JWTs) — `.env.local` itself was never edited — and
confirmed via the `sb-127-auth-token` cookie that every run in this
session targeted local only.

Microcopy: no new UI-facing strings — the one copy change swaps a
hardcoded test-file literal for the existing, already-shipped
`AUTH_COPY.codeSentHelper` string (no voice change, no new surface).

body:
## Why

Workflow discovery now preserves host and executor filesystem authority, but session construction still needs a small, explicit contract for assembling the fixed discovery roots. This slice provides that contract without coupling `codex-core-workflows` to config/session internals.

## What

- adds `WorkflowRootAssembly` with a mandatory Codex-home root and named optional user-home/project inputs
- emits project, personal, then Codex-home roots in fixed precedence order
- requires callers to pass an already-resolved project boundary instead of treating an arbitrary cwd as the repository root
- keeps host paths as `AbsolutePathBuf` and executor paths as `PathUri`
- retains the exact executor filesystem authority and never projects foreign paths onto the host
- fails closed when an opaque executor URI cannot be joined
- performs no filesystem probing; missing directories remain discovery's responsibility

## Validation

- `just test -p codex-core-workflows`: 22/22 passed
- `cargo check --locked -p codex-core-workflows --all-targets`: passed

## Scope

This is an additive root-assembly API only. It changes no config, core session behavior, dependencies, lockfiles, CLI, app-server, persistence, or UI. The next stacked slice consumes it during session construction, resolves the project boundary through the selected primary environment filesystem, and caches the resulting registry.

author: sdilshan91
body:
## DF-19 / ISSUE-045 — pool-aware carry-forward restoration

Persists the BR-4 **FIFO carry-forward/accrual split** on leave-balance consumption so cancel restores each pool to its correct bucket (preserving the carried expiry) and the year-end expiry job forfeits exactly the remaining carried days. Closes the last item in the DEFERRED-FOLLOWUPS queue.

### Model + migration
- `LeavePool` enum; `LeaveLedger.Pool` + `CarryForwardTrackingId`; `LeaveCarryForwardTracking.ConsumedDays`
- Migration `20260722005029_LeavePoolAllocation` — columns + backfill converging `ConsumedDays` to the prior derived `MIN(carried, used-in-to-year)` so existing buckets stay **byte-identical**
- `ProcessExpiryAsync` now reads the persisted `ConsumedDays` (`remaining = carried − consumed − expired`); `GetUsedInYearAsync` retired

### Consumption wiring — a CRITICAL caught in review
The first cut bumped `ConsumedDays` **only on approval**, so encashment + LOP consumption became invisible to the expiry job → **over-forfeiture** of already-consumed carried days (a money regression the `integration-enforcer` flagged CRITICAL).

Fix — extract the FIFO split into **one shared choke point** and route **every** consumption path through it:
- `PooledLeaveLedger.AppendDeductionAsync` — draws carry-forward first, tags each row's pool (+ bucket id), bumps `ConsumedDays`, returns a `PooledDeductionResult` with `Undo` for rollback
- Wired: leave **approval** (delegates), **HR encashment** (`Encashed`, with `Undo` on adjustment-reject), **compulsory-leave**, **LOP-conversion**
- Backfill (`Used`+`Encashed`) and runtime now agree across all four paths

Re-audit verdict: **PASS** — CRITICAL closed; backfill↔runtime parity, encashment rollback atomicity, and multi-row aggregate integrity all confirmed.

### Tests
`LeavePoolAwareCarryForwardTests`: approve-split → cancel-restore (per-pool, expiry preserved) → expiry-forfeit lifecycle; expired-bucket → accrual fallback; shared-helper bump → no over-forfeit; `Undo` rollback. Mutation-sensitive per `test-authenticator` (AUTHENTIC).

**617 Leave + 64 LOP/Encashment** unit arms green. Testcontainers Postgres arms (incl. `FinalSettlementPostgresTests.Encashment_MoneyFigure…OnPostgres`) defer to the Docker-enabled run per the standing method.

### Follow-up filed
- **DF-65** (LOW): the year-end auto-encashment writer (`LeaveCarryForwardService.cs:189`) also doesn't bump `ConsumedDays` — different (batch-sweep) semantics; needs-decision, not wired here to avoid double-counting the sweep's own forfeiture.

author: sahilkanger
body:
# docs: document single-argument link_error errback used by send_task

Closes #9034

## Summary
The [Linking (callbacks/errbacks)](https://docs.celeryq.dev/en/stable/userguide/calling.html#linking-callbacks-errbacks) guide documents only one errback calling convention — a direct call with `(request, exc, traceback)` — and states the worker "won't actually call the errback as a task." That isn't universally true, and following the documented pattern with `app.send_task(..., link_error=...)` fails with `TypeError: ... missing 2 required positional arguments: 'exc' and 'traceback'` (reported in #9034, confirmed by a second user). This PR documents the second convention and softens the blanket claim.

## Root cause
Celery chooses the errback convention per-errback in the failure path (`celery/backends/base.py`, errback-dispatch loop):
- The errback is called directly as `errback(request, exc, traceback)` **only** when it is a registered task, not a `bind=True` partial, and accepts **more than one** argument.
- Otherwise — a single-argument errback, or one that isn't registered on the worker handling the failure — it is re-applied **as a task** with the failed task's **id** as the sole argument (the code comments: *"Previously errback was called as a task so we still need to do so if the errback only takes a single task_id arg."*).

`send_task` references the task by name, so its `link_error` errback commonly takes the single-argument path — which the docs never mentioned. This is a documentation gap, not a code change (the behavior is intentional/back-compat), matching the issue's `Category: Documentation` label.

## Solution
In `docs/userguide/calling.rst`, errbacks section:
- Soften "The worker won't actually call the errback as a task…" to "In most cases…", with a pointer to the new note.
- Add a `.. note::` explaining the two conventions and, for the single-argument form, a runnable example using `allow_join_result` + `app.AsyncResult(task_id)`, ending with the `app.send_task(..., link_error=on_error.s())` usage.

## Changes
```
docs/userguide/calling.rst | 32 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++--
1 file changed, 30 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)
```

## Testing performed
- Docs-only change; no code touched. Root cause verified directly against `celery/backends/base.py`.
- **`make -C docs html` was not run locally** — sphinx/dev tooling isn't installed in this environment. The new RST reuses the same directives/roles already present in this file (`.. note::`, nested `.. code-block:: python`, `:meth:`~@send_task``), and indentation was verified by inspection; relying on the docs CI build for the final render check.

## Checklist
- [x] Change is focused and minimal
- [x] Follows the project's code style / conventions
- [ ] Tests added or updated where appropriate (n/a — documentation only)
- [x] Documentation updated where appropriate
- [ ] `lint` passes locally (`flake8`) — dev tooling not installed locally
- [x] `typecheck` passes locally (`mypy`)
- [ ] `test` passes locally (`tox`) — dev tooling not installed locally
- [ ] `docs` passes locally (`make -C docs html`) — sphinx not installed; deferred to CI

author: tokuhirom
body:
## Summary

Fixes Hash::Agnostic (dist ticket T-051) subtests 17-20 (`throws-like X::Hash::NoImplementation`), taking the dist from 12/22 to 16/22 passing subtests.

Two focused fixes:

1. **Tied `AT-KEY` throw was swallowed on read.** A `%h<key>` read on a tied Associative instance went through the `(Instance, Str)` index arm which used `.unwrap_or(Value::NIL)`, turning an exception raised by `AT-KEY` (e.g. Hash::Agnostic's NYI stub raising `X::Hash::NoImplementation`) into a silent `Nil`. Now the error propagates when the class actually has a user `AT-KEY` method; the `Nil` fallback is kept for a non-Associative instance with no `AT-KEY` (`$obj<foo>` stays `Nil`).

2. **`throws-like` `:message(/.../)` / `:gist(/.../)` ignored a user-defined `.message`.** The matcher compared against the raw error carrier string, which for a user-defined exception is the class gist (`X::Hash::NoImplementation()`) rather than its computed `.message` ("No implementation of AT-KEY method found for ..."). Now the exception's `message`/`gist` method is invoked when the class overrides it; built-in `X::` carriers keep using the carrier string so their native rendering (e.g. `X::Phaser::PrePost`) is unaffected.

## Testing

- Pin: `t/tied-hash-atkey-throw.t` (throw propagation, non-Associative Nil fallback, present/missing-key reads, user-exception message matcher).
- `make test` PASS (2218 files, 20851 tests).
- Verified no regression on `roast/S32-exceptions/misc.t`, `misc2.t`, `roast/S04-phasers/pre-post.t`, and the built-in `X::TypeCheck` / `X::Phaser::PrePost` message matchers.

author: abdulaziz-alfalahi
body:
Fixes #124.

**Root cause**: `EnhancedJobMatchingEngine.enhanced_single_match` makes one Qwen/DashScope LLM call per candidate. `match_candidates` fed it the entire passive pool (`LIMIT 1000`; ~4,000 active candidates on staging) synchronously — minutes per request, and since staging runs a single gunicorn worker for Socket.IO, one match call stalls the whole app.

**Fix**: two-stage scoring.
1. Rank the full filtered pool with the existing **cheap rules scorer** (no LLM).
2. AI-score only the top `AI_SHORTLIST_CAP` (default **40**, `MATCH_AI_SHORTLIST_CAP` env).

LLM calls per request drop from ~1000 to ~40. Below the cap the pre-filter is skipped entirely, so small pools behave exactly as before. Response now reports `ai_scored_candidates`.

Quality: the AI pass still selects the winners — just from the rule-shortlisted top rather than the whole pool. Geography remains unscored (#12).

**Tests** (4): AI scorer called ≤ cap on a 500-pool, all-scored below cap, and a genuinely-strong candidate survives the rule pre-filter into the AI pass.

**Follow-up left on #124's thread as viable next steps**: async/progress for the AI pass, or precomputed embeddings — the cap is the pragmatic fix that makes the feature usable now.

## Problem

The command registration in deploy-commands.js wrapped the Discord REST PUT call in an AbortController with a hard 30-second timeout. author: javo787
body:
## Причина "голос не отправляется"

Эффект AppState/unmount в VoiceCapsule.tsx и VoiceRecorder.tsx был завязан в зависимостях на stopRecordingInternal. Тот транзитивно зависит от transcribeAudio -> onResult (проп с экрана-родителя, напр. AddSaleScreen.handleVoiceResult), который передаётся без useCallback и пересоздаётся на каждом ре-рендере экрана.

Из-за этого эффект пересоздавался на каждый такой ре-рендер, и его cleanup безусловно вызывал safeStopRecorder(recorder) ПРЯМО ВО ВРЕМЯ активной записи (fire-and-forget, без .then()) — recorder реально останавливался, полученный uri терялся. К моменту, когда пользователь по-настоящему отпускал кнопку, recorder.isRecording уже было false, и итоговый stopRecordingInternal возвращал uri=null, ничего не отправляя.

Подтверждено логами: мгновенные тапы (durationMs < 20) -> uri=ok; записи дольше ~1с (durationMs 2343-8976) -> uri=null.

## Фикс

Подписка на AppState и unmount-cleanup теперь используют ref на последнюю версию stopRecordingInternal. Сам эффект зависит только от recorder/clearTimers (стабильны для жизни компонента) и больше не пересоздаётся на каждый ре-рендер родителя.

Проверено: npx tsc --noEmit чисто.

## Рекомендация на будущее (не входит в этот PR)

onResult (и onShowBatchReview) в экранах (AddSaleScreen, AddExpenseModal, StockOperationModal) стоит обернуть в useCallback — это уберёт саму нестабильность у истока, а не только её следствие.

author: yamz8
body:
## Problem

`charts/index.yaml` on `dl.forgente.com` is uploaded to S3 with **no `Cache-Control` header**, so CloudFront (distribution `EEPB3PCM02W1F`) falls back to its ~24h default TTL. After every release the S3 origin is fresh but the CDN edge keeps serving the **stale previous chart index**.

The publish-CI IAM user can `PutObject` but cannot create CloudFront invalidations, so today someone runs a manual, per-path `aws cloudfront create-invalidation --distribution-id EEPB3PCM02W1F --paths /charts/index.yaml` every release. This bit twice during the v2.0.1 release (2026-07-22).

## Fix

The upload was a single `aws s3 sync chart-repo/ …` that pushes **both** the mutable `index.yaml` **and** the immutable versioned `.tgz`/`.prov` artifacts. Applying a short TTL to the whole sync would wrongly shorten caching on the immutable artifacts, so this splits them:

- `aws s3 sync … --exclude "index.yaml"` — artifacts keep default/long caching.
- `aws s3 cp chart-repo/index.yaml … --cache-control max-age=300` — the mutable index gets a 5 min TTL so a new chart version goes live at the edge within minutes with no manual invalidation.

## Verify

After the next release:

```
curl -sI https://dl.forgente.com/charts/index.yaml | grep -i cache-control
# expect: cache-control: max-age=300

# artifacts must NOT have the short TTL (default/long caching)
curl -sI https://dl.forgente.com/charts/forgente-<version>.tgz | grep -i cache-control
```

author: rasaha
body:
New workstream: a read-only, observational pilot measuring whether frozen TAP-E7-BASE (Companion Package v1.2.0) provides useful assurance on realistic artifacts. It modifies nothing — the spec, profile, package v1.2.0, mandatory corpus, and both implementations are untouched. The pilot consumes Implementation B read-only as the reference engine and verifies the config fingerprint before evaluating. No production decision depends on TAP-E7; every result is observational.

Deliverables (design/): pilot design, evaluation methodology, metrics spec, failure taxonomy, governance plan, report templates, dashboard spec, execution checklist, risk register, and final readiness assessment.

Working demonstration (pilot/run_pilot.js): 162 synthetic cases across 9 domains (compliance, financial, insurance, healthcare, legal, governance, audit, policy, agent-summary) x 9 issue types, run through the frozen engine read-only.

Measured results (results/metrics.json, reports/):
- precision 1.00 (zero false positives — never flags a faithful artifact)
- recall 1.00 on BASE-detectable classes, 0.75 overall
- indeterminate rate 0.22 (correctly routes spoofed/ambiguous inputs to humans)
- 36 engine-gap misses (scope-expansion / omitted-qualifier ASSURED) — BASE cannot see semantic distortions that leave the content-token set unchanged; certainty-inflation was caught only incidentally (extra token), not by certainty analysis.

Honest interpretation: TAP-E7-BASE is a high-precision, bounded-recall STRUCTURAL assurance layer — a complement to, not a replacement for, human semantic review. Its INDETERMINATE verdict provides correct human escalation. reviewer-agreement and review-time are human-pilot metrics (N/A in the synthetic demonstration).

Verdict: the pilot design would generate credible, honest evidence of TAP-E7's practical value (and its limits) while preserving complete version stability. Findings route to disposition buckets (implementation / generator / documentation / future protocol / future optional profile / TAP-E8), never back into frozen TAP-E7. author: djlim00
body:
## 개요

Baton MVP의 **플랜 01~05 전체 구현**을 담습니다. 사내 슬랙·문서·엑셀을 흡수해 검증된 LLM 위키의 기반을 구축하는 파이프라인이 종단간 연결됩니다(위키 컴파일은 다음 PR).

- **누적 60 유닛 테스트 통과 · 실패 0**
- 6 커밋 각각이 플랜 하나에 대응 (WDO-01~06)
- 리팩터: 90+ Java 파일을 역할별 서브패키지(entity/repository/service/adapter/storage/event/worker/web/pipeline/llm/embedding)로 재배치. IntelliJ Package Explorer에서 도메인 내부 계층이 즉시 눈에 보입니다.

## 커밋 단위 = 실제 작업 단위

| 커밋 | 플랜 | 요약 |
|---|---|---|
| `[WDO-01]` | 01 세팅 | Gradle Kotlin DSL, Spring Boot 3.5.5, Spring AI 1.0 Bedrock, docker-compose(pgvector+redis), Flyway V1/V2, SecurityConfig 스켈레톤, HealthController |
| `[WDO-02]` | 02 스키마 | Flyway V1의 34개 테이블 각각에 @Entity 1개 + 6개 @IdClass record. SourceClaim·WikiRevision은 @Immutable로 INSERT/append-only 강제. 리플렉션 스모크 8케이스 |
| `[WDO-03]` | 03 인증·권한 | **단일 권한 필터** (WikiAccessGuard + VisibilityCalculator, 순수 자바) + OAuth2 세션 + 조직/프로젝트 CRUD + dev 프로파일 우회 |
| `[WDO-04]` | 04 인제스트 | SourceAdapter 4종(Slack/Docx/Xlsx/PlainText) + ObjectStorage + IngestJobWorker(SKIP LOCKED) + IngestPipeline + PromptGuard(인젝션 방어) |
| `[WDO-05]` | 05 클레임 | Flyway V3(claim_extraction_task), 문장 청킹·룰 필터·데이터셋 분기, Claude Converse 추출, 속성 사전 LLM 판정, Titan v2 임베딩(pgvector), 큐 브릿지 정착 |
| `[WDO-06]` | (문서) | Mermaid 6장 + SVG + 렌더 스크립트, 플랜 04 상세 설명서 |

## 최종 실행 가능한 흐름

```
POST /uploads (multipart)
  → ObjectStorage 저장 + uploaded_file·ingest_job INSERT (queued)   [즉시 응답]
  ↓ 5초 후
IngestJobWorker @Scheduled
  → SourceAdapter로 텍스트 추출
  → SHA-256 중복 스킵
  → raw_source INSERT
  → PreLintService 관찰 룰
  → IngestEventPublisher.rawSourceIngested
    → DbQueueIngestEventPublisher가 claim_extraction_task INSERT
  ↓ 5초 후
ClaimExtractionWorker @Scheduled
  → DatasetRouter (표 vs 텍스트)
    표: reference 클레임 1개
    텍스트: SentenceChunker → RuleFilter → ClaimExtractor(Claude) → JSON 파싱
             → AttributeDictionaryService (사전 미적중 시 Claude 판정)
             → ClaimPreLintService (dedupe)
             → source_claim INSERT + claim_source_link
             → EmbeddingService(Titan) → claim_embedding (pgvector 1024차원)
             → ClaimPreparedEventPublisher (다음 PR에서 위키 컴파일로 연결 예정)
```

## CLAUDE.md 불변 규칙 준수 상태

| # | 규칙 | 구현 지점 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 소스 클레임 INSERT 전용, 위키 클레임은 저장 안 함 | `SourceClaim @Immutable`, 리포지토리에 update/delete 메서드 없음 |
| 3 | 표·엑셀은 reference 클레임 1개 | `DatasetRouter.of("xlsx") → TABLE`, `ClaimPipeline.insertReference` |
| 5 | 린트를 인제스트 트랜잭션 안에 넣지 않음 | 사전 관찰 룰만 인라인, LLM 판정은 별도 워커에 위임 |
| 7 | 단일 권한 필터 | `WikiAccessGuard` 하나 — 열람·검색·챗봇·린트 조회 모두 여기 통과 |
| 8 | 실효 가시성 = min(설정, 소스 상한), 민감 카테고리 강제 제외 | `VisibilityCalculator` |
| 9 | 위키 리비전은 append-only | `WikiRevision @Immutable` (실 사용은 플랜 06) |
| 10 | LLM 프롬프트에서 외부 텍스트 격리 | `PromptGuard` — 모든 LLM 호출이 통과 |

## Kafka 대비 (00-overview 결정사항)

파이프라인 단계 경계는 이벤트 인터페이스만 남기고 DB 큐 구현체 하나로 시작.

- `IngestEventPublisher` → 현재 `DbQueueIngestEventPublisher` (claim_extraction_task 적재). 미래 Kafka 컨슈머로 갈아끼울 때 호출부 손대지 않음.
- `ClaimPreparedEventPublisher` → 현재 `LoggingClaimPreparedEventPublisher` (임시). 다음 PR(플랜 06)에서 DB 큐 구현체로 교체 예정.

## 테스트 60개 브레이크다운

- 스키마 매핑 스모크: 8
- 권한/가시성: 14 (VisibilityCalculator 5 + WikiAccessGuard 9)
- 인젝션 방어: 3
- 인제스트: 16 (어댑터·해시·백오프·워커·파서)
- 클레임: 19 (청킹·필터·라우팅·JSON 파싱·pgvector 코덱)

실제 DB·Bedrock 통합 스모크는 Testcontainers 도입 시점 & 실데이터 검증 시점으로 미룸 (플랜 05 §주의사항).

## 실행 방법

```bash
cp .env.example .env         # AWS 자격증명·모델 ID 채우기
docker compose up -d          # postgres:5432 + redis:6379
./gradlew bootRun             # localhost:8080
curl -s localhost:8080/health # {"status":"UP"}
```

Flyway 자동으로 V1(schema)+V2(demo seed)+V3(claim queue) 적용. AWS Bedrock 자격증명은 `~/.aws/credentials` 프로필 + `AWS_PROFILE` 환경변수 방식 권장.

## 아키텍처 문서

`docs/description/architecture/` — 6장 Mermaid + SVG. 브라우저에서 SVG 열면 무한 확대 가능. `README.md`에 뷰잉 방법 4종 안내.

## 다음 단계 (다음 PR 예정)

- **플랜 06 위키 컴파일**: 클레임 유사도(임계 0.7 top-k) → 위키 페이지 라우팅/머지, `wiki_revision` append-only 컴파일, `page_source_link` 매핑
- 플랜 07 린트 (야간 배치, 룰 순서 고정)
- 플랜 08~12 (역질문, 챗봇, 품질, 프론트, E2E)

body:
[JIRA - BRU-2508]

**Cause:** When a workspace was opened, any local collection that couldn't be loaded, its folder had been moved or deleted, or the path held no valid collection config was silently discarded during resolution. Because it was dropped entirely, Workspace Home showed nothing, no notification fired, and the user had no way to see why it failed or to remove the stale entry.

**Resolution:** Instead of discarding the broken entry, it's now kept and flagged with a failure reason (either "not found" or "invalid"). On switching workspaces the user gets an error notification, the collection stays visible with a red "Missing" / "Failed to open" badge, clicking it explains the reason, and it can be removed from the workspace via the row menu. The flags are transient in-memory state, so nothing changes on disk.

author: fushanbobfan
body:
## Summary
- Adds `dijkstra.js` and `astar.js`: both account for a cell's `weight` as the cost of entering it (BFS treats every step as equally costly, so it ignores weight entirely). A* adds a Manhattan-distance heuristic on top of Dijkstra, giving the same optimality guarantee (admissible as long as every weight is at least 1) while typically exploring far fewer cells.
- Adds `setNodeWeight` to the grid model, independent of `setNodeType` so clearing a wall doesn't erase whatever weight the ground underneath had.
- Adds a "Draw weighted terrain" tool alongside "Draw walls" in the UI, and wires both new algorithms into the algorithm selector.
- Documents all three algorithms' tradeoffs in the README, including why BFS ignores weighted terrain while Dijkstra/A* route around it.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm test` (26/26 passing, including new cases: Dijkstra/A* matching BFS on unweighted grids, routing around walls, reporting unreachable, and — the key new behavior — preferring a longer route over cheap terrain to a shorter one through expensive terrain)
- [x] Manually verified in a browser: drew a weighted cell directly on the straight-line path between start and end, then ran all three algorithms on the identical grid — BFS took the shorter 25-step route straight through it (ignoring cost), Dijkstra took a 27-step detour around it, and A* found the same 27-step detour while exploring only 78 cells vs Dijkstra's 384. No console errors.

author: felipesauer
body:
Read-side hardening of the proof engine found by an end-to-end audit of the core, before the surfaces. Four fixes, each with a regression test proven by neutralizing the guard (remove the check → the test fails; restore → it passes).

## Fixes
- **who != which compared in canonical form.** `verify` compared the two raw bytes, but the gate compares them trimmed + NFC-normalized. A forger with their own committed key could set `which = who + " "` — byte-distinct, but the same identity the gate refuses as self-authorization — and verify green. `verify` now compares in the same canonical form the gate uses.
- **an entry is bound to the tail directory it lives in.** The entry hash folds the stored `link.tail`, but nothing checked it equalled the directory the file was read from. Copying a *residual* tail's segments under a fabricated directory name read as a second, independent tail — verify green, every event counted twice by projections. `verify` now requires the stored tail to equal the directory (the checkpoint's own `tail` field only caught this once a checkpoint existed).
- **a torn last checkpoint line is tolerated** like a torn entry line. A crash mid-checkpoint-sign left a partial line that made `verify` throw a JSON error (a verifier crashing on a crash artifact) and locked a fresh writer out of its own tail on recovery. Both now drop the one torn trailing fragment.
- **recovery heals a torn last entry** by truncating the fragment before resuming. Without it, the next append landed after the fragment, turning a once-benign torn line into permanent mid-file corruption that every later read threw on. The prior recovery test never re-verified after the resume, so it missed this.

## Validation
- `pnpm build` clean; `pnpm lint` clean; **374 tests** (was 368; +6).
- Each guard proven: neutralized → its regression test fails; restored → passes.
- Validated on the committed state (clean tree).

Part of the core audit (chain+core) before building the MCP/CLI surfaces. First of a stack.

author: zasper32171
body:
## Summary

SDK **4.0.1**: the Pyth Pro migration hardened end to end — one `pythGeneration` knob, base-path-safe URLs, self-healing missing-feed discovery, and a resilient shared fetch policy.

## The one-knob contract (4.x)

- **`pythGeneration: 'core' | 'pro'`** is the ONLY oracle option. `'core'` = `pyth_rule` (Hermes VAA, keyless Core endpoints); `'pro'` = `pyth_lazer_rule` (ONE Lazer leEcdsa verify per PTB, no per-feed update fees) + auth-first Pro Hermes for reads. `oracleSource` is **derived**, no longer a create option; `assertOracleSourceConfigured` fails fast at client creation when the config lacks the required rule package.
- `pyth_rule::feed` always pins the **Core** PythState (`PYTH_DEFAULTS[network].state_id`) — the deployed rule package is compiled against Core pyth; passing the generation-selected state caused `CommandArgumentError { TypeMismatch }` on every order build under pro.
- Ghost config fields purged (`hourly_mint/burn_limit`, `trusted_emitters`).

## URL + fetch correctness

- **`joinEndpointPath`**: preserves the endpoint's own base path — `new URL(path, endpoint)` silently dropped the Pro compat endpoint's `/hermes` prefix and 404'd every feed. One canonical trailing-slash trim shared with the memo key.
- **`fetchWithPolicy`** (the ONE retry/timeout/Bearer policy for every oracle fetch): per-attempt timeout, bounded retry + backoff, Bearer attach-iff-non-empty, intermediate `body.cancel()` — and now honors a numeric **`Retry-After`** on 429 within the backoff cap.

## Missing-feed self-heal

- Pyth 404s an entire batch when ANY id is unknown (and the body naming them is unreadable under undici). Discovery is now **catalog-first** — one `GET /v2/price_feeds` names every id the endpoint serves for this credential (verified live: WTI absent+404, BTC present+200) — with the batch-**bisection** retained as fallback when the catalog is unavailable. Survivors re-fetch as one clean batch; results are memoized.
- The memo is **credential-scoped** (`endpoint + apiKey`): Pro entitlements are per-key, so two clients in one process can no longer cross-poison each other's view (`endpointSupportedFeedIds` gains an optional `apiKey` — backward-compatible).
- Lazer: `fixed_rate@200ms` channel (the only channel all our feeds publish).

## Verification

1009 unit tests (incl. engine-shape coverage of the discovery paths), tsc + lint clean. Order builds verified on mainnet via devInspect under `pro`: oracle leg passes with no per-feed update fees.

author: dustinjuliano
body:
Introduce origin-agnostic service import resolution, a startup network event loop, and end-to-end static analysis across local file and P2P network boundaries.

Previously, static checks skipped member resolution and type checking for imported services via defensive early returns and warning flags, leaving cross-service member accesses unvalidated at compile time. Furthermore, nodes lacked a unified startup event loop to dynamically fetch remote code prior to running static semantics checks.

Startup Network Event Loop:

The `on_node_startup` boot sequence in `node.rs` introduces a dedicated event loop that drives the `Imports` state machine. It dispatches `ServiceCodeRequest` messages to remote network peers, polls incoming `ServiceCodeResponse` messages over libp2p, parses remote source code using the process `Interner`, and recursively resolves transitive dependencies before finalizing the `unified_ast`.

Import Topology and Mutual Import Exploration:

To guarantee static safety while maintaining simple runtime invariants, import dependencies are strictly restricted to a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG). Mutual/cyclic service imports (e.g., Service A importing Service B while Service B imports Service A) were explored during design. Supporting mutual imports across the network creates a circular dependency chicken-and-egg problem: neither node can complete static type checking without the other's source code, requiring nodes to instantly serve unverified local files over P2P before running their own static checks.

While the `Imports` state machine and runtime thunk system in `nameres.rs` detect evaluation cycles during static resolution, enforcing a strict DAG topology for network imports eliminates inter-node deadlocks and ensures all remote source is fully verified by the sender before being served.

Static Cross-Service Dependency Cycle Rejection:

To guarantee that cross-service member definition cycles across service boundaries are caught prior to execution, `tt/check.rs` introduces a structured `Error::DependencyCycle { service: Symbol, member: Symbol }` error variant. During static type synthesis, `Context::type_of_member` maintains an active `checking_stack` scratchpad of `(service, member)` tuples. If a member reference recurses into a tuple already present on the stack, type checking halts immediately and returns a `DependencyCycle` error.

To ensure user-facing error messages are clear and actionable, `format_tt_error` in `node.rs` matches on type check errors and resolves interned `Symbol` identifiers to human-readable string names using `self.interner`. Error messages follow standard lowercased formatting with trailing periods (e.g., `type check error: dependency cycle detected at service 'server_b', member 'val_b'.`).

In-Memory Integration Test Suite & MKN Test Harness:

The test suite in `imports_test.rs` has been refactored to execute entirely in memory using `parser::parse_string`, eliminating disk file I/O and temporary directory thrashing while verifying transitive import resolution and network cycle rejection (`test_imports_network_cycle_static_check_rejection`).

In addition, negative integration test manifests (`circular_imports` and `cyclic_member_imports`) have been added to `scripts/tests/integration/imports/` and registered in `test_imports.py`. These verify that `mkn.py` and peer node runtimes detect and reject circular manifest dependencies and cross-service member cycles cleanly during node boot without process deadlocks.

* **New Features**

  * Updated the CLI/server flow to resolve imports over the network before running static checks.
* **Bug Fixes**
  * Missing imported services now fail with clear name-resolution errors (instead of warnings).
  * Cross-service cyclic member references now report explicit “dependency cycle” failures.
  * Improved network dispatch/re-send behavior, with better failure handling and logging.
* **Tests**

author: craus81
body:
## Root cause, finally

The read-back probe shipped in #353 caught it live: the System Health banner reported *"upsert reported success but read-back shows 2026-07-22T03:28:39"* — a timestamp from **after** #353 deployed. The `health_probe` row was created successfully and every write since has landed too; it's the **read** that keeps returning the same first-ever value.

`sync_state` **writes were landing the whole time. The reads were frozen.** Next 14 patches global fetch, and its Data Cache serves cached PostgREST GETs across requests — and, on Vercel, across deployments. So:

- System Health and the health watcher read a days-old snapshot → the whole board showed "Stale, 38–39h" while jobs ran fine (confirmed in the cron-fallback Actions logs: parts-email-scan processing mailboxes minutes before a health check that swore it hadn't run in hours).
- The watcher's alert-dedupe state lives in `sync_state` too, and its reads were cached → admins re-alerted every 30 minutes instead of every 6 hours (the 48-alert badge).
- The gmail auto-import always read fresh because `auto-import-status` hit this **exact** failure once before and got a per-route `cache: 'no-store'` fetch wrapper — its route comment documents the earlier field evidence.

## Change

That proven wrapper becomes a shared `createServiceClient()` in `src/lib/supabase-service.ts`, now used by every cron route, `/api/system-health`, and both gmail auto-import routes (12 routes total). Route-level `dynamic = 'force-dynamic'` is not sufficient — the Data Cache is keyed per fetch URL and survives it.

With this deployed, the #353 read-back verification reads live data, so the "heartbeat writes failing" banner clears and the dashboard shows true ages. (Some jobs will legitimately read stale until the scheduler question is sorted — the GH Actions cron-fallback hasn't been scheduled since Jul 22 01:10 UTC, which is a separate infra item.)

## Tests

Full suite: 228 passing, `tsc --noEmit` clean. No behavior change beyond cache bypass — client construction is otherwise identical.

## Summary

Effective-Python audit (Mode 2) over all production/script files changed since the last audit baseline (`e2c99ca`, 2026-07-04) — v0.14–v0.15 resolver-pipeline, LSP, and MCP-handler work. 8 confirmed findings fixed; 1 reviewer finding refuted during verification (write-lock `__aexit__` never suspends, so no stale-searcher race — hardened structurally anyway).

## Changes

**HIGH — concurrency safety (mcp_server)**
- `handle_clear_index` / `handle_delete_project` now take the per-project `get_reindex_rwlock(project).write()` before tearing down search resources and deleting index files, draining in-flight searches first (mirrors `handle_index_directory`). Previously guarded only by the mutation lock, which searches never acquire — a concurrent search could hold open files mid-deletion (PermissionError on Windows → partially-deleted index). `delete_project` keys the lock by the project being deleted, which may differ from the active one.
- `with_mutation_lock` docstring corrected: it serializes mutations against each other ONLY; mutation-vs-search protection comes from the reindex rwlock (this overclaim is what masked the gap).

**MEDIUM — observability (LSP client)**
- `_kill_process_tree`: psutil-path failure now logged at debug before the `proc.kill()` fallback.
- `_LspClient._reader_loop`: terminating exception logged at debug instead of a silent `break`.

**LOW**
- Remaining sync `open()` JSON reads in async handlers offloaded via `asyncio.to_thread` (project-info read in `_run_index_directory`; whole `handle_list_projects` sweep as one closure) — ruff ASYNC230 now clean.
- `search_orchestrator`: `reset_searcher()` moved inside the write-lock block so the fresh-searcher invariant is structural.
- `measure_parse_once.py`: unparseable-file skip count reported after the timed loop; `main()` docstring.

## Tests

- Prevents malformed truncated Markdown syntax from confusing the agent

## Problem

When a user replies to a long assistant message (especially one containing tables, code blocks, or other formatting), the raw Markdown was injected verbatim into the agent prompt. For long messages, this was truncated mid-structure, leaving partial table pipes, unmatched emphasis markers, or broken code fences in the prompt. The agent would then treat the malformed syntax as a new instruction, sometimes abandoning the active task.

## Changes

- **`gateway/run.py`**: Added `_sanitize_reply_snippet()` helper that:
  - Strips Markdown table separator rows (`|---|---|`)
  - Cleans table cell pipes into plain text
  - Applies `strip_markdown()` from `gateway.platforms.helpers` for bold, italic, code blocks, headings, and links
  - Collapses whitespace into single spaces
  - Truncates at word boundary with `…` when exceeding 500 chars
- **`tests/gateway/test_reply_to_injection.py`**: Added tests for Markdown stripping and word-boundary truncation

## Test plan

- [x] All 8 existing + new tests pass
- [ ] Manual test: reply to a long Markdown message in Telegram and verify the agent receives clean plaintext context

Fixes #69060

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>simplecov-ruby/simplecov (simplecov)</summary>

### [`v1.0.1`](https://redirect.github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#101-2026-07-14)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/compare/v1.0.0...v1.0.1)

\==================

#### Enhancements

- The gem now ships type signatures under `sig/`, covering the public API: the configuration DSL (including the criterion-scoped `coverage` block and the legacy deprecated verbs), the `Result` / `FileList` / `SourceFile` / `CoverageStatistics` read API that formatter authors consume, the formatter and filter class hierarchies, exit codes, and the `ParallelAdapters::Base` contract. Internal classes carry repository-only skeleton signatures (`sig/internal/`, excluded from the gem package) so the entire codebase type-checks under Steep in strict mode, while the shipped signature payload stays small. Signatures are checked with `rbs validate` and `steep check` as part of the default rake task. RBS and Steep users no longer need the third-party signatures from `ruby/gem_rbs_collection`, which cover the 0.22 API and predate 1.0's configuration redesign.

#### Bugfixes

- Branch tuples synthesized for tracked-but-unloaded files now match Ruby's `Coverage` exactly for `elsif` and for `if` arms with empty bodies. `StaticCoverageExtractor` attributed the outer else arm of an `elsif` to the clause's body rather than the whole clause, and an empty `if` then-body to the whole node rather than Coverage's zero-width point at the predicate's end. Since resultset merges combine branch arms by their exact location, a simulated entry merging with a real one for the same file (parent and worker under Minitest's `parallelize`, or RSpec and Minitest suites collated together) produced phantom, permanently-missed branch arms. A new differential spec now pins every branch construct tuple-for-tuple against Ruby's `Coverage` — which promptly caught that CRuby 3.4 changed several of these conventions, so the extractor now emits whichever shape the running Ruby's `Coverage` uses (on 3.2/3.3: elsif clause ranges end at the chain's last content rather than the shared `end`, empty `if`/`else`/`when` bodies fall back to enclosing ranges, and empty `while`/`in` bodies collapse to points). Reported with an exemplary diagnosis by [@​hasghari](https://redirect.github.com/hasghari). See [#​1226](https://redirect.github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/issues/1226).
- `merge_subprocesses` no longer silently drops all worker coverage under Minitest's fork-based `parallelize(workers: N)` (the setup the `rails` profile exists for). When Minitest's autorun was armed before `SimpleCov.start` — which is how `rails test` loads — SimpleCov deferred its report to `Minitest.after_run`, and forked workers inherited that deferral even though Minitest pins its `after_run` hook to the parent's pid, so no exit path in the worker ever stored its resultset. Workers now reset the inherited at\_exit state on fork and re-arm their own hook, so their resultsets are stored and merged as documented. Reported with an exemplary diagnosis by [@​hasghari](https://redirect.github.com/hasghari). See [#​1227](https://redirect.github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/issues/1227).
- Fixed `SimpleCov.formatters=` raising `NoMethodError` when given a single formatter instead of an Array — a regression from 0.22.x, where `MultiFormatter.new` normalized the value internally. This restores the long-documented `SimpleCov.formatters = SimpleCov::Formatter::MultiFormatter.new([...])` pattern, in which `MultiFormatter.new` returns a Class rather than an Array. The regression surfaced in ruby/ruby's CI through net-imap's test helper. Thanks [@​koic](https://redirect.github.com/koic). See [#​1224](https://redirect.github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/issues/1224).
- Formatter status lines ("Coverage report generated for X") and threshold-enforcement output (violation reports, "SimpleCov failed with exit N") no longer route through `Kernel#warn`. They still print to stderr, but they are program output rather than Ruby warnings, so `Warning.warn` hooks — warning trackers and raise-on-warning test setups — no longer intercept them as unaddressable noise, and threshold failure explanations now survive `ruby -W0`, which previously reduced a failing check to a bare exit code with no explanation. Genuine warnings (deprecations, dropped-file notices, parse failures) still use `warn`. Suppression remains explicit: `silent: true` for formatter status lines, `print_errors false` for enforcement output. Thanks [@​viralpraxis](https://redirect.github.com/viralpraxis). See [#​1225](https://redirect.github.com/simplecov-ruby/simplecov/issues/1225).

</details>

author: rswerve
body:
## Silent data loss: relative Markdown links were being deleted on save

Opening a document in Quill and letting autosave run **deleted relative link targets from the user's file**. Found by accident: firing a `quill://open?file=…README.md` deep link at the shipped app destroyed three links in this repo's own README — `[User Guide](docs/USER_GUIDE.md)` ×2 and `[v1.1.7 release note](docs/release-notes/v1.1.7.md)` — while the 24 absolute `https://` links survived.

### Root cause

`@tiptap/extension-link` 3.26.1's default URI validator uses:

```
^(?:(?:http|https|ftp|…):|[^a-z]|[a-z0-9+.-]+(?:[^a-z+.-:]|$))
```

The class `[^a-z+.-:]` contains `.-:`, which JS parses as a **character range** (U+002E–U+003A) silently covering `/`. So a scheme-less path *with* a slash fails validation while one without passes:

| href | stock validator |
| --- | --- |
| `GUIDE.md` | allowed |
| `docs/GUIDE.md` | **rejected** |

A rejected href makes `parseHTML` return `false`, dropping the link mark at load. The next Markdown write then emits bare text — the destination is gone from disk. Confirmed independently against the installed 3.26.1 source.

### The fix

Two halves, because fixing only the first would have been useless:

1. **Load/save** — `isAllowedLinkUri` accepts any scheme-less reference and defers anything with an explicit scheme to the stock allowlist (still blocking `javascript:`/`data:`/`vbscript:`). The scheme test first strips the same whitespace class Tiptap strips, so ` javascript:…` and `java\nscript:…` can't pose as relative paths and skip the allowlist.
2. **Edit** — `normalizeHref` was sending every scheme-less string to `https://`, so Link-editor Apply, a label-only change, typed/pasted Markdown links, and AI link edits re-corrupted the targets half 1 preserves. It now distinguishes a relative path from a bare domain by the first segment (`docs` is not a hostname, `example.com` is). Bare-domain convenience is unchanged.

Link policy is now exported as `LINK_OPTIONS` from `utils/linkEditing.ts` and consumed by the editor **and every test harness** — seven harnesses still configured the old validator while claiming to mirror production.

### Also included

`scripts/open-in-quill.mjs` + `.claude/commands/open-in-quill.md` restore the "open this in Quill from Claude Code" path dropped with the plugin in #14, and pre-link the document to the calling session by writing the sidecar binding before firing the deep link. It deliberately does **not** claim `createdByQuill` to dodge `authorizeSidecarAccess`, so the first open of a document still asks for a grant once, as designed.

### Verification

- The real README round-trips with all 27 links intact (was 24).
- Full gate green: typecheck, eslint, prettier, **143 files / 1817 tests**.
- Reviewed independently by Codex, which confirmed the root cause against the installed source and ran a BMP-wide differential probe against the WHATWG URL parser, finding **no** string the widened validator admits that resolves to an executable scheme. Its HIGH finding (the `normalizeHref` mutation path) and its test-drift finding are both fixed here.

### Known, not fixed here

Pre-existing and out of scope, reported by Codex: empty `[x]()`, Windows drive paths, and custom schemes (`obsidian://`, `ipfs://`) are still dropped silently; a crafted workspace `docJSON` can inject a link mark that bypasses validation (requires local app-data manipulation). Worth their own issue.

author: oorabona
body:
## Summary

`any(col, array)` chose the SQL array element type from the **JavaScript runtime types** of the values, not from the target column. Ids read back from PostgreSQL arrive as JS strings, so `any('id', ancestorIds)` on an `integer` column emitted `symbols.id = ANY (CAST($1 AS text[]))`, and PostgreSQL rejected `integer = ANY(text[])` with `operator does not exist: integer = text`.

## Fix

The `any` handler now resolves the target column's DB type with the same `resolveColumnPgType` the scalar comparison handlers use, and casts the array param with the same `createTypeCastParamRef` that `IN` / `inArray` already use, so it emits `CAST($1 AS integer[])` regardless of the JS value types. The previous `decision.dataType` / runtime value-sniffing path is preserved as a fallback for the cases where no column DB type can be resolved (an expression left-hand side, or a column without an `originalDbType`). The shared batch/UNNEST array-type helper and the `IN` path are untouched.

## Verification

- `pnpm -r typecheck` clean; `pnpm biome check .` clean.
- Unit: `@dbsp/adapter-pgsql` 11269 (+2 todo) · `@dbsp/core` 3483 · `@dbsp/types` 213 — all green, including new coverage for integer columns with string arrays, empty arrays, mixed-null arrays, text columns, and a dotted relation `any('file.project_id', ['1'])`.
- Compile-only doc examples (`pnpm test:docs`) green.
- e2e (testcontainers): 651 passing, including `from(posts).where(any('id', ['1','2']))` on an integer `id` column — the compiled SQL is `CAST($1 AS integer[])` (not `text[]`) and the query returns the rows with no `operator does not exist` error.

Closes #347

## What & why

A panel review (Engineering Manager / OSS / Developer-Experience lenses) of the unreleased wave (`v0.5.0..HEAD`, 9 PRs) found the wave release-ready with **no blockers and no high-severity issues**. This PR applies only the confirmed, in-scope doc/polish fixes so the wave is clean before the next release. **No intended-behavior changes.**

## Changes

- **CHANGELOG** — Add the genblaze-core `[Unreleased]` entry for the sink #162 fix that was missing, including the tradeoff: object existence is no longer independently probed for backend-owned asset URLs (a byte-level `genblaze verify --fetch` remains available for post-hoc confirmation).
- **`tools/batch_plandoc.py`** — Correct the validator docstring/comment to match what `validate()` actually does: planned-but-closed issues abort the run; issues opened *after* planning are intentionally deferred to the next `batch-plan`, not a drift trigger. Soften "tamper-evident / enforcement" language since the content token is an unkeyed `sha256` digest that catches accidental edits, not a motivated editor — the human approval gate is the trust boundary.
- **`genblaze-lmnt`** — Emit the dropped-`speed` warning **once per provider** instead of once per clip (mirrors `model_registry`'s `_warned_deprecated` dedup), avoiding log spam in batch pipelines. Adds regression test `test_speed_warning_emitted_once_per_provider`. The `speed` param is still dropped on every call; only the warning is deduped.

- **elevenlabs `>=2.0` floor is correct** — inspected the 2.0.0 wheel; `AudioWithTimestampsResponse.audio_base_64` and `convert_with_timestamps` both exist at exactly that floor, so the hard attribute use is safe. No bump needed.
- lmnt keeps its `logger.warning` channel (a tested design choice in `test_speed_param_dropped_with_warning`); only the per-call repetition was addressed.

## Deferred (follow-ups, not this PR)

- CLI `verify` imports private core internals (`_http_get_stream`, `ALLOWED_FILE_ROOTS`, `_DEFAULT_*`). Reusing the SSRF-pinned path is correct, but the cross-package coupling to core's private surface should be replaced with a thin public core accessor. All three reviewers flagged it as a follow-up, not urgent; deferred to avoid growing this PR's scope.

author: jcarney2024
body:
## What

Rebuilds the onboarding contract at `/onboard/[token]` so it mirrors HAVEN's legacy Airtable form, and gives directors a builder to maintain it. Closes the gaps flagged in the request: the "Epic access is required for my role" checkbox and the "I can speak Spanish with patients" checkbox are gone, agreement bodies now carry real prose (they rendered empty before, which is why signatures showed no terms), Epic access type only appears once you declare an existing Epic ID, the HIPAA section has its full instructions back, and the whole form reads in sections like the old one.

## How it works

The contract is an ordered list of typed blocks (`system_field`, `agreement`, `custom_question`, `section`), each able to carry a `visibleWhen` condition. Prose renders through a small markdown subset (bold, bullets, links). The applicant-facing form filters blocks by `visibleWhen` on the client, and the server validates the **frozen snapshot** through the *same* filter, so what is shown and what is required can never diverge.

**Epic provisioning** is now derived, not self-reported. Each department carries `requiresEpicDirector` / `requiresEpicVolunteer` (`ALL` / `NONE` / `SOME`). At submit, `epicNeeded` resolves from the acceptance's department and track; only `SOME` departments (LCC patient-navigator/TOC roles, QA/QI) ask the applicant. This fixes a latent bug where the old `epicNeeded` form field was never rendered, so it was always false in production and nobody was auto-provisioned.

## Key pieces

- `src/modules/recruitment/contract/` — block model, markdown renderer, visibility resolver, Epic-requirement resolver, and the volunteer/director default layouts (including 21 department-specific responsibility blocks, one shown per director).
- `src/app/onboard/[token]/` — the reworked applicant form and submit path.
- `src/app/(app)/recruitment/cycles/[id]/builder/contract/` — section/condition/confirm-kind editing.
- New columns on `Person`, `OnboardingContract`, `Department`, `RecruitmentCycle` + the `EpicRequirement` enum; a data migration and catalog update seed each department's Epic requirement.

## New fields

Pronouns and staff title are captured and carried onto the Person at promotion. Yale affiliation and graduation year now use the app's canonical option lists (so prefilled values render correctly) instead of free text.

## Testing

TDD throughout; ~250 new tests. The full suite passes except two pre-existing `createdAt`-tie ordering flakes (`review.test.ts`, `inbox.test.ts`) in files this branch does not touch — both pass in isolation. `npm run lint` and `tsc --noEmit` are clean.

**Not done:** a manual browser walkthrough of the two rendered contracts. Render and submit are covered by unit (`renderToStaticMarkup`) and DB-backed integration tests, but a live end-to-end click-through against a seeded onboarding token is worth doing before this reaches applicants.

## Notes for review

- The build went through a per-task review gate; the design/spec and per-task notes are in `docs/superpowers/`.
- A final whole-branch review caught and fixed a submission-blocker (the director "second department" dropdown rendered with zero options); that fix is the last commit.
- Cross-term departments not in the legacy Epic lists (senior/junior clinical team members, patient navigation, etc.) were seeded as Epic-requiring by decision, since they chart in Epic. All values are editable in the admin departments screen.

author: tomoakinishimura
body:
## 概要
`#pj_fun-base` のバグ報告・機能改善要望を **毎時自動でトリアージ → ゴール達成まで修正 → PR＋レビュー依頼＋Slack返信** するプロアクティブループの土台を追加します。[Loop Engineering](https://note.com/inady/n/n1b3df42b4ba2) の「ゴールベースループ＋完了条件のスキル化」を fun-base に実装したものです。

## 追加内容
- **skills**
  - `goal` — 達成条件だけ渡す汎用ゴールループ（達成判定は別コンテキストでバイアス回避）
  - `triage-from-slack` — Slack 分類（bug/feature）・重複除外
  - `fix-and-ship` — worktree 隔離 → `/goal` → `/code-review` → 出荷
  - `funbase-triage-cycle` — 1 サイクル統括（`/loop`・`/schedule` の呼び先）
- **agent** `bug-fixer` — TDD 修正ワーカー
- **AGENTS.md** — 完了条件（typecheck/lint/test/build）・PR 規約・escalation 対象
- **docs/superpowers/** — 設計書 + 運用 runbook

## 起動構成
`/loop`（試用）or `/schedule`（本番） → `funbase-triage-cycle` →（各投稿で）`/goal`
外側タイマーは一つだけ。`/goal` は 1 実行の中で回る内側ループ。

## 安全設計
- 既定 **shadow モード**（PR/Slack 返信を出さず方針提示のみ）
- **worktree 隔離**（作業ツリー非干渉）・main 保護
- **escalation**（migration / 認証 / crypto / 削除 / 依存）は自動化しない
- 重複除外・thrash 防止・1 実行 3 件まで・全ゲート green のときのみ push

## 状態
⚠️ **未検証**（まだ 1 サイクルも実行していない）。すぐマージする前提ではなく、まず shadow dry-run で検証するための土台 PR です。設定は `~/.claude/funbase-triage/config.json`（リポジトリ外）。

author: schienstockd
body:
## Why
A project's uid was baked into project-internal files as *data*, so importing under a new uid (and a
future rename) left stale references — the reason import-as-**copy** was hidden. This makes project
identity come from **location** (the directory name), not an embedded value, and re-enables copy.

Invariant (now in `docs/OBJECTMODEL.md`): **a project-internal file must not bake in its own uid.**

## Changes
- **Analysis boards → uid-relative.** `frontend/src/utils/boardKeys.ts` (new, unit-tested): on-disk
  layout keys are `tab:<id>` (no uid); `analysisLayout.serialize` strips the `analysis:<uid>:` prefix,
  `load(groupKey, …)` re-applies the *current* uid and tolerates a legacy baked-in old-uid key. So a
  project's boards survive a uid change instead of orphaning. Existing projects migrate transparently
  on the next autosave.
- **Chain runs → location-derived.** `load_chain_run` uses `proj.uid` (the project it's loaded from),
  not the persisted `project_uid` (now advisory) — runs resume correctly after import/copy.
- **`reidentify_project!(proj_uid, new_uid; new_name)`** — the canonical identity change (rename dir +
  `project.json` + best-effort notebook `load_project("…")` rewrite via `_reidentify_files!`). Unblocks
  a future in-place rename; the import-copy path re-identifies inline.
- **Copy import re-enabled** — the collision prompt is back to Replace / Copy / Cancel.
- Docs: `docs/OBJECTMODEL.md` (invariant), `ANALYSIS.md`, `INVENTORY.md`, `PROJECT_IO_PLAN.md`.

## Tests
`boardKeys` unit tests (3/3); package suite **1558 pass, 0 fail** (adds `reidentify_project!`, copy
notebook-rewrite, and the replace/copy round-trip). Frontend `vue-tsc` + `vite build` green.

## Caveats
- **Live GUI unverified** (no frontend/WS integration test) — the board re-key on load and the
  re-enabled copy dialog aren't clicked through; the `boardKeys` *logic* is unit-tested.
- Opening an existing project **rewrites `analysisBoards.json`** to the relative format on the next
  autosave (transparent; the loader reads both).
- Copy's notebook rewrite is **best-effort** (literal `load_project("<old>")` only).
- The chain 1-liner has **no dedicated resume test** (heavy template-cache setup); relied on obvious correctness.
- `reidentify_project!` isn't wired to any UI yet (no rename button) — canonical helper + used by copy.

- Add `payroll.controller.js`: aggregates a target month's attendance (regular/overtime hours, days present) and approved leave (leave days taken, excluded from absence) per employee, computes working days in the month (excluding Saturdays, Nepal's standard weekly off), feeds the results into the existing `payroll.service.calculatePayslip`, and persists the result

- Regenerating a payslip for the same employee/month upserts (overwrites) the existing record; response message says so when it happens
- `generate-all` runs across all active employees and reports how many were newly generated vs. regenerated

Closes #12

- Booted the backend against local MongoDB, seeded an employee with hand-crafted attendance (regular + overtime days) and an approved leave block for June 2026, called `POST /generate/:employeeId` and confirmed every persisted field (`earnedBasic`, `overtimePay`, `grossMonthlyPay`, SSF contributions, `annualTaxableIncome`, `monthlyTax`, `unpaidLeaveDeduction`, `netPay`) matched hand-calculated values from the PRD §3.6 formula

- Verified role guards: employee gets 403 on admin-only routes, `GET /me` returns only the caller's own payslips
- Verified validation: invalid `employeeId` → 404, out-of-range `month` → 400
- Confirmed all four endpoints render correctly in the generated Swagger spec (`/payroll/generate/{employeeId}`, `/payroll/generate-all`, `/payroll/me`, `/payroll/{employeeId}`)

author: timothyb89
body:
This fixes an issue in tbot's Envoy SDS API where, if the user also configured their cluster to use Workload Identity issuer overrides to provide their own CA chain, the Envoy SDS handler would attempt to pass through the entire DER-formatted chain inside a single PEM block instead of splitting it into multiple PEM blocks as it should.

The root cause was mostly a historical artifact: there was no need to support CA chains when the SDS API was first implemented because there was no way it would ever try to serve an SVID with a custom CA chain. When issuer overrides were later added, the file output was updated to support chains properly, but the Envoy SDS path was missed.

This fixes the issue by re-parsing the DER chain and reformatting it into separate PEM blocks properly.

No server-side changes were needed; the most complex part of the change is the tests, which needed to be updated to handle actual certs since `newTLSV3Certificate` now actually parses the cert bytes and failed on the test fixture data. That was complicated by the use of `golden` so we need golden-stored certs.

Fixes #68853

Changelog: Fixed an issue where use of Workload Identity X.509 issuer overrides could result in `tbot` serving invalid certificate bundles via its Envoy SDS-compatible API


## Manual Test Plan
### Test Environment

I had Claude replicate the customer issue in my [`teleport-harness` test environment](https://github.com/timothyb89/teleport-harness/commit/7d7371a8a9240300f599db52e5959b433c78d160) with some test cases. It builds a Teleport cluster, connects a `tbot` with the `workload-identity-api` service enabled, configures a Workload Identity Issuer Override resource, and then attempts to serve those SVIDs to Envoy.

The full report can be found here: https://gist.github.com/timothyb89/1f038f673e71f14b403b98dc8ee2939a along with config and log files.

### Test Cases
- [x] Envoy no longer rejects certs served via `tbot`'s SDS API with intermediates

author: laurigates
body:
## What

Add root-anchored `.chezmoiignore` entries for `docs/`, `tests/`, `LICENSE`, `DOCKER.md`, and `tmp/`.

## Why

These live at the source root for working *in this repo*, but with no `dot_` prefix chezmoi was applying them to `~/docs`, `~/tests`, `~/LICENSE`, `~/DOCKER.md`, and `~/tmp` — the footgun documented in `.claude/rules/chezmoi-conventions.md` ("A Non-`dot_` File at the Source Root Silently Applies to `$HOME`"). Same category as the `README.md` / `Dockerfile` / `plugins/` entries already ignored here.

Surfaced during a `$HOME` cleanup audit: `~/docs`, `~/tests`, `~/LICENSE`, `~/DOCKER.md` were sitting in the home directory as chezmoi-managed copies.

## How

- Root-anchor each pattern (leading `/`) so only the source-root copy is ignored, never a managed nested target of the same basename.
- `tmp/` is gitignored scratch (one-off notes previously dropped there, not in the public repo); chezmoi should not manage it.

## Safety

- Home targets are byte-identical to source (`chezmoi diff` empty for each), so removing the leaked `~/` copies loses nothing — their source of truth is this repo.
- Verified the ignore delta is exactly `docs`/`tests`/`LICENSE`/`DOCKER.md` (+ children); no nested over-match.

## Post-merge follow-up

After merge + `chezmoi apply`, the already-deployed `~/docs`, `~/tests`, `~/LICENSE`, `~/DOCKER.md` and the managed `~/tmp` scratch files can be removed from `$HOME` (they will no longer be redeployed).

author: barenatico
body:
## O problema
Ao criar anúncio com vídeo, a tela mostrava a página de erro crua do nginx:
`413 Request Entity Too Large`.

Não era a Meta: nenhum dos dois nginx (`deploy/nginx.allinone.conf` e
`packages/web/nginx.conf`) definia `client_max_body_size`, então valia o
**default de 1 MB** — qualquer vídeo estourava antes de chegar na API, que
aceita 500 MB (`limits.fileSize` do `@fastify/multipart`, `index.js:59`).

## O que mudou
- **nginx (os dois)**: `client_max_body_size 512m` + `client_body_timeout 600s`
  e `proxy_send/read_timeout 600s` no `/api/`. Vale pra todos os uploads
  (criativo, anúncio clonado, áudio do WhatsApp, mídia social).
- **web**: helper `upload()` único no client, com mensagem legível quando quem
  responde é o proxy (413 → "arquivo grande demais... comprima o vídeo") em vez
  de despejar o HTML do nginx na tela.
- **web**: os dois formulários barram arquivo > 500 MB antes de subir.

## Deploy
Precisa de redeploy (muda a imagem do nginx e o bundle do front).

author: bojanrajkovic
body:
Boots a linux guest end to end on a windows host via bare Hyper-V compute systems (HCS) — no vmms `Get-VM` visibility, no tart binary at runtime — mirroring `vz_darwin.go`'s `Manager`/`Machine` shape on `internal/vm`'s existing interfaces.

- `HCSManager`/`hcsMachine` (`internal/vm/hcs_windows.go`): Boot creates an HNS endpoint on the Default Switch, attaches the slot's differencing VHDX, and starts a schema-2.1 compute system (`HvSocket` populated, Secure Boot applying the Microsoft UEFI CA template, `Chipset.Uefi.BootThis` deliberately omitted). `CreateComputeSystem`/`Start` are bounded by their own `runAsync`+`select` against `ctx`, mirroring `vz_darwin.go`'s abandoned-boot pattern, since the vendored notification wait doesn't itself respect cancellation.
- WaitIP polls the host IP neighbor table for the guest's MAC (`internal/vm/neighbortable_windows.go`, a hand-written `iphlpapi` binding) rather than HNS endpoint state or KVP, both confirmed non-viable on real hardware. Teardown scrubs the neighbor-table entry explicitly — it outlives endpoint deletion and would otherwise accumulate one stale row per boot cycle.
- `internal/tart.Bundle` now accepts `linux/amd64`/`linux/arm64` bundles and a VHDX in place of a raw disk image; `internal/vhdx.Convert` is atomic (temp-file-then-rename) so a converting disk can't be observed as complete mid-copy; `internal/oci`'s pull headroom scales with the extra disk usage VHDX conversion needs; `internal/clonefile.Clone` and `cmd/runnyd/hostprobe_windows.go` (RAM detection) get real windows implementations instead of stubs.
- Guest arch validation is shared between both platforms and host-relative (`runtime.GOARCH`), not hardcoded to amd64 — Hyper-V on arm64 Windows should boot arm64 Linux.
- `cmd/runnyd`'s doctor gains a `hyperv-preflight` check (schema-2.1 build support, Default Switch present) and OpenCensus spans from the vendored HCS binding bridge into runny's OTel pipeline.

Full boot → IP → TCP:22-reachable → graceful-then-force stop cycle validated on real Hyper-V hardware (Windows 10 Pro 19045) before this PR, including the neighbor-table WaitIP mechanism and the HNS endpoint-delete leak. See ADR-0026 for the design and `internal/vm/CLAUDE.md` for sharp edges.

Closes #308

## Ruthless-audit cleanup, pass 1 — safe + high-value only

Two coherent changes, both verified. The full AI-OS deletion is **deliberately not here** (see below).

Verified 0 call-sites by grep across app/ + tests/:

- `app/services/call_manager.py` (55) — never imported.
- `lead_validator.score_lead()` + `score_lead_for_orova()` (~157) — dead scorers superseded by `score_lead_icp`.

### 2. Lean human Nova replaces the 24-tool agentic Telegram chatbot
You asked for Nova to "speak like a regular human" and keep you posted, not run an autonomous tool-loop. New `app/core/nova_chat.py`:
- Gathers a compact **live snapshot** (metrics, top leads, pending approvals) and hands it to **one grounded AI call** with a warm human persona. No tools → no injection surface, no tool-loop memory blow-up, never invents data.

I mapped it: `planner`/`semantic_firewall`/`self_learning`/`self_improvement` are **entangled** into `ceo_brain` (auto-execute), `hermesclaw_endpoints`, the outreach pipeline, and 6+ dashboard observability routes; `memory` is used by 13 modules incl. `_db_base`. author: grahamsnz
body:
## Why
`cb_storage` binds the global `*.authorize` hook, so its `authorize/N` runs on the authorize phase of **every** request. `maybe_deny_owner` denied on `crossbar_owner_authz:is_enforced/1` alone, without checking scope — so with `crossbar.owner_authz` enabled (filter or reject), **every** endpoint returned 403 for owner-restricted (non-admin) users, not just `/storage`. Wherever `cb_storage` is loaded, the whole per-user API was denied for restricted users.

## How
Compute `set_scope/1` once and gate the owner deny on `scope =/= 'invalid'`, so a non-storage request defers (`false`) exactly as before and only real storage scopes are hard-denied. Admins / flag-off keep the stock behaviour.

## Testing
Adds `cb_storage_authz_tests.erl` (EUnit, meck): enforced + non-storage -> defer (`false`); enforced + storage -> `{stop, _}`; not-enforced + storage (same account) -> allow; not-enforced + non-storage -> defer. 4/4 green (`rebar3 eunit --module=cb_storage_authz_tests`).

Verified on a live node (CouchDB + RabbitMQ, prod release) with `cb_storage` enabled and `crossbar.owner_authz` in filter — the state that reproduced the issue:
- devices / cdrs / users / vmboxes scope to the caller again (own-only list, own record 200, another user's record 403); before the fix all of these returned 403.
- `/storage` still returns 403 for a restricted user and passes admins, so the admin-only intent is preserved.

## PII
None. Restricts access to account/system storage config; no PII stored or logged.

## Notes
Targets `feature/owner-authz-storage` — this corrects the owner-deny wiring added on that branch. ~10 lines of change + a focused test module.
