author: ignacioreyes
body:
## Why

The status page was overly dramatic: a single failed check in a day painted the
whole day red and dropped that component's uptime by a full ~3.3% (1/30 days).
Daily bars were colored by the **worst** 5-min sample and uptime counted a day
as "ok" only if *every* sample that day was operational — so ~287 of 288 daily
data points were thrown away, and there was no way to see what fraction of
attempts actually failed or for how long.

## What changed

**Frontend ([`frontend/app.js`](../blob/uptime-fractions/frontend/app.js)) — the fix that reaches production:**

- Daily bars are now colored by the **fraction** of samples in each state, not
  the single worst one:
  - `≥99.5%` operational → 🟢 green (a lone 5-min blip is absorbed)
  - `>5%` of the day down → 🔴 red
  - anything in between → 🟡 yellow
- **Uptime %** is sample-weighted: a 5-min blip costs 5 min out of the window
  (≈99.99%) instead of a whole day.
- Each bar's hover tooltip reports that day's exact figures, with degraded and
  down tracked separately:
  `12 Jul 2026 · 99.7% up · 5 min down · 30 min degraded (1 down, 6 degraded / 288 checks)`

This is **frontend-only** — the 5-min buckets were already in `history.json`;
the prober, S3 payload, and the "no raw metrics in the payload" rule are
unchanged. Thresholds are named constants (`OK_GREEN_FRAC`, `OUTAGE_RED_FRAC`)
for easy tuning.

**Dev tooling (not deployed):**

- New `scripts/demo_data.py` generates a demo dataset anchored to *now* with
  288 samples/day and scripted showcase days, so `DEMO=1` actually demonstrates
  the new behavior. The old `demo/*.json` snapshot froze timestamps (fell
  outside the 30-day window, tripped the stale-data warning) and its 1-sample/
  day history couldn't show intra-day fractions.
- A `tick` loop keeps `updated_at` fresh so a running demo never goes stale.
- Removes the now-unused `demo/history.json` (superseded); `demo/status.json`
  and `demo/incidents.json` are reused as content templates.

## Verify

```
DEMO=1 python scripts/dev_server.py   # → http://localhost:8000
```

Showcase components (validated by running the generated data through the real
`app.js` aggregation):

| Component | Day | Bar | Tooltip |
|---|---|---|---|
| `api-ztf-lightcurve` | −9d | 🟢 green | `99.7% up · 5 min down (1/288)` — blip absorbed |
| `api-ztf-features` | −5d | 🟡 yellow | `97.2% up · 40 min down (8/288)` |
| `api-crossmatch` | −14d | 🔴 red | `93.8% up · 1h 30m down (18/288)` |
| `api-lsst-lightcurve` | −20d | 🟡 yellow | `100% up · 5h 30m degraded` — up but slow |
| `api-lsst-probability` | today | 🔴 red | ongoing outage |

## Blast radius

Only `frontend/app.js` is deployed (the deploy workflow syncs `frontend/` +
`incidents.json`). No AWS/IAM/infra changes, no new permissions, no payload
changes. `scripts/*` are local dev tools only.

author: wenqingw-nv
body:
Long autoregressive HY-WorldPlay rollouts drift: each chunk conditions on self-generated history and small errors compound into saturation/contrast runaway. This PR adds a trained drift corrector (Clean Forcing), the zero-real-data recipe that produced it, and a content-keyed deploy hook. `drift_corrector=None` (default) is byte-identical to current behavior.

## Contents
- `hy_worldplay/_drift_corrector.py` + two runner-config fields (`drift_corrector`, `drift_corrector_gain`) — content-keyed per job: static (locked-off camera) trajectories run untouched base weights (static scenes measure *negative* drift on this host — correction there is pure artifact cost); commanded-motion trajectories apply the LoRA at `alpha*(t) × gain` per denoise step.
- `integrations/hy_worldplay/drift_correction/` — full recipe, zero real videos: strafe-loop pair construction, step-0 `alpha*(t)` systematicity gate (go/no-go + the deploy gain profile), v1 counterfactual-teacher training, v2 DAgger + drift-contraction, gain-sweep eval, drift/dynamics/progression/seam scoring, static-scene demo suite. README documents the ~2.5 GPU-day reproduction.
- `tests/test_drift_corrector.py` (`ci_cpu`, 6 tests) — LoRA wrapper is a strict identity until a checkpoint is loaded and gated on; content-keyed selection triggers on action labels.

## Docs
- Our drift corrector LoRA method (clean-forcing) repo: https://gitlab-master.nvidia.com/wenqingw/clean_forcing
- Location in flashdreams-hy: https://github.com/wenqingw-nv/flashdreams-wq/tree/clean-forcing-hy-worldplay/integrations/hy_worldplay/drift_correction
- Clean-Forcing as a FlashDreams library designDoc: https://github.com/wenqingw-nv/flashdreams-wq/blob/hy-worldplay-counterfactual-forcing/integrations/hy_worldplay/drift_correction/LIBRARY_DESIGN.md

## Measured (704×1280, 24-chunk ≈19 s rollouts, held-out trajectories, GB300)
| config | MUSIQ ↑ | Δ-drift ↓ | dynamic degree |
|---|---|---|---|
| base | 68.0 | +1.70 | 19.3 |
| **shipped `alpha*(t) × 0.5`** | 70.4 | **−48%** | **20.3 (≈ base)** |
| flat gain 1.0 | 72.1 | −133% (negative drift) | 11.7 (−40%) |

Shipped config cuts the drift metric ~50% with no dynamics loss and no added chunk-boundary pulse; commanded trajectories keep advancing (owner-verified side-by-sides). The method/reproduction details: `drift_correction/README.md` (quick start)

## Deploy notes
- Per-step `alpha*(t)` gating cannot merge into one weight set → motion jobs run the LoRA unfused (~0.3% extra matmul); static jobs run the base at zero overhead.
- v2 LoRA checkpoint (~59 MB) hosting: currently a fork release asset (https://github.com/wenqingw-nv/flashdreams-wq/releases/tag/clean-forcing-hy-v2); release asset here vs HF — maintainer preference welcome.
- Correctors encode a checkpoint-specific error map: re-instantiation on a new base checkpoint is ~1 GPU-day with the included recipe (prompts only).

## Inference overhead (GB300, same rollout protocol as Measured; 3 runs, steady-state mean ± std)
| config | per-chunk (ms) | end-to-end 24 chunks (s) | effective fps | peak VRAM |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| base | 1265.9 ± 34.9 | 28.87 ± 0.72 | 13.2 | 47.41 GB |
| **shipped `corrgate050` (pre-merged)** | 1268.8 ± 1.5 | 28.98 ± 0.03 | 13.1 | 52.69 GB |

- **+0.22% per-chunk (+2.8 ms).** The deploy hook pre-merges `alpha*(t) × gain` into one cached copy of the target projection weights per distinct gate value at load (3 sets, +8.1 GiB) and swaps the set per solver step, driven CPU-side from the denoising schedule — the corrected forward issues the same kernels as base: no LoRA matmuls, no GPU timestep readback. Overhead is therefore GPU-independent (base runtime on any card).
- **Output equivalence vs the runtime fp32 delta path**: first-chunk latent diff ~1.2% relative (bf16 weight-merge rounding); on the seeded 24-chunk equivalence pair MUSIQ 70.2 vs 70.5 and Δ-drift 0.89 vs 0.73 — parity; side-by-side frame stacks are visually equivalent.
- `DRIFT_CORRECTOR_UNFUSED=1` selects the previous runtime fp32 delta path (1461 ± 69 ms/chunk, +12%).
- Static (locked-off camera) jobs run the untouched base weights per the content-keyed ship rule — zero overhead, no module surgery.

## Video Comparison

Left: FlashDreams-HY (base), Right: w/ Clean Forcing LoRA drift corrector (better details/color preservation across time):


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4830e24b-0444-4ec6-b6b1-358cb0eac5fa


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/472d7856-c43e-4c76-b990-fa42572bd08e


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d9f355b8-2af5-4a85-8d3d-ec2c3dda6b1c


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ea63dfd8-8458-4808-a5d6-c71921b0ee1e


## VBench Ablation:

| config | subj cons | bg cons | aesthetic | imaging | motion smooth | dyn degree | mean |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| base | 86.4 | 88.6 | 65.3 | 77.6 | 91.4 | 100.0 | 84.9 |
| corr050 | 92.0 | 92.9 | 67.1 | 77.0 | 91.8 | 100.0 | 86.8 |
| corrgate | **94.6** | **94.2** | **68.3** | 77.2 | **93.9** | 100.0 | **88.1** |
| **corrgate050 (shipped)** | 88.7 | 90.2 | 64.5 | 76.5 | 93.0 | 100.0 | 85.5 |

author: ewen-poch
body:
Closes #287

## Problem

Long-running agent tasks can take several minutes. Users switch to another application while waiting and don't notice when a task finishes, fails, or stalls on an approval — causing unnecessary waiting and delayed follow-up actions.

## Proposed change

Post a native desktop notification while the app is **unfocused** for these task lifecycle moments:

- `stop` events → **"Task completed"** (`end_turn`), or **"Task needs attention"** for early stops (`max_tokens` / `max_turn_requests` / `refusal`). User-cancelled turns stay silent (deliberate action).
- `error` events → **"Task failed"** for genuine prompt failures (discriminated via a shared `ACP_PROMPT_FAILED_EVENT_TITLE` constant). Ancillary session-scoped errors (artifact cleanup, cancel timeout) and recoverable context-overflows (auto-retried by the renderer) stay silent.
- Permission requests → **"Approval needed"** naming the waiting tool — a parked turn otherwise hangs unnoticed until the user returns. Connector approvals (the external data-egress gate, up to five minutes) get the same treatment, naming the connector call and targeting the in-flight turn that triggered it.
- The notification body names the task by the prompt's first line (bounded; bodies are truncated hard on some platforms).
- **Clicking** a notification surfaces the main window (`showMainWindow`) and opens the conversation: main records the target consume-once (`notifications:take-pending-open-session`) and the renderer pulls it once its session store is hydrated, so a click that recreates the window can never lose the navigation. The `notifications:open-session` push is only a nudge for a live renderer.
- New opt-out **Settings → General → Notifications → "Task notifications"** toggle, persisted as `notificationsEnabled` in `settings.json` and read fresh at notification time (no restart needed). Defaults to enabled.

Design notes:

- `src/main/notifications/task-notifications.ts` is Electron-free (delivery/focus/settings injected), so the filtering rules are unit-testable; the Electron wiring lives in `main/ipc.ts` and the click activation in `main/index.ts` (where `showMainWindow` exists). `showMainWindow` now returns the window it owns so the nudge targets it directly.
- Notification eligibility = *a prompt was tracked*, i.e. the turn came through the `acp:send-prompt` IPC handler (user-initiated). Internal turns injected via `runtime.sendPrompt` directly — the reviewer's auditor-correction loop — stay silent by construction.
- Delivery is guarded end to end: `Notification.isSupported()`, focus check, fresh settings read (fail-closed on error), swallowed delivery errors reported via `onDeliveryError`, and `Notification` instances retained until `click`/`close` so handlers can't be GC'd mid-banner.

### Example notifications

Bodies name the task by the prompt's first line (here: "Plot the dose-response curve"). Early-stop reasons are phrased in plain language — the raw ACP stop reasons never reach the user.

| Moment | Title | Body |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Completed | Task completed | "Plot the dose-response curve" finished. |
| Output truncated (`max_tokens`) | Task needs attention | "Plot the dose-response curve" stopped early — the answer hit the model's length limit. |
| Turn cap (`max_turn_requests`) | Task needs attention | "Plot the dose-response curve" paused — send a message to keep it going. |
| Refusal | Task needs attention | "Plot the dose-response curve" was declined by the agent. |
| Failed | Task failed | "Plot the dose-response curve" failed: Rate limit reached. |
| Approval wait | Approval needed | "Plot the dose-response curve" needs your approval: Run command |
| Connector approval | Approval needed | "Plot the dose-response curve" needs your approval: pubchem search compound |

### Platform behavior

- **macOS** — Notification Center via Electron's `Notification`; banners auto-suppress while the app is focused (we additionally gate on focus for deterministic behavior everywhere). Packaged builds are signed/notarized, so banners work in production.
- **Windows** — toast notifications; the app already sets an AppUserModelID (`com.aipoch.open-science`), so toasts are attributed correctly in packaged builds. Click activation is supported.
- **Linux** — delivered through the freedesktop notification daemon (libnotify); guarded with `Notification.isSupported()` so desktops without a daemon degrade to silent. Click support varies by DE. Headless `--serve` deployments never notify: the headless flag is threaded into the wiring and delivery is disabled outright, and click activation stays inert.

## Scope and non-goals

- Only user-facing agent prompt turns and their permission waits. The background reviewer loop stays silent by design; notebook runtime provisioning already has in-app progress UI (could be a follow-up).
- No notification for events while the app is focused.
- No notification-center history/management UI; the toggle is the only setting.

## Acceptance criteria and validation

- [x] Unit tests for the event→notification mapping and service gating rules (`src/main/notifications/task-notifications.test.ts`): completion/early-stop/failure/approval mapping, cancelled + recoverable + ancillary-error silence, internal-turn silence, focus gating, disabled preference, settings-read failure (fail-closed), prompt-snippet tracking/forgetting, delivery-error containment, consume-once click target.
- [x] Click-navigation tests: nudge-while-hydrated and consume-after-hydration (`App.test.tsx`), `openSessionById` (`navigation-store.test.ts`).
- [x] Settings chain tests mirroring the `reasoningEffort` pattern: repository persistence + sanitize (`repository.test.ts`), service view projection + setter (`service.test.ts`), IPC validation rejection (`ipc.test.ts`), preload channel pin (`preload/index.test.ts`), renderer store optimistic/revert behavior (`settings-store.test.ts`), toggle render + click (`GeneralPanel.render.test.tsx`).
- [x] CI green on all platforms (typecheck, lint, full test suite on macOS/Ubuntu/Windows).
- [x] Full typecheck, lint, and test suite validated in CI across every commit on this branch.

Manual verification on Windows and Linux desktops is still worthwhile (author machine is macOS): toast attribution/click on Windows, and `isSupported()` behavior across Linux DEs.

## Review focus

- The terminal-event filter rules in `describeTaskNotification` and the approval mapping in `describePermissionNotification` (`src/main/notifications/task-notifications.ts`).
- The tracked-prompt eligibility rule (user-initiated turns only) and the consume-once click-target handoff between main and renderer.
- The `notificationsEnabled` default (enabled) and its placement under Settings → General.

body:
## Fullscreen video
Tapping the inline TV surface enters fullscreen: forced landscape, immersive (system bars hidden), borderless `Dialog` that covers the whole app including the pager's bottom bar. The two separate seed actions (TV / Radio) in both the overflow menu and the empty state collapse into one `seedSamples()` that loads both bundled playlists at once, merged by `streamUrl`, single persist. (Old `seed_tv`/`seed_radio` strings left in place, now unused.)

author: scottlovegrove
body:
Reported in [\[CLI\] Can't remove/add users to groups](https://comms.todoist.com/69/ch/CaVwVqsJ5M73bmSTT4geh/t/Cd4BtmFKN2xEhHs2DgKag/) — `tdc groups add-user` / `remove-user` fail with a bare `Request failed with status 401`. Tracked as [Comms Issues](https://app.todoist.com/app/task/6h63gxG6f2gQFC3M).

Every group write route (`add`, `update`, `remove`, `add_users`, `remove_users`) requires the `workspaces:write` scope, which the CLI only requests under `--full-access`. On a default login we round-tripped to the API and surfaced whatever the server said, with no hint that the grant was the problem.

## Changes

- `src/lib/permissions.ts` — `API_METHOD_SCOPES` table + `ensureScopeAllowed()`. An under-scoped grant now fails immediately, naming the scope and the command that fixes it, instead of after a request. **Fails open** when the granted scope is unknown (`COMMS_API_TOKEN`, manually-saved tokens) — those may be session tokens, which bypass scope enforcement server-side, so blocking them would break working setups.
- `src/lib/api.ts` — guard wired into the client proxy alongside `ensureWriteAllowed`; new 401 → `INVALID_TOKEN` branch in `wrapResult`, so a rejected token gets re-auth guidance rather than the raw SDK message.
- `src/lib/errors.ts` — `isInvalidToken()` predicate, alongside the existing `isInsufficientScope` / `isForbidden`.
- README, skill content, `groups` command description — group writes need `--full-access`; group reads work on a default login.

Channel writes are deliberately absent from the scope table: they already surface a clean 403 from Comms, which `wrapResult` turns into the same guidance.

## Before / after

```
# before
Error: Request failed with status 401

# after
Error: INVALID_TOKEN
Comms rejected the token: 401.

  - Re-authenticate with `tdc auth login`, then check `tdc auth status`
```

An under-scoped grant never reaches this path: Comms returns a 403 `Insufficient scope` (handled by the existing branch), and the pre-flight guard catches it locally before any request goes out.

## Note for reviewers

While tracing this I found a separate server-side issue in the group write path and have written it up for the Comms backend team — it's independent of this PR, which stands on its own as the client-side scope handling.

## Testing

`npm run type-check`, `npm test` (847 pass), `npm run lint:check`, `npm run build` all clean. New coverage in `permissions.test.ts` (blocks/allows, whole-scope matching not substring, fails open on unknown scope, all five group methods) and `api.test.ts` (guard runs before the request fires; 401 translation).

The 401 mapping is verified against the live API. **The scope-guard path is unit-tested only** — verifying it end-to-end requires a default-scope login, which I didn't want to force.

author: jspinak
body:
## Symptom

`E2E Integration Tests` on `main` goes red ~daily on a single test:
`frontend/tests/e2e/pages/runner-connection.spec.ts` — "Download Page › shows
download files for selected platform" (the `Recommended`-badge visibility
assertion times out after 15s). A red main holds the coord merge train for the
repo. Occurrences: runs **29859706423** (2026-07-21, red ~11h) and
**29696362417** (2026-07-19).

## Root cause

The test depends on live, **anonymous** `api.github.com` release data fetched
by the backend (`backend/app/api/v1/endpoints/releases.py`). Shared
GitHub-Actions runner IPs exhaust the 60/hr anonymous rate limit
(`403 rate limit exceeded` visible in the failing job's backend log), and the
endpoint's deliberate silent fallback (200 + `available: false` + empty
`assets`) converts the upstream rate limit into a UI assertion timeout: no
assets → no "Recommended" badge → red main.

## Fix (two independent layers)

1. **Determinism (the actual fix):** stub `/api/v1/releases/runner/latest` in
   the "Download Page" describe of `runner-connection.spec.ts` — the exact
   pattern `marketing.spec.ts` already applied to `/runner/download` for the
   same rot class on 2026-06-24. The stub is extracted into a shared helper
   (`tests/e2e/helpers/runner-release-stub.ts`) so both specs use one
   canonical fixture instead of two copies.
2. **Authenticated fetch in CI (belt-and-braces):** plumb the workflow's
   `GITHUB_TOKEN` into the frontend E2E step env. `global-setup.ts` spawns the
   backend with `...process.env`, and `releases.py` already sends
   `GITHUB_TOKEN`/`GH_TOKEN` as a Bearer when present (5000/hr authed limit) —
   covers any other test touching the endpoint unstubbed. Read-only,
   public-repo metadata; no `permissions:` change.

No backend changes: token support and the degraded marker
(`available: false` + `reason`) already ship on main.

This clears a recurring red-main source that has been holding the merge train
(the same single-test failure red-mained 2026-07-19 and 2026-07-21).

Plan: `2026-07-22-web-e2e-release-fetch-flake-hardening` (vetted).

author: armelatwork
body:
## What
Completes the booking status machine from APPROVED through to a terminal state: owner marks ready for pickup -> borrower confirms pickup (loan clock starts) -> optional urgent-return (owner shortens the deadline with a reason, borrower may counter-propose once, owner accepts/rejects) -> borrower marks returned -> owner's single "return & inspect" action resolves to COMPLETED (tool back to available, waitlist re-settled) or DISPUTED (tool stays unavailable).

## How
`RETURN_REQUESTED_URGENT` and `PICKED_UP` are both treated as "active loan" for marking returned, since a borrower can return the tool whether or not an urgent request was ever countered — otherwise an uncountered urgent request would leave no path back to a returnable state.

Also fixes a pre-existing high-severity CVE (GHSA-f88m-g3jw-g9cj, libvips via sharp <0.35.0) inherited transitively through Next.js's optional `sharp` dependency — pinned via `package.json` overrides to 0.35.3, semver-compatible and verified against the full test/lint/build suite.

## Testing
- Unit tests for the loan-lifecycle domain rules and service (pickup, urgent-return, counter-propose, resolve, mark-returned, inspect), covering authorization and status-guard edge cases.
- Full suite passes locally, `npm audit` clean.
- Manually walked the entire lifecycle in a real browser end-to-end: approve → ready for pickup → confirm pickup → urgent return requested → counter-proposed → accepted → marked returned → inspected as complete → tool available again.

## Security
- `npm audit` clean (previously 2 high-severity findings from the sharp CVE).
- Every action re-checks the caller's role (owner vs. borrower) against the current booking, not just the UI.

## Notes
- Stacked on #3 (`feat/booking-engine`).

body: ## Huatli, Poet of Unity // Roar of the Fifth People (LCI #189) Implements the transforming DFC **Huatli, Poet of Unity** (front, `{2}{G}` Legendary Creature) / **Roar of the Fifth People** (back, Enchantment — Saga), plus the engine support its Saga back needs. ### Card - Assembled with `CardDefinition.doubleFacedPermanent` (creature front → non-creature Saga back), reusing the FIN/TLA transform-loop primitive `ExileAndReturnTransformed`. - **Front** — ETB basic-land tutor (`Patterns.Library.searchLibrary`); `{3}{R/W}{R/W}` sorcery-speed ability exile-returns Huatli transformed. Roar re-enters as a Saga and picks up its on-enter lore counter (CR 714.3a) via the shared Saga-entry hook — no explicit lore effect needed. - **Back (Saga)** — I: two 3/3 green Dinosaur tokens · II: grants Roar the Citanul-Hierophants static "creatures you control have '{T}: Add {R}, {G}, or {W}'" · III: tutor a Dinosaur to hand · IV: Dinosaurs you control gain double strike + trample. ### Engine The only genuinely new capability is honoring a **granted** `GrantActivatedAbility` static (chapter II grants it via `GrantStaticAbility`, rather than it being printed on a card): - Both ability-enumeration read sites — `CastPermissionUtils` (the enumerator) and `ActivateAbilityHandler` (the activation handler) — now resolve granted ability-granting statics through a single shared helper, `CastPermissionUtils.getGrantedStaticGrantActivatedAbilities`, so the two can never drift. - `ZoneTransitionService` prunes a permanent's battlefield-scoped granted statics when it leaves the battlefield (CR 400.7), so a grant like Roar chapter II doesn't linger on the card in the graveyard. Player-anchored grants (e.g. Malicious Eclipse) are untouched. ### Web client Active-effect hover tooltips (`CardOverlays`, `CardPreview`, `LifeDisplay`) now render mana symbols via `AbilityText`, so granted-ability descriptions like "{T}: Add {R}, {G}, or {W}" show glyphs instead of raw braces. ### Tests - `HuatliPoetOfUnityScenarioTest` — sorcery-speed timing, ETB tutor, transform → Roar Saga (lore 1) + chapter I tokens, and chapter II proving a controlled creature gains the granted mana ability (rejected before the grant, accepted after). - `GrantedStaticAbilityCleanupScenarioTest` — a granted static is pruned when its holder leaves the battlefield, driven through the real `ZoneTransitionService` path. Oracle text verified against Scryfall; canonical printing placement verified with `just check-card-printing`. `card-sdk-language-reference.md` updated for the granted-`GrantActivatedAbility` read site. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## 概要 / Summary

`/lp` の「無料で始める」CTAの可読性と、スマホ表示のメモ画面における切替タブとツールバーの間隔を改善しました。

Improved the readability of the `/lp` "Get started for free" CTAs and the spacing between the view switcher and toolbar on the mobile memo page.

## 変更内容 / Changes

- プライマリCTAを、白文字と十分なコントラストを持つ濃い緑へ変更
- 最終CTAを固定の明色背景・濃色文字にし、ダークテーマで文字が背景に埋もれる問題を解消

In dark mode, the final CTA used dark theme tokens for both its background and text. On the mobile memo page, the parent container's gap was overridden to `0`, leaving the switcher directly against the toolbar.

author: prezbar
body:
Closes #5 — with the publish itself deliberately left to a human. See **Before you tag** below.

## Summary

- **README completed.** All three entry points, the Reset Hook seam with the faker recipe, the options table, the no-static-app-imports rule, the `onTestFinished`-vs-`afterEach` cleanup caveat, the typed-`inject` note, Postgres-only / Prisma 7 / Vitest 4 / Node >= 20 stated loudly, and a guard-error table covering all ten real guards in `src/`.
- **`release.yml`** — `v*` tag → guard → full CI gate → build → pack assertion → `npm publish --provenance --access public`.
- **`ci.yml` gains `workflow_call`** so release reuses the exact everyday gate instead of a second copy that would rot.
- **Version bumped to 0.1.0** to match the tag.

Nothing publishes on merge. The workflow only fires on `v*` tags.

## Validation

A scratch Prisma 7 + Vitest 4 project was built from zero, wired **only from this README**, against a local `npm pack` tarball — no registry involved. It runs 5 passing tests, including:

- one that asserts a pristine database *after* a prior test wrote to it, proving the rollback is real;
- a faker-seeded factory whose output is byte-identical under a full run and under `-t` (`Eulah Murray` both times, despite different test sets and ordering), proving the seed derives from the test name alone.

The repo's own gate is green: 85 tests, 0 clones, typecheck + lint clean.

## How the plan evolved

The scratch validation earned its place immediately: it found that **`prisma.config.ts` was entirely undocumented**, and Prisma 7's `migrate deploy` fails without a `datasource.url` there. A reader following the old README would have hit a wall on their first run. That became a fifth wiring file (commit `47572ce`) and a row in the error table.

## Assumptions

- Consumers already have a Prisma schema, migrations, and a `prisma generate` step — the README documents the harness's wiring, not Prisma setup. Noted inline where the generated-client import path is reader-specific.
- `NPM_TOKEN` over trusted publishing for the *first* publish, per the discussion in this thread — a trusted publisher is configured on a package's settings page, which needs the package to exist. The switch to tokenless is documented inline in `release.yml`.

## Review

One fresh `general-purpose` reviewer, read-only, briefed with issue #5 and the goal statement rather than my account of the work. **0 blockers, 3 should-fix, 5 consider.**

Fixed:
- **`NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` was step-scoped**, but `setup-node` writes an `.npmrc` referencing it that `pnpm install` also expands — the release could have failed at *install* with an error resembling a lockfile problem. Hoisted to job scope.
- **No credential preflight** — the most likely first-run failure surfaced only *after* the full container suite. Added a check in `guard`.
- **The `refusing to open a test transaction` table row misdirected.** It blamed a `databaseName` mismatch; that guard's headline purpose is catching a client still pointed at your *dev* database. Rewritten to lead with reading `<name>` in the message.
- Two `consider`s worth taking: the `vi.mock` factory silently drops non-`db` exports (real consumers have them; the minimal dogfood client hides this), and the generated-client import path is reader-specific.
- Added top-level `permissions: contents: read`.

Verified and dismissed: `package-manager-cache` is a real `setup-node@v6` input (checked against the action's `action.yml`, default `true`).

**Left for you (`consider`-level, not acted on):**
- `on: push: tags: ["v*"]` matches prereleases like `v0.2.0-rc.1`, and `npm publish` with no `--tag` would push an rc to `latest`. Doesn't bite at 0.1.0; bites the first time you cut a prerelease. Fix is `--tag next` when the version contains `-`.
- No check for "this version already exists on the registry" — re-running a release fails at the last step with an `E403` after the whole container suite has run.

**These fixes were not re-reviewed.**

## Before you tag

The last two acceptance criteria on #5 (provenance badge visible, package page reads correctly) can't be verified until a real publish, so **#5 should stay open until then**:

1. Create an npm **automation** token, add it as the `NPM_TOKEN` repository secret.
2. Merge this PR, then `git tag v0.1.0 && git push --tags`.
3. Verify the provenance badge and the package page.
4. Configure trusted publishing on the now-existing package, then delete the secret, the job's `env:` block, and the guard's credential check — all marked inline.

author: loumalouomega
body:
## Summary

Adds a new `interpolate` mesh operation (cross-mesh field transfer) across every binding surface, and adds a C++ (xeus-cpp) counterpart to the example notebooks, reorganizing `example/` into `example/python/` + `example/cpp/` in the process.

## `interpolate`: cross-mesh field transfer (v7.13.0)

The first **two-mesh** operation that moves *data* rather than just comparing (`diff`) or concatenating (`merge`) — it samples a source mesh's arrays onto a target mesh and returns a copy of the target with its own geometry, connectivity, data, and sets preserved exactly.

- `interpolate(source, target, method=, arrays=, extrapolate=, default_value=, on_conflict=)`. Source `point_data` is sampled at the target's points; `cell_data` always by nearest source-cell centroid, regardless of method.
  - `method="nearest"` (default): bit-for-bit copy of the nearest source point's value (dtype-preserving).
  - `method="barycentric"`: simplexifies the source and interpolates linearly — exact on a linear field; always Float64 output. `default_value`/`extrapolate` cover target points outside the source domain.
  - `on_conflict`: `error` (default) / `overwrite` / `suffix` (`name + "_interp"`).
  - Output is byte-identical across the three mesh backends, thread counts, and the C++-core/numpy-fallback boundary.

- Exposed everywhere: pybind `_core` + numpy fallback, C API `mio_interpolate`, Fortran module-level `mio_interpolate`, WASM `interpolate`, and the `interpolate SOURCE TARGET OUT` verb on both CLIs.
- New shared `detail/spatial_hash.hpp`: hoists `merge`'s weld bucket-grid spatial hash verbatim and extends it with the queries `interpolate` needs.
- Bugfix along the way: `clean.cpp`'s `CleanKeyHash` switched to `uint64_t`.
- Tests: new C++ gtest suite, Python suite, C API coverage, Fortran, WASM smoke test.
- Docs: `doc/interpolate.md`, CLI reference, README section, notebook demo.
- Version bumped to **7.13.0** across all five version files, with the CHANGELOG entry.
- Single-header amalgamation regenerated.

## Example notebooks: `example/python/` + `example/cpp/`

- `example/` split into `example/python/` (existing notebooks, moved as-is) and a new `example/cpp/` — a from-scratch C++ counterpart on the [xeus-cpp](https://github.com/compiler-research/xeus-cpp) kernel against the committed single-header amalgamation, no Python involved. Shared assets stay at the `example/` top level.
- `example/cpp/` notebooks (01 read/visualize, 02 convert/inspect, 03 operations tour) mirror the Python set, including the new `interpolate` demo, rendering via meshio++'s own SVG writer through a small helper, `mio_notebook.hpp`.
- `example/cpp/example.vtu` is used as input instead of `example/example.msh` directly, since Gmsh's `$Entities` section is a documented gap in the C++ reader with no fallback in a C++-only kernel.
- All six notebooks re-executed and committed with outputs.
- `.gitignore`: added `.micromamba/`. Docs updated: `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `doc/single_header.md`.

author: jcschaff
body:
## What

Migrates the Composite Explorer's **generator-branch** state build off the HTTP process — the flagship `resolve_composite_state` method (env-worker-protocol.md §11, "the ~1–3s call").

`composite_state_views.composite_state_via_subprocess` previously spawned a one-off `sys.executable -c <embedded script>` **per request**. It now routes `resolve_composite_state{ref}` through the **warm pool**, keeping its exact return contract (`{state,module,emitters}` / `{__build_error__,emitters}` / `{__not_registered__}` / `None`) so `build_composite_state`'s branch logic — and every `_patch_subprocess` test — is untouched.

Two structural wins over the old subprocess:
- **Correct interpreter.** The worker builds on the *workspace's own* venv, so a workspace like v2ecoli (pins Python 3.12.12) can build at all.
- **Warm, not per-request.** No process spawn + `build_core` on every Explorer open/pop-out.

## Supporting changes

- **Port `process_docs` into the worker** (`_summarize_large_values` / `_attach_process_docs` + the `local:<addr>`→class-description helpers). The worker can't import `vivarium_workbench`, and both must run where the data lives: `summarize_large_values` collapses the multi-MB numpy `bulk` store *before* JSON crosses the socket; `attach_process_docs` imports the workspace process classes to read their descriptions.
- **`_write_frame` → `json.dumps(default=str)`**, matching the old subprocess's coercion of odd leaves in a state doc (no-op for the string-only methods).
- **Spawn the worker with `cwd=workspace`** so cwd-relative composite reads (e.g. v2ecoli's `out/cache/initial_state.json`) resolve as they did under the old `cwd=ws_root` subprocess. Safe — a worker is dedicated to one workspace, so this is not a process-global `chdir`.
- `resolve_composite_state` primes the workspace-package import (like `list_generators`) so a non-installed workspace's `@composite_generator`s register.

## Verification

- **Fixture** (`ws_increase_demo` `hint_test`): builds → `{state, module=pbg_ws_increase_demo.composites, emitters}`; unknown ref → `{__not_registered__}`; full route → `kind="generator"`, 200.
- **Real v2ecoli** on its own venv (opt-in e2e): the baseline build hits the known **ParCa-cache-absent** path → `__build_error__` → the workbench's static-fallback serves the pre-generated state (exactly the pre-existing behavior; the code comment names this case). Any returned state is finite JSON (numpy summarized away).
- Full gate: 14 pre-existing env-noise failures (observables/readouts/composite_runs — missing `polars` locally), **zero new**. mypy clean (78 files), import-linter clean.

## Scope / follow-up

The **static-fallback** and **spec-file** branches still call `attach_process_docs` in-process (graceful-degrade under multi-workspace: the imports simply fail → no docstring). Moving those onto the worker (via a `document`-taking method per §11's freshness model) is a tracked follow-up. This generator-branch migration is independently correct.

author: basquin-bot[bot]
body:
## What & why

Load-mode replay was **method-unaware**: it fired every fuzz-found corpus entry as a bare GET. Replaying JPetStore's Stripes form handlers as sessionless GETs produced ~14% 5xx + a 30s-timeout tail that **saturated the target**, which then **starved the `/__basquin/drift` poller** — so the heap-fatigue curve silently reported `heapDriftKb:0`, indistinguishable from a real flat heap. One root cause, chained:

```
method-unaware replay → target saturates → drift poll times out → pollDrift()=null → heapDriftKb silently 0
```

(Investigation confirmed the agent boundary/drift endpoint are correct — the real trigger in benchmarks was an undersized 512MB target heap; at 2g, drift answers in ~2ms under load. No boundary bug.)

## The four fixes

1. **Method-aware replay** — corpus format v2: a line is a TAB-separated ordered sequence of `METHOD? path( SP body )?` steps; a bare `/…` line = a 1-step GET sequence (**backward-compatible**; no operator/CRD changes). New `RequestLine` record + sequence helpers.
2. **Session-aware replay** — each load worker keeps its own cookie jar (captures/sends `JSESSIONID`), like a real user.
3. **Full-sequence replay** — explore emits the *whole* cost-ranked sequence (not the orphaned tail); each worker replays a random sequence's steps in order with its session. Multi-step seeds route through `pendingSequences` (un-gated from grammar presence). Replay-only sequences are guarded out of single-request mutation.
4. **Drift honesty** — `pollDrift`/toggle failure now surfaces as `"driftUnavailable":true` (heap/thread omitted) instead of a fabricated `0`; `setTargetMode` verifies `ok:load`; e2e now asserts drift was *sampled* over the Service DNS while in load mode (asserts sampled-ness, not `drift>0` — GC can make drift ≤0).

## How it was built

Subagent-driven development, 9 tasks, fresh implementer + reviewer per task, **opus whole-branch final review** ("Ready to merge: Yes"). The review loop caught and fixed **two Criticals** the happy path missed: (a) a replay-only TAB sequence reachable as a single-request mutation parent → garbled-URL false crashes; (b) `driftUnavailable` initially only checked the baseline poll, not the terminal one. Design + plan under `docs/superpowers/`; decision record **DD-035** in `docs/DESIGN-DECISIONS.md` (with rejected alternatives).

## Testing

- **158 unit tests green** (`./gradlew test`), +36 new for this feature.
- Backward-compat, value-file exclusion, no-sequence-corruption, drift-honesty, and cross-task integration all verified in the final review.
- e2e drift assertions added (needs the in-cluster run to exercise).

## Benchmark context (separate deliverable)

Controlled 3-way, same profile: k6 10,856 rps / Locust(8-proc) 9,600 / **Basquin 6,848** (best p50) — all converge on the target's capacity, validating Basquin's engine, plus it uniquely captures server-side heap drift + invariants.

author: orangepeachpink
body:
Refs #1439. The v0.8.0 window's single red main (e979be7).

## The gap

`continue-on-error` was on the **compile step only**. So the job *named* "experimental board (esp32s3) — non-blocking" was non-blocking for one step — and any **other** step (uv sync, pip install, a cache miss) failing still red the job, and red main. The name promised non-blocking; the wiring delivered it for one step.

## The fix — complete the design, don't reverse it

Both `ci.yml` and `weekly-battery.yml`: **every step** of `experimental-boards` is now `continue-on-error: true`. This *completes* the #504/#546 green-reporting pattern (step-level, so the job's own badge stays green — deliberately not job-level, which shows a red X) instead of applying it to one step. Whatever breaks, the job cannot fail, so it cannot red the run. The warning now fires on `always() && compile != success`, so a break still surfaces even when an earlier step caused it.

## The real fix is the test

`test_experimental_nonblocking.py` parses both workflows and asserts the invariant **structurally**: every step of the non-blocking job is `continue-on-error`.

**Red-proofed** — stripping `continue-on-error` from one step fails the test, naming it:
```
assert not ['Sync the locked environment']
```
So a newly-added step can't silently reopen the hole — which is exactly how #546 regressed (a guarantee with nothing testing it). This is the AC's "add the S3-red case to the workflow's own test," made concrete: the falsehood-family principle applied to a CI job — test the guarantee the *name* makes.

## Per-AC
- ✅ `continue-on-error` re-asserted at the level the run verdict consumes (every step → the job conclusion the run reads)
- ✅ red-proofed against a simulated broken step
- ✅ the S3-red case added to the workflow's own test (the structural invariant)

Not cross-seam. Gate green — 168 dx + 1058 analytics.

**V2** — Workflow verifies and lands.

— DX 🧰

author: suvarna4
body:
## Summary

Design-diff follow-up to WS25 (T1–T5), discovered live: `auth.ts` had no `pages.error`/`pages.signIn` configured, so any sign-in failure that reaches Auth.js's top-level error routing landed on an Auth.js-owned page instead of this app's UI — the same class of bug WS25 fixed on the *send* side, just on the *verify* side. This was reported by a real user hitting Auth.js's raw "Server error — There is a problem with the server configuration" page for both an expired magic link and, separately, other email accounts.

- `auth.ts` now sets `pages: { error: '/claim', signIn: '/claim' }`. **Both keys matter, not just `error`**: `@auth/core`'s `Auth()` picks the redirect destination from the thrown error's own `kind` property — `Verification` (an expired/already-used magic-link token) has `kind: "error"`, but `EmailSignInError` (WS25-T4's own rate-limit/transport-failure wrapper) and every OAuth callback error class extend `SignInError`, whose `kind` is `"signIn"`. An earlier revision of this PR set only `pages.error`; independent review caught (empirically, via `@auth/core`'s real `Auth()` function) that `EmailSignInError` was still falling through to Auth.js's own unbranded default `/api/auth/signin`, completely unaffected. Fixed in a follow-up commit.
- `/claim` reads `?error=...` and passes it to `ClaimEntry` (new `authError` prop), which skips the ghost-confirmation ceremony (already done once to get this far) and shows a clear retry message — specific "link expired or already used" copy for `Verification`, one generic retry message for everything else rather than exposing internal Auth.js error codes.
- New test coverage in `auth-error-routing.test.ts` proves both `kind` values now route to `/claim` against the real `@auth/core` library (confirmed as a genuine regression guard — the test was verified to fail if `pages.signIn` is removed). New e2e coverage in `claim-flow.spec.ts` for `ClaimEntry`, which has no RTL/jsdom harness in this repo.

Went through two independent-review rounds. Round 1 confirmed the mechanism and caught the `pages.signIn` gap. Round 2 confirmed the fix closes it — including a live reproduction against a running server (real Postgres/Redis, production build): exhausting the real §14.1 rate limit now redirects to `/claim?error=Configuration` instead of the pre-fix `/api/auth/signin?error=Configuration`.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter web typecheck` / `test` (750/750) / `build` — clean
- [x] `eslint` on all touched files — clean, 0 warnings
- [x] `apps/web/test/auth-error-routing.test.ts` — 8/8 passing, directly exercising the real `@auth/core` `Auth()` function for both `kind: "error"` (`Verification`) and `kind: "signIn"` (`EmailSignInError`) cases
- [x] `claim-flow.spec.ts` e2e — 11/11 passing (`/claim?error=Verification`, `/claim?error=Configuration`, and the no-param case, plus existing regression coverage)
- [x] **Live end-to-end reproduction**: built the app, ran it with `next start` against real Postgres/Redis, exhausted the real 5/hour rate limit for a fresh test email, confirmed the 6th attempt redirects to `/claim?error=Configuration` (branded) rather than `/api/auth/signin?error=Configuration` (unbranded, the gap round 1 found) or `/api/auth/error?error=Configuration` (the original bug)

author: brianorwhatever
body: Hardens the durable Originals host routes. Both issues were flagged by Greptile on **#432**, but are **not** about #432's change — they're anchored to that PR's *earlier polluted diff* (before it was force-pushed to just the SDK `network:'testnet'` fix). The code is already merged into `main` via #431, so it's fixed here against main. ## 1. Namespace pre-squat (the "scary" P1) `hostPut` confined keys to did:webvh artifact shape and relied on the store's first-writer-wins owner sidecar — but never checked the per-user namespace. An authed user could `PUT user-/did.jsonl` before the victim, claim it, and lock the victim's publish out. The sidecar only protects an *already-claimed* key. `webvh.ts` even documented an enforcement that didn't exist. **Fix:** a `user-` segment must equal the caller's own `user-${sub.slice(0,16)}`, else 403. Asset paths are hash-derived (not `user-`-prefixed) and stay open — unguessable + sidecar-protected. `webvh.ts` doc corrected. *Severity:* needs the victim's subOrgId (not public pre-publish) and only yields a publish-DoS — but code contradicting its own security doc is worth closing. ## 2. Malformed URL → 500 A crafted `%GG` made `decodeURIComponent` throw an uncaught `URIError` → 500. Both `hostPut`/`hostGet` now decode via a guarded helper → clean **400**. ## Tests Pre-squat 403 (unclaimed victim path), malformed-key 400 (PUT+GET). Full landing suite 115/0, typecheck clean. Also removes a stray empty changeset. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) > [!NOTE] > ### Enforce per-user namespace on host PUT and return 400 on malformed percent-encoded keys > - Adds a namespace guard in `createOriginalsRoutes.hostPut` that rejects writes to a `user-*` path not owned by the authenticated caller with 403 (`forbidden_namespace`). > - Replaces raw `decodeURIComponent` calls in both `hostPut` and `hostGet` with a `decodeKey` helper that returns `null` on malformed encoding, causing the handlers to return 400 instead of throwing a 500. > - Behavioral Change: PUT requests to another user's predictable `user-` namespace now return 403; previously malformed keys would have caused unhandled exceptions. > > > > Macroscope summarized b0fecce. > >

## Summary

**Fix — international customers can now pay (prod bug)**
- Every Stripe checkout flow (rental event, rental custom dates, product purchase, admin send-invoice) restricted the shipping address to `allowed_countries: ['US']`, so the country dropdown offered only United States and non-US customers could not complete payment. Two European/South American Vakaros rental customers were blocked in prod.
- All flows now use `WORLDWIDE_SHIPPING_COUNTRIES` (`lib/stripe/shipping-countries.ts`, new) — the full Stripe-supported list (237 codes, typed against the SDK enum, `readonly`). The address form stays on rentals by owner decision: each rental request's address is reviewed for shipping viability, with manual refunds when it isn't worth it. Verified in Stripe **test mode**: one `sessions.create` with all 237 codes succeeded.
- Hardening (found by adversarial review, cross-model confirmed): admin send-invoice now checks the reservation update that attaches the new checkout session **before** emailing the payment link. Previously a failed write still returned 200 and emailed a link that could take payment with no fulfillable reservation.

**Docs**
- One-word correction in the webhook-recovery design doc (maru sessions confirmed unpaid).

## Test Coverage

Audit ran mid-ship (75%, 3 gaps); both unit gaps were closed before landing:
- Added: send-invoice `purchase` branch (worldwide shipping ternary — previously zero route-level coverage), send-invoice `rental_custom` branch, and a regression test for the new update-failure guard (500 + no email).
- All flows assert country-list invariants (contains US/ES/AR/DE/BR, ≥200 entries, no `ZZ`) instead of tautological equality with the source constant.
- Remaining gap is E2E-only: the shipping form renders on Stripe's hosted domain, so it can't be asserted from Playwright. Mitigated by the test-mode `sessions.create` smoke test.

Tests: 376 → 379 (+3 new)

## Pre-Landing Review

Checklist pass (SQL safety, races, enum completeness, etc.): **No issues found.** Verified the webhook tolerates the shape change (`toShippingAddress()` already null-safe; `orders.shipping_address` nullable).

Adversarial review (Claude subagent + Codex, cross-model):
- **Fixed in this PR:** unchecked send-invoice DB write (both models flagged it); mutable exported constant (now `readonly`); tautological test assertion.
- **Verified safe:** full 237-code list accepted by Stripe test mode (kills the "one bad code 503s every purchase" risk).
- **Pre-existing, not introduced here (follow-ups):** webhook idempotency is check-then-act (duplicate fulfillment possible on concurrent delivery — ties into the paused webhook-recovery workstream); invoice `expires_at` cleared before fire-and-forget email.

## Design Review

No frontend UI files changed — design review skipped.

## Eval Results

No prompt-related files changed — evals skipped.

## Scope Drift

Scope Check: CLEAN. Intent: unblock international Stripe payments. Delivered: exactly that, plus review-driven hardening in a touched file and a one-word docs fix.

## Plan Completion

No plan file detected (interactive /investigate hotfix).

## Verification Results

- Full Jest suite: 68 suites, 379 tests, 0 failures (fresh run on final code).
- `tsc --noEmit`: no new errors (2 pre-existing errors in untouched db test files, confirmed identical with changes stashed).
- Stripe test-mode smoke: `sessions.create` with the full 237-country list → PASS.

## Follow-ups (also in local TODOS.md)

1. **P1** — International orders collect $0 freight and $0 tax (`tax_cents` hardcoded 0, no `shipping_options`/`automatic_tax`). Owner currently absorbs freight or refunds manually.
2. **P2** — Curate the country list: it includes export-controlled destinations (RU, BY, AF, …) and uninhabited territories (AQ, BV, …). Stripe accepting payment ≠ legal/practical to ship marine electronics there. One-line change at the constant.
3. **P2** — Rental invoices emailed before this deploy contain US-only checkout links; once expired, send-invoice 409s ("already sent") and can't re-issue without a manual DB touch.

body:
## erdos-18-wip-01 — Practical Numbers: closure under doubling + structural bounds

Extends `proofs/Proofs/Erdos18WIP01.lean` (previously: powers of two + evenness
necessary condition) with a **multiplication (closure) rule** and two **structural
bounds**. All 0-axiom, host + `#print axioms` verified, no `sorry`.

### Closure under doubling

- `sum_image_two_mul` — doubling a divisor-subset doubles its sum (`d ↦ 2d` injective).
- `image_two_mul_subset_divisors` — `S ⊆ divisors m ⟹ 2·S ⊆ divisors (2m)` (`d∣m ⟹ 2d∣2m`).
- `repr_two_mul` / `repr_two_mul_add_one` — a representation of `q` by divisors of `m` doubles to `2q` (and `2q+1`, adjoining the odd divisor `1`) by divisors of `2m`.
- **`two_mul_practical`** — **`m` practical ⟹ `2m` practical.** Split `k < 2m` as
  `2q + r` (`r ∈ {0,1}`, `q ≤ m−1`), represent `q` via `m`, double, add `1` if `r=1`.
  The `n = 2` case of the Stewart product criterion `n ≤ σ(m)+1 ⟹ mn practical`.
- **`two_pow_mul_practical`** — iterating: `2^n · m` practical whenever `m` is.
- `two_pow_mul_six_practical` — concrete new family `2^n · 6` (6, 12, 24, 48, …).

### Structural bounds

- **`two_mul_sub_one_le_sigma`** — for practical `m`, `σ(m) ≥ 2m − 1` (`m−1` is a
  sum of proper divisors; adjoin the divisor `m`).
- **`odd_practical_eq_one`** — the only *odd* practical number is `1`.

### Verification

- `lake env lean Proofs/Erdos18WIP01.lean` → exit 0 (host, Mathlib-only + parent olean).
- `#print axioms` on every new theorem = `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.

Parent Erdős #18 ($250, h(n!) growth) stays OPEN; this is elementary structural progress.

body:
## What
Sends a reminder email at T-2 days, on the due date, and daily while overdue, for every active loan.

## How
Which reminder (if any) applies is pure UTC calendar-day math in `domain/reminder-schedule.ts`, so it's testable without touching a clock or a database. Idempotency doesn't rely on a prior read-then-write — the service attempts to INSERT into `ReminderLog` first and treats a unique-constraint violation (P2002) as "already sent," so two overlapping or retried cron runs for the same booking+type+day can't double-send even under concurrency.

Runs two ways: `/api/cron/reminders`, protected by `CRON_SECRET` and wired to Vercel Cron via `vercel.json` for prod, and `npm run reminders:watch` (node-cron) for local dev.

## Testing
- Unit tests for the reminder-schedule domain logic and the reminder service, including the idempotency backstop.
- Full suite passes locally.
- Verified idempotency live, not just in unit tests: seeded a real booking due today, hit the cron route twice — first run sent 1 email, second sent 0, exactly one `ReminderLog` row remained. Also confirmed an unauthenticated request is rejected with 401.

## Security
- The cron route fails closed: if `CRON_SECRET` isn't set, or the request's bearer token doesn't match, it returns 401.

## Notes
- Stacked on #4 (`feat/loan-lifecycle`).

author: gemisis
body:
## What

A single-file, append-only record of an **entire agent run** — `leviath-core::run_archive` — designed so a run can be copied to another machine and resumed (or replayed for debugging). This is the foundation for demand-paging (unload = flush archive; reload = read it) and for future cross-machine run migration.

### Identity / ownership
`RunIdentity { run_id, machine_id, world_id, created_at }` makes a run unambiguously attributable when several daemons share a filesystem and might otherwise collide on `run_id`. `RunRecord::OwnershipChanged` models a handoff. Per the follow-up direction, this deliberately reserves room for **future cross-machine migration** — start a run on one machine, pause, resume on another; a host declining a run whose tools it lacks and waiting for a capable one — without building that scheduling yet.

### Journal
A versioned, framed record stream:
```
MAGIC ("LVR1") | version (u16 BE) | frame*
frame := len (u64 BE) | JSON-encoded RunRecord
```
Records: `Header`, `Inference`, `ToolBatch`, `Message`, `StatusChanged`, `ContextCheckpoint`, `ContextDiff`, `OwnershipChanged`, `Checkpoint`. The frame layout is codec-agnostic, so the JSON payload can become a compact binary encoding later without changing readers that seek by frame length.

### Efficiency (context diffs)
Context windows are the bulk of a run, so between full checkpoints they're stored as diffs: `diff_context` / `apply_delta` encode per-region `Append` / `Set` / `Clear` / `Remove`, reducing the common between-inference case (a pure append to one region) to a compact `Append`.

### Reconstruction
`fold()` replays the journal into a run's current state (identity, meta, window, messages, counters) for resume and inspection.

## Scope
Pure data + codec + fold, no I/O beyond the `Read`/`Write` traits. **Wiring the daemon to write archives and reload from them is a deliberate follow-up** (see `docs/design/agent-paging.md`). Adds `PartialEq` to the `run_meta` snapshot types (needed for diffing/round-trip assertions).

## Tests
diff/apply round-trips for every region-delta shape, codec round-trips over every record kind, every truncation / bad-magic / bad-version / invalid-payload / reader-error / writer-error path, and fold reconstruction. leviath-core at 100% coverage; clippy + rustdoc clean.

author: alejandrominor
body:
## Why

Navigating a large overview with only arrow keys means several key
presses to reach a window on the other side of the grid — the more
windows open, the more it drags. This adds a way to jump straight to
any preview in one shot: glance at its number/letter, press it, done.
It doesn't replace arrow-key/mouse navigation, just gives a faster
path when you already know (or can see) exactly which window you want,
especially with many windows across workspaces where the target might
be several key presses away.

## Summary

- Adds an optional pick-label overlay (`1`-`9`, then `A1`-`Z9`) on each
  preview's top-right corner for direct keyboard selection, alongside
  existing arrow-key/mouse navigation
- New config: `pick_labels_enabled` (default `0`) and
  `pick_labels_direct_activate` (default `0`; `1` activates and closes
  overview immediately on a hit, `0` only moves the selection like
  arrow keys, still needs `Return`)
- Label order follows visual reading order (monitor, then row, then
  column) — not window creation or focus order
- Past 9 windows, a letter key (`A`-`Z`) arms a short prefix waiting
  for its digit (e.g. `A` then `2` picks `A2`); any other key cancels
  the prefix without losing its own normal effect (`Esc` still closes
  overview, arrow keys still navigate)
- Styling reuses `close_button_color` / `close_button_glyph_color` /
  `close_button_size` — no dedicated pick-label color/size config
- Previews too small to hold a legible label skip drawing it; the
  window stays selectable by its key, mouse, or arrow keys
- `docs/spec.md` (section 6.3, section 8) and `README.md` updated to match


## Preview
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e73d2f6f-ff48-4be3-a059-0a01e29a178a

The video starts with both pick_labels_enabled and pick_labels_direct_activate off, showing the original navigation. I then turn on pick_labels_enabled, so pressing a number now selects that preview (still needs Return to confirm). Next, I turn on pick_labels_direct_activate too. Now hitting a number key (or a letter+digit combo, e.g. A1) immediately focuses that window in Hyprland, no Return needed. Finally, I open many windows to show that once a preview gets too small, its number stops being shown, but it still works if you press it.

author: javierarce
body:
Adds a **New deck…** action to the command palette (⌘K) so a deck can be created without navigating to the Decks page.

The existing inline "Create New Deck" dialog from `all-decks-list.tsx` is extracted into a shared `CreateDeckDialog` component (owning its input/busy/error state and the case-insensitive duplicate guard), which both the Decks page and the palette now reuse. No new duplication is introduced: the two create-deck flows now share one dialog.

author: quickmythril
body:
## Summary

- Adds protected `SET_ACCOUNT_AVATAR` and `SET_GROUP_AVATAR` bridge actions in desktop and native/renderer paths.
- Adds public-node-safe `FETCH_ACCOUNT_AVATAR` and `FETCH_GROUP_AVATAR` actions using Core's authorization-info and exact-byte endpoints.
- Returns bounded base64 image data, source and descriptor metadata, and structured `PENDING` results for Core/QDN `202` responses.
- Uses magic-byte-only raster validation and a 500 KiB limit.
- Supports custom service/name/identifier publishing through the existing QDN publish action; SET actions accept only the exact transaction signature.

## Trust and migration behavior

- Core authorization info is checked first and an explicit authorized signature always wins.
- Explicit invalid/unavailable content fails closed and never falls back to a mutable resource.
- Only an info `404` enables legacy lookup.
- Account legacy order: `THUMBNAIL/<primaryName>/avatar`, then `THUMBNAIL/<primaryName>/qortal_avatar`.
- Group legacy lookup: `THUMBNAIL/<ownerPrimaryName>/qortal_group_avatar_<groupId>`.
- Legacy results are marked `source: LEGACY`; authorized results are marked `source: AUTHORIZED` and carry `{ signature, service, name, identifier }`.

## Publishing defaults

- Account: `THUMBNAIL/<primaryName>/avatar`
- Group: `THUMBNAIL/<ownerName>/qortium-group-avatar-v1-<groupId>`
- Publishing and authorization remain separate approvals.
- `SET_ACCOUNT_AVATAR` always uses `txGroupId: 0`.

## Verification

- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`
- `npm run build:electron`
- `npm run build:renderer`
- `npm run test:qdn-group-avatar-input`
- `npm run test:qdn-manager-action-catalog`
- `git diff --check`

author: simsimhugh
body:
## 배경

저장소 visibility 가 **PUBLIC** 인데 코드·문서·이슈·PR 에 사내 도메인/개인 식별자/사내 조직·제품명이 마스킹 없이 들어가 있었다 (이슈 #456). 본 PR 은 **저장소 파일** 쪽 조치다. GitHub 이슈/PR/코멘트/리뷰/제목 33곳은 별도로 API 마스킹 완료.

## 변경

**1. 마스킹** — 실제 값은 `.env`(gitignore)로만 주입하고 파일에는 플레이스홀더만 남긴다. 사내 레지스트리/git/PyPI 호스트 → `<harbor-registry>` / `<internal-git-host>` / `<internal-pypi-host>`, Knox ID → 사내 사용자 ID, 사내 LLM 제품명 → `<사내 모델>`, 사명 이메일 도메인 → `corp.example.com`.

`x-dep-ticket` / `x-service-id` 같은 **헤더 이름**과 `A2G` · `DS API HUB` · `Harbor` 는 사명이 드러나지 않아 유지. 공개 모델명(gpt-oss/Gemma/Qwen)도 유지.

**2. 재유입 게이트** (`scripts/check_internal_leak.sh` + `.github/workflows/internal-identifiers.yml`)

초판은 금지 식별자를 조각으로 쪼개 스크립트에 담았는데, 보안 리뷰가 **조각 결합으로 원값이 전부 복원된다**고 지적했다 — public 저장소 재노출이고, 개인식별자·서비스 UUID·사내 IP 3종은 원래 이력에 없던 값이라 그 커밋이 최초 노출이었다. 브랜치를 재작성하고 아래로 재설계했다.

> ⚠️ **정정**: 브랜치 재작성으로 노출이 제거되지는 **않았다**. force-push 로 떨어져 나간 커밋이 GitHub 에 그대로 살아 있다(익명 `curl` HTTP 200 실측). GitHub 은 dangling object 를 자동 GC 하지 않는다. 위 3종은 영구 유출로 취급해야 하며, **서비스 UUID 재발급 + GitHub Support 에 purge 요청**이 필요하다 — 이슈 #456 에서 추적 중이다.

- **구조 규칙만 저장소에** — RFC1918 사설 IP, `.github/allowed-domains.txt` 밖 FQDN, `x-service-id` 인접 UUID. 정확값은 한 글자도 없다.
- **정확값 denylist 는 repo secret** `INTERNAL_LEAK_PATTERNS` 로만 주입. CI 인데 미주입이면 **fail-closed(exit 1)** — 조용한 green 방지. fork PR 은 secret 을 못 받으므로 구조 규칙만 수행하고 그 사실을 로그에 남긴다.
- **검사 범위**: 파일 내용 + 파일·디렉터리 **이름** + `origin/main..HEAD` 의 **커밋 메시지와 도입 시점 blob**. 커밋 A 에서 넣고 B 에서 지운 PR 도 막는다 — public 이라 A 의 blob 은 SHA 로 영구 접근된다.
- **위반 시 본문을 출력하지 않는다** — 위치만 알려 CI 로그 재유출을 막는다. 오탐은 줄 끝 `leak-gate-ok` 마커로 면제.
- `secrets.yml` 과 분리한 이유: 이 게이트는 PR 전 브랜치 push 시점(= 이미 public)에도 돌아야 하는데 Actions 는 job 단위 트리거가 없어, workflow 레벨 `on:` 을 넓히면 gitleaks 까지 매 push 마다 돈다.

**3. Mergify** — auto-merge rule 2곳 모두에 `check-success = internal-identifiers` 추가. 없으면 게이트 FAIL 이어도 머지된다.

**4. `deploy.sh` fail-fast** — compose 이미지 기본값에서 레지스트리를 뺀 결과, 기본 pull 모드에서 env 미설정이면 `docker.io/library/...` 를 시도해 사내망에서 **DockerHub 타임아웃 행**이 된다(이슈 #303 증상). `docker compose pull` 직전에 `MACRO_LOGBOT_BACKEND_IMAGE` / `OPEN_WEBUI_IMAGE` 미설정을 `die` 로 잡는다. `--local` 은 대상 아님.

## ⚠️ 동작 변경 (배포자 조치 필요)

1. **레지스트리 pull 배포는 `.env` 에 `MACRO_LOGBOT_BACKEND_IMAGE` / `OPEN_WEBUI_IMAGE` 필수.** 미지정 시 `deploy.sh` 가 pull 전에 명확히 실패한다. backend 와 gc 는 동일 참조 유지(`pull_policy: never`).
2. **`scripts/build_push.sh` 의 `HARBOR_REGISTRY` 기본값 제거**, 미설정 시 `die`. 잘못된 레지스트리로 push 하는 사고보다 명확한 실패가 낫다.

## 검증 (로컬 실측)

- 게이트 3모드: 로컬(패턴 미주입) → 경고 후 구조 규칙만, exit 0 / CI+패턴 주입 → `구조 규칙 + 정확값 denylist, 매치 0건`, exit 0 / CI+미주입 → **exit 1 fail-closed**
- 양성 확인: 가짜 사설 IP + 허용목록 밖 FQDN 파일 추가 → exit 1, 위치만 출력(본문 미출력)
- `tests/shell/test_check_internal_leak.sh` → PASS=13 FAIL=0
- `tests/shell/test_build_push.sh` → PASS=9 FAIL=0 (신규 `HARBOR_REGISTRY` 케이스 포함)
- `tests/shell/test_deploy_build_order.sh` → PASS=13 FAIL=0
- `pytest` → **921 passed** (`PYTHONPATH=<worktree>/src`)
- `ruff check` + `ruff format --check`, `tools/add_doc_anchors.py --check`, `tools/check_doc_links.py` → 통과
- 추가 라인(`git diff origin/main..HEAD | grep '^+'`)에 사내 정확값 **0건**

## 남은 조치 (본 PR 범위 밖 — 이슈 #456 코멘트에 기록)

- git history 의 커밋 메시지·과거 blob, GitHub 편집 이력·제목 변경 이벤트에 원문이 남는다. 조치 선택지(개별 삭제 vs history rewrite vs private 전환)는 이슈에서 판단 대기 중.

Closes #456

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Summary

- split the fat Developer Platform client contract into capability-focused application ports for credentials, Webhooks, connectors, external links, imports, idempotency, and rate limits
- add focused InMemory and DynamoDB adapter bundles while preserving the existing single-table schema, record keys, idempotency behavior, and encryption contexts
- move pure validation, identifier/secret generation, and Webhook signing into domain modules, and move Connector DynamoDB/Secrets Manager implementations behind adapter-out boundaries
- update production/test composition so consumers receive only the ports they use, with common focused-adapter contract coverage

## Verification

- `bun run server:test` (1252 pass)
- `bun run typecheck:server`
- `bun run oxc:lint`
- `bun run dependencies:check`
- `bun run knip:check`

- pre-commit subagent review: no blocking findings

Closes #71

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## 変更の目的
`DeveloperPlatformClient` を機能別（APIキー/OAuth、Webhook購読/配信、コネクタ、外部リンク、Import、冪等性、レート制限、取引用トランザクション）に分割したアプリケーションポートへ整理し、依存注入は必要なポートのみを渡す形に変更しました。あわせて、入力検証・識別子/秘密生成・Webhook署名などの責務をドメイン/アプリ側へ寄せ、AWS SDKや実行環境依存は `adapter-out` に閉じ込めています。

## 主な影響範囲
- **依存注入/wiringの分解**
  - API ルータ/ Public API から `developerPlatform` の集約依存を撤廃し、`apiKeys / oauthCredentials / webhookSubscriptions / webhookDeliveries / connectors / externalLinks / imports / idempotency / rateLimits / transactions` へ委譲するよう置換。
  - 本番/テストの composition を「単一クライアント生成」から **DynamoDB/InMemory の capability-focused adapter bundles 合成**へ移行（`createDynamoDbDeveloperPlatformAdapters` / `createInMemoryDeveloperPlatformAdapters` など）。
- **公開サーフェスの整理**
  - `DeveloperPlatformPorts` と各 port の入出力型（credential / webhook / connector / external link / import / request-control / secret protector）を新設し、公開モジュールの再エクスポートを明示・最小化。
  - Webhook署名生成を `domain/webhook-signature` に集約（ローカル実装の置換）。
- **adapter-out の拡充（capability-focused）**
  - in-memory/dynamodb の focused adapter を追加し、契約として「各ポートが自分のメソッドのみを保持」「列挙可能なプロパティを持たない」ことを契約テストで検証。
  - Connector 関連の DynamoDB 実装を adapter-out 境界へ移動（例: コネクタOAuth状態ストア、コネクタ同期永続化、external-link/競合/監査 outbox/カーソル署名検証/CAS競合制御など）。
  - 透過ラッパ（例: `ApiKeyAdapter` / `OAuthCredentialAdapter` / `WebhookSubscriptionAdapter` / `WebhookDeliveryAdapter` / `ConnectorAdapter` / `ExternalLinkAdapter` / `IdempotencyAdapter` / `RateLimitAdapter` / `ImportAdapter`）を追加し、source port への委譲を統一。
- **実行時のセキュリティ/設定**
  - Secrets Manager 経由のコネクタ runtime secret loader を追加・テスト化（相関ID/失敗診断の境界、上流エラーのコードマッピング）。
  - 本番の KMS キーIDを起動時に必須化し、ローカル/テストでは AES fallback を維持。
  - コネクタ runtime 環境ロードは fail-closed 側へ調整（ローダ未指定時の挙動を明確化）。

## 確認したテスト・未確認事項
- **確認したテスト（追加/更新）**
  - focused adapter 契約テスト（各ポートのメソッド所有範囲/列挙可能性、`connectors` と `externalLinks` の互換性検証、connector install→external link 作成→list の整合）。
  - Secrets Manager connector runtime secret loader の失敗時挙動テスト（AWS SDK の requestId を相関IDに用い、失敗診断が期待通りであること、メッセージサニタイズ）。
  - コネクタ同期永続化/競合処理のリトライ上限・retryable 判定の検証（CAS競合注入と期待する PutCommand 回数など）。
  - Webhook署名検証の境界テスト（署名が非文字列の場合の失敗）。
  - developer-platform test の条件付き Put 失敗注入による冪等性リザベーション競合リトライ上限の検証。
- **成功報告**
  - `bun run server:test`（1,281 tests）、server type checking、lint、Knip、依存チェック、Lambda build などが通過したことが報告されています。
- **未確認事項**
  - 追加/置換のテスト以外で未確認事項の記載はありません。

body:
시연 안정성 제언 반영 — AI 변경안 중앙 비교(성능 개선 예상 카드)가 **오른쪽 위 닫기(X) 버튼으로만** 닫히게 합니다.

## 왜

지금은 배경 클릭·카드 클릭·Esc 어디서든 닫힙니다. 중앙 강조는 요청당 한 번만 열리므로, 시연 중 오클릭·키 실수 한 번이면 되돌릴 수 없이 사라집니다. 명시적 닫기 하나로 좁혀 발표 사고를 방지합니다.

author: acoliver
body:
## Summary

Harden the OCR review workflow (`.github/workflows/ocr-review.yml`) with 10 operational controls from issue #2576, referencing Luther PR 130 patterns.

## Changes

### Workflow (`.github/workflows/ocr-review.yml`)

1. **Single OCR version source (1.6.1 → 1.7.9)** — Added `OCR_VERSION: '1.7.9'` workflow-level env var; install step uses `@alibaba-group/open-code-review@${OCR_VERSION}` instead of a hardcoded version.

2. **Configurable provider concurrency** — Added `OCR_CONCURRENCY: '2'` workflow-level env var; review command gets `--concurrency "$OCR_CONCURRENCY"`.

3. **Provider failure classification** — Multi-branch classifier in the review step now distinguishes HTTP 429 (rate limit), HTTP 529 (overloaded), authentication/configuration errors, timeout, all-file failure, and generic failure — each with a distinct `mark_infrastructure_failure` reason.

4. **Fail-closed redaction** — Artifact redaction now writes a `[REDACTED-PENDING]` placeholder immediately after reading original content, before attempting the redacted write. If the final write fails, the file contains only the safe placeholder, never original bytes.

5. **Retry only idempotent operations** — Removed `retry_gh` wrapper from `gh issue create` and `gh issue comment` (non-idempotent). Only `gh issue list` (read) retains retry.

6. **Reconcile ambiguous writes** — Sticky summary posting now uses `createOrUpdateMarkerComment()` / `reconcileMarkerComment()` functions. On `createComment` failure, it re-lists comments to check if the comment was actually created before retrying, preventing duplicates from ambiguous responses.

7. **Label-verified issue creation** — `create_infrastructure_issue` captures stderr from the labeled create, checks for label-related errors (`label|labels|not found|does not exist`), and only retries without labels if the failure was specifically label-related.

8. **Tracking issue convergence** — Added `converge_duplicate_tracking_issues()` that lists open issues with the tracking title, keeps the oldest (`created-asc`), comments on it, and closes duplicates. Runs on both comment-on-existing and create paths.

9. **Candidate deduplication** — Added `deduplicationKey()` / `deduplicateFindings()` to the Post OCR results step. Exact duplicate findings (same path, start_line, end_line, body) are deduplicated before inline/lineless split.

10. **Suppression recording** — The summary comment includes `Suppressed N exact duplicate finding(s).` when duplicates were removed.

### Tests

- **`scripts/tests/ocr-review-workflow.test.js`** — Updated existing tests for the new retry/label behavior.
- **`scripts/tests/ocr-review-workflow-behaviors.test.js`** (new) — 12 dedicated contract tests for all 10 behaviors, split out to stay under the 800-line max-lines rule.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run test:scripts` — all OCR workflow tests pass (44 total)
- [x] `npx eslint` — no errors in changed files
- [x] `npx prettier --check` — all files formatted
- [x] YAML parsed and validated with js-yaml
- [x] OCR local review completed (3 findings addressed: beforeAll error handling added; contract test pattern dismissed as established convention)

## Closes

Closes #2576

  - Improves diagnostic redaction with a **[REDACTED-PENDING]** placeholder.

author: kerianlaurier
body:
Résorbe les vulnérabilités de dépendances signalées en revue QA pré-livraison (P2). **Départ : 14 vulnérabilités (6 hautes).**

## Cause racine
`shadcn@^4.8.1` était en **`dependencies` (production)** alors que c'est un **outil CLI** utilisé uniquement à la compilation, via `@import "shadcn/tailwind.css"` dans `globals.css` (aucun import runtime). Il tirait `hono` en production — à lui seul 6 advisories **hautes** (adaptateurs AWS Lambda, serve-static, XSS JSX…) via `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`.

## Changements
- **`shadcn` → `devDependencies`.** Le sort du tree de production (avec `hono` et une chaîne `js-yaml`). L'import CSS de build continue de résoudre (les devDeps sont présentes à la compilation).
- **`overrides` `postcss ^8.5.10` et `sharp ^0.35.3`.** Force les versions patchées des copies **imbriquées dans Next** ; l'`audit fix --force` proposé aurait rétrogradé **Next 16 → 9** (inacceptable). Build vérifié : aucun impact, CSS intacte.
- **`npm audit fix`** (non forcé) : bumps transitifs patchés (`brace-expansion`, `fast-uri`, `@opentelemetry/*`) hérités de Sentry/glob.

## Résultat
| Périmètre | Avant | Après |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Production** (`npm audit --omit=dev`) | plusieurs | **0 vulnérabilité** |
| Tree complet (`npm audit`) | 14 (6 hautes) | **3 modérées** |

Les 3 restantes sont **dev-only**, dans le CLI `shadcn` (→ `@hono/node-server`) : jamais déployé ni exécuté en production. Les neutraliser exigerait un `override` sur `hono` au risque de casser le CLI — non fait, sans bénéfice pour la sécurité du produit livré.

## Vérification
`tsc` · ESLint · **126 tests** · **build des 34 routes** · rendu de la landing (styles intacts malgré l'override postcss).

author: freebuff-web[bot]
body:
## What

Three small frontend-only affordances, no backend changes:

- **Reset Pet** (`game.resetPet()`): `confirm()` prompt, then `clearInterval`,
  posts a fresh pet via the existing `POST /api/pet/create`, restart the polling
  loop, refresh UI. No doubling of `setInterval` handles.
- **Export Sketch as PNG** (`game.exportSketch()`): pure client-side.
  Uses `canvas.toBlob(blob => URL.createObjectURL(blob), "image/png")` plus
  a temporary `<a download>` to trigger a download with filename
  `sketch-<isostamp>.png`.
- **History limit indicator**: `DrawingEditor.historyLimit = 20`,
  `saveHistory()` drops the oldest entry on overflow, new `#historyIndicator`
  span shows current step/total (`↶ N/M ↷`) and is refreshed from
  `saveHistory` / `undo` / `redo` / `clear`. (`clear()` already routes through
  `saveHistory()`, so it picks up indicator logic automatically.)

## Why

User asked to "tweak the UI" with these three affordances and open a PR
so the next iteration can be reviewed.

## Mirroring note

The literal request was to modify `frontend/templates/index.html`. That
file is a near-duplicate of `frontend/index.html` (which is what Flask
currently serves from `/` via
`send_from_directory("../frontend", "index.html")`). Without mirroring,

author: ben-dev-au
body:
## Summary

Makes fnd run on **Linux and Windows** alongside macOS, behind a small, tested
platform-abstraction layer. Core search, indexing, the TUI, syntax-highlighted
preview, in-file navigation, and the "Open with…" launcher work on all three
OSes; a handful of macOS-only integrations degrade gracefully elsewhere.

Previously fnd hard-exited on any non-Darwin platform and assumed macOS paths,
`open`-based launching, and POSIX-only behaviour throughout.

> Draft: opened to run the cross-platform CI matrix (the real Windows gate) and
> for review. Not for merge until the matrix is green and a real-machine
> Linux/Windows smoke test is done.

## Architecture

Three cohesive seams, each following a pattern already in the codebase, so
OS-specific behaviour is branched **once** and callers query capabilities:

- **`fnd/paths.py`** (new) — one source of truth for every per-user directory,
  resolving the data and cache roots with a consistent `appauthor=False`. Fixes
  a Windows split-brain where the config root and eight other call sites resolved
  to two different roots.
- **`fnd/launcher.py`** (new) — a `Launcher` strategy (`Mac`/`Linux`/`Windows`
  + a cached `get_launcher()` factory) for open-in-app / open-URL / reveal, with
  injectable runners so every branch is unit-testable without spawning. The two
  prior `reveal` implementations are consolidated onto it.
- **`fnd/apps.py`** (extended) — the app registry gains page-jump-capable PDF
  viewers that self-gate via `available()`: Zathura/Okular (Linux), SumatraPDF
  (Windows), plus cross-platform Obsidian detection and best-effort per-OS
  page-jump promotion. AppleScript/Accessibility paths are gated to macOS.

## Genuine cross-platform bug fixes

- `walk.py` matched include/exclude globs against `str(Path)` (backslashes on
  Windows) so they never matched — now uses the POSIX form.
- The extractor pool's `os.kill(pid, SIGKILL)` silently no-op'd on Windows →
  `multiprocessing.Process.kill()`.
- The docling daemon used `select()` on a pipe (sockets-only on Windows) → a
  bounded background-thread read; uv's tool root now resolves via `uv tool dir`
  with the correct per-OS venv layout.
- Best-effort created-date off macOS (Windows `st_ctime`, statx Linux
  `st_birthtime`); Windows junk-dir presets; UTF-8 on sidecar/sentinel writes;
  POSIX-only permission hardening documented.

## Packaging, CI, docs

- Broadened OS classifiers and the package description.
- The pytest job now runs a **macOS · Linux · Windows** matrix (`fail-fast: false`).
- README rewritten with a per-OS capability table and terminal notes;
  `docs/apps.md` gains a per-OS "Open with…" catalogue.

## Testing

- **macOS:** full suite green (2101 passed).
- **Linux:** verified in a native-`aarch64` container — functional smoke
  (index → search returned correct BM25 results, config path resolved to
  `~/.local/share/fnd`) plus the full suite green. The one failure was a
  pre-existing, unrelated preview-scroll load flake (passes 5/5 in isolation).
- **Windows:** not verified locally — this PR's CI matrix is the gate. Every
  OS-specific branch is covered by platform-injected unit tests.

## Notes

- No dependency changes; `uv.lock` is unchanged — every core wheel already ships
  Linux and Windows builds. Only `pyproject.toml` metadata changed.
- The actual desktop open/reveal **round-trip** (a real viewer launching) on
  Linux/Windows is verified at the command-construction level; a real GUI smoke
  test is a sensible follow-up.

author: dibranmulder
body:
Makes the QERDS AS4 bench exercise a real Domibus access point end to end, instead of only the in-process stub.

## Changes

**Compose bench**
- Pass `QERDS_*` through to the backend, and gate the backend on a Domibus WSDL healthcheck via an optional (`required: false`) dependency — a plain `docker compose up` still works, but with the `domibus` profile the backend no longer loses the boot race against Tomcat.
- Add a one-shot `domibus-provision` service that uploads the blue→red PMode once the WS plugin is healthy (a fresh Domibus answers `EBMS:0010` until a PMode exists).
- Disable cert validation via `JAVA_OPTS` (the bundled 2017 sample certs are expired). This is enough for `submitMessage` to be accepted and logged — what the app and the test rely on. A terminal `SENT` on the self-loopback would additionally need regenerated keystore certs (message is signed by the expired sender cert), which this bench does not do.

**Tests**
- New tag-gated live integration test (`domibus_integration_test.go`, gated on `QERDS_TEST_DOMIBUS_URL`) that uploads the PMode, pings, sends, and asserts Domibus returns a provider ref — the real round-trip the offline marshalling tests cannot cover. Those unit tests stay.
- The committed `testdata/pmode.xml` is shared by both the provision service and the test.

**CI**
- The `backend-integration-test` job now runs Domibus + MySQL service containers so the live test executes on every push.

## Notes
- The stub source and the `stub` config default are unchanged; switching to Domibus is opt-in via env.
- No SENT on the loopback yet — see the cert caveat above.

## Summary
- "전체 보기" and "학생 활동지 보기" both export documents via the classic technique of downloading an HTML string as a `.doc` file (`Blob` with `application/msword` MIME type and a `.doc` filename) — this relies on Word sniffing the content and opening it as HTML.
- The exported HTML was missing the Office-specific namespace declarations and `mso` conditional-comment block that real Word HTML exports always include. Without them, newer Word builds treat the extension/content mismatch as a hard error ("파일을 읽는 동안 오류가 발생했습니다") instead of opening the file.

## Changes
- Added a `toWordDoc()` helper in `public/app.js` that injects the standard `xmlns:o`/`xmlns:w` namespace attributes on `<html>` plus the `ProgId`/`Generator`/`Originator` meta tags and `w:WordDocument` block Word looks for to recognize the file as a Word-compatible HTML document.
- Applied it to both export paths: `saveAsWord()` (전체 보기 → Word 저장) and `saveWorksheetAsWord()` (학생 활동지 보기 → Word 저장). The PDF/print paths are untouched since they don't go through Word.
