author: eldara-cruncher
body:
Closes #13.

The pull loop. Fetch → render → plan → apply, per application, on its own timer in its own goroutine.

```go
func New(apps []application.Spec, o Options) *Reconciler
func (r *Reconciler) Run(ctx context.Context) error         // until cancelled
func (r *Reconciler) Sync(ctx context.Context, app string) error     // applies if the policy is automated
func (r *Reconciler) SyncNow(ctx context.Context, app string) error  // always applies
func (r *Reconciler) View(app string) (application.View, bool)
func (r *Reconciler) Views() []application.View
func (r *Reconciler) Diffs(app string) ([]application.ReleaseDiff, error)
```

Wired against CE's backend through the `swarms` seam, per the sequencing you chose: everything downstream is testable now, and #10–#12 swap in behind `charts.NewEngineWith` without touching this package.

## Decisions worth challenging

**A successful apply is followed by a fresh plan.** It costs a second render. It buys the difference between *reporting that a sync was attempted* and *observing that it landed* — and it catches a chart whose render is not deterministic, one that would otherwise sit permanently OutOfSync and redeploy on every single tick, on the first sync rather than never. `TestApplyThatDoesNotConvergeStaysOutOfSync` pins it.

**A failed fetch keeps the last known status.** An unreachable repository does not make the swarm's state *unknown*; it makes it *unverified*. The last observed sync state stands and `status.error` says why it could not be rechecked. The alternative — resetting to unknown — throws away true information because a network blipped.

**Drift is announced on the transition only.** A manual-policy application sits OutOfSync indefinitely by design; notifying every three minutes would train an operator to ignore the one that matters.

**Default interval is 3 minutes**, matching ArgoCD. Every tick costs a git fetch, a full render of every release, and a read of the swarm's release records. Per-application override via `syncPolicy.interval`.

**Backoff doubles per consecutive failure, capped at 30 minutes** — long enough to stop hammering a dead remote, short enough that fixing the cause does not need a restart to be noticed. The shift is capped so a long interval cannot overflow into a negative duration.

**`Sync` vs `SyncNow`.** A manual policy means "do not deploy on a schedule", not "never deploy". The API's sync action needs the second one.

**Releases are stamped `cd/<application>`.** The command line stamps `apply/<owner>`, so a release file applied by hand and an application reconciled here can never claim each other's releases — which is exactly what that prefix exists for.

**Destinations are resolved once at startup and a failure is fatal.** #22 deliberately leaves them alone because only the swarm registry knows what it can reach, so this is where a typo in a swarm name becomes a startup error rather than a per-application failure discovered three minutes later.

**Diffs come from the stored last plan**, not a fresh render. The diff endpoint then reports what the status reports; re-rendering on an HTTP request could disagree with the status shown beside it.

## A bug the tests caught

The first implementation read the previous sync state *after* recording the new one, so the two were always equal and drift was never announced — not once, ever. It looked entirely correct in review.

## Left unfinished on purpose

`Health` is `unknown` rather than optimistically healthy. The rollup is #15, and it waits on Eldara-Tech/swarmcli#500 so the convergence rules are not duplicated here. `ReleaseStatus.Revision` is zero for the same reason — chart revision numbers live in the release records, which the health rollup reads.

## Verification

`gofmt`, `go vet`, `go test -race`, `golangci-lint run` and `scripts/check-spdx.sh` all clean. **98.8% statement coverage**, race-clean. The engine, fetcher, builder and swarm registry are all interfaces here, so the whole loop is driven by fakes with no daemon and no network — including the scheduler, cancellation, and one application failing while another keeps reconciling.

Still nothing in `cmd/controller` imports this, so the shipped binary is unchanged.

author: enricolorenzoni59
body:
## Summary

Update `dvb-t/it-All` to match the Italian terrestrial television spectrum plan currently published by AGCOM.

The existing table was compiled in 2010 as a generic Western European raster and still included:

- VHF-III channels 5-12 (177.5-226.5 MHz)
- UHF channels 49-69 (698-858 MHz)

The current Italian PNAF-DTT uses 470-694 MHz for terrestrial television. On an 8 MHz channel raster this corresponds to channels 21-48, with center frequencies from 474 to 690 MHz. AGCOM states that VHF-III (174-230 MHz) is planned and used exclusively for DAB+.

## Changes

- keep UHF channels 21-48 only
- remove VHF-III channels 5-12
- remove UHF channels 49-69, released by the 700 MHz refarming
- replace the obsolete Wikipedia references with current official AGCOM sources
- document the national-authority source policy in the repository README

The existing generic DVB-T tuning parameters for the retained channels are unchanged. This PR updates the frequency raster; it does not attempt to model individual regional mux assignments or the progressive DVB-T2 transition.

## Official references

- [AGCOM: Radiodiffusione televisiva digitale terrestre](https://www.agcom.it/competenze/comunicazioni-elettroniche/reti/frequenze/frequenze-radio-e-TV/radiodiffusione-televisiva-digitale-terrestre) — states that television currently uses 470-694 MHz and that 174-230 MHz is planned and used exclusively for DAB+.
- [AGCOM Resolution 145/25/CONS](https://www.agcom.it/provvedimenti/delibera-145-25-cons) — removes national television network no. 12 from the PNAF-DTT, reduces the plan to 11 national UHF networks, suppresses television protection constraints in 174-230 MHz, and repurposes the VHF resources for DAB+.
- [AGCOM Resolution 93/26/CONS](https://www.agcom.it/provvedimenti/delibera-93-26-cons) — addresses the UHF resources from the former national network no. 12 and confirms its status as a previous/ex television network.

## Validation

The resulting table was checked programmatically:

```text
channels=28 min=474000000 max=690000000 invalid=0 raster_errors=0
```

This verifies that all 28 retained center frequencies are on the expected 8 MHz raster and fit wholly within the 470-694 MHz television allocation.

author: copilot
body:
Adds image/video panning when zoomed in, via mouse drag and keyboard shortcuts.

## Changes

- **`pan(dx, dy)`** — shifts `image_center` by the given pixel delta; no-ops when the image fits within the viewport (nothing to scroll)
- **Mouse drag** — `<ButtonPress-1>` / `<B1-Motion>` on the canvas; each motion event computes an incremental delta so the image tracks the cursor smoothly
- **Keyboard** — `<Alt-Left/Right/Up/Down>` pan by `PAN_STEP = 50` px per press
- **`_drag_start`** state variable tracks the previous drag position for incremental deltas

Pan is intentionally suppressed when `current_scale <= fit_scale`, keeping fit/fill modes unaffected.

`test_wrappers_table_matches_what_the_tools_declare` compares footman's
hand-written `_WRAPPERS` table against wrappers extracted from whatever tools
are installed on the machine. On CI runners those tool versions differ from the
ones the table was curated against — docker in particular is present but not
always introspectable (`docker --help` yields nothing usable when the daemon or
Windows-container state is off), so extraction returns empty and the assertion
fails. It flaked `py3.13 · windows-latest` on the v0.17.0 release PR (#14).

Tool-wrapper accuracy can only be validated in CI once CI generates the tables
too (post-1.0). Until then, gate the test on the standard `CI` env var: it still
runs in the local `fm check` gate (real, curated tools, so drift is caught
before commit) and is skipped in CI.

/ `installed` / `DRIVERS` / `.wrappers()` independently, so local coverage stays

제출은 스토어의 목 액션으로 처리하고, `// TODO: shared/api/http.ts 경유 실API로 교체` 주석을 남겼다.
컴포넌트에서 `fetch`·`axios`를 직접 호출하지 않는다.
개설 후 라우팅은 즉시 시작이면 `/rooms/:id/live`, 예약이면 `/rooms/:id/waiting`이다.

유효성 검사는 제출 버튼 활성/비활성 + 필드별 한국어 에러 메시지로 보여준다.
단계 진입 직후에는 에러를 띄우지 않고, "다음"·"제출"을 누른 뒤부터 표시한다.

## 스키마 제약 반영 내역 (docs/04 §3.4)

| 제약 | 반영 |
| --- | --- |
| `start_type IN ('IMMEDIATE','SCHEDULED')` + `ck_auction_room_schedule` | 시작 방식 2지선다. `SCHEDULED`면 날짜·시각 입력이 필수 검증이고, `IMMEDIATE`로 되돌리면 시각 필드를 비워 `scheduled_at: null`로 보낸다 |
| `reserve_price > 0` | 0 이하·비정수·미입력 차단 |
| `duration_minutes > 0` | 프리셋(10/15/30) + 직접 입력, 0 이하 차단 |
| `product.description NOT NULL` | 필수 입력. 공백만 입력하는 것도 차단(trim) |
| `product.title VARCHAR(100)` | `maxlength` + 100자 초과 검증 + 글자 수 카운터 |
| `product.condition_status` nullable + `IN ('NEW','LIKE_NEW','USED','DAMAGED')` | 4지선다 + "선택 안 함". 필수로 만들지 않았다 |
| `uq_product_single_thumbnail` | 대표 이미지는 **라디오** 1장. 체크박스 아님 |
| `product_image`: `sort_order > 0`, `UNIQUE(product_id, sort_order)` | 추가·삭제·순서 이동 시 1부터 연속으로 재계산 |
| `product_category.code` UNIQUE | 표시는 `name`, 전송은 `code` |
| `moderation_status` | 폼에 노출하지 않고 "등록 후 검수" 안내 문구로만 |
| `extension_count BETWEEN 0 AND 3` | 진행 시간 카드의 연장 안내 문구를 "최대 3회"로 |

## 대체한 토큰 목록

`src/app/styles/main.css`는 수정하지 않았다(병렬 작업 충돌 방지). 디자인 소스의 하드코딩 색은 가장 가까운 기존 토큰으로 대체했다.

| 디자인 소스 값 | 용도 | 대체 토큰 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `#818181`, `#626262` | 보조 설명 텍스트 | `text-dim` |
| `#919191`, `#B0B0B0` | 비활성 라벨·플레이스홀더 | `text-faint` |
| `#CCCCCC` | 업로드 영역 점선 테두리 | `border-line` |
| `#D6D6D6` | 스텝 연결선 | `bg-line` |
| `#E6E6E6` | 비활성 스텝 원형 배경 | `bg-line` |
| `#F7D4D4` | AI 카드 테두리 | `border-line` |
| `#A30000` | AI 카드 본문 텍스트 | `text-dim` |
| `#3B4A5E` | 예약 안내 박스 텍스트 | `text-slate` |
| `#fff` (카드 배경) | 폼 카드 배경 | `bg-white` (기존 화면과 동일한 관행) |

## 디자인 대비 타협

- **AI 자동완성·AI 시세 카드**: 연동 대상 API가 없어 자리만 잡은 안내 카드로 두었다. "추천가 적용" 버튼과 예상 낙찰가 수치는 가짜 값이 될 수 있어 넣지 않았다.
- **상품 사진**: 외부 이미지 URL(picsum 등)을 쓰지 않고 로컬 파일 선택 + `URL.createObjectURL` 미리보기로 처리했다. 업로드 엔드포인트 전환 TODO를 남겼다.
- **드래그 재정렬** 대신 ↑/↓ 버튼으로 순서를 바꾼다(`sort_order` 재계산 규칙은 동일).
- **진행 시간**: 디자인은 프리셋 3개뿐이지만 `duration_minutes > 0`만이 제약이므로 직접 입력 필드를 함께 두었다.
- 2단 그리드는 `lg` 이상에서만 적용하고 좁은 화면에서는 1단으로 쌓는다.

## 확인이 필요한 사항

- `product.category_id`의 NULL 허용 여부가 스키마 메모에 없어 카테고리를 **필수**로 두었다. 서버가 선택 항목으로 받는다면 완화가 필요하다.
- 방 개설이 단일 요청인지 단계별인지 미확정(docs/04 §6.4)이라, 페이로드를 `{ product, room }` 한 덩어리로 정의했다.
- 목 액션은 `scheduled_at`을 ISO 문자열로 보낸다. 서버가 epoch ms를 기대하면 변환 지점이 바뀐다(docs/04 §6.3).

## 검증

- `npm run format` → `npx prettier --check .` 통과
- `npm run lint` (경고 0) 통과
- `npm run build` (vue-tsc 포함) 통과

author: napetrov
body:
## Summary

Five independently-scoped P0 fixes from a toolchain/provenance/evidence audit against a much larger (30-section) target spec. The full spec describes a multi-week program (compiler/dialect matrix engine, trust-boundary security layer, AST↔DWARF coherence subsystem, 13 new example fixtures); this PR ships only the items that are well-scoped, honestly completable, and backed by real passing tests — everything else is called out explicitly as **not** done, in the "Out of scope" section below.

## Motivation

An audit (5 parallel research agents against the real `main`) found concrete active bugs and gaps:
- A naive regex made C++20 dialect auto-detection fire on `#error Foo requires Base` (and on the same text in a string literal), silently forcing the wrong `-std=` onto both snapshot sides.
- Hidden-friend findings were unconditionally kept in the public surface regardless of whether the befriending class lived in a system/private header.
- No runtime floor existed on the CastXML version at all — the legacy PyPI `castxml` distribution could silently produce an "authoritative" L2 scan.
- `semver.recommend_release()` gave a confident SONAME-bump recommendation purely from `Verdict`/`ChangeKind`, even for a comparison that never examined a real binary.
- `action/run.sh` forwarded the full L2 compile-context (`--gcc-path`/`--sysroot`/etc.) to `dump` only, behind a comment that incorrectly claimed those flags weren't exposed on `compare`'s CLI — they are (`compile_context_options`, ADR-037 D3, shared by `dump`/`compare`/`scan`).

## Changes

- **C++20 detector** (`dumper_ast_config.py`): directive/string/comment-aware rewrite (`_find_cpp20_requirements`) replaces the naive per-line regex; also fixes a latent false-negative (`concept` not at line-start).
- **Hidden-friend surface** (`surface.py`): new `Function.hidden_friend_owner` (schema **v12**), resolved from castxml's `befriending` attribute and clang's friend-scope walk; `_classify_hidden_friend_surface` checks the owner's header origin before applying the not-exported exemption.
- **CastXML version gate** (new `castxml_policy.py`): enforces `>=0.7.0,<0.8.0` (verified against the current conda-forge feedstock) before any header is parsed; raises `UnsupportedCastxmlVersionError` unless `ABICHECK_ALLOW_UNSUPPORTED_CASTXML=1`. New `AbiSnapshot.ast_toolchain_supported`/`ast_toolchain_unsupported_reasons` (schema **v13**).
- **SONAME/release-recommendation gating** (`semver.py`): new `SonameAction.NOT_DETERMINED` + `ReleaseRecommendationState` (`actionable`/`review`/`unavailable`). A `BREAKING` verdict with zero binary-level evidence (`DiffResult.evidence_tiers == ["header"]`) is now `unavailable`/`not_determined` instead of a confident bump; `API_BREAK` is now explicitly `review`. A `DiffResult` that never populates `evidence_tiers` (nearly every hand-built test fixture) is treated as "unknown" and keeps prior behavior — verified by a dedicated regression.
- **Action parity** (`action/run.sh`, `action.yml`, docs): `compare` and `scan` now forward the same 6 compile-context flags `dump` always had; stale "(dump mode only)" doc claims corrected.
- **Housekeeping**: `dumper.py` and `diff_symbols.py` were sitting exactly at the AI-readiness 2000-line hard cap; extracted castxml-diagnostics and hidden-friend-diff code into new sibling modules (`dumper_castxml_probe.py`, `diff_hidden_friends.py`) rather than growing them further.

Schema version bumped **11 → 13** (v12: `hidden_friend_owner`; v13: `ast_toolchain_supported`/`ast_toolchain_unsupported_reasons`), both purely additive. 11 committed G20 snapshot fixtures regenerated (`scripts/gen_g20_fixtures.py`) for the schema bump only — no fixture content changed beyond the version/new key.

## Out of scope (explicitly not attempted this pass)

- Full toolchain-profile/compiler-matrix contract (`profiles:` compiler/dialect/flags axes, trusted bindings, run-plan/matrix execution engine — confirmed unbuilt, "G30 P1.4").
- Trust-boundary security gating for compiler paths in auto-discovered config (only `build.query` has this today).
- AST↔DWARF coherence-checking engine and the full 8-status evidence-provider model (§15/§18 of the source spec) — no such comparison exists anywhere in the codebase; not something to patch in.
- 13 new example cases (`case196`–`case208`) + PVXS end-to-end acceptance fixture — needs a real gcc+castxml sandbox to validate (`integration` marker), not available here.
- Conda feedstock / `action/install-castxml.sh` pin bump to a verified ≥0.7.0 build — the *policy* is enforced, but I did not fabricate a new pinned tarball URL/SHA256 without being able to actually download-and-verify it. **This is a live gap**: the Action's current pinned CastXML (`0.6.20260105-g9864b1e`) is now below the new policy floor and needs a maintainer to re-pin it.
- Reachability-role taxonomy for stdlib types, provenance fingerprints, redaction of persisted compiler argv.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/ -m "not integration and not libabigail and not abicc and not slow and not golden"` — **17827 passed, 27 skipped, 4 xfailed, 0 failed**
- [x] `mypy abicheck/` — clean (260 source files)
- [x] `ruff check abicheck/ tests/` — all checks passed
- [x] `ruff format --check` on every individually-touched file — clean
- [x] `python scripts/check_ai_readiness.py` — 0 errors, 52 warnings (pre-existing baseline, no new warnings)
- [x] `python scripts/gen_g20_fixtures.py --check` — clean
- [x] `python scripts/publish_schemas.py --check` — clean
- [x] `bash -n action/run.sh` — syntax OK
- [ ] `integration`/`libabigail`/`abicc` marker lanes — **not run** (no castxml/gcc/clang toolchain in this sandbox); the new gate/detector code is exercised entirely through mocked-subprocess unit tests, not against a real castxml binary. macOS/Windows-specific paths (Apple Clang, MSVC/PDB) were not exercised.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests added / updated for new behaviour (see PR diff: `test_dumper_ast_config_cpp20.py`, `test_castxml_policy.py`, `test_castxml_version_gate.py`, `test_action_compile_context_parity.py`, plus extensions to `test_surface.py`, `test_dumper_clang.py`, `test_serialization_roundtrip.py`, `test_semver_recommendation.py`, `test_schema_compat.py`)
- [x] Changelog fragment added (`changelog.d/20260722_120000_claude_toolchain_audit_p0_a1b2c3.md`)
- [x] Docs updated (`docs/reference/snapshot-format.md`, `docs/reference/environment.md`, `docs/troubleshooting.md`, `docs/user-guide/github-action.md`)
- [x] mypy/ruff clean

body:
Subticket D of TM-923. Proves that a phone **linked** to an account (TM-930) is a valid SMS sign-in method for the **same** account. Firebase-native mechanism — **expected server-side change: none**. Web/e2e only; backend read-only.

## STEP 1 — verify-first gate (PASS)
`web/e2e/verify-tm933-uid-equality.mjs` against the Auth emulator: create an email account, link a distinct unowned phone to its uid via the admin `accounts:update` REST (the deterministic stand-in for TM-930's `linkWithCredential`), then run the app's SMS flow (`startPhoneSignIn` -> `confirm`). Result: the SMS-sign-in uid **equals** the email account's uid, `isNewUser=false`. The ticket premise holds.

```
email-account uid : ifdQ1iQ4MKRzBqvHp126rdkSpuhS
sms-signin  uid   : ifdQ1iQ4MKRzBqvHp126rdkSpuhS
isNewUser         : false
UIDS EQUAL        : true
```

## New spec — `web/e2e/tests/sms-signin-linked.spec.mjs` (3 tests, 3/3 local green)
Auth-emulator harness, modelled on `tm867-otp-6box`'s SMS path (emulator `verificationCodes` fetch, six-box auto-submit, tour suppression).

1. **Linked-phone SMS sign-in = same account** — `GET /me` email + uid match the original account, `me.phone` == the linked number, `accountState.phoneVerified` true, and no `#/onboarding` gate.
2. **TM-720 reset** — sign-out from the SMS session restores the email step (`#sms-step-phone` visible, `#sms-step-code` hidden, OTP boxes empty); email-code sign-in then reaches the same account.
3. **Current-state pin** (tripwire, not a blocker) — an **unowned** number creates a fresh phone-only session routed to `#/onboarding`. Commented in-spec that B/C will flip this expectation.

## Login copy
One line of helper copy on the SMS step (`#sms-signin-hint`, `.auth-hint`): _"Sign in with the mobile number on your account."_ (post-A framing). No `login.js` `els`-map id renamed (the hint is a brand-new element); the "Try another way" disclosure placement is unchanged. Before/after 390px screenshots under `docs/qa/evidence/TM-933/`.

## Must-not-break (verified green locally)
`tm867-otp-6box.spec.mjs` (new-number SMS path) + `signout-state-leak.spec.mjs` pass. Maestro `android/maestro/login-sms.yaml` is **unaffected** — it matches "Try another way" / "Text me a code" / `#sms-disclosure`, none of which this copy change touches (the hint is a new node), so no flow edit needed.

## Drift (code over contract)
The ticket says assert `UserResponse.phoneNumber`; the self endpoint `GET /api/v1/me` returns `MeResponse` (not the admin `UserResponse`), whose fields are `phone` (the PATCHed E.164 = the linked number) + `accountState.phoneVerified` (live Firebase). The spec asserts those — same claim ("this account owns the linked number"), read from the fields `/me` actually returns.

## Fail-before / pass-after
The spec + its same-identity assertion are net-new: the file does not exist on `origin/main` (Playwright finds no such test there — inapplicable pre-branch). Pass-after = 3/3 green on this branch. The standalone verify script is the direct mechanism proof and exits non-zero if the uids ever diverge.

Tests run locally on Node 20 against the live Auth emulator + backend + Postgres.

author: mpcosmin-mcp
body:
## Feedback adresat

> „la graphic, în partea de jos, nu mai merge selectorul, și e by default selectat pe 30 de zile, dar apar doar 7"

## Cauza reală

Selectorul (7 / 30 / tot) **nu era stricat** — problema era la citirea datelor, nu la chart.

După migrarea pe Neon, `/api/sheets` cădea înapoi pe Google Sheet **doar cât timp Neon era gol**. Din momentul în care a apărut primul rând în Neon (un log manual sau o migrare parțială), Sheet-ul — care ține lunile de istoric **și** sincronizarea automată Garmin — a devenit invizibil. Toate intervalele filtrau apoi aceleași ~7 zile din Neon, așa că 7/30/tot arătau identic și selectorul părea mort.

## Fixul

Servim **reuniunea** celor două surse printr-un `getMergedEntries()` nou:

- **Neon câștigă** la coliziune pe `(date, name)` (acolo se duc editările).
- Orice rând din Sheet care lipsește din Neon e **backfill-uit după răspuns** (`after()` din `next/server`) — store-ul converge singur spre complet, fără să mai fie nevoie să rulezi manual `/api/migrate`.
- Odată ce un read dovedește că Sheet-ul nu mai are nimic în plus, citirea din Sheet e sărită pentru restul lambda-ului (read-urile în regim normal rămân rapide, Neon-only).
- `/api/garmin/sync` scrie nopțile noi direct în Neon când e legat (Sheet doar în dev local) și deduplică față de vederea unificată.

Zero risc de regresie dacă migrarea rulase deja complet: Sheet-ul se „golește" logic la primul read și e ignorat după.

## Verificare

Testat local cu un mock de Sheet (40 de zile × 3 persoane) și browser headless pe chart-ul din pagină:

| Interval | Puncte în chart | Buton activ |
|----------|-----------------|-------------|
| 7 zile   | 8               | ✅ 7 zile   |
| 30 zile (default) | 31     | ✅ 30 zile  |
| tot      | 40              | ✅ tot      |

`npm run build` trece, zero erori runtime în consolă. Înainte de fix, toate cele trei arătau aceleași ~7 puncte.

## Fișiere

- `src/lib/entries-store.ts` (nou) — read unificat Neon ∪ Sheet + backfill.
- `src/app/api/sheets/route.ts` — GET folosește `getMergedEntries()`.
- `src/app/api/garmin/sync/route.ts` — scrie în Neon, deduplică pe vederea unificată.

> ⚠️ Draft — nu e pe `main` încă. Deschide preview-ul din branch și confirmă, apoi îl facem merge. Nu atinge producția până nu dai OK.

author: qazuor
body:
Closes HOS-232

## Problem

A soft-cancelled subscription (`cancelAtPeriodEnd = true`, still inside its access window) had **no way to undo the cancellation**. The web `SubscriptionDashboard` only surfaced a resume action for `paused` subscriptions, never for the `cancelAtPeriodEnd` state, and no `uncancel` capability existed in the API/service/billing layers. The only workaround — re-subscribe — creates a **second live MercadoPago preapproval** while the original is still live → **double-charge risk** at period end (US-7.3's own unguarded acceptance criterion).

Found during SMOKE-19-07 prod smoke (E7 / US-7.4 / US-7.3).

## Fix

An idempotent **un-cancel** action that, while `cancelAtPeriodEnd = true` and the period has not yet finalized, clears the flag on the **existing** live preapproval — no new checkout, no charge.

- **qzpay-core `>= 1.17.0`** (published from qzpay PR #61/#62): new `subscriptions.uncancel()` primitive re-authorizes the paused MP preapproval (`PUT status: authorized`) and clears qzpay's own `canceledAt`, WITHOUT changing `status` (a `trialing` sub stays `trialing`). Mirrors `cancel(cancelAtPeriodEnd)`. Pinned across the workspace via `pnpm-workspace.yaml` overrides (`@qazuor/qzpay-core@1.17.0`, `@qazuor/qzpay-mercadopago@2.8.0`) to collapse version fragmentation.
- **API service** `subscription-uncancel.service.ts`: clears the local `cancelAtPeriodEnd` flag FIRST inside a `FOR UPDATE` transaction (writes a `USER_UNCANCELED` audit event), THEN re-authorizes the provider; a provider failure ROLLS the flag back so we never report "kept" while MP is still paused. `canceledAt` is left to qzpay-core.
- **Route** `POST /api/v1/protected/subscriptions/:id/uncancel`, gated by `HOSPEDA_USER_CANCEL_ENABLED`; added `uncancel` to the billing-admin-guard allowlist.
- **Web**: "Descartar cancelación" button in the cancelled-but-in-grace state (mirrors paused→resume), with i18n (es/en/pt).
- **Guard**: the `start-paid` soft-cancel guard message now points users to un-cancel instead of re-subscribing, closing the duplicate-preapproval hole.

## TOCTOU / money-safety (the hard part)

The `finalize-cancelled-subs` cron scans `WHERE cancelAtPeriodEnd = true` and flips due soft-cancels to `cancelled` (and, since HOS-237, hard-cancels the MP preapproval). Un-cancel races this cron. Both sides now serialize on the row lock under a `FOR UPDATE` re-read:

- **Un-cancel wins**: cron's in-tx re-read sees `cancelAtPeriodEnd = false` → new `skipped` outcome (no status flip, no addon revoke, no audit, no cache clear, no reconcile, no featured revoke, no hard-cancel).
- **Cron wins**: un-cancel's in-tx re-read sees a terminal `status` → aborts with `VALIDATION_ERROR` **before** the provider call, so a hard-cancelled preapproval is never re-authorized.

Zombie state (MP charging + status `cancelled` + zero entitlements) is unreachable in both directions.

## Tests

- `subscription-uncancel.service.test.ts` — 7 tests incl. the divergent-read TOCTOU abort (Step-1 eligible, in-tx `FOR UPDATE` re-read sees `cancelled` → throws, provider never called).
- `finalize-cancelled-subs.test.ts` — `skipped` regression (row un-cancelled mid-batch → no side-effects, `skipped 1` in message).
- `billing-admin-guard.middleware.test.ts` — `uncancel` sub-path allowed.
- Full trio green (87), api typecheck clean, `@repo/billing` rebuild clean (stub adapter `uncancel` no-op added).

## Review

3 rounds of judgment-day (dual blind adversarial). Round 3: both judges confirm both race directions closed; the final blocker (missing divergent-read regression test) is now covered.

## Smoke gate — billing CORE

`status-needs-smoke-staging` + `status-needs-smoke-prod` retained. The MercadoPago preapproval re-authorization MUST be verified by the owner against the real MP sandbox/prod before this is considered done. **Do not close HOS-232 on merge** — the smoke-gate Action bounces it to In Review while the labels are present.

author: xyaohubery
body:
## Summary

Diagnostic tool for detecting and localizing non-determinism in NCCL collective operations, addressing [Issue #4](https://github.com/Tencent/hpn/issues/4).

## Problem

Two identical training runs can diverge bitwise due to floating-point non-associativity in collective reductions (ring vs tree vs PAT algorithms, topology changes). This tool pinpoints the exact call and algorithm that introduces divergence.

## What's Included

- **`bitwise_determinism_checker.py`**: Core engine with simulated Ring/Tree/PAT/NVLS algorithms, bitwise comparison framework, algorithm sweep, and actionable recommendations
- **`nccl_config_injector.py`**: NCCL config sweep, topology pinning, and torch.distributed integration

## Usage

```bash
# Single-op diagnostic
python bitwise_determinism_checker.py --op allreduce --size 1M --runs 10

# Sweep across all algorithms
python bitwise_determinism_checker.py --sweep-algos --op allreduce --size 128M

# Full diagnostic suite
python bitwise_determinism_checker.py --full-suite --output report.json
```

## Key Findings

- **Ring + Simple**: Deterministic (fixed rank order) — recommended for internode
- **NVLS**: Deterministic (hardware tree) — recommended for intranode with NVSwitch
- **PAT**: Potentially non-deterministic (atomic operations in shared memory)
- **Tree**: Non-deterministic without topology pinning (dynamic parent selection)

## Thinking Path

> - Paperclip is the control plane people use to manage AI agents, so review state and review artifacts need to stay visible in the board UI.
> - The reviewed-assets work already established the shared artifact model and panel behavior in the reviewed-assets foundation PRs.
> - The remaining gap was page wiring: issue detail and approval detail did not actually load or render those reviewed assets on their primary review surfaces.
> - That left reviewers without the artifacts they were supposed to inspect, even when the reviewed-assets backend and panel component were already in place.
> - This pull request restores that wiring on top of the refreshed reviewed-assets foundation branch and adds page-level tests around the two affected detail views.
> - The benefit is that board and engineering reviewers can inspect selected review assets directly from the issue and approval pages where the review decisions happen.

## Linked Issues or Issue Description

Refs #36

author: emilthaudal
body:
**Problem:** Atlassian rotates the OAuth refresh token on every use and invalidates the previous one. `getAccessToken()` in `lib/session.ts` correctly returns the rotated token, but every caller (`lib/jira.ts`'s `resolveAuth`, and the `/api/auth/me`, `/api/auth/sites`, `/api/auth/select-site`, `/api/auth/refresh`, `/api/jira/site-url`, and `/api/jira/*` routes) discarded it instead of writing it back to the session cookie — `app/api/auth/refresh/route.ts` even said so explicitly in a comment. The in-memory `tokenCache` masked this within a single warm Lambda instance, but once Vercel recycled the instance (or routed to a different one), the app retried with the stale, already-invalidated refresh token from the cookie, the refresh failed, and the session was destroyed — forcing users to fully re-log in far more often than the 1-hour access-token lifetime should require.

**Solution:** Added `persistRotatedToken()` to `lib/session.ts`, which saves the session cookie when `session.refreshToken` was rotated during the request. `resolveAuth()` in `lib/jira.ts` now updates the in-memory session with the rotated token, and every route that calls `getAccessToken`/`jiraFetch`-derived functions persists that change before responding. The one streaming route (`/api/jira/issues/project`) forces the refresh before the stream starts, since `cookies()` can't be mutated once response headers are sent.

---

**Security Impact:** None — this only changes when an already-valid rotated token is persisted; no new token material is exposed or transmitted differently.

---

**Testing:** `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint` both pass clean on the changed files. Manual runtime verification of the OAuth refresh flow requires a registered Atlassian OAuth app (client id/secret) which isn't available in this environment — recommend testing on a preview deploy by forcing a refresh (e.g. via `/api/auth/refresh`) across two separate Lambda invocations and confirming the session survives, versus the prior behavior where a second refresh after rotation returned 401 and destroyed the session.

author: metalmmagic
body:
`stalledJobTimeoutMs` was a wall-clock deadline measured from `claimedAt`, which cannot distinguish **wedged** from **working**.

A 400-page PDF transcribed a page at a time blew through the 5-minute default, was requeued mid-flight, re-claimed, and killed again at the same page. Not a lost job — an **infinite loop** that burns model calls forever while the file sits at `pending`, looking like it is still being worked on.

Jobs now carry `progressAt`, advanced as each page completes, and stall detection measures from the **last sign of life**. The timeout finally means what its name says: nothing has happened for N ms.

## The case that's easy to miss

Jobs claimed by a build older than this field carry **no `progressAt` at all**. Without a fallback to `claimedAt` they would never be recovered — the opposite failure, and equally silent. The rule keeps that fallback.

It's extracted as `stalledJobFilter` and **verified by mutation in both directions**:

| mutation | fails |
|---|---|
| revert to the wall-clock rule | the "still working" cases |
| drop the pre-heartbeat fallback | the legacy-job cases |

Each fails only its own cases.

## Also: truncation is no longer silent

Same question from the other side. The VLM path caps at `maxPages` (default 50), and used to truncate while reporting **success** — the only trace an HTML comment buried in the converted markdown, not logged, not stored, file marked `complete`. A 400-page document silently became its first 50 pages, and recall then answered confidently from a tenth of it.

It now logs a warning naming the file and both page counts, and the marker records **how many of how many** pages were read. This matters more than it used to: since `auto` began resolving up to the VLM path whenever a vision model exists (#349), more instances are on the capped path.

## Test scope, stated rather than glossed

`stalledJobFilter` is evaluated against document fixtures with a minimal matcher, so it checks **the rule** — which of three cases a job falls into — not that MongoDB agrees with the matcher. A database-level test isn't possible from the host: the test stack publishes no Mongo port and no standalone test connects to one. That gap is real and tracked; it isn't a reason to leave the rule unchecked, since the branch that actually bites is a coverage question rather than a query-semantics one.

Standalone **1094 pass**, integration **919 pass**, **0 fail**.

author: mike-thompson-day8
body:
Executes the **rf2-p6f6u ruling** (Mike, 2026-07-22, in chat): options **(b) + (c)** now; option (a) — real Xray-on-element-substrate support via the bundled slim renderer + a reg-view reactivity bridge — stays **parked behind a named demand trigger** (fires when a consumer demonstrably needs live Xray panels on a UIx / re-frame.ui app, or the re-com port's tooling wave demands it).

Context: Xray's panel shell is hiccup and mounts through the ratom-family substrates. On UIx (element-shaped React) the mount verbs refuse cleanly (rf2-qgfo4) — so the `:uix` template scaffold shipped a devtools panel that could never open, and the spine's element-shaped render slot let hiccup produce a spray of cryptic per-child React errors.

## (b) Honest `:uix` scaffold — `tools/template`

- The `:uix` variant ships **no Xray pieces**: no `day8.re-frame2-xray.preload`, no `[data-rf-xray-host]` layout host / `.rf2-xray-host` CSS, no `day8/re-frame2-xray` coord, no `@xyflow/react` + `elkjs` npm deps — across the **plain and Tailwind** css variants. `:reagent` keeps its full Xray wiring byte-for-byte; `:ui` is unchanged (no coord/preload, documented inert host).
- Mechanism: the Reagent-only wiring rides flat substitution values, extending the #6671 `{{xray-npm-deps}}` pattern (`{{xray-preload}}`, `{{xray-host-aside}}`, `{{xray-host-css}}`, `{{xray-readme-devtools}}`, `{{xray-readme-csp-note}}`, `{{xray-readme-inline-styles-note}}`, `{{csp-style-src-note}}`, `{{csp-style-src-note-tailwind}}`), so shared sources stay single-sourced and the Tailwind overlay cannot reintroduce the host.
- The `:uix` README + emitted comments note the devtools story honestly (Xray rides the ratom-family substrates today; what instrumentation the scaffold still gives; support follows when element-substrate mounting lands).
- Tests pin the split both ways: `assert-shape!`'s Xray cluster is now per-substrate, a new `assert-no-xray-host!` counterpart audit runs for `:uix` (and a new `:uix`+`:css :tailwind` Xray-free cell); the emitted-run `:local/root` Xray rewrite was already presence-gated (#6667) and degrades cleanly — verified by the `:uix` emitted-run arm below.
- Template spec docs updated to the narrowed scope: `001-Substrate-Variants.md`, `002-Generated-Shape.md` (§Xray devtools + substitution-variable table), `DESIGN-RATIONALE.md` §9 amendment.

## (c) Fail-loud element-slot guard — `re-frame.substrate.spine/make-render`

- CLJS data (hiccup vector / seq / map) handed to the element-shaped render slot now throws **one** structured `:rf.error/hiccup-on-element-render-slot` **before any root is created**, instead of React's per-child "Objects are not valid as a React child" spray. Always-on (the rf2-vxgfnd.292 misuse-guard idiom — the misuse breaks every build identically; three predicate calls at mount time, no hot path), message via `rf-error/throw-error!` with the `[:rf.error/…]` greppability token, ex-data carrying an **EP-0015-safe shape summary** (never the raw tree — mirrors `make-render-to-string`).
- Spec 009 §Error event catalogue row added in the same PR (co-edit invariant); the throw-axis source-scan conformance test pins it.
- Covers Xray's `panels.cljs` `mount-<panel>!` hiccup aggregators (the ungated failure shape the bead names) by construction — they funnel through `substrate-adapter/render`.
- Focused suite test (`assert-render-rejects-cljs-data-render-tree`, forwarded via the react-shared-suite macro list): the diagnostic fires on hiccup / seq / map with no content leak; a legitimate React element passes (predicate leg on node, end-to-end mount leg in the browser).
- Rider: the spine docstring's "UIx and Helix duplicated this body" comment reworded to the post-W13 truth (Helix removed at S7/W13, rf2-d6epb).

## Quality gates

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `tools/template` `clojure -M:test` (fast tier) | 62 tests / 729 assertions / **0 failures, 0 errors** |
| `:uix` emitted-run arm (`RF2_TEMPLATE_RUN_EMITTED_TESTS=1`, `uix-emitted-tests-run-test`) | emitted app (no Xray pieces) compiles `:app` + `:test` and runs green — 8 assertions / **0 failures** |
| `implementation/core` `clojure -M:test` | 2104 tests / 10413 assertions / **0 failures, 0 errors** (incl. the error-catalogue channel/throw-axis conformance over the new error-id) |
| `npm run test:cljs` | 10258 tests / 50945 assertions / **0 failures, 0 errors** |
| `npm run test:adapter-smokes` | 3 specs / **0 failures** (exit 0) |

Emission spot-checks (deps-new, all four cells): `:reagent` plain + Tailwind keep the full Xray wiring; `:uix` plain + Tailwind carry zero Xray artefacts (only the honest README/deps.edn notes mention the word).

author: cmddirexit
body:
## Description

When inputting non-ASCII characters (e.g. Chinese) via the terminal/PTY,
the UTF-8 byte stream can occasionally be truncated mid-character due to a
PTY buffer boundary race condition. Python's `input()` raises
`UnicodeDecodeError` in such cases, crashing the entire REPL.

This is **not** a deterministic bug — it depends on typing speed, PTY buffer
size, and kernel scheduling. Most Chinese inputs go through fine, but when
the PTY boundary happens to split a multi-byte character (e.g. 能 = 3 bytes
`\xe8\x83\xbd`, but only the first 2 bytes arrive), the REPL crashes
without this fix.

This PR catches the exception gracefully and shows a warning instead,
allowing the user to re-enter their input without losing their session.

## Changes

- `deeptutor_cli/chat.py`: Added `UnicodeDecodeError` handler in the REPL
  input loop alongside the existing `EOFError` and `KeyboardInterrupt` handlers.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `deeptutor chat`
2. Type a Chinese message (e.g. `你有什么功能`) — under certain PTY timing
   conditions the UTF-8 stream is truncated and the REPL crashes
3. The bug is intermittent; it may take several tries to trigger
4. With this fix, the error is caught and the user is prompted to try again

## Related

None reported on GitHub Issues yet.

author: liamsarsfield
body:
Fixes https://linear.app/a8c/issue/BOOST-604

A finished LCP analysis was being thrown away on the plugin side with nothing logged. On a live Atomic site the cloud returned correct results for nine cornerstone pages, yet the dashboard still said "Click the optimize button to start optimizing". Two independent paths cause it, and both are live on trunk today.

## Proposed changes

A `page-navigated` error blanks the whole panel:
* `class-lcp.php`: add `finalUrl` to the error `meta` schema so boost-cloud's `page-navigated` meta (Automattic/boost-cloud#736) stops being stripped to an empty `[]`. `meta` stays nullable, so an unknown shape parses to null instead of failing the whole state.
* `lcp-state-types.ts`: mirror `finalUrl`, accept `[]`/`null`/`{}` as empty meta, and move the `.catch()` off the whole state down to the page and error level so one bad entry no longer wipes the good ones.

A homepage entry in the custom cornerstone list wipes state on write:
* `Cornerstone_Utils::get_list()`: dedupe by provider key, since a `/` homepage collides with the predefined `home_url()`.
* `LCP_State::set_pages()`: give every entry a default status so a duplicate key can't produce a status-less page that fails the schema.
* `Update_LCP::response()`: check the update return, log failures, and save only when a result was actually applied.

## Does this pull request change what data or activity we track or use?

No.

## Testing instructions

Run `pnpm jetpack test js plugins/boost` and `pnpm jetpack test php plugins/boost`. Both chains have regression tests:
* JS: a state with `errors: [{ type: 'page-navigated', meta: [] }]` used to parse to the not_analyzed fallback; it now parses intact.
* PHP: state built from a `get_list()` with a homepage custom entry, then `set_pages()->set_pending_pages()->save()`, used to store `{ pages: [], status: 'not_analyzed' }`; it now stores the pending pages.

author: tokuhirom
body:
## Problem

```raku
say (1, 2, 4, 5, 6) ~~ (**);   # raku: True   mutsu: False
say ()              ~~ (**);   # raku: True   mutsu: False
```

`(**)` is a bare `HyperWhatever` (its `.WHAT` is `HyperWhatever`). Smartmatching
any value against it should be `True` — it matches everything, like `*`.
`pure_smart_match` had a `(_, ValueView::Whatever) => Some(true)` arm but none
for `HyperWhatever`, so `**` fell through to an ordinary type/value comparison
and returned `False`.

## Fix

Extend the Whatever arm to also match `HyperWhatever`. A `**` *inside* a list
pattern (`(1, **, 3)`) is a separate span matcher that already worked and is
unaffected — only the bare-`**` RHS changes.

## Tests

- `t/smartmatch-hyperwhatever.t` — bare `**` against list/scalar/string/type/empty,
  plus the list-pattern `**` cases as guards, and the full List.rakudoc example.
- `t/smart*.t`, `t/whatever*.t`, `t/hyperwhatever*.t` suites still green.

Found via the raku-doc/doc/Type/List.rakudoc doc-diff sweep.

author: adhithyan15
body:
## What & why

**NUM-6** (precision/format ops — `round_to`, `round_sig`, `to_scientific`, `to_percent`, `to_currency`) is the next **Substrate** item. Its signatures were already in `ADJ-NUMERIC-SUBSTRATE.md` §4, but tracing the engine surfaced its one genuinely-open design question — the **surface binding** — which the repo mandates pinning in a spec *before* implementation code. This PR settles it (specs-first); no code.

### The finding

Every rounding and transcendental built-in in ADJ today (`Round`/`Floor`/`Ceil`/`Abs`/`Trunc`/`Sign`, the trig family) enters through the **single `latex "…"` frontend**; formula bodies compose only *user* formulas via `Apply` (`quotient(a, b)`). There is deliberately **no** native built-in-call grammar. `round_to(x, places)` is binary (an integer precision arg), so it fits none of the existing unary latex nodes — the real fork is *extend the one LaTeX surface* vs. *invent the first native call grammar*.

### What §4 now pins

- **§4.1 Surface** — `round_to`/`round_sig` are the precision-carrying twins of the integer roundings, written as the two-argument operator-name applications `\operatorname{round}(x, n)` / `\operatorname{roundsig}(x, n)` on the **same** LaTeX frontend (reusing the existing comma/semicolon fence machinery). Zero new lexer/parser grammar, no second way to write a call. Unary `\operatorname{round}(x)` is unchanged and is exactly `round_to(x, 0)`. A non-integer/negative `n` is a **compile error**, never a silent truncation.
- **§4.2 Mode** — each narrowing **states** its rounding mode, defaulting to round-half-even (§3), deliberately distinct from legacy integer `Round`'s ties-away default — which is *why* the mode is recorded rather than implicit.
- **§4.3 Audit** — rounding is a **first-class narrowing**: the record carries the exact source value, target precision, mode, and rendered result; `adj-verify` re-rounds the exact value to confirm the rendering. Never a silent lossy coercion.
- **§4.4 Engine + sub-staging** — new `ComputeExpr::Round { spec, mode, expr }` (`RoundSpec = Places | SigFigures`), dimension-preserving, evaluated on the **exact path** via bignum-core `round_to_scale`/`div_round` (both already exist). Lands in focused PRs **NUM-6a** (`round_to`) → **NUM-6b** (`round_sig`) → **NUM-6c** (formatters + per-`KnowledgeBase` `BigDouble` precision). §6 rung bullet cross-links these.

## Scope

- `code/specs/ADJ-NUMERIC-SUBSTRATE.md` only (+64 lines). Docs-only — no code, no security surface.

## Unblocks

The **NUM-6a** implementation PR (`round_to` engine node + LaTeX surface + exact eval + audit + e2e), which can now proceed mechanically against a pinned design.

Follow-up to the agency policy-page discovery pass. Ingests the highest-confidence, genuinely multi-policy agencies from `_meta/catalog/agency-policy-pages.yml`, following the mechanical `ingest_policies.py` pattern already used for DOC/DHS/OHA.

## What's in

| Agency | Docs | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Oregon Youth Authority** | 156 | Single numbered "Policy Statement" series; listing page's own link text carries `NUM  TITLE`, so no PDF-header parsing needed. Added a new reusable `discovery: 'link-list'` mode to `ingest_policies.py` for this shape. |
| **Oregon Military Department** | 4 | Its policy page mostly re-links DAS statewide HR policies + bare forms — classified every `/omd/` PDF by header and kept only genuinely OMD-authored "AGP-" numbered policies. 2 more are image-only PDFs, left out per HC-1 (never OCR). |
| **Oregon Watershed Enhancement Board** | 3 | Only 3 of 4 PDF links on its page are real policies (one's a parking-lot map). No numbering scheme; 2 of 3 have no machine-readable effective date (image signature-stamp) — left `null` rather than guessed. |
| **Public Utility Commission** | 1 | Single 30-page "Internal Operating Guidelines" governance document, not a numbered series. |

## Bug fix

`ingest_policies.py`: for `identity: 'path'` profiles, re-ingesting (e.g. via `--only`) corrupted the manifest — the post-ingest `notes` rewrite used a free-text `"title (citation)"` summary instead of preserving the `num|title` shape the next parse expects, so a second run mis-derived `doc_id` from the whole summary string. Fixed to preserve the round-trip shape (caught and fixed live while re-ingesting OWEB).

## Deferred: DEQ

Its "Internal Management Directives" are real — a 73-item SharePoint **list** (found via the anonymous `_api/web/lists` enumeration endpoint after the page's own JS-rendered table led nowhere) — but each item links to an external records-management viewer (`ormswd2.synergydcs.com`), not a directly downloadable PDF. Publicly reachable, no auth, but needs its own text-extraction approach distinct from the PDF-manifest pattern. Documented in `_meta/agency-profiles.yml` and `_meta/catalog/agency-policy-pages.yml` for whoever picks it up next; nothing ingested for DEQ in this PR (its empty scaffold was removed rather than left half-finished).

body: ## Why Riipen (Ruby app, Forest v2 agent via the Ruby gem) wants the MCP server but it's Node-only — no "mounted" version on the Ruby agent, and none planned. To remove the friction of running Node next to Ruby, we ship a **Docker image** they deploy on their own infra. Same approach as `workflow-executor` (and Qonto before). ## What Mirrors the `workflow-executor` image setup, trimmed of executor-specific parts. - **`GET /health`** — unauthenticated liveness probe (Docker HEALTHCHECK / k8s), returns `200 {"status":"ok"}`. Registered before `allowedMethods(['POST'])` so the GET isn't rejected. + test. - **`Dockerfile`** — 3-stage, digest-pinned `node:22-bookworm-slim`, non-root `node` user. Isolated prod-deps install over the 5-package `@forestadmin` closure (`mcp-server` + `agent-client` + `forestadmin-client` + `datasource-toolkit` + `agent-toolkit`). `EXPOSE 3931`, healthcheck on `/health`. - **`docker/`** — deps-manifest generator, closure-drift check, dedicated `deps/yarn.lock`, boot smoke-test, README. - **`docker-publish-mcp-server.yml`** — PR validate (closure check + build + smoke-test + trivy OS blocking, npm libs report-only) and, on release, multi-arch (amd64+arm64) push-by-digest to `ghcr.io/forestadmin/mcp-server` with mutable `:latest`/`:minor`/`:major` + immutable `:version` tags. - **`build.yml`** — release job dispatches the image publish on a new `@forestadmin/mcp-server@*` tag (same pattern as the executor). - README + CLAUDE docs. ### Differences vs the executor image (intentional) - **No OpenTelemetry** → simpler entrypoint, no OTel deps/gate. - **No `notify-server` job** → the client deploys the image themselves; no Forest prod auto-deploy. ## Verification (local) - `yarn workspace @forestadmin/mcp-server test` → **609 passing** (incl. the new `/health` test); `lint` clean (0 errors). - author: ddeskov-limechain
body:
## Description

Closes #4261 — each of the 7 `it.skip` tests in `test/integration/CustomFeesIntegrationTest.js` now carries a comment documenting exactly why it is skipped and (where applicable) what would be needed to re-enable it.

### Investigation results, per test

| Test | Why it can't pass as written |
| --- | --- |
| L204 — transfer to non-associated fee collector | The fee is a fixed **HBAR** fee; collectors only need token association for token-denominated fees (that case is covered by the active test "cannot create custom fee with un-associated token fee collector"). The update succeeds, and `INVALID_CUSTOM_FEE_COLLECTOR` signals a missing/invalid collector account, not a missing association. |
| L299 — fractional fee > 1 | Consensus nodes don't reject a fraction > 1 at creation time. Moreover, the expected `Status.InvalidCustomFractionalFeesSum` **does not exist in the SDK's Status enum** — it evaluates to `undefined`, so the assertion could never match a real status. |
| L328 — fee schedule update with no fee schedule set | Adding fees to a token that has a fee schedule key but no fees yet is a supported operation — the update succeeds. `CUSTOM_SCHEDULE_ALREADY_HAS_NO_FEES` only applies to clearing fees when none exist. |
| L359 — update signed with wrong key | Wrong expected status: the network returns `INVALID_SIGNATURE` for a missing fee-schedule-key signature; `INVALID_CUSTOM_FEE_SCHEDULE_KEY` is a creation-time status for an unusable key. The comment documents the path to re-enable (assert `INVALID_SIGNATURE`, verify against a network). |
| L596 — clearing custom fees when none present | Expanded the existing one-line note: this is no longer an error on current networks, so `CUSTOM_SCHEDULE_ALREADY_HAS_NO_FEES` is never returned. |
| L654 — recursive custom fees | The two-token fee cycle settles within the network's allowed custom fee nesting depth, so `CUSTOM_FEE_CHARGING_EXCEEDED_MAX_RECURSION_DEPTH` cannot be reproduced. |
| L757 — more than 20 balance changes | Current consensus node configurations allow more balance adjustments per transfer than the historical limit of 20 this test targeted, so `CUSTOM_FEE_CHARGING_EXCEEDED_MAX_ACCOUNT_AMOUNTS` is not returned. |

### Notes

- Comments-only change — no test logic was modified and no tests were removed, so reviewers can still see exactly what each scenario intended.
- The tests remain skipped rather than deleted so the documented expectations can be revisited if network behavior changes (e.g. the L359 status fix can be verified against solo/local-node in a follow-up).
- Prettier passes; the eslint `parserOptions.project` error on this file pre-exists on `main` for all integration test files linted individually.

## What

Redesign the Library home so translated card labels stop unbalancing the grid, and make it adapt by Material 3 window size class (width, not orientation). Adds a navigation rail in medium/expanded.

body:
## What changed

- add the Nginx + Go personal gateway skeleton with token auth, text input, single-file upload, tool registry, timeouts, and input limits
- add Go builtin, process worker, and Linux C ABI execution adapters
- add the static frontend, Docker image, Compose deployment, and NAS-oriented runtime limits
- add `mental1104/common` as the `common/` Git submodule pinned to `33e33a31b68dfeaca598153238f055ee77b319b6`
- make local Go builds, CI, and Docker consume the same gitlink commit instead of cloning an unconstrained `common` revision during image build
- add submodule initialization/update commands and CI validation of the pinned Go sources

## Why

The gateway should remain a thin HTTP and cross-language adapter layer. Reusable business logic stays in `common`, while the parent repository records the exact dependency commit through a gitlink so development, CI, and NAS deployment do not silently use different revisions.

## Submodule handling

- local and NAS builds use `git submodule update --init --recursive`
- Docker copies the initialized `common/` worktree into the image and links `./common/golang`
- CI reads the `common` gitlink SHA from the parent commit and sparsely fetches only `common/golang` at that exact SHA, avoiding a full checkout of the large multi-language repository during Go-only tests

## Validation

author: lsd-cat
body:
Acquisitions stream into internal storage with no size known ahead of time, so a full disk would surface as an ENOSPC mid-write, mislabelled as module failures and leaving the archive unfinalized.

Add a reserve-based FreeSpaceGuard: as artifacts stream, once free space would drop below the reserve it throws, and the writer leaves the entry out of the hash manifest. Modules are reordered so the small high-value ones run first and the large ones (Files, Bugreport, Packages) last; the runner then skips the module that ran out and every remaining one, keeps what was collected, and still writes the index and closes the archive. The result surfaces as a distinct "skipped, not enough free space" card and notification.

Addresses https://github.com/osservatorionessuno/bugbane/issues/85

Part of #705 (scope item 2 — drive-by attachment on symbol surfaces). Closes #845. This completes scope item 2: all four symbol surfaces — symbol_lookup, impact_surface, read_chunk, and now semantic_search — attach distilled decision records.

Each semantic_search hit is a code chunk with `(path, symbol_path)`, so it reuses read_chunk's `records_for_chunk_symbol` lane (continuation-suffix handling and all).

- **Payload** — `SearchHit` gains a `distilled_records` field (skipped when empty), populated by a per-hit enrichment pass (`attach_distilled_records_to_search_hits`) in `search_with_graph_meta`, alongside the existing graph + load-bearing passes. Capped at 2, labeled unreviewed.
- **Gate** — on `include_papertrail` (default on). Records are papertrail-derived decision context, and semantic_search has no `include_memories` flag to ride, unlike the other three surfaces — a deliberate cross-surface difference.
- **Cost** — the pass hoists its batch invariants like the adjacent load-bearing pass: it early-returns when no hit has a symbol; resolves the `papertrail_distill` store existence and `active_repo_id` **once** (skipping the whole loop — and so all per-hit symbol resolution — when the store is absent, i.e. any repo that never distilled); and memoizes records by `(path, symbol_path)` so the many chunks of one symbol resolve and fetch a single time.

The search tool serializes `SearchHit` directly, so the field surfaces with no handler change. Empty for the vast majority of hits (facet-gated: provider fix edge + a qualified symbol anchor). Because `docs_for_symbol` also routes through `search_with_graph_meta`, its hits pick up records too — a harmless, consistent extension.

**Test**
`semantic_search_attaches_distilled_records_gated_on_the_papertrail_include` rebuilds a real index, seeds a provider-edge, selected-anchor record for the target symbol, and asserts the record surfaces on the matching hit with the papertrail include on, and that no hit carries records with it off.

## EPIC-09 — Profile Page

Implements the profile page and its three sub-issues. Route already exists in the protected-prefix list (`src/proxy.ts`); this fills it in. Closes #56, #57, #58, #59.

### PROFILE-01 — Display / edit user information
- New `/profile` page (`src/app/profile/page.tsx`), auth-gated with a sign-in prompt fallback and per-user `robots: noindex` metadata.
- Account header (`profile-info.tsx`): avatar (Google image + initials fallback), name, email, role badge and "member since".
- Inline **display-name editor** via a validated `updateProfile` server action + `useActionState`. Email/avatar come from Google and stay read-only.
- The page reads the account row from **Neon** (`getUserProfile`) rather than the JWT session, so an edit is reflected immediately — ahead of the 30-day token refresh.

### PROFILE-02 — Atmospheric background
- `ProfileBackground`: a CSS recreation of the reference videos (DESIGN-SPEC §6.2) — dark, low-brightness warm/green-grey radial glows over black that fade in from black and drift slowly, leaving the upper area clear for the card. Mirrors the search-page background approach until an admin uploads real videos (ADMIN-04). Honours `prefers-reduced-motion`.

### PROFILE-03 — Watch history / favorites quick view
- **Continue watching**: `title`/`image` are now denormalized onto `watch_progress` (migration `0004`, like `favorites`) so history renders without a Consumet round-trip; `saveWatchProgress` and the watch page thread the anime title/poster through. New `listRecentWatchHistory` collapses to one entry per anime with a resume progress bar.
- **Favorites**: a first-row preview (reusing `FavoriteCard`) with a "see all" link to the Favorites page.

### i18n
- New `profile` namespace across **EN / TR / RU** (account, editor, validation, history, favorites).

### Design & conventions
- Black bg, Netflix-red accent, sharp corners, SVG icons — no gradients/glassmorphism/emoji in the UI (the atmospheric layer is the documented exception). Fully responsive (mobile card is centered, desktop is a row).
- No `setState` in effects (render-phase adjust pattern in the editor and grids).

### Verification
- `npx eslint` — clean
- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- `npm run build` — succeeds; `/profile` route registered. (The 451 logs are the known dead Consumet public API degrading gracefully, unrelated to this change.)
- Note: the authenticated edit/history flow needs Google OAuth + a Neon `DATABASE_URL`, which aren't available in this environment; the signed-out and build/compile paths are verified.

body:
fix(auth): sessionen överlever ITP — native token-spegling + rullande cookie

869e69y3q ("måste logga in ofta"): WKWebView/ITP raderar cookies för
remote-laddade Capacitor-appar efter ~7 dagars inaktivitet. Sessionen bodde
ENBART i cookie-jaren; när cookien försvann myntade middleware tyst en ny
anonym identitet och användaren dumpades på inloggningen. Dessutom förnyades
en giltig cookie ALDRIG — klockan frystes vid login.

Tre delar:

1. Native spegling: GET /api/session/token ger inloggad anropare sitt eget
   signerade sessionsvärde (samma som cookien — inget nytt läcker, HMAC gör
   det oförfalskbart; utfärdas bara när profil finns). SessionPersistence
   (AppShell, båda grenarna — ITP-offret landar på publika heron!) speglar
   värdet i @capacitor/preferences vid appstart; saknar cookien profil men
   speglingen finns → POST /api/session/restore verifierar HMAC + att kontot
   finns → cookien sätts om → reload. 410 (raderat konto) slänger speglingen.
   Mount-only räcker: alla loginflöden gör full navigering → remount.

2. session/restore undantas från middleware-matchern (som session/init):
   annars myntar middleware en anonym nw_uid på SAMMA svar som restore sätter
   den återställda — två Set-Cookie för samma namn.

3. Rullande förnyelse i middleware: giltig nw_uid re-stampas med färsk 1-års
   maxAge, throttlat via nw_last (5 min) så det blir max ett Set-Cookie per
   5 min. httpOnly:false enligt middlewarens etablerade val (hasAuthCookie
   behöver se cookien; signaturen är förfalskningsskyddet).

Ny @capacitor/preferences → cap sync körd (backslash-fix i Package.swift per
skillen). KRÄVER NY APPFLOW-BUILD (görs ihop med Info.plist-ändringen i nästa
PR).

author: deazstar
body:
# Fix: Schema Alignment, Query Generation, and UI Parameter Mapping

## Summary

This PR fixes a series of cascading issues discovered during end-to-end testing of the annotation query builder — from schema processing bugs that silently dropped edges, to malformed Cypher queries, to missing node properties in the UI parameter panels. Changes span the backend query pipeline, schema manager, and BioCypher schema config files.

---

## Changes

### `graph.py` / `schema_manager.py`
- **Edge key collision** — `get_schema_representation` and `get_schema_represnetion_per_source` were keying edges by `output_label`, causing edges that share the same label (e.g. `participates_in`, `involved_in`, `enables`) to silently overwrite each other. Fixed by keying on `input_label` (always unique per entry) while preserving `output_label` as the display label.
- **`UnboundLocalError` / `TypeError`** — `get_schema_by_source_logic` crashed when all sources in `query_list` were `'all'` or not found, leaving `sub_schema` and `source` unassigned before the fallback block. Fixed by initializing both to `None` before the loop and guarding the fallback with `None` checks.

### `cypher_generator.py`
- **Malformed regex** — `_escape_regex` used `re.escape` which escapes spaces (`breast\ cancer`) and stray quotes from user input were injected directly into the Cypher string, producing invalid queries like `'(?i)breast\ cancer''`. Fixed by only escaping actual regex metacharacters and stripping quotes from input values.

### `constants.py`
- Added missing node types to `form_fields`: `disease`, `anatomy`, `tissue`, `cell_type`, `cell_line`, `phenotype`, `small_molecule`, `reaction`.
- Added missing properties to existing nodes: `snp` (`raw_cadd_score`, `phred_score`), `protein` (`canonical_accession`, `isoform_name`, `is_canonical`, `is_isoform`), `pathway` (`taxon_id`), `gene` (`synonym`), `reaction` (`taxon_id`).

### Schema files (`primer_schema_config.yaml` + data source schemas)
- **`expressed in`** — changed `target: ontology term` to `target: anatomy` so `validate_request` can construct and match the key `gene_expressed_in_anatomy`.
- **`gene to reaction association`** — changed `source: biolink:GeneOrGeneProduct` to `source: gene` to fix the same key mismatch.
- **`gene tf snp association`** — added missing entry (`gene → snp` via `tf_snp`) to `primer_schema_config.yaml` and `MotifDiff.yaml`.
- **`Alliance.yaml`** (new file) — added to cover three gene→disease orthology relationships (`biomarker_via_orthology`, `implicated_via_orthology`, `is_implicated_in`) and `is_marker_for` that had no data source schema home.
- **`REACTOME.yaml`** — added 12 missing protein/reaction/pathway relationships (`enables`, `produced_by`, `regulates`, `negatively_regulates`, `positively_regulates` for both pathway and reaction targets); reverted incorrectly suffixed `output_label` values back to original names.
- **`OBO_Foundry.yaml`** — added `id` and `term_name` to all ontology nodes that were missing them (`anatomy`, `cell_type`, `cell_line`, `tissue`, `small_molecule`, `phenotype`, `experimental_factor`, `developmental_stage`); added `cell_type → tissue` and `tissue → anatomy` part_of edges.
- **`UniProt.yaml`** — added missing protein properties (`id`, `accessions`, `is_canonical`, `is_isoform`, `canonical_accession`, `isoform_name`); removed stale xref targets not present in Neo4j; added `protein → small_molecule` xref.
- **`CADD.yaml`** / **`dbSNP.yaml`** — added all SNP properties including `raw_cadd_score` and `phred_score` which were completely missing from CADD.
- **`RNAcentral.yaml`** — added `id`, `source`, `source_url` to `non_coding_rna` node; added three missing relationships (`participates_in`, `enables`, `located_in`).
- **`GTEx.yaml`** — corrected `expressed_in` edge to use consistent `input_label` with Bgee.
- **`Bgee.yaml`** — removed `gene_expressed_in_developmental_stage` edge since `developmental_stage` node has no data in Neo4j.
- **`STRING.yaml`** — removed `protein_coexpressed_with` edge not present in Neo4j.

---

## Testing

~80% of the query catalogue was manually verified end-to-end through the UI against the live Neo4j instance, covering single node lookups, single-hop relationships, and multi-hop traversals across all major node types.

Verified query patterns include:

- `gene (gene_name) -[expressed_in]-> anatomy` ✅
- `gene -[is_implicated_in]-> disease (term_name)` ✅
- `gene -[is_marker_for]-> disease` ✅
- `gene -[participates_in]-> pathway (taxon_id)` ✅
- `snp (phred_score, raw_cadd_score) -[eqtl_association]-> gene` ✅
- `protein -[produced_by]-> reaction` ✅
- `gene -[tf_snp]-> snp` ✅
- `protein (protein_name, is_canonical) -[interacts_with]-> protein` ✅

author: pan3793
body:
### What changes were proposed in this pull request?

Add a new config `spark.sql.hive.showCreateTableAsSerde` (default `false`). When enabled,
plain `SHOW CREATE TABLE` on a Hive serde table routes to the existing
`ShowCreateTableAsSerdeCommand` and renders Hive DDL, instead of converting to Spark DDL.

### Why are the changes needed?

We get some reports from customers: they are confused that `CREATE TABLE ... STORED AS Parquet` but `SHOW CREATE TABLE ...` displays `CREATE TABLE ... USING Parquet`.

Background: SPARK-27946 (#24938) deliberately changed plain `SHOW CREATE TABLE` to always emit Spark DDL, to push and simplify migration from Hive to Spark. `AS SERDE` was introduced in the same PR as the intended escape hatch for users who still need Hive DDL, and the failure modes were intentional: transactional Hive tables error out by design, and tables whose serde has no Spark data source mapping (e.g. RCFILE) are meant to be served by `SHOW CREATE TABLE AS SERDE`.

This PR keeps that direction intact: the default behavior is unchanged, and `AS SERDE` remains the per-query escape hatch. It only adds a session-level toggle that turns "append `AS SERDE` every time" into a config, which helps users and integrations (e.g. BI tools, metastore sync jobs) that cannot easily rewrite the SQL they issue.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. New config `spark.sql.hive.showCreateTableAsSerde`, default `false` (no behavior
change). When `true`, `SHOW CREATE TABLE` on Hive serde tables returns Hive DDL; data
source tables and views are unaffected.

### How was this patch tested?

Added tests to `o.a.s.sql.hive.execution.command.ShowCreateTableSuite` covering: Hive
table (matches `AS SERDE` output), data source table and view (unaffected), RCFILE and
transactional Hive tables (Hive DDL rendered instead of erroring).

### Was this patch authored or co-authored using generative AI tooling?

author: mikolaj
body:
This is the benchmark, test, documentation and tooling half of the #123
  work, split out so it can land before the engine change: it contains no
  changes under `src/HordeAd/Core` beyond a comment-link pin — the gather
  shn-sort contraction fix and its printed-AST refresh follow in a
  companion PR. Follow-up to #128 and #129.

  **Benchmarks.** `bench/ConvVjpBench.hs` is reworked into an honest,
  pairwise-comparable suite: the two #123 pipelines (S = Symbolic, H =
  handwritten-vectorized) are decomposed into adjacent stage pairs —
  `S-fullpipe-honest`/`H-fullpipe`, `S-artifact`/`H-term`,
  `S-exec`/`H-exec`, `S-exec-raw`/`H-exec-raw` — with the incoming
  cotangent kept as a variable on both sides; known measurement traps
  (artifact hoisting, constant-cotangent embedding) are quarantined as
  single recorders in a `pitfalls` group, so the sweep groups hold only
  honest variants. New `cnn-*` groups time a real shaped two-layer CNN
  gradient at 6x6, 12x12 and 24x24, sharing the objective with the
  printed-AST test via `cnnObjective`, newly exported from TestMnistPP —
  share code, not configuration. The `gather48`/`scatter48`
  micro-benchmarks are completed (fused-then-sorted gather variants, the
  shn-sorted scatter adjoint), benchmark names adopt the ad/vec
  vocabulary for the two gather orientations, and every gather/scatter
  chain pair is verified at startup via the adjoint law: for all `f`,
  `x` and `y`, `sdot0 (sgather x f) y == sdot0 x (sscatter y f)`.

  **Time properties.** The module haddock states fifteen numbered
  (in)equalities between the criterion means of a full run, each checked
  up to 10% tolerance and classified: accounting identities (a violation
  means the measurement broke), a simplifier recorder, engine invariants
  (a violation is a regression) and cost-model rulings (to re-measure
  when the kernels change). `tools/check-conv-bench-props.py` is the
  list in executable form and guards its own coverage — a benchmark no
  property touches is a failure. All 89 checks pass on a full criterion
  run with the companion fix applied; on this branch alone, property 6
  (`time(S-exec) <= time(H-exec)`) documents the target state — its
  failure against the current engine is exactly the #123 gap the
  companion PR closes.

  **Tests.** TestConvCorrect now value-checks the interpreted
  handwritten gradient path — the one every `H-` variant and every
  HandwrittenVectorized poor man's benchmark times, which no test had
  pinned: six vectorized legs plus a var-cotangent case (raw and
  contracted, dKrn and dInp). Non-vacuity was proven by deliberately
  breaking each new assertion and confirming exactly the expected
  failures. TestConvQuickCheck's haddocks defer stage-for-stage
  comparison to the criterion suite and explain why
  HandwrittenVectorized cannot be amortized.

  **Rename.** `conv2dSame`/`conv2dSameS` and family become
  `conv2dPreserving*`: "same" collided with the English word in every
  comment around it, so the family is named for the property itself —
  the output image size is preserved. Ancient code included; plain-prose
  "same" untouched.

  **CI.** The benchmarks step smoke-runs the entire suite with
  `--benchmark-options='-n 1'` — every benchmark once, no statistics,
  seconds total — on all three GHC versions: build-and-runtime
  protection, not a perf tripwire.

  **Tooling and docs.** `tools/check-plan-citations.py` re-validates
  file:line citations and pinned permalinks in reference documents (the
  one unpinned source permalink, AstInline.hs's CHAD reference, is
  pinned accordingly); `.hlint.yaml` keeps `-XNoStarIsType` (mirroring
  the cabal's `default-extensions`) and drops `--cpp-simple` for the
  fixed hlint v3.10; the README's Coding style section spells out the
  comment-prefix and alignment rules; and CLAUDE.md (guidance for Claude
  Code sessions) is added. CLAUDE.md's performance model documents the
  whole #123 investigation, so parts of it describe the companion branch
  (the contraction rule, `notes-add-zero-gather.md`); they are kept
  verbatim deliberately.

  **Validation.** Build, minimalTest and the full CAFlessTest suite are
  green on this branch — the printed-AST expectations match the
  unchanged engine — and every commit compiles in isolation;
  stylish-haskell is clean on all touched files; hlint reports zero
  errors repo-wide.

author: shaft3796
body:
## Summary

Adds the awaited **`session.turn.complete.before`** plugin hook (P1) plus the shared **`rootSessionID` identity helper** (P4a), in two bisectable commits on top of `conv-main` (post-P2, post-#4 p3-tool-warn).

A plugin may veto a turn's completion at the exact per-session boundary — after final assistant output, **before** idle publishes / the parent `task` resolves. `decision:"continue"` appends a synthetic user continuation and re-enters `runLoop`; `decision:"allow"` (default) completes as today. The hook input carries the full identity triple `{sessionID, parentID?, rootSessionID}` (`rootSessionID` derived by P4a, stamped into `task` metadata) and `continuationActive` to guard re-entry. Root ⇒ Stop, foreground child ⇒ SubagentStop.

**Design:** a single `Plugin.trigger` at the `runLoop` **post-loop convergence point** — every completion break (normal Stop, structured-output, content-filter, result-stop) and the genuine-error `halt` paths converge there. `processor.halt` no longer publishes idle on genuine-error paths (they route through the veto); only an abort/kill still publishes idle directly and is never vetoed (D-11). Additive-only, narrowest insertion; `TriggerName` auto-derives the new hook (no dispatcher edit).

### Fail-closed hardening (review findings closed)

The completion gate is an enforcement boundary, so a crashing/failed gate must not fail **open**:
- **Guard-crash (brief attack #4):** the hook runs via `Effect.promise`, so a throwing completion plugin was a defect that killed `runLoop` while the runner still published idle — silently completing the turn as if it returned `allow`, emitting **no** error. Now captured via `Effect.exit`: a genuine failure publishes a visible `Session.Event.Error` and re-raises (turn ends **errored**, never a clean idle); an interrupt (abort/kill) is re-raised untouched so D-11 semantics are preserved.
- **Identity resolution:** `rootSessionID` no longer `Effect.orDie`s — a broken ancestor chain falls back to the session's own id so the gate still fires with a valid triple, instead of dying and skipping the veto.
- **Cycle guard:** the `rootSessionID` ancestor-walk carries a visited-set so a corrupt `parentID` cycle stops instead of hanging the session (this walk sits on the completion path).

## Turn-termination inventory (every `status.set(idle)` producer / `runLoop` exit)

| # | Termination path | Coverage |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Normal Stop break (last assistant finished non-`tool-calls`) | Veto fires (convergence point) |
| 2 | Structured-output / content-filter / json-schema / result==`stop` breaks | Veto fires (same convergence) |
| 3 | Compaction result `stop` break | Veto fires |
| 4 | `halt` context-overflow, auto-compaction OFF → `finish=error` | Veto fires (idle removed; routed through boundary) — tested |
| 5 | `halt` generic error, non-abort | Veto fires (idle now gated `if (aborted)`) |
| 6 | Abort / cancel / instance-shutdown (interrupt) | **Excluded (D-11)** — interrupt bypasses veto, lands as own terminal state; re-raised untouched — tested |
| 7 | Foreground child (`task`/handleSubtask) completion | Veto fires with `parentID` + `rootSessionID` set — tested (E2E) |
| 8 | Background-forked child | **Excluded by card** (closed by P4c) |
| 9 | Shell turn (`startShell`) | Excluded — not an agentic/LLM completion |
| 10 | Queued continuation joins existing runner | Next turn = fresh `runLoop`; `continuationActive` call-scoped |
| 11 | Completion **gate itself throws** / identity resolution fails | **Fail CLOSED** — visible `Session.Event.Error` + turn errors, never a silent allow — tested (unit + E2E) |

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] AC1 `plugin/src/index.ts` exports the hook; typecheck passes; `TriggerName` resolves it, no dispatcher edit.
- [x] AC2 `allow` (or unset) ⇒ identical to stock: idle publishes, parent `task` resolves.
- [x] AC3 `continue` + `parts` ⇒ loop re-enters with synthetic continuation; no idle / no task-resolve until a later `allow`.
- [x] AC4 error-path `halt` (overflow-no-auto + generic) still fires the veto — regression test drives an induced error.
- [x] AC5 `continuationActive=true` on re-entry; plugin can terminate; `allow` never loops.
- [x] AC6 Root fires with no `parentID`; child fires with `parentID`/`rootSessionID` (SubagentStop).
- [x] AC7 Colocated regression tests (`turn-complete-veto.test.ts`, `root-session-id.test.ts`).
- [x] AC8 `conv-conformance.yml` `p1` + `p4a-identity-triple` real behavior gates replace the pending stubs.
- [x] P4a: `SessionTable` schema unchanged (derived, no `root_id`); metadata carries identical `rootSessionID` across descendants; `parentID` still the immediate parent.

## E2E evidence — real `opencode-conv` binary (`nix build .#opencode`, `1.18.4+aaaf4c8`), stub plugin loaded from config against a mock OpenAI-compatible LLM

```
(a) allow       exit=0  turncount=1  output "world"   1 obs {parentID:null, rootSessionID==sessionID, finish:stop, continuationActive:false}
(b) continue    exit=0  turncount=2  output "I am done." + "BANANA, now I am done."  <- model RE-ENTERED post-veto; 2 obs: continuationActive false then true; idle once at true end
(c) child       exit=0  turncount=3  task tool ran -> "parent wraps up"
                child obs: {sessionID:ses_..PNJ, parentID:ses_..BXx, rootSessionID:ses_..BXx(agent general)}   root obs: {parentID:null, rootSessionID:self}
(d) no plugin   exit=0  turncount=1  output "stock world"  (no obs — hook never fired; stock behavior)
(e) gate throws exit=1  UnknownError published; obs shows hook fired (finish:stop) -> turn ERRORED, not a clean "allow" (contrast (a): same mock reply -> exit 0 + text)
```

`bun run typecheck` clean; `turn-complete-veto.test.ts` (allow / continue-re-entry / foreground-child parentID+root / genuine-error-halt honors / **gate-throws-fails-closed** / abort-not-vetoed) + `root-session-id.test.ts` (root / depth-1 / depth-3) ⇒ **9 pass, 0 fail**. Pure source patch — no dependency manifest touched, no Nix hash regen. No self-merge intended; parks at awaiting review.

## What to check
1. Convergence-point insertion + `processor.halt` idle-gating are the whole veto surface (grep no other `runLoop` early-return skips it).
2. Fail-closed path: `Effect.exit` handling preserves interrupts (D-11) while erroring genuine gate failures.
3. `rootSessionID` derived-only (no schema/migration) and the metadata stamp equals the child's derived root.

author: sammozaffari
body:
## Why
Live prod verify of #106 (with `LENS_WEB_SEARCH=on`) showed **doxylamine at 88s with webFindings:0** — the web call ran *after* the study path, so it got only the ~22s leftover (not enough for the Exa search + generation → timed out) and pushed total wall time to the 90s Vercel ceiling.

## Fix
Fire the reputable web research **in parallel** (right after resolution) so it **overlaps** the ~60s study work — it adds no wall time and gets the full window to complete. It's awaited + filtered at the end (`attachWeb`, was `enrichWithWeb`). The web call's timeout is bounded (45s) and clamped under a wall budget so it can never approach `maxDuration`.

Same firewall, same server-side filters (reputable-host re-check + sleep + framing + grade + domain recompute) — **only the timing changed**. Fired only on the researched path (never refused/short-circuit).

## Live proof
`doxylamine` → assessed in **60.0s** (was 88s) with **2 web findings** (ncbi.nlm.nih.gov, drugs.com) + study evidence.

Lens red-team **238** / card 39 / loop 40; build + framing green. Control-flow change to the engine; the firewall + all filters are byte-identical, directly resolving the adversarial review's latency should-fix.
