author: qiukelab
body:
## What

Extend `scripts/check-component-wiring.mjs` with a new assertion (section 16) that ties every **human-facing component-count literal** to the real number of component directories under `packages/react/src`.

Eight sites are now guarded (EN + TH):

| File | Phrase |
|---|---|
| `home-copy.ts` | EN hero lead (`… accessible components`, spelled as a word) |
| `home-copy.ts` | TH hero lead (`… 28 ตัว`) |
| `content/docs/index.mdx` / `.th.mdx` | docs-index "Components" card |
| `content/docs/components/index.mdx` / `.th.mdx` | frontmatter description + body intro |

## Why

These counts live in free prose. Nothing breaks the build when they drift, but a landing page that says "28 components" while more actually ship is a visible, embarrassing lie — the same failure mode `check-component-wiring` already closes for registration points (exports, CSS, sidebar meta, CI floors). This matters right before we add the Field cluster (28 → 32): the guard will now fail loudly if any of these eight sites is left stale.

Each entry anchors on its surrounding phrase, so an unrelated number is never matched; a reworded sentence throws (a signal to update the anchor), a stale number fails with a precise message. The EN hero is written as a word for readability, so it is checked against a small 0–99 number-to-words table.

## Verify

- `pnpm check-component-wiring` → green (28 == 28 across all eight sites).
- Broke two literals on purpose (a digit → `29`, the word → `Thirty`): the guard reported both with exact locations and exited 1; reverted.
- `pnpm lint` green · `pnpm format:check` green (oxfmt-formatted).

Tooling-only change — no package output, no changeset.

author: slorek
body:
## Summary
- The backend no longer makes any authorization decision based on role claims (paired change: [epr-register-enrol-management-be#61](https://github.com/DEFRA/epr-register-enrol-management-be/pull/61)) — it trusts any signed request and defers all access decisions to this BFF.
- Removes the unconditional `case-worker` role injection and all `x-cdp-user-roles` forwarding in `backend-api.js`. Only `x-cdp-user-id`/`x-cdp-user-name` are still sent, for audit attribution.
- Bumps the HMAC canonical signing payload from `v2` to `v3` in `sign-request.js`, dropping the roles field.

## Follow-up items from review (addressed in this PR)

An independent security review (Opus) and an independent code-quality review (Opus) were run against this branch (together with the paired `management-be`/`epr-register-enrol-backend` branches) after it was first opened.

**From the security review:** no issues found specific to this repo. The reviewer independently recomputed the `v3` HMAC test vector in `sign-request.test.js` and confirmed it matches what's committed — a genuine regression guard, not a tautological one.

**From the code-quality review:**
- **Fixed stale JSDoc in `backend-api.js`**: `assignWorkItem` and `approveReAccreditation` doc comments still claimed "the backend enforces role-based rules" / "decision-maker role membership" / "tenant filtering." It doesn't any more — that's this BFF's responsibility now, and the comments were rewritten to say so.
- **Fixed a stale test fixture** in `logger-options.test.js`: the log-redaction test used `'x-cdp-user-roles': 'standard,case-worker'` as its example of a header that gets preserved (non-redacted) in logs. That header is never sent by this BFF any more, so the example no longer represents a real header — swapped for `x-cdp-cognito-client-id`, which is.

## ⚠️ Coordinated deploy required
This is a **breaking change to the auth signing contract**. Must deploy together with:
- [epr-register-enrol-management-be#61](https://github.com/DEFRA/epr-register-enrol-management-be/pull/61)
- [epr-register-enrol-backend#55](https://github.com/DEFRA/epr-register-enrol-backend/pull/55)

Signing `v2` against a `v3`-only backend (or vice versa) gets a `401 Invalid x-cdp-auth-signature` — no dual-accept window.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm test` — 733 passing
- [x] Full `epr-register-enrol-mgmt-tests` e2e suite run against this branch + the paired `management-be` branch, with `AUTH_SHARED_SECRET` set (exercises the real signed-request path) — matches baseline `main` results (3 pre-existing environment-only failures, everything else green)
- [x] Independent security review (Opus, fresh context) — no findings specific to this repo
- [x] Independent code-quality review (Opus, fresh context) — should-fix findings addressed above

author: ricardogarim
body: ## Proposed changes (including videos or screenshots) Skin-toned emoji variants (e.g. `high_five` ✋🏽) stayed small when sent as an emoji-only message, while the default version (✋) was correctly enlarged. **Root cause:** A message made only of emoji is enlarged only when it is recognized as a *single* emoji. A skin-toned emoji is actually two parts — a base emoji plus a separate skin-tone modifier — that must be joined into one. Emoji are spread across several Unicode ranges, and the message parser only joined the skin-tone modifier for some of them. For two of those ranges (which include hands like ✋ ✌ ✍ ☝ ⛹), the modifier was not joined, so a skin-toned emoji was read as two things: the base emoji plus a leftover skin-tone swatch. The result was a big default-colored hand next to a tiny swatch, instead of one enlarged skin-toned emoji. The plain version (✋) worked because it has no modifier to lose. **Fix:** Allow those two ranges to join the skin-tone modifier too, like the others already did. Now a skin-toned emoji is read as a single emoji and enlarges correctly. Emoji without a skin tone are unaffected. ## Issue(s) - [CORE-2456](https://rocketchat.atlassian.net/browse/CORE-2456) - introduced by https://github.com/RocketChat/Rocket.Chat/pull/39411 ## Steps to test or reproduce 1. Send `high_five` (✋) alone → enlarged. 2. Pick a skin tone and send `high_five` with different tone (✋🏽) alone. 3. Before: stays small. After: enlarged with the correct skin tone. ## Further comments [CORE-2456]: https://rocketchat.atlassian.net/browse/CORE-2456?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Improved recognition of additional Unicode emojis with skin-tone modifiers. * Correctly parses combined emoji sequences and emojis embedded within surrounding text. * **Tests** * Added coverage for hand, arm, and activity emojis, including modified and concatenated forms.

author: weirdmachine64
body:
## Problem

Comments produced by the comprehensive function rewrite were silently dropped whenever the model addressed them by a symbol/label (e.g. `{"op":"comment","address":"entry",...}`) instead of a numeric address.

`applyComment` resolved addresses only through `AddressFactory.getAddress(String)`, which parses numeric address strings and does **not** consult the symbol table. So `getAddress("entry")` returned `null`, `setComment(null, …)` threw, the exception was swallowed, and the comment never appeared. The model had no way to do better — the prompt sent plain decompiled C (`DecompiledFunction.getC()`) with no addresses in it at all, so any comment address was a guess.

## Fix

Give the model real addresses, and validate strictly instead of guessing:

- **`buildAddressAnnotatedCode`** renders the function via Ghidra's own `DecompilerUtils.toLines` + `PrettyPrinter.getText`, prefixing each source line with the minimum backing instruction address (blank prefix for declaration/brace lines). This feeds the prompt in place of `getC()`.
- **Prompt** tells the model each line carries its address, to copy one verbatim from the `/* … */` prefix, and never to invent one.
- **`applyComment`** now rejects any comment whose address does not parse, falls outside the function body, or is not a code-unit boundary — with a clear log line. No fallback: if a comment can't be placed correctly, it fails.

## Testing

- `mvn test`: 32/32 pass.
- Headless round-trip check on a real ELF: every address shown to the model is accepted by `applyComment`'s rules (8/8), and label-style addresses (`entry`, `main`) are rejected. Confirmed manually in Ghidra with a live model — comments land correctly.

author: smbrownai
body:
## Summary

Promotes the Sparkle-appcast validator (written during the 1.0 update-chain review) into `dist/` and wires it into `ship.sh`'s PUBLISH phase, immediately after `appcast-publish.sh` rewrites the feed and **before anything is tagged or pushed**. A malformed feed can no longer reach a release.

`dist/validate-appcast.py` checks the failure modes that silently break the update every existing user receives:
- malformed XML / missing channel or items
- missing/truncated `sparkle:edSignature`, invalid `length`, non-`.dmg` enclosure
- an item carrying **both** `<sparkle:releaseNotesLink>` and inline `<description>` — Sparkle shows the link's web page and drops the HTML (the precedence trap)
- non-monotonic or duplicate build numbers, build↔shortVersion mismatch
- `--expect-version X.Y.Z` → the newest item must be the version being shipped (catches a stale top entry / a publish step that didn't insert)
- `--dmg PATH --sign-update PATH` → **deterministic Ed25519 cross-check**: re-sign the built DMG and confirm it reproduces the appcast signature + length. Catches signing-key drift (→ every update silently rejected) and a DMG/appcast mismatch, entirely offline using artifacts already present during PUBLISH.

`ship.sh` calls it with `--expect-version "$VERSION"` and, when the DMG + `sign_update` are present, the signature cross-check too; it `die`s on any error.

## Test plan

- [x] `bash -n dist/ship.sh` — syntax clean
- [x] Validator passing case: `validate-appcast.py dist/appcast.xml --expect-version 0.9.7` → 0 errors, exit 0
- [x] Negative control (wrong `--expect-version`) → errors, exit 1
- [x] Signature cross-check against a non-matching binary → signature + length mismatch errors, exit 1
- [x] Signature cross-check positive case proven manually during the review (re-signing the published 0.9.7 DMG reproduced the appcast `edSignature` byte-for-byte)
- Runbook (`dist/README.md`) PUBLISH steps + script table updated

The 4 warnings the validator emits on the current feed are the ancient 0.1.0–0.1.3 entries that lead with an HTML comment instead of `<h2>` — cosmetic, pre-existing, and non-fatal (warnings never fail the run).

author: iareanthony
body:
## What changed

- serialize Chromium recovery so concurrent capture failures share one restart
- keep the capture guard active throughout browser recovery
- enforce a five-second minimum delay between browser launches
- detach stale page references and bound graceful browser shutdown before forcing cleanup
- disable Puppeteer's per-launch signal handlers and retain application-owned shutdown handling
- retry a failed browser launch without allowing a restart storm
- add regression tests for concurrent single-flight behavior, backoff, and recovery after failure

## Root cause

When a screenshot failed, the capture loop cleared `isCapturing` before awaiting `startBrowser()`. The 100 ms capture timer could then enter again while recovery was still running. Each overlapping callback closed and launched Chromium independently, creating dozens of Chromium and crashpad processes until the container exceeded its 1 GiB memory limit.

## Impact

One failed Chromium session now produces at most one browser recovery operation. Additional requests coalesce into it, and failed launches retry with a bounded delay instead of multiplying processes.

## Validation

- `node --check index.js`
- `node --test` — 4 tests passed

This PR does not deploy or alter the Kubernetes workloads.

author: laposhbaby
body:
## Summary

Expands Playwright end-to-end test coverage for the Soroban escrow feature from **4 to 9 tests**, covering the full lifecycle: create, claim (full & partial), cancel, and five edge cases (claim-before-release, cancel-after-release, partial-claim balance reduction, non-XLM asset escrows, and metadata completeness). Additionally implements the **partial claim** feature in both the Stellar integration layer (`buildClaimEscrowPartialTransaction`) and the escrow page UI, enabling recipients to withdraw a portion of locked funds after the release ledger has elapsed — a contract capability (`claim_escrow_partial`) that previously had no frontend exposure.

**Closes #161**

---

## Type of change

- [x] New feature (partial claim UI + transaction builder)
- [x] Tests (E2E — 5 new Playwright tests, retaining 4 existing)
- [x] Configuration change (`playwright.config.ts` timeout increases)
- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Smart contract change

---

## Architecture

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        Escrow Feature                              │
├───────────────┬────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┤
│  Contract     │  Frontend Lib      │  UI Page                      │
│  (lib.rs)     │  (stellar.ts)     │  (escrow.tsx)                 │
├───────────────┼────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────┤
│ create_escrow │ buildCreateEscrow  │ Create form                   │
│ claim_escrow  │ Transaction        │  ├─ Recipient input           │
│ cancel_escrow │                    │  ├─ Amount (XLM)              │
│ claim_escrow_ │ buildClaimEscrow   │  ├─ Release ledger            │
│   partial  ◄──┤   Transaction      │  └─ Submit button             │
│               │                    │                               │
│ get_escrow    │ buildCancelEscrow  │ Manage section                │
│               │   Transaction      │  ├─ Lookup input              │
│               │                    │  ├─ Claim button              │
│               │ buildClaimEscrow   │  ├─ Cancel button             │
│               │   Partial       ───┤  └─ Partial claim input+btn   │
│               │   Transaction (NEW)│                               │
│               │                    │                               │
│               │ getEscrow          │ Metadata display <dl>         │
│               │ getCurrentLedger   │  ├─ Status / From / To        │
│               │                    │  ├─ Amount / Release ledger   │
│               │                    │  └─ Current ledger            │
└───────────────┴────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────┘
         ▲                                    ▲
         │                                    │
    ┌────┴────────────────────────────────────┴────┐
    │        E2E Tests (escrow.spec.ts)             │
    │  page.route() mocks all RPCs                  │
    │  addInitScript mocks Freighter wallet         │
    │  9 hermetic tests, fully mocked               │
    └───────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Data flow — Partial Claim

```
1. Recipient enters partial amount (XLM)     → escrow.tsx state: partialClaimAmount
2. Clicks "Partial claim" button             → handleAction("partialClaim")
3. Validation: amount > 0, amount ≤ balance   → error if invalid
4. Build tx: buildClaimEscrowPartialTransaction(publicKey, id, stroops)
5. Simulation via Soroban RPC                → contract::claim_escrow_partial(id, amount)
6. Sign with Freighter mock                   → signTransactionWithWallet(xdr)
7. Submit to Horizon                          → submitTransaction(signedXDR)
8. Refresh lookup                             → handleLookup() → updated remaining balance
```

---

## Files Changed

### Modified files (4)

| File | Insertions | Deletions | Purpose |
|------|-----------|-----------|---------|
| `frontend/e2e/escrow.spec.ts` | 479 | 0 | Expanded from 4 to 9 E2E tests with comprehensive Soroban RPC mocking for entire escrow lifecycle |
| `frontend/lib/stellar.ts` | 29 | 0 | Added `buildClaimEscrowPartialTransaction` helper: constructs + simulates Soroban `claim_escrow_partial` call |
| `frontend/pages/escrow.tsx` | 99 | 50 | Added partial claim UI (input + button), extended `actionPending` to include `"partialClaim"`, updated `handleAction` to route to the new builder |
| `frontend/playwright.config.ts` | 2 | 2 | Global timeout 30s → 60s, action timeout 10s → 15s for escrow test stability |
| `frontend/package-lock.json` | — | — | Dependency lockfile updated by `npm install` |

---

## Detailed Implementation

### 1. `buildClaimEscrowPartialTransaction` (`frontend/lib/stellar.ts`, +29 lines)

**Location:** After `buildCancelEscrowTransaction` (line ~1936), before `getEscrow`

```typescript
export async function buildClaimEscrowPartialTransaction(
  fromPublicKey: string,
  id: number,
  claimAmountStroops: bigint,
): Promise<Transaction> {
  if (!CONTRACT_ID) throw new Error("Contract ID is not configured.");
  const sourceAccount = await server.loadAccount(fromPublicKey);
  const contract = new Contract(CONTRACT_ID);
  const tx = new TransactionBuilder(sourceAccount, {
    fee: STELLAR_BASE_FEE_STROOPS_STRING,
    networkPassphrase: NETWORK_PASSPHRASE,
  })
    .addOperation(
      contract.call(
        "claim_escrow_partial",
        nativeToScVal(id, { type: "u32" }),
        nativeToScVal(claimAmountStroops, { type: "i128" }),
      ),
    )
    .setTimeout(STELLAR_TRANSACTION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS)
    .build();
  const simulated = await sorobanServer.simulateTransaction(tx);
  if (rpc.Api.isSimulationError(simulated)) {
    throw new Error(`Simulation failed: ${simulated.error}`);
  }
  return sorobanServer.prepareTransaction(tx);
}
```

**Design decisions:**
- Follows the same pattern as `buildEscrowMutation` (load account → build → simulate → prepare) for consistency
- Accepts `claimAmountStroops` as `bigint` to avoid precision loss with large stroop values
- Only requires `fromPublicKey` (the recipient), `id`, and `claimAmountStroops` — the contract derives the escrow record and validates ownership
- Throws on simulation failure rather than returning a result type, matching the existing error handling convention in `stellar.ts`

### 2. Partial claim UI (`frontend/pages/escrow.tsx`, +99 / -50 lines)

**New imports:**
```typescript
import {
  buildClaimEscrowPartialTransaction,  // NEW
  STELLAR_STROOPS_PER_XLM,             // NEW — for XLM → stroops conversion
  // ... existing imports
} from "@/lib/stellar";
```

**New state:**
```typescript
const [actionPending, setActionPending] = useState<null | "claim" | "cancel" | "partialClaim">(null);
const [partialClaimAmount, setPartialClaimAmount] = useState("");
```

**Modified `handleAction`:** The function now accepts `"partialClaim"` as a third action variant. When selected:
1. Validates the entered amount is a positive finite number
2. Converts XLM to stroops: `Math.round(parseFloat(partialClaimAmount) * STELLAR_STROOPS_PER_XLM)`
3. Validates the stroop amount ≤ escrow balance (prevents over-claiming)
4. Calls `buildClaimEscrowPartialTransaction(publicKey, escrow.id, BigInt(partialStroops))`
5. Signs, submits, and refreshes the lookup (same flow as full claim/cancel)

**New UI section** (below Claim/Cancel buttons, separated by a border):
```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Or claim a partial amount (XLM):            │
│  ┌─────────────────────────┬──────────────┐  │
│  │ Partial amount (XLM)    │ Partial claim │  │
│  └─────────────────────────┴──────────────┘  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Disabled-state logic for "Partial claim" button:**
| Condition | Disabled? | Tooltip |
|-----------|-----------|---------|
| `actionPending !== null` | Yes | (no tooltip — general pending) |
| `currentLedger < releaseLedger` | Yes | "Release ledger not reached" |
| `publicKey !== escrow.to` |

author: raul1934
body:
Deixa ligar o WhatsApp virar configuração em vez de refatoração. Parte da #156.

> Toca `config/concierge.php`, que a #161 também toca. Se a #161 entrar primeiro, o conflito é de uma linha.

## O problema

O detector chamava `Mail` direto. Trocar o canal exigiria mexer nele — e no lançamento o alerta provavelmente sai por WhatsApp, não por e-mail.

Agora ele pede `OpsAlerter` e não sabe no que aquilo vira.

## Três implementações

| Canal | Quando |
|---|---|
| `MailOpsAlerter` | **Padrão.** Não depende de integração nenhuma e já resolve |
| `WhatsAppOpsAlerter` | Cloud API oficial da Meta, pronta para quando as credenciais existirem |
| `StackOpsAlerter` | Os dois ao mesmo tempo — para validar o WhatsApp sem apostar a operação nele |

Escolha por `CONCIERGE_CHANNELS=mail,whatsapp`.

## Por que a via oficial

Z-API, Evolution, Baileys e afins dirigem o WhatsApp Web por baixo dos panos e são **exatamente o que faz número ser banido**. O canal que existe para avisar a operação não pode ser o que derruba o canal de atendimento.

## Duas armadilhas, documentadas na config e no `.env.example`

1. **Um número registrado na Cloud API deixa de funcionar no aplicativo do WhatsApp.** Não pode ser o +55 17 99647-5590, que a landing publica como suporte. Precisa de um número separado.
2. **Fora da janela de 24h a Meta só entrega template aprovado.** Como o alerta é sempre iniciado por nós, é sempre template — o que torna o nome e a **ordem dos parâmetros** parte do contrato, não detalhe de implementação. O template espera `{{1}}` minutos, `{{2}}` categoria, `{{3}}` endereço.

## A regra da interface

**Avisar não pode quebrar quem disparou o aviso.** Cada canal engole a própria exceção e registra. Um chamado sem cobertura já é um problema; virar exceção no scheduler — e derrubar a detecção dos outros chamados da mesma rodada — seriam dois.

## Verificação

**17 testes, 36 asserções.** Os **9 testes originais do detector passam sem uma linha alterada**, que é a evidência de que o refactor não mudou comportamento.

Os 8 novos cobrem: seleção do canal por config nas três combinações, e-mail enviando e se calando sem destinatário, WhatsApp montando o POST correto, canal não configurado ficando quieto, canal com erro 400 não lançando, stack entregando nos dois, e o detector usando o canal configurado sem saber qual é.

O teste do payload do WhatsApp trava as coisas que quebrariam em silêncio:

```
type === 'template'          // trocar por 'text' parece mais simples e não entrega
to   === '5517996475590'     // a Meta rejeita máscara
parâmetros na ordem 1,2,3    // trocar manda o endereço para o lugar do tempo
```

**O que isso não prova:** o payload foi verificado contra `Http::fake()`, não contra a Meta. O formato segue a documentação da Cloud API, mas a primeira chamada real pode revelar detalhe de conta — template não aprovado, permissão faltando, número fora de forma. É verificação de contrato, não de integração.

## Para ligar

```
CONCIERGE_CHANNELS=mail,whatsapp
CONCIERGE_WA_TOKEN=...
CONCIERGE_WA_PHONE_ID=...
CONCIERGE_WA_TO=5517...      # número que RECEBE o alerta
```

Antes disso: criar o app no Meta Business, verificar a empresa, registrar um número **separado** e submeter o template `chamado_sem_proposta`. Nada disso é código.

author: ondiekochieng
body:
## Discovery — Who is the Coach?

**Product discovery only. No implementation, personalities, prompts, or dialogue.** No existing docs changed.

> Not *what should he sound like?* — but *who is standing in the athlete's corner?*

### Verdict: **PARTIALLY — and a reframe: the Coach is a *relationship*, not a personality.**
We kept treating the Coach as a *personality* (how he sounds). He is a **relationship** (who he is *to the athlete*). Personality is what **varies**; relationship is what the Coach **is**.

### What a Coach *is*
> The athlete's corner — made audible. A *someone* who exists entirely for the athlete's boxing: **present without being the protagonist, honest without claiming to see, continuous (never stops).** Corner already went voice-pack → *a human*; this is human → **relationship** (a thing that exists *for someone*).

### The four owners (sorting the "must-survive" list)
- **Corner** — time, the bell, the athlete-as-north-star, the promises (*forget the phone*, behaviour over information, success is an athlete experience).
- **Every Coach** — never stops coaching · perfect timing · never claim to see · silence · *always for the athlete, never the protagonist*.
- **Personality** — tone, vocabulary, pacing, intensity, and **what the athlete feels** (dangerous / composed / calm).
- **The athlete** — the boxing, the experience, whether they forgot the phone.

So: changing personality changes neither the boxing nor the philosophy — only the *feeling*.

### Key answers
- **Who serves whom?** The Coach serves the athlete; the athlete serves the boxing. *The Coach exists for the athlete; the athlete does not exist for the Coach.*
- **North-star test** — the aim is a different **relationship**, **distinguishable in retrospect, invisible in the moment** (during the round the athlete thinks about the bag, not the coach).
- **No Coach may become** a protagonist, a narrator, a timer, an interruption, or *a collection of prompts* ("a relationship is not a template").
- **Already answered?** Yes — *what belongs to every Coach* is settled. **Not answered:** what makes each Coach a distinct *relationship*, and the distinguishability-vs-immersion tension.

### Recommendations — future Coach Personality discovery only
Start from the **relationship**, not the voice · measure by the **athlete's felt experience**, not transcript distinguishability · define success as *distinguishable in retrospect, invisible in the moment* · every Coach inherits the invariants unchanged · **never begin with prompts** ("a prompt library is a relationship's corpse").

> Answer *who is he to the athlete?* and the words take care of themselves.

## Why
High-value customers hand over a cheque and expect the locker opened. Lockers are **online-only on LockerHub** — contract v1.2 §A10 retired offline `record-payment` and it 400s for every caller — so **NCD cannot settle a locker leg with a cheque**. This records the instrument and its clearance in *our* books so nothing is lost operationally while that remains true.

## What it deliberately does NOT do
It does not pretend the locker is paid. **Clearing a cheque releases NCD's own hold and nothing else** — the leg still needs **A9** (payment link) or **A12** (back the deposit with an NCD investment). Every API response carries a `note` saying so, and every screen repeats it. Faking settlement locally would desync us from LockerHub and leave a locker that never allots, which is worse than the current gap.

## Changes
- **migration 032** — `locker_cheques` (leg, amount, cheque no, bank, received/cleared dates, status, notes, who recorded/settled). A **partial unique index** stops one leg holding two `Pending` cheques, while re-recording after a bounce stays allowed.
- **Routes** — `POST /api/lockers/cheques`, `GET` (the register), `POST /:id/clear`, `POST /:id/bounce`.
  - Recording is enrolment-tier (`lockers:enroll`).
  - **Clearing asserts money landed in the bank**, so it additionally requires `applications:confirm-collection` — branch staff *take* the cheque, management *confirms* it cleared. Verified that admin / ncd_manager / super_admin hold both permissions and branch_staff / branch_manager hold only the first.
  - Every state change is audited.
- **Locker enrolment UI** — record a cheque against an unsettled leg (showing `awaiting clearance` / `cleared`, always with "still settle the leg above"), plus a **Cheques awaiting clearance** register with *Funds cleared* / *Did not clear*.

## Verified
6 new tests: staff can record and the response never claims settlement; a second pending cheque per leg is refused (409); staff **cannot** clear (403) while a collection-confirming user can; double-clear refused; a bounce frees the leg for a replacement; the register lists pending with the customer joined.

`npm test` — **387 passed (72 files)** · api typecheck ✓ · web build ✓

## Follow-up
If LockerHub reinstates an offline settlement path (the A10 successor we're asking for), the clear action can then also settle the leg on their side — the register is the natural place to hang that.

author: puneetrinity
body:
Two of the three root causes from the Stage-3 offline gate failure (the third — thin embed text — is the Stage-4 blob-enrichment work, sequenced after these per re-plan):

1. **Cap 200 → env-tunable 500** (`GLOBAL_SEARCH_LIMIT_MAX`). Signal asks for 300 and was silently getting 200. Server remains the authoritative binding limit; the response now returns `applied_limit` so callers log truncation.
2. **Location filter**: substring match + NULL pass-through. Exact `ILIKE` dropped 'Greater Bengaluru Area' (48 rows) and all 332 NULL-location rows. Signal's ranker demotes unknown locations and its country guard treats no-location as an escape, so hiding them server-side silently shrank the pool.

Evidence: job-147 replay showed only 41/88 served pool members (7/18 of served top-20, incl. the #1 candidate) retrievable by vector; Bengaluru-eligible segment is 815 rows. With N≈500 + these filter fixes the vector set approaches the whole segment.

No schema/migration changes (ledger untouched). ruff format/check clean.

Next: signal-side HOME_POOL_LIMIT 300→500 + truncation log, then re-run the offline gate (≥95% of served top-100, 100% of top-20) → flip `SOURCE_TWO_LAYER_POOL_ENABLED` + one live run.

author: princesseuh
body:
Fixes gaps in walked trails caused by sparse GPS sampling. When a new fix arrives, the Worker now fills every H3 cell along the straight line from the previous fix to the new one (via `grid_path_cells`), so a continuous walk paints a continuous trail even when the phone only reports every 100–200 m.

Guards so it never draws a false line across a big jump:
- **distance**: skip if the two fixes are more than ~80 hexes (~3.5 km) apart
- **time**: skip if more than 10 min elapsed (tracking was paused/closed)

Stores the previous fix under `__last` (excluded from `/scratchmap/cells`). Still only writes new hexes (KV write quota stays low). Verified locally: two fixes ~500 m apart fill the ~12 hexes between them; an ~11 km jump adds only its own cell.

author: anoopsypereddi
body:
## What

Adopts finding #5 from the firstmate upstream-comparison report: a backend-independent off-machine alarm when an away-mode (`/afk`) injection wedges.

Previously, when an away-mode injection wedged past max-defer, the daemon only logged, wrote a durable marker, and did an unconditional `tmux display-message` that dies silently on non-tmux (herdr) backends - the exact blind spot behind a documented ~8.5h silent overnight wedge upstream. The flash string was also still the stray hardcoded `fm:` prefix left over from the port.

## Change

- `inject_wedge_alarm` now calls `wedge_alarm_notify`, fanning out a **backend-independent, default-on** active alert alongside the unchanged durable marker and tmux flash:
  - `osascript` - macOS Notification Center banner (OS-level, reaches the Chef even when every pane is unreadable)
  - `herdr` - herdr UI notification, off the dead pane
  - `command:<cmd>` - generic escape hatch (`sh -c`, summary on `$1`/stdin) so the Chef can wire ntfy/Slack/SMS to a phone
- **Rate-limited** to once per max-defer window; **timeout-bounded** per channel via a process-group watchdog (`SC_WEDGE_ALARM_TIMEOUT_SECS`, default 10s, no dependency on the `timeout` binary).
- **Default-on** (`auto` -> macOS `osascript`); **kill switch** via `config/wedge-alarm` = `off` or `SC_WEDGE_ALARM_CHANNEL=off`.
- Each channel is best-effort: a missing binary or non-zero exit logs and falls through, never crashing the daemon loop.
- Fixes the stray `fm:` flash string to `souschef:`.
- A test-forced `SC_WEDGE_ALARM_EXEC` seam, defaulted to `discard` whenever the daemon is sourced, makes it structurally impossible for a test to post a real notification.

## Docs / config

- `docs/wedge-alarm.md` - behavior, channels, kill switch, test-safety seam, and a bounded manual verification (osascript + herdr forms, both verified exit 0 on macOS 26.3).
- `docs/examples/wedge-alarm` - copyable starting config.
- One-line pointers added to the `/afk` skill and AGENTS.md §8 away-mode stub.

## Validation

- `shellcheck bin/*.sh bin/backends/*.sh tests/*.sh setup.sh` - clean.
- `bash -n` on all scripts - clean.
- Full test suite: **22/22 suites green**, including 9 new daemon tests for channel selection, multi-channel fan-out, `off` kill switch, graceful degradation on channel failure, `command:` dispatch, failing-command secret-hiding, library-mode discard default, and once-per-window rate-limiting.

author: dancinlife
body:
lab(v6): the pooled readout had seen every test offset — narrowing H_9921, and holding the fire

I sent the retrain design to both frontier models and asked, explicitly, how to avoid training
on the test distribution. Fable answered by pointing at the result I had published one commit
earlier: H_9921's pooled decoder was fitted on the training halves of ALL NINE offsets, so it
had seen every offset it was then scored on. That shows a single map covers offsets it has
seen. It does not show it covers offsets it has not. The trap I asked about was already inside
my own evidence.

The check is free -- same dumps, same instrument, fit on a subset and score the rest:

  train {0,2,5,8}   -> held {1,3,4,6,7}   seen 1.0000   held mean 0.8812  min 0.6844 (d=7)
  train {0,2,4,6,8} -> held {1,3,5,7}     seen 1.0000   held mean 0.9039  min 0.8469 (d=1)
  shuffled-label floors: 0.5719 and 0.5656

PARTIAL. It is not dead: held-out offsets read 0.68 to 0.98, clearly above the floor, so there
is real cross-offset generalisation. It is also not "sufficient": against 1.0000 on seen
offsets the held cells scatter, and one split misses the >=0.90 held-out bar fable set as the
condition for firing. Coverage density is the variable -- training every other offset
generalises better than a sparser set, and the worst cells are the ones furthest from a
training point.

So H_9921 should now read: one map covers the offsets it was fitted on, and generalises to
unseen ones really but incompletely, by an amount that depends on how densely the training
offsets are spread. The direction survives -- the failure is fitting range, not representation,
since held-out sits far above floor. The strength does not: there is no basis for claiming a
few offsets buy the rest for free.

On firing, the two models split -- fable said do not fire below 0.90 held-out, sol said fire. I
took the cheapest check first, and it lands on the bar's edge depending on the split. Reading
only the split that passes is exactly tune-to-green, so I am not declaring a pass. The fire is
held, and the condition that would justify it is frozen now, before any further run: held-out
mean >= 0.90 on BOTH splits and a minimum cell >= 0.80. The cheap route there is denser
coverage -- start by putting delta one into the training set and re-measuring, which is free.

Unchanged limits: this is still a linear probe on the trunk hidden, not the lane's actual
readout, and the offset was varied with whitespace only. Fable wants entity length varied too,
to block a whitespace-counting shortcut; sol wants whitespace alone. That conflict is recorded
and stays open until firing is justified. One checkpoint, one seed, synthetic drill --
drill-only.

- New kernel `SystemServiceManager` (real D-Bus + mock, mirroring `PowerManager`) reads live `ActiveState`/`LoadState` for a server-side catalog of units: `dnsmasq`, `systemd-resolved`, `systemd-timesyncd`, `ssh`, per-interface `wpa_supplicant@<iface>`/`dhcpcd@<iface>` (dynamic, from live interfaces), and `pigate.service` itself (status-only).
- Restart is only ever performed against a unit name resolved from the server-side catalog by slug — the `{id}` path param from the client is never used as a raw unit name (closes off systemd unit-injection). `pigate.service` is hard-blocked from restart at the service layer (403), independent of the frontend.
- Successful restarts are recorded in the audit event log.
- `docs/openapi.yaml` / `frontend/public/openapi.yaml` and the README Feature Status table updated to match.
- **Follow-up fix (found during real-hardware testing):** the status badge could get stuck on "Restarting..." forever after a restart, because `RestartUnit` over D-Bus only queues the job and returns immediately — the one-shot fetch right after the POST usually caught a mid-transition state, and nothing re-fetched after that. Now polls every 1.5s (~12s max) until the status settles. Also fixed a leftover mislabel where the "stopped" badge always showed "Restarting..." regardless of cause.

Full architecture rationale, decision log (D1–D4, owner-approved), and cautions: `docs/ref/todo/os-service-status-control-plan.md` (Definition-of-Done fully checked off, including the post-merge follow-up).

Closes #82

author: lucasmaurice
body:
## Why CI is red

Every job in the `Go` workflow fails at the **Get dependencies** step, before the build even runs:

```
go: go.mod file not found in current directory or any parent directory.
	'go get' is no longer supported outside a module.
```

`go get onewire_exporter/v2` runs from the repo root, which has no `go.mod` (the module lives in `src/`). The step was also redundant — `go mod -C ./src download` already fetches everything.

Removing it exposes a second, real breakage: two APIs used by `main.go` were **removed** from `github.com/prometheus/common` after the version Renovate bumped us to (v0.70.1).

## What's in this PR

- **`.github/workflows/go.yml`** — drop the `go get onewire_exporter/v2` line.
- **`src/main.go`**
  - `common/promlog` → `common/promslog`. It returns a stdlib `*slog.Logger`, so `go-kit/log` and its `level.X(logger).Log("msg", …)` wrappers are gone in favour of `logger.Info(…)` / `logger.Debug(…)` / `logger.Error(…)`.
  - `common/version.NewCollector` → `client_golang/prometheus/collectors/version.NewCollector` (it moved packages).
  - An unparseable `-log.level` now exits with a clear error instead of being silently ignored — `promlog.AllowedLevel.Set` returned an error the old code discarded.
  - `none` dropped from the `-log.level` help text; `promslog` accepts only `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error`.
- **`src/go.mod` / `src/go.sum`** — `go.sum` was stale (still pinning `common v0.44.0` and `client_golang v1.17.0`); regenerated via `go mod tidy`. The `go` directive goes `1.21` → `1.25.0`, which is what `prometheus/common v0.70.1` requires.

## Behaviour change to be aware of

Log output format changes from go-kit logfmt to `slog`'s text handler, and the error key stays `err`. If anything downstream parses these logs, it will need updating. `promslog.Config{Style: promslog.GoKitStyle}` is available if the old shape is preferred.

## Verification

`go build`, `go vet` and `gofmt -l` are clean, and all six `GOOS`/`GOARCH` combinations from the CI matrix cross-compile.

body:
## Problem

Maven compilation failed with "incompatible types" errors in AdminController.java and OrderController.java because both deleteOrder methods call ApiResponse.success(String) while their return type requires ApiResponse<Void>. Since ApiResponse only defines success(T data) and success(String message, T data) overloads, the compiler infers conflicting bounds for T (String from the argument vs Void from the return type).

## Solution

Updated both calls to explicitly use the two-argument overload with a null data value: ApiResponse.success("message", null). This unambiguously resolves T to Void, matching the declared return type and fixing the build.

- **Modified** `printhub-backend/src/main/java/com/printhub/controller/AdminController.java`

author: h0x91b
body:
Hi — this is Claude (the AI assistant working on this branch). Three fixes for `dev3 remote` / headless Linux boxes:

**1. Wait for the Cloudflare tunnel to be reachable before printing the `dev3 remote` link.** cloudflared announces the `*.trycloudflare.com` hostname a few seconds before Cloudflare's edge actually routes it. Printing the link at announcement time let the user click too early and cache a `DNS_PROBE_FINISHED_NXDOMAIN`, which then hangs long after the tunnel is live. `awaitTunnelReady` now actively probes the URL (HEAD fetch; a Cloudflare 520–530 edge error = not ready) with progress dots before printing. Also removed a duplicated `awaitTunnelReady` call in `startDetached`.

**2. Gate the tunnel `connected` state on cloudflared's `/ready` endpoint (fixes the desktop Remote button too).** The backend flipped a tunnel to `connected` the instant the hostname was parsed — so the GUI Remote Access modal showed a URL/QR that could NXDOMAIN. `startEntry` now waits for cloudflared's own `/ready` (200 only with a live edge connection) before marking connected, with a bounded timeout + best-effort fallback. `getRemoteAccessQR` awaits `startTunnel`, so the modal keeps its "Starting tunnel…" state until the link is routable.

**3. Ensure `~/.dev3.0/bin/dev3` resolves on headless boxes.** Agent hooks, the injected skill, and lifecycle onExit commands all invoke the CLI by the hardcoded absolute path `~/.dev3.0/bin/dev3` (`agent-hooks.ts` `DEV3_CLI`). Only the GUI entry and the Settings toggle ever create/refresh it — `headless-entry.ts` (the `dev3 remote` server) never did, so on a headless box the file was simply absent and every hook failed with `/bin/sh: …/.dev3.0/bin/dev3: not found` (tasks stopped auto-moving status). New `ensureDev3CliSymlink()` symlinks it to the running binary on headless startup (realpath-resolved to avoid the ELOOP self-link class).

Decisions: 155 (tunnel reachability), 156 (headless CLI symlink). Tests added for all three; `bun run lint` + `bun run test` green.

author: m-tkg
body:
## Problem

`AgentStatusPollingCoordinator` polls every 0.5s on the main thread and called `TerminalAgentProcessDetector.provider(processID:)` for every pane's foreground pid on every tick. Each call does `proc_pidpath`, a two-call `sysctl(KERN_PROCARGS2)` (size probe + full copy of the args/environment region — a multi-KB allocation), and lowercase/join/Set string classification. A pane's foreground process rarely changes, so with N panes this was N × 2/s of redundant syscalls, allocations, and string churn on the UI thread.

## Fix

New `AgentProcessProviderCache` (per-surface, `@MainActor`) in front of the detector:

- Cache key = `(pid, process start time, executable path)`. Start time (`proc_pidinfo(PROC_PIDTBSDINFO)`) defeats pid reuse; executable path (`proc_pidpath`) defeats in-place `exec` to a different binary. While the key is stable, a tick costs only these two cheap probe syscalls — the argv copy and classification run on a key miss only.
- Negative results are cached too: a plain shell (`nil` provider) is the steady state and no longer re-scans argv every tick.
- A transient probe failure falls through to full uncached classification, so it can never pin a stale or wrong result. Entries for closed surfaces are purged each tick, mirroring `AgentSessionThrottleCache.purge`.
- Known accepted staleness (documented): `exec` from one script to another under the same interpreter binary keeps pid, start time, and path, so the cached classification sticks until any of them changes.

Probes are injectable closures (production defaults on `TerminalAgentProcessDetector`, whose other entry points are untouched), following the existing closure-seam pattern.

## Testing

- `AgentProcessProviderCacheTests` (10 tests): cache hit invokes classify once; re-classification on pid / start-time / path change; negative-result caching; probe-failure fallback without cache poisoning; invalid pid; purge of removed surfaces; per-surface isolation.
- `swift build` and full `swift test` pass.

## Summary

Implements Milestone 3 as a stacked change on top of #3.

- add snapshot runs, distinct attempts, raw-page metadata, candidate members, finalized members, required uniqueness, and database triggers that block updates/deletes after finalization
- add exact IANA-timezone cutoff calculation for 23:59 on the final local calendar day, current/next run pre-creation, bounded automatic retries, and interrupted-attempt recovery
- add fake and verified public-web guard-roster sources with a sanitized provider fixture
- persist original response bytes as private gzip objects with SHA-256 metadata while keeping full raw JSON out of PostgreSQL
- reject missing/out-of-order pages, duplicate UIDs, total/page drift, first-page drift, unknown tiers, count mismatch, and timeouts
- classify punctuality from capture start, auto-finalize only on-time consistent attempts, and require owner/admin approval for late consistent attempts
- add creator-scoped snapshot APIs, evidence integrity checks, audited finalization/approval/rejection, and an operator UI for runs, failures, evidence, retry, and approval
- document the provider limitations and mark M3 complete; M4 remains unstarted

## External verification

On 2026-07-22, `/xlive/app-room/v2/guardTab/topListNew` was exercised with anonymous in-memory web credentials against a non-empty public room. All declared pages were retrieved. The response exposes total/page/current-page fields, repeats `top3`, and carries tier under `uinfo.guard.level`, but supplies no atomic snapshot timestamp or consistency token. The implementation therefore records a complete capture interval and re-fetches page one rather than claiming provider-side atomicity.

- **H1 — QuizPage crash on empty quiz**: `q = topic.quiz[i]` then renders `q.q` with no empty-array guard; topics are routinely created with `quiz: []`, so opening their quiz throws `Cannot read properties of undefined`.

Report also covers medium items (committed `.env` files, backend default `PORT` 8080 vs 5000 used everywhere else, user-deletion orphaning bookmarks/progress/ai-keys, corrupt `.docx` export) and low/hygiene items (red lint, dead/diverging `supabase/functions/*`, 3.7 MB bundle). author: puket
body:
Root cause: bootTenantable() wrapped addGlobalScope() in an "if (auth()->check())" guard evaluated at model boot time. Eloquent boots each model class only once per PHP process. In long-running processes (queue workers, scheduler, artisan/tinker) the first touch to a Tenantable model can happen before a user is authenticated, permanently skipping scope registration for the rest of the process even after login succeeds.

Verified with a reproduction: touching Department pre-auth, then logging in as a company_id=1 tenant, could still read a company_id=2 probe record. Fixed by always registering the scope and moving the auth()/role check inside the scope closure, which re-evaluates on every query instead of once at boot.

Also closed gaps found while auditing tenant isolation coverage:
- PayrollItem / PayrollOtDetail: company_id was missing from $fillable, so PayrollController's explicit "company_id => ..." on create() was silently dropped by mass-assignment protection (confirmed via the generated INSERT statement). Added company_id to $fillable and applied Tenantable so these rows are both scoped and auto-tagged going forward.
- EmployeeDocument, EmployeeEducation, EmployeeExperience, EmployeeTraining, EmployeeSchedule: have a company_id column (migration 2026_04_26_155739) but were not using Tenantable at all, leaving them unscoped. Added the trait.

Verified via tinker with two real tenants (Yupensuk company_id=1, Puket Stores company_id=2): each only sees their own data post-fix, and super_admin still sees everything (scope bypass unchanged).

author: kai392
body:
## Summary

The JetStream (safety-critical) consumer callbacks parse each message with `deserialize_message()` **before** validating it against a wire model, but their parse `except` clauses caught only `MessageValidationError`. `deserialize_message()` (`json.loads(data.decode("utf-8"))`) raises `json.JSONDecodeError` on malformed JSON and `UnicodeDecodeError` on non-UTF-8 bytes — **neither** is a `MessageValidationError`, so a corrupt message escaped the poison/term path entirely.

This affects both durable JS paths in `sdk/src/activelearning/nats_client.py`:

- **`js_subscribe` callback** — the decode error skipped `_route_to_poison()` **and** `msg.term()`, so the message was never dead-lettered to `dlq.<subject>`, never acked, and never `term`-ed. On a JetStream consumer it then redelivered up to `max_deliver` and stuck un-acked — a **silent loss on a stream whose documented contract (see the `js_subscribe` docstring) is that messages are "never silently dropped".** These are the safety-critical subjects `proposal.new`, `code.proposal`, and `decision.>`.
- **`wait_for_decision` waiter** — the un-acked garbage redelivered to the ephemeral waiter until it was torn down at timeout.

## Root cause

`deserialize_message()` runs before `validate_payload()`, so its decode exceptions are raised outside the type the parse block was written to catch. The core-NATS `subscribe()` path already handles this correctly with a broad `except Exception` (it logs and moves on); the two JetStream paths were narrower and let decode errors propagate out of the callback.

## Fix

Both parse blocks now treat a decode failure the same as a schema violation — structurally unprocessable, can never succeed on retry:

- `js_subscribe`: `except (MessageValidationError, json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError)` → route to poison + `term()` (dead-lettered, stops redelivering, observable).
- `wait_for_decision`: same widened `except` → `ack()` (drop the un-fixable message) and keep waiting, so the caller still **fails closed** on timeout.

Minimal and backward-compatible — no API or wire-format change; valid messages are unaffected.

## Tests

Adds `sdk/tests/test_jetstream_decode_poison.py`, which captures the **real** subscription callbacks and drives them with malformed-JSON and non-UTF-8 payloads:

- `js_subscribe` → asserts the message is dead-lettered to `dlq.proposal.new` and `term()`-ed, and **not** ack/nak-ed.
- `wait_for_decision` → asserts the garbage is acked (dropped), does not satisfy the wait, and the caller times out (fails closed).

Verified the tests **fail without the fix** (the decode error propagates out of the callback) and pass with it.

```
tests/test_jetstream_decode_poison.py ....  4 passed
```

Full SDK suite: 351 passed, 71 skipped (broker-dependent tests skipped locally; the 3 unrelated `test_unified_db_migration.py` failures are Windows-only SQLite temp-file locking, not reproducible on the Linux CI runners). Local gates green: `ruff check` (real-bug + full), `black --check --line-length 100`, and `mypy --python-version 3.11 --ignore-missing-imports sdk/src/activelearning` ("Success: no issues found").

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Component(s) affected

`sdk` (`activelearning.nats_client`) — bumped to **0.2.1** with a CHANGELOG entry.

## Risk / tradeoffs

Low. The change only widens two `except` tuples to also catch decode errors and routes them into the existing, already-tested poison/ack machinery. Valid-message behavior is unchanged. No new dependencies.

## Architecture / safety alignment

- [x] Does **not** weaken the safety layer — it strengthens it: corrupt messages on safety-critical streams are now dead-lettered/observable instead of silently lost, and the decision waiter still fails closed.

author: stefanoamorelli
body:
## What

The engine already saved state to a debounced `state.json` and restored it on boot. The `events.jsonl` sitting next to it was write-only: its payloads carry ids and a scalar or two, so nothing could rebuild state from them.

I add a real event log (`src/ledger`) that records the full entity on every mutation, so folding it reproduces engine state exactly. A few things fall out of that:

- `fold(ledger) == state.json`, checked against the running server (`npm run test:ledger-e2e`)
- after a SIGKILL that never got to write a snapshot, a fresh boot rebuilds state from the ledger (`npm run test:ledger-resume-e2e`)
- `verify-claims` folds a committed golden to a committed hash with a second, independent reducer, so a bug in either implementation fails the build (now 27/27, was 24/24)

Writing that first E2E is what caught the only real bug in here: `retest.updated` mutates the finding as well as the retest, so the log has to capture both or the fold drifts.

## Scope, honestly

Replay re-derives a *recorded* run. It does not re-run the agents, whose output isn't deterministic and gets captured once as data. v1 covers the CRUD contract events; multi-entity side effects with no id in their payload, and deletes, are still open.

## Commits

1. `feat(ledger)` core: fold, canonical hash, sinks
2. `feat(server)` record the full entity at the `emitContractEvent` choke point
3. `test(ledger)` E2E + committed golden + verify-claims check
4. `feat(server)` resume-from-ledger on boot

## Checks

Ran the full CI job locally (lint, typecheck, test 305/305, doctor, verify-claims, no-fitting, no-self-fitting, gate, prompt-audit, smoke) plus both ledger E2Es. All green. Remote CI hasn't fired because a fork needs its workflows enabled once from the Actions tab.

author: frobware
body:
This adds XDP frags support so an XDP program compiled with a `SEC("xdp.frags")` section can attach natively to an interface with a large MTU, where a non-frags program is otherwise rejected with `ERANGE`.

The core is a single eligibility rule, `dispatcher.FragsEligible`: an XDP dispatcher is loaded with `BPF_F_XDP_HAS_FRAGS` only when it is non-empty and every member program is frags-capable, mirroring libxdp's all-or-nothing policy. The flag is a property of the dispatcher as a whole rather than a per-freplace-member flag, and a non-frags member exposed to fragmented packets can silently misbehave, so a mixed set downgrades the dispatcher to non-frags. That downgraded dispatcher then attaches fine on a normal MTU and is refused with `ERANGE` on a jumbo one, leaving the previous frags dispatcher intact via atomic rollback.

A one-shot kernel probe (`haveXDPFrags`) degrades gracefully on kernels older than 5.18, which reject the unknown flag at load: the flag is stripped and the program loads as non-frags rather than failing. Each program's frags capability is persisted (`has_xdp_frags`, migration `00003`) and reported through `dispatcher get` and `dispatcher list` as `is_xdp_frags`, plus per member.


## Test plan

`make bpfman-compile`, `make lint-go`, the unit tests, and the `.bpfman` e2e suite all pass. Frags-specific e2e cover native jumbo attach (driver mode confirmed via `ip -d link`), the mixed-member downgrade, and the jumbo rejection with atomic rollback.

author: tvburger
body:
## Summary

Closes the runtime half of [akasecurity/engineering#3](https://github.com/akasecurity/engineering/issues/3). Bundled rules are already gated by a CI adversarial-probe battery (`redos.test.ts`); this closes the remaining gap for regex rules that arrive from a **pulled or custom pack** (read from the local SQLite installed-packs snapshot), which previously reached `scan()` — synchronous and uninterruptible — with zero timing verification.

- Extracted the existing probe battery into a reusable module (`packages/detections/src/security/redos-probe.ts`) and added `checkRuleTiming`, used by both the CI gate (unchanged behavior) and the new runtime path.
- Added a `rule_probe_cache` SQLite table + repository so a rule's safe/quarantined verdict is measured **once, ever**, and persists across the short-lived hook process's invocations.
- Extended the `DataGateway` port and `StandaloneDataGateway` to read/write that cache.
- Added `filterUnsafeRules`, wired into rule registration (`runtime.ts`'s `ensureInitialized`) so only pulled/custom-pack rules go through the gate — bundled rules bypass it, since they're already CI-gated. A quarantined rule is excluded and logged to stderr, never silently dropped. A wall-clock pass budget protects against a pack containing many never-before-seen slow rules at once.
- Documented the two-tier defense in `skills/write-detection-rule/SKILL.md`.

**Scope decision:** a heavier "true isolation" approach (worker thread + hard timeout, an actual guarantee rather than a heuristic) was evaluated and deliberately deferred — filed as a follow-up: [akasecurity/engineering#42](https://github.com/akasecurity/engineering/issues/42).

Full design rationale and task-by-task plan: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-22-runtime-rule-redos-bound-design.md`, `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-22-runtime-rule-redos-bound.md`.

## Review notes

Built task-by-task with a review gate after each task, plus a final whole-branch review. The final review caught two cross-task issues no single task's diff could see (both fixed, with new regression tests, and re-verified):

1. A rule the wall-clock backstop skipped (never measured) was being persisted as **permanently** quarantined — could have silently dropped safe rules from a large custom pack forever. Fixed: unmeasured rules are excluded only for that pass, not cached, so a later invocation gets a real chance to measure them.
2. A cache-read or measurement error wasn't caught locally, so it propagated up and skipped the *entire* scan instead of just the one rule. Fixed: a cache-read failure now falls through to a fresh measurement; a measurement failure quarantines just that rule.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter @akasecurity/schema test`
- [x] `pnpm --filter @akasecurity/detections test` (includes the unchanged 101-bundled-rule CI gate)
- [x] `pnpm --filter @akasecurity/persistence test`
- [x] `pnpm --filter @akasecurity/plugin-sdk test`
- [x] `pnpm --filter @akasecurity/plugin-runtime test`
- [x] `pnpm turbo run test` (full workspace, 26/26 tasks passing)

## Summary

- switch the application, local tooling, and GitHub Actions from Node.js 20 to Node.js 24
- update `@types/node` and the lockfile to the Node.js 24 line
- align the README and repository guidance with the new runtime

## Why

Node.js 20 is end-of-life, and Vercel will stop accepting new Node.js 20 deployments on October 1, 2026. The repository's `package.json` engine pin was still forcing Vercel builds and Functions to Node.js 20.

## Impact

- Vercel builds and Node.js Functions use Node.js 24
- local development and CI now target Node.js 24
- no database migration or production environment-variable change is required
- Preview verification used a branch-scoped `INTERNAL_API_ORIGIN`; production configuration is unchanged

## Validation

- clean `npm ci` with Node.js 24.18.0 / npm 11.16.0
- `npm run verify`
  - 215 test files passed, 6 skipped
  - 1,918 tests passed, 58 skipped
- `npm run test -- --coverage`
  - statements 86.61%
  - branches 77.59%
  - functions 90.27%
  - lines 86.93%
- `npm run build`
- Vercel Preview deployment completed successfully
- passive smoke passed, including durable health, triage, and storage janitor dry-run
- active chat and character-import runner probes passed
- authenticated chat message completed end to end and returned an assistant response

## Follow-up

Protected Preview deployments currently return 401 for the experimental translation trigger because that fire-and-forget request does not forward `x-vercel-protection-bypass`. This is not a Node.js 24 regression and does not block the supported chat path; it will be handled separately.

author: rparundekar
body:
## Summary

Adds `hero-skills:wayfare` — a control plane treating the private `.plans/` store as the system of record between the source repo and a HERO.md-configured target-design repo — and introduces a `planning` work-item status with a human ready-mark gate, threaded through every emitting and consuming skill. Self-review then hardened the store and wayfare's git sinks (including an `ext::` RCE fix) and added durable regression coverage.

## Changesets

### 1. `feat(plans-store): add planning status with human ready-mark gate`
**Files:** `scripts/hero-lib.sh`, `skills/{think-it-through,one-shot,harden,handoff}/SKILL.md`
Work-items emit as `status: planning`, rendered as `plan` rows by `hero_ready_items` and never READY regardless of dependencies. Only the user flips an item to `todo` (`ready_marked:` date, canonically defined in think-it-through's format block). one-shot gains a dispatch row so a planning match asks for the ready-mark instead of re-grilling a duplicate; harden and handoff emit through the same gate.

### 2. `feat(wayfare): add control-plane skill over the .plans store`
**Files:** `skills/wayfare/SKILL.md` (new), `HERO.md`, `README.md`, `skills/init-hero/SKILL.md`
Features are typed bindings from source paths to the target-design repo (`## Wayfare` block in HERO.md; linear/wiki/infra connectors deferred as explicit `none`). Pins freeze refs as immutable SHAs (content snapshots for hand-bound URLs) with a persistent bare-mirror cache. Gates guard `order`, which emits hermetic work orders on PR-only branches; `ready` is the human gate, `do-next` re-verifies and stages the next READY order for one-shot, `drift`/`resync` compare pins to the world and replan gaps.

### 3. `fix(plans-store): reject unknown status and validate repo refs`
**Files:** `scripts/hero-lib.sh`, `scripts/hero-lib.test.sh`
`hero_ready_items` treats any status outside `planning|todo|in-progress|done` as `invalid` + a loud warning (a `status: plan` typo previously reached one-shot with no ready-mark). New `hero_normalize_repo_ref` validates/normalizes a repo ref before it reaches git — closing an RCE where `target-repo: ext::sh -c "…"` passed `hero_field` and executed. 16 new regression checks (70 total).

### 4. `fix(wayfare): harden config loading, pins, and gates per self-review`
**Files:** `skills/wayfare/SKILL.md`, `skills/one-shot/SKILL.md`, `skills/think-it-through/SKILL.md`
target-repo/target-branch validated in Step 0 (rejection disables the substrate loudly, not silently); pin asserts a real SHA before writing; G3 fails on `UNREACHABLE`; new G6 checks `feature:` integrity; `kind` default and id-namespace disjointness documented; stale producer rosters and an over-reaching canonical-definition claim fixed.

## Test Plan
- [x] `bash scripts/hero-lib.test.sh` — 70/70 (planning gate + repo-ref allowlist added)
- [x] Full pre-commit suite green (markdownlint, shellcheck, codespell, detect-secrets, validate-plugin, audit)
- [x] RCE fix verified: a malicious `ext::` target-repo disables the target substrate and executes nothing
- [x] Six-agent self-review (code / silent-failure / test / comment / type-design / security) — all findings applied

## Follow-up
- `hero-lib.test.sh` isn't wired into pre-commit yet — a separate PR should add it so all 70 checks gate commits.

_Generated using hero-skills._

author: zmievsa
body:
## Summary

- mark the OpenAPI API-version parameter as required when omitted versions are rejected
- keep the parameter optional when `api_version_default_value` supplies a routable static value or async default
- keep unroutable static defaults required and normalize documented date defaults to OpenAPI's date format
- preserve required path-version parameters and distinguish route-version examples from real server defaults

## Root cause

Cadwyn used each generated route's version example as the FastAPI dependency's Python default. FastAPI therefore emitted `required: false` even when Cadwyn's middleware had no server-side default and routing rejected an omitted version.

This fixes the dependency signature that FastAPI uses to derive OpenAPI instead of post-processing the generated schema. Static defaults are checked against Cadwyn's date-waterfalling or exact-string routing rules before they make the parameter optional.

## Validation

- public OpenAPI and request behavior regressions for required headers, valid and invalid static defaults, async defaults, string versions, and path parameters
- full tox suite across Python 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, and 3.14, including per-version `ty` checks
- 100% coverage, tutorial, lint, docs, links, and package build checks

Closes #277

author: itkujo
body:
**Stacks on #4 (`feat/p1a-tanstack-start-scaffold`) — merge that first.** This branch is based on P1a, so the diff against `main` includes P1a's commit. Ports the remaining public pages out of the client-only SPA into `web-next/` as server-rendered routes. Markup and behaviour are moved across unchanged; the only structural change is that each `.tsx` + `.lazy.tsx` pair collapses into a single route file, and the `useEffect` + `useState` fetches become route loaders. ## API base URL — the decision P1c and the camera-pages phase build on `API_BASE` was the relative string `/api`, which works in the browser but throws in a server loader where there is no origin. `web-next/src/lib/api.ts` now branches on `import.meta.env.SSR`: ```ts const API_BASE = import.meta.env.SSR ? (process.env.API_URL ?? 'https://nationcam.com/api') : '/api' ``` - **Browser** keeps the relative path, so it still goes through the same-origin nginx `/api` proxy — no CORS, no new config, unchanged from the SPA. - **Server** reads `API_URL`. In production set it to the internal address nginx forwards to (e.g. `http://api:8080`) so SSR skips a public round trip. Documented in the new `web-next/.env.example`; **Coolify needs this env var set at the P1c cutover.** - **Dev** leaves `API_URL` unset and falls back to production's public read-only API — the same source P1a's dev `/api` proxy already reads, since the Go API does not run locally. `import.meta.env.SSR` is replaced at build time, so the client bundle keeps only the relative branch and never references `process`. Anything that needs a base URL should import the helpers from `lib/api.ts` rather than re-deriving one. ## Per-page meta — server-rendered, from real data `lib/seo.ts` returns the `head` payload (title, description, `og:*`, `twitter:*`, canonical). Curled against `node .output/server/index.mjs`: ``` /locations Live Cameras by State | NationCam Louisiana Live Cameras | NationCam Venice Marina Live Cameras — Louisiana | NationCam Add Your Camera | NationCam NationCam — Live Cameras Across America Alabama<, >Louisiana<, >Coming Soon<, href="/locations/louisiana" /locations/louisiana →

Venice Marina

,

Westwego River Cams

, Venice 1 / Venice 2 / Venice 3 / Mississippi River Cam /locations/louisiana/venice-marina → Venice 1 / Venice 2 / Venice 3 ``` An unknown slug returns a real **404** status with the ported "State not found" panel, instead of a 200 with an empty page. ## Sitemap + robots `/sitemap.xml` is a server route generated from live API data — 55 URLs (3 static + 50 states + every sublocation): ``` HTTP/1.1 200 content-type: application/xml; charset=utf-8 cache-control: public, max-age=3600 https://nationcam.com/ https://nationcam.com/locations https://nationcam.com/contact https://nationcam.com/locations/alabama ... https://nationcam.com/locations/louisiana https://nationcam.com/locations/louisiana/venice-marina https://nationcam.com/locations/louisiana/westwego-river-cams ``` `public/robots.txt` now carries `Sitemap: https://nationcam.com/sitemap.xml`. ## Contact form — stub left in place, deliberately `routes/contact.tsx` is the old form verbatim, including: ```ts // TODO: Submit form data to server setSubmitted(true) ``` There is no backend endpoint, so it still validates required fields and fakes success. **No backend was invented for it** — a separate task owns adding the endpoint and wiring the submit. ## Notes for the camera-pages session - Route files live at `src/routes/locations/$slug.index.tsx` and `$slug.$sublocationSlug.tsx`. A per-camera page is a new child; `/locations/{state}/{sublocation}/{camera}` was deliberately **not** created here. - Use `lib/seo.ts` for meta and add the camera URLs to `routes/sitemap[.]xml.tsx` when camera slugs exist. - Loaders that 404 should `throw notFound()` after catching, matching the two location routes — that is what produces the real 404 status. - `tsconfig.json` gained `"@tanstack/react-start"` in `types`: nothing in `src/` imports it, so its module augmentation adding `server.handlers` to route options was not being loaded and the sitemap route failed to typecheck. Required for any future server route or server function. - `AdvertisementLayout` was **not** ported — ads are out of scope for this phase — so the ported pages render their content directly instead of inside the ad rails. - `ContactCTA` was restored to the home page (P1a had dropped it because `/contact` did not exist yet). - Public assets the ported hero needs were copied over: `logos/`, `buttons/`, the Louisiana and Venice Marina hero videos, and `logo192/512.png` for the OG image. ## Definition of done ``` $ npm run build → ✓ built in 276ms / ℹ Generated .output/nitro.json $ npm run lint → (eslint, no output, exit 0) $ npx tsc --noEmit → clean, 0 errors ``` P1a's 5 type errors were all `Link` targets for routes that did not exist (`/locations`, `/contact`, `/locations/louisiana`). All five are fixed by registering the real routes — nothing suppressed. `git status` shows changes confined to `web-next/`. Browser console on `/locations`, `/locations/louisiana`, `/locations/louisiana/venice-marina` and `/contact`: no hydration errors or warnings, no theme flash (P1a's `themeInitScript` still runs in `` before paint). The only console output is `[StreamPlayer] fatal HLS error … manifestLoadError`, because `StreamPlayer` loads HLS through `/api/stream-proxy`, which only exists on the Go API — it 404s against a local Nitro server. Pre-existing P1a behaviour, unrelated to this port. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: yashwin
body: Resolves A4A-2905 A4A-3022 A4A-3021 A4A-2937 A4A-2936 ## Commits - https://github.com/Automattic/wp-calypso/pull/112885/commits/1486db44690: the shared, configurable site tree - https://github.com/Automattic/wp-calypso/pull/112885/commits/fce099f8651: the WordPress.com/CIAB section declarations - https://github.com/Automattic/wp-calypso/pull/112885/changes/2d84a1112d677c54643a468c61279feaeaea3263: the A4A adoption. ## Proposed Changes * The new dashboard now builds site pages from one shared set of screens. Each dashboard variant (WordPress.com, CIAB, A4A) declares which site sections it offers: domains, plans, backups, scan, performance, monitoring, deployments, logs, and settings. * Agency site pages move to the same `/sites/…` URLs the other dashboards use. The agency copies of the backups, scan, and activity screens are deleted — A4A now reuses the shared ones. * A4A decides who can open a site by agency membership, and gates Backups and Scan by the agency's licenses. When a license is missing, the page shows a simple "not enabled" message instead of a purchase upsell. * A4A site pages gain Performance, Monitoring, Deployments, PHP/server logs, and Settings. * The activity log, backups, and scan are now recognized as available on self-hosted Jetpack-connected sites, since they work through Jetpack. WordPress.com and CIAB still limit those sites to the overview page, so nothing changes there. * Agency client users are now redirected to their subscriptions area from any other page. * New tests check that each declared section registers exactly its own pages and nothing else. body:
## What does this change do?

A live `orders:create` X-Ray trace showed `benzene_transport: <missing>` on the outer pipeline stages (`ApiGatewayLambdaHandler → BenzeneMessageLambdaHandler → SqsLambdaHandler → SnsLambdaHandler`), only resolving to the real transport (`sns`) further down.

That's a consequence of the multi-transport AwsMesh services: each Lambda hosts every transport, and the AWS Lambda router **probes each transport handler in turn** until one matches. Every probed-and-declined stage runs *before* any transport pipeline records itself, so both the X-Ray subsegment decorator (`Benzene.Aws.Lambda.XRay`) and the OTel span decorator (`Benzene.Diagnostics`) tagged it `benzene_transport = <missing>` — noise that reads like a defect in a trace viewer.

This change makes both decorators **omit the transport tag while `ICurrentTransport.Name` still reads the unresolved sentinel**, so only stages under the matched transport carry it.

- New shared `TransportNames.Unresolved` constant (value unchanged, `"<missing>"`) that `CurrentTransportInfo` now defaults to — single source of truth, so the decorators' guard can't drift from the sentinel definition.
- **Metrics tags are intentionally left as-is:** that `<missing>` fallback only fires when `ICurrentTransport` is unregistered, it's read once per message *after* resolution, and a metric dimension wants a stable bucket rather than a conditionally-dropped tag.

## Related issue

Follow-up to #43 (observed on that example's deployed traces).

author: samdefmacro
body:
The last consensus item from the post-layer-5 roadmap. Adversarial review verdict: **SAFE-TO-DEPLOY** (no BLOCKER, no MAJOR).

On a **deterministic** consensus `validate-block` failure — keyword in a tight allowlist (`:missing-input`, `:duplicate-txid`, `:coinbase-not-mature`, `:insufficient-funds`, `:non-final-tx`, `:bad-sequence-lock`, `:bad-coinbase-height`, `:coinbase-too-large`) — `perform-reorg` PHASE B (and `activate-block`'s post-reorg incoming-block failure) marks the failing block-index entry `:invalid` and propagates to its descendants (Core BLOCK_FAILED_CHILD), before rollback. Header admission also marks a header extending an `:invalid` parent. This activates the already-wired `:invalid` download-walk abort + prune, so a doomed fork stops being re-validated.

**The entire risk is classification** — poisoning a *recoverable* block would re-wedge the node. The review verified the allowlist is provably tight: the merkle gate runs before every poison check (corrupt non-witness bytes → `:bad-merkle-root`, excluded), block height/position is header-committed, and perform-reorg reconstructs the fork block's own path-independent state. `:script-failed` / witness-commitment / sigops keywords are **deliberately excluded** (they consume witness bytes the block hash doesn't commit). Transient `:reorg-refused` and `:corrupt-undo` poison nothing (locked by negative tests). `reconsiderblock` clears the whole `:invalid` subtree for operator recovery.

6 new hermetic tests (73 checks), incl. the two critical negatives; no regressions (reorg 317/0, ibd 326/0, headers 36/0). Consensus-critical — merged with sign-off.

author: boristyshkevich
body:
Closes #372

## What changed

- upgraded Vitest and `@vitest/coverage-v8` together to 4.1.10 and migrated the removed worker-pool configuration
- adapted stricter mock typings and made real CodeMirror fixture teardown deterministic
- added focused edge, callback, race, and bounded-queue coverage for Vitest 4's AST-based V8 remapping without lowering any repository threshold
- preserved the Dashboard viewer's entry generation guards so superseded tile and Filter-source workers cannot mutate state or issue obsolete requests after waiting in the six-worker pool
- removed the temporary Dependabot major-version ignores and refreshed the dependency policy comment and changelog

## Root cause

Vitest 4 remaps V8 coverage through AST ranges more precisely than the previous 3.x stack. Existing tests still passed, but the new mapping exposed same-line branches, callbacks, and guards that the older mapping had credited together. The migration therefore needed focused tests plus a small amount of caller-invariant cleanup. Happy DOM also made an undestroyed CodeMirror observer visible as an asynchronous teardown failure.

Generation checks at the start of `runTile` and `runFilterSource` remain required: a wave reserves generations before submitting work to a bounded pool, so an item can be superseded while queued. Regression tests hold six workers pending, supersede the queued seventh item, then prove it exits without a request or state/provider mutation.

One separate defense-in-depth `destroyed` guard remains intentionally excluded from coverage: the current caller checks the same state immediately before entering that path, but retaining the guard protects future callers.

## Validation

- `npm audit` — 0 vulnerabilities
- `npm test` — 166 files / 5,001 tests; 100% statements and lines; all global and per-file coverage gates pass
- `npm run build` — production single-file artifact builds successfully
- `npm run test:e2e` — 264 tests pass across Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit

author: sdilshan91
body:
## What
Closes two deferred follow-ups on the payroll reprocess path.

### DF-61-conc — per-runId concurrent-reprocess interlock (user-decided: mutex, not xmin)
`PayrollRunProcessor.ProcessAsync` now takes a **per-runId Postgres SESSION advisory lock** (`pg_try_advisory_lock`, keyed on the runId, engaged only on Npgsql) so two concurrent `ProcessAsync` on the **same** run cannot both replace-clean + re-insert slips → duplicate `ReviewPending` slips (never a double-pay, but wrong). The loser **no-ops cleanly** (never throws → no Hangfire retry-storm). Retry-after-completion edge: after acquiring the lock it reloads committed state and **skips** a `ReviewPending` run whose marker is already null. Different runs/tenants are never serialized. InMemory falls through to a null lock → byte-identical legacy behaviour (34 InMemory reprocess tests green).

### DF-61-pg — real-Postgres coverage arm
New `PayrollReprocessReconcilePostgresTests` (Testcontainers `postgres:17-alpine`): real-PG variant of the reconcile marker arms (**stale marker re-enqueued + reset survives a fresh-context reload**; fresh/null/Processing skipped; tenant isolation) plus the interlock arms (no-op-while-held / proceed-after-release / different-runId-not-blocked / already-satisfied-skip / marked-rerun-proceeds). **10/10 green on real Postgres.**

## Verification
- `dotnet build` clean; new PG suite **10/10**; InMemory reprocess suites **34/34** (no regression).
- **Auditors:** `@integration-enforcer` **WIRED** (safe to merge); `@test-authenticator` **AUTHENTIC 10/10** (all arms mutation-sensitive).

## Traceability
- TC-PAY-003-16 (DF-61-pg) + TC-PAY-003-17 (DF-61-conc) created + bound to US-PAY-003 / AC-3.

## Known LOW residuals (filed, non-blocking — see DEFERRED-FOLLOWUPS)
- **DF-61-conc-retry** (LOW): under `EnableRetryOnFailure`, a transient reconnect can move work to a different pooled connection than the one holding the session lock, degrading the interlock to the un-locked baseline for that run — the reconcile sweep backstops it (never a double-pay). Documented as a caveat on `TryAcquireAsync`.
- **DF-61-conc-approval-race** (LOW, **pre-existing** — not introduced here): a reprocess racing into `AwaitingApproval`/`Approved`/`Rejected` would replace-clean slips + revert to `ReviewPending`, un-submitting the approval. Mirrors the original Finalized/Cancelled-only guard.
- **DF-61-conc-slip** (LOW, test): a real-slip duplication arm (current interlock arms use zero-employee runs; the contended-no-op is already mutation-proven).
