body:
## Summary

Closes finding #5 (Next #3) from the `2026-07-22` (`1b428f6`) maintainability assessment.

The "assessment link goes stale the same day a new assessment supersedes the old one" pattern had recurred three cycles running (`180a3db`→`9eb3a9a`, `9eb3a9a`→`1b428f6`), each time predicted by the outgoing assessment about its own successor, each time fixed with the same two-line patch that just set up the next recurrence. Found a **third** live instance while implementing this: `tests/contract/README.md` was pointing at `384e5de`, several cycles further stale than either `README.md` or `docs/README.md`.

**The fix**: `docs/MAINTAINABLE_ARCHITECT_V4_ASSESSMENT.md` is now a permanent, stable path - no date, no revision hash. Every external pointer (`CLAUDE.md` ×3, `README.md`, `docs/README.md`, `tests/contract/README.md` ×2) links there once and never needs updating again. The hash-suffixed naming convention still exists, but only in `docs/archive/`: each new assessment cycle now archives the *outgoing* content under a `..._<date>_<revision>.md` name and overwrites the stable path with the new cycle's content - flipping which name is "live" versus "archived," rather than creating a new hash-named file and repointing every link at it every time.

A naming-convention note is added near the top of the assessment file itself, so the next cycle (human or AI) has the instructions in the one place they'll actually be looking.

Docs-only - no code change.

## Test plan
- [x] `gofmt -l .` clean (docs-only, but confirms nothing else broke)
- [x] `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` - all pass
- [x] `golangci-lint run ./...` (root) and `cd tools/generator && golangci-lint run ./...` (separate module)
- [x] Full-repo grep confirms zero remaining references to either the old hash-suffixed live filename or the stale `9eb3a9a`/`384e5de` pointers anywhere outside `docs/archive/`'s own historical chain-link banners (which correctly still resolve hop-by-hop and don't need rewriting)

body:
## What

Fixes documentation typos and factual copy-paste errors in the M4, M5, and PHM2008 dataset/evaluation classes, found during the 2026-07-19 Nixtla site QA review.

## Why

Several docstrings and doc pages had been copy-pasted between the M3/M4/M5/PHM2008 modules without updating the dataset-specific details, leaving factually wrong descriptions of what each method does.

## How

- Spelling: `bechmark`→`benchmark`, `competiton`→`competition`, `recevie`→`receive`, `Wheter`→`Whether`.
- `PHM2008.load()`'s docstring said "Downloads and loads M3 data." (copied from the M3 loader) — now says PHM2008 data, matching what the method actually downloads/loads.
- `M5Evaluation.evaluate()`'s docstring said "according to M4 methodology" and its `Returns` block described M4's `OWA`/`SMAPE`/`MASE` columns — now correctly describes M5's WRMSSE methodology and its actual return shape (single `wrmsse` column indexed by `Level_id`, verified by reading the method body).
- `docs/m5.html.md` had an entire "Kaggle-Competition-M5 References" section that was actually about the Favorita Kaggle competition (NWRMSLE metric, Favorita leaderboard entries and citations) — removed, since fabricating new M5/WRMSSE benchmark citations to replace it isn't something I can do responsibly without a verified source.
- Removed a stale commented-out M3 dataset URL in `phm2008.py`, a leftover from the same copy-paste origin.
- Corrected the M5 bottom-level series count (30,480 → 30,490 — 3,049 products × 10 stores, per the M5 competition's own published dataset description).

Leaves `datasetsforecast/long_horizon2.py` untouched — its `arxiv.org` link typo is already covered by #106.

## Testing

- [x] `python3 -m py_compile` on all 3 changed `.py` files (no new warnings/errors beyond pre-existing unrelated `\s` regex warnings in `phm2008.py`).
- [x] Verified both docstring corrections against the actual method bodies (traced `PHM2008.load()`'s download URL and file reads; traced `M5Evaluation.evaluate()`'s full computation to confirm it returns a `wrmsse`-only frame, not `OWA`/`SMAPE`/`MASE`).
- [x] Confirmed no other stray instances of the fixed typos remain anywhere in the repo.

## Checklist

- [x] Title follows conventional commits format
- [x] PR is focused on a single concern (documentation accuracy)
- [x] Self-reviewed the diff before requesting review
- [x] No secrets, credentials, or PII in the diff

author: alt-glitch
body:
## Summary
Restores nix CI (ripped out in 9eb0bcd60 "to be re-added later when we have more stable ci flows") in a deliberately minimal, opt-in form:

- **Triggers only** on `workflow_dispatch` (job: check|build) or adding the `ci/nix` label to a PR — no push/PR auto-runs, so it costs nothing until asked.
- **`scripts/nix-ci.sh`** is the single entrypoint: `check` = `nix flake check -L` (16 checks on x86_64-linux), `build` = cold-builds `.#default .#tui .#web .#desktop`. Devs run exactly what CI runs.
- Reuses the orphaned-but-intact `.github/actions/nix-setup` composite (Determinate installer + Cachix `hermes-agent`, `CACHIX_AUTH_TOKEN` optional).
- The old workflow's stale-`npmDepsHash` diagnosis/auto-fix machinery is **not** restored: since #48883 (`importNpmLock`, hashless) that failure class is structurally gone, and `.#fix-lockfiles` no longer exists.

Note for merging: the `ci/nix` label needs to exist once (`gh label create ci/nix --description "run nix CI on this PR"`).

## Test plan
- YAML validated (PyYAML + yq), `bash -n scripts/nix-ci.sh`, mode 755
- `scripts/nix-ci.sh check` locally = the same `nix flake check -L` that passed green today at cbc1054e2
- Trigger gating: job-level `if` requires dispatch or exact label `ci/nix`

author: adamcongdon
body:
Closes #195, closes #196. **Merging this to beta cuts beta.51** — and does so through the corrected pipeline, so beta.51's installers are named consistently and no run can race.

## #195 — release concurrency (regression of #107)

Two pushes to beta in quick succession (the #192/#194 merges) fired **two overlapping release runs**: they raced on the git tag + manifest push, one failed with a non-fast-forward `failed to push some refs`, and the beta.50 release ended up with mixed `beta.82`+`beta.83` dmgs. That mismatch window is what surfaced as the **HTTP 409** on your in-app update.

Fix: top-level concurrency group, `cancel-in-progress: false` so an in-flight run finishes (tag + manifest) before the next starts and recomputes the next beta.

## #196 — installer version drift (regression of #106)

`package-windows` and `package-macos` computed `version = jq .version package.json (0.0.1) + github.run_number` → `0.0.1-beta.82/83`, drifting from the real `compute-version.ts` tag (`1.0.0-beta.50`) and differing across racing runs. The **binary was already stamped correctly** (`getCurrentVersion()` returns the right value); only the installer filenames drifted.

Fix: expose the build job's `qual_version` as a job output; both installer jobs consume `needs.build.outputs.qual_version`. Now tag, manifest, baked binary, and installer filename all agree.

## Verification

- `yaml.safe_load` parses; **actionlint** clean on every changed region (the only findings are pre-existing shellcheck `info` on the untouched original version steps).
- `needs.build.outputs.qual_version` wiring confirmed — both packaging jobs already `needs: build`.
- Scope: single file, +36/-12.

## After merge — how beta.51 proves the fix

- One release run (not two); its dmgs are named `privacy-screen-1.0.0-beta.51-darwin-*.dmg`; manifest `version` = `1.0.0-beta.51`; the manifest push to beta is never rejected.

python3 -m build --sdist --wheel --outdir dist
```

The unit suite creates a dedicated build environment, installs `build`, setuptools, and wheel once, and builds both artifacts from a temporary source copy. It verifies required archive paths and rejects forbidden metadata, then installs each artifact into a separate environment and runs:

```bash
qacraft doctor
python -m qacraft eval-list
qacraft evaluate --input <bundled-example>
qacraft release-check --json
qacraft install feature-qa --agent codex --destination <project> --apply
qacraft verify-install --agent codex --destination <project>
qacraft uninstall --agent codex --destination <project> --apply
```

## Resolved CI findings

1. The runner Python did not provide global setuptools, so direct `setup.py sdist` from the test process was not portable. Artifact tests now use a dedicated build environment.
2. PEP 517 executes `setup.py` without guaranteeing the project root is importable. `setup.py` now loads `qacraft_build.py` by absolute path.
3. Both corrections were validated by the final single Python 3.12 job.

## Safety and Actions usage

- One canonical source tree; no generated bundle committed
- No runtime dependencies
- No runtime network, customer, production, or external-system access
- No package-index upload or publication claim
- No automatic user-global installation
- No new workflow job
- Existing PR-only Python 3.12 job remains
- No automatic post-merge workflow
- Diagnostic artifact runs only after failure and expires after one day

## Next PR phase

Phase 3.3 will expand verified agent adapters only after official project-level discovery paths and behavior are confirmed. Each new adapter will receive an independent manifest, lifecycle/coexistence tests, documentation, and the same preview-first safety model.

Advances issue #16 without closing it.

## Resumen

Fija la **primera versión estable (1.0.0)** como línea base y monta el **esquema de versionado** para que, de aquí en adelante, cada PR se declare como una versión distinta (MAYOR/MENOR) o un fix (PARCHE) según la cantidad y naturaleza de sus cambios. Incluye además la funcionalidad de **auto-recuperación de contraseña** como parte de esta primera versión.

## Tipo de cambio (SemVer)

- [x] **MENOR** — nueva funcionalidad retrocompatible (auto-recuperación) + establecimiento del versionado. Publica la línea base **1.0.0**.

**Versión objetivo:** `1.0.0` (primera versión etiquetada; base para futuros incrementos)

## Cambios

**Esquema de versionado**
- `CHANGELOG.md` — formato *Keep a Changelog* + SemVer, con la sección **1.0.0** que documenta el alcance entregado y un bloque **`## [Sin publicar]`** para acumular cambios futuros.
- `docs/versionado.md` — política `MAYOR.MENOR.PARCHE` con **criterios concretos para decidir** si un PR es una versión distinta o un fix, y el procedimiento de liberación (actualizar `app/__init__.py` + `pyproject.toml`, mover el bloque «Sin publicar», etiquetar `vX.Y.Z`).
- `.github/pull_request_template.md` — obliga a declarar el **tipo de cambio** y la **versión objetivo**, y a anotar el CHANGELOG.
- `tests/test_version.py` — impide que la versión se desincronice entre `app/__init__.py` (fuente de verdad), `pyproject.toml` y el `CHANGELOG.md`.
- `README.md` y `docs/guia-desarrollo.md` enlazan la política y el registro de cambios. `app/__init__.py` documenta que es la fuente de verdad de la versión (ya expuesta por `GET /healthz` y la metadata de la API).

**Auto-recuperación de contraseña** (incluida en la 1.0.0)
- Flujo de 3 pasos por el propio usuario: **identidad** (usuario + email deben coincidir) → **segundo factor** (código TOTP en vivo o un código de recuperación de un solo uso) → **nueva contraseña**.
- Doble interfaz (JSON `/api/web` y Jinja) con paridad; desafío efímero server-side (solo se guarda el hash del token; cookie httponly + SameSite=strict), TTL de 10 min y tope de intentos.
- **Anti-enumeración** en los dos pasos mediante desafíos «señuelo»: la respuesta y la latencia son idénticas exista o no la cuenta (cierre del hallazgo MEDIO de la revisión de seguridad).
- Al cambiar: valida la política, exige contraseña distinta, **revoca todas las sesiones** del usuario y envía una alerta. Migración Alembic `0004`.

## Verificación

- [x] `ruff`, `bandit` y `pytest` (cobertura ≥ 70 %) en verde; incluye 8 pruebas del flujo de recuperación y 3 de coherencia de versión. Migración Alembic == `Base.metadata`.

- [x] Recorrido real con Playwright del flujo de recuperación (claro y oscuro), con confirmación funcional de que la nueva contraseña inicia sesión.
- [x] Entradas registradas en `CHANGELOG.md` bajo la sección **1.0.0**.

author: jumaanebey
body:
Fixes the balance regression guard that's been red on `main` since ~July 14.

## Root cause
`campaignBase` picked its enemy-base template via `ENEMY_BASES[(stage-1) % length]`, coupling the **campaign** to the **raid** template pool. Commit `7e87a90` grew that pool 2→6 (for raid variety), which silently shifted the s12 Championship from `tech` (difficulty-2) to the `ridge` fortress (difficulty-6) at the same ×13.75 scaling. The T4 sim clear dropped from the tuned **46% → 15%** — a far harder final boss than was ever tuned. Confirmed by forcing the old template (→ 46% exactly) and `git show`ing that the array was length 2 when 46% was tuned.

## Fix
- **Decouple (root cause):** pin campaign geometry per stage by template **id** (`CAMPAIGN_TEMPLATE_IDS`), independent of `ENEMY_BASES` order/length. Adding raid templates can never re-shift campaign difficulty again. Ridge fortress kept as the intended finale.
- **Retune:** soften campaign turret-dmg coeff 13→9 so the fortress boss lands at **38%** (band 30–62) — a legitimate "demands actives even at T4" boss.
- **Docs:** update BALANCE.md target 46%→38% + the sim assertion message, per the doc's own "move a target → update the band and the doc" rule.

## Verification (all green)
- `npm test` — 41/41 pass
- `npm run build` — clean
- `npm run balance` — exit 0, all targets within band (Championship T4 = 38%; raids still T3 46% / T4 67%, unaffected — the change is campaign-only)

CI (`test → build → balance`) should pass on its own now — no admin-merge needed.

author: tutkli
body:
## Summary

- Closes [#1375](https://github.com/tutkli/forty-cdk/issues/1375). `LiveAnnouncer` now stamps `MODAL_EXEMPT_ATTRIBUTE` on each live region so screen-reader announcements raised over an open modal (the documented toast-over-modal contract, #1083/#1087) actually reach assistive tech — fixing a silent WCAG 4.1.3 status-message failure.
- Root cause: `#createRegion` appended the `polite` / `assertive` regions to `<body>` unmarked, so `InertSiblingsStack` inerted and `aria-hidden`ed them while a modal dialog / drawer was open (both on the initial sweep and via its late-sibling `MutationObserver`). A `ForToast` silences its own DOM and routes through `LiveAnnouncer`, so the announcement landed in an inerted region and was never heard.
- Fix stamps the marker in [live-announcer.ts](projects/forty-cdk/core/src/live-announcer/live-announcer.ts) **before** the region is appended, so the late-sibling observer skips a region created while a modal is already open too. The attribute is already exported from `forty-cdk/core` and honoured by `InertSiblingsStack` for both pre-existing and late children — no other change needed.
- Added three cases to [live-announcer.spec.ts](projects/forty-cdk/core/src/live-announcer/live-announcer.spec.ts): the marker is present at construction, existing regions stay non-inerted when a modal opens, and a region created while a modal is already open stays non-inerted (flushing the observer microtask).

- [x] `pnpm typecheck` passes.

- [x] `pnpm build` — library compiles cleanly via ng-packagr; all postbuild entry-point checks pass.

author: alex0xhodler
body:
Verifier **PASS, LOW, 6/6** (additive-only diff, fully guarded, honesty framing independently confirmed, tests bite). Adds explicit acquisition capture to `analytics.js`.

## Diagnosis first (the honest part)
The reported "undefined referrer" is **not** a stripping/capture bug:
- `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin` (vercel.json:51) is standard — it does **not** strip `document.referrer`.
- The official Mixpanel lib auto-captures `$referrer`/`$referring_domain`/`utm_*` (confirmed from `mixpanel-js` source); `track_pageview:false` doesn't disable it.
- `analytics.js` already sends `referrer: document.referrer || 'direct'` — never literally undefined.

So the undefined values on the recent sessions are the **correct** value for referrer-less bot/direct traffic — they corroborate the crawler read rather than indicating a bug.

## The real, forward-looking fix
The app relied solely on the library's super properties and added no acquisition props of its own. Since item 064 makes the 069 spotlight links carry `utm_*`/`ref`, this makes that traffic robustly attributable on our **own** events:
- `captureAcquisition()` — parses `utm_source/medium/campaign/term/content`, `ref`, ad click-ids, and `referring_domain`; captured **once at landing** (survives SPA nav clearing the URL); fully guarded; absent params emit **no key** (never `"undefined"`); values capped 200 chars.
- Spread into every event's `getBaseContext`.

Additive only — existing `referrer` property, the 096 host-gate, and all track* helpers untouched. `analytics.js` ships unminified (no min regen). `test_analytics_acquisition.js` → 17/17, wired into `npm test`.

## Expectation-setting
Does **not** recover the current bot traffic's undefined referrers (those are correct). It hardens real referral/campaign attribution going forward — exactly what's needed before 069 goes out.

body:
## Motivation

Le check CI `Security audit` (`npm audit --audit-level=high`) est passé rouge sur toutes les PR (dont #236) suite à la publication d'advisories **CVE-2026** cet après-midi. **Aucune régression de code** — dérive purement environnementale (mêmes vulns sur `main`).

## Diagnostic

Après `npm audit fix` (body-parser réglé, non-breaking), 2 HIGH restaient, **toutes deux enracinées dans les CVE libvips héritées de sharp** (CVE-2026-33327/33328/35590/35591, GHSA-f88m-g3jw-g9cj) :

| Vuln | Sévérité | Cause |
|------|----------|-------|
| `sharp` | high | notre devDep (`scripts/generate-pwa-icons.ts`) |
| `next` | high | `next@16.2.6 → optionalDependencies sharp@^0.34.5` (image optim) — le `via` est littéralement `sharp`, PAS une faille Next.js |
| `esbuild` | **low** | transitif (tsx/vite) — sous le seuil `--audit-level=high`, dev-only, non touché |

`next` épingle `sharp@^0.34.5` (< 0.35), donc un simple bump devDep laisserait la copie de next vulnérable. Le fix npm suggéré (`next@14.2.35`) est un **downgrade absurde** (casse App Router 16).

## Fix

`overrides.sharp = ^0.35.3` (même pattern que les overrides sécu existants : tmp, postcss, basic-ftp, ip-address, uuid) → force sharp 0.35.3 sur **tout l'arbre**, y compris la copie de next. + devDep alignée.

## Evidence

- `npm audit --audit-level=high` → **0 high** (reste 1 low esbuild, sous le seuil CI)
- `npm run build` → **next 16.2.6 build OK** avec sharp 0.35.3 (compat image optim vérifiée)
- `npm run icons` → 6 icônes générées OK
- `npm run typecheck` → clean
- sharp deduped 0.35.3 pour next ET le script

## Débloque

Cette PR merge en amont → #236 (engagements cockpit) et toutes les futures PR retrouvent un `Security audit` vert.

author: fmmenchi
body:
Release hardening + cleanup in one pass.

## Fix "bumps all projects" (nx #34542)
`nx release` in independent + conventionalCommits attributes **root-file** changes (`pnpm-lock.yaml`, workflows) to **all** projects → every one bumps (confirmed: api-client et al. bumped to 0.0.3 with zero commits). No config parameter exists ([nx #34542](https://github.com/nrwl/nx/issues/34542) is open). Workaround: the release job computes the projects whose **own** files changed since their last tag (`git log <tag>..HEAD -- <root>`) and runs `nx release --projects=<those>`. nx still bumps dependents. A workflow-only push now releases nothing.

## Serialize the release job
`concurrency: { group: release, cancel-in-progress: false }` — two quick merges no longer race on the tag push (the failure when #32 and the docs merge overlapped).

## Remove the placeholder packages
`api-client`, `config`, `api-contracts`, `core` were pure `nx g` stubs (each `foo() => 'foo'`, no code, no dependents). Removed via `@nx/workspace:remove`; a `.gitkeep` keeps the `server` scope folder.

## Docs
`AGENTS.md` + `.agent/releases.md`: scoped release + inline Slack.

author: irfndi
body:
## Plan §9 G2.5 — make the `AetherHook` oracle a REAL time-weighted average of POOL STATE

The correctness foundation the V4-native TP/SL/auto-recenter keeper (Phase 2) will verify triggers against. Isolated worktree off green `main`; **does not touch** `apps/*`, docs, fee semantics, or hook permission logic.

### Problem
- The 1024-slot observation buffer sampled `amountIn/amountOut` — the swap's **volume-dependent average execution price**, not the pool's terminal spot price. After any cross-tick trade, holding that value to the next observation yielded an incorrect TWAP regardless of time-weighting.
- `getCurrentTwap` accumulated a delta over **sample counts**, not elapsed time.

### Fix (`src/hook/AetherHook.sol` + 2 new errors in `src/lib/Errors.sol`)
- **Sampling:** `afterSwap` reads the pool's terminal tick via `StateLibrary.getSlot0(poolManager, key.toId())` (v4 `extsload` slot0) and stores `(timestamp, tickCumulative, tick)` — accumulating `tickCumulative += lastTick * elapsedSeconds` (int56 two's-complement, Uniswap-v3 `Oracle` style). Fee capture is byte-for-byte unchanged.
- **Read path:** `observe(poolId, secondsAgos[])` — binary search over the ring with linear interpolation between stored points and extrapolation from the latest terminal tick; `getTwapTick(poolId, secondsAgo)` = `(cum(now) − cum(then)) / elapsed`; `getCurrentTwap` / `getCurrentTwapInverted` convert the avg tick via `TickMath.getSqrtPriceAtTick` (FullMath, 1e18 scale; reciprocal for reverse pair direction).
- **Edge cases:** first observation lazily initializes slot 0 · identical-timestamp samples fold in place (no zero-delta slot → no div-by-zero) · zero window or window older than the retained buffer reverts (`InsufficientElapsedTime` / `InsufficientObservations`) · negative ticks/cumulatives supported · 1024-saturation wraparound walks `[oldest..newest] mod 1024` · `observationAt()` added for slot-level inspection.

### Tests — 134 passing (was 121), `AetherHook.sol` at **100%** statements/branches/functions/lines
- `test/unit/AetherHookTwap.t.sol` (new): deterministic multi-observation sequences with known elapsed times asserting the **exact** expected time-weighted tick *and* price across full/interpolated/exact-boundary/intra-span windows; cross-tick (+6000×30s / −6000×70s → −2400); a time-vs-sample-count discriminator; reciprocal identity at tick 0 / 6000 / small price + zero-price guard; interpolation/extrapolation exactness; negative cumulatives; 1100-observation ring wraparound verified against an independent trace; div-by-zero & insufficient-observations guards.
- `test/unit/AetherHook.t.sol` (reworked to the corrected semantics — nothing weakened): pool-state sampling, same-timestamp folding, exact cumulatives, revert guards, overflow; adds fuzzed two-tick exact time-weighting + TWAP-in-observed-range property.
- `test/fuzz/AetherHookInvariants.t.sol` (extended): handler drives random `(tick, Δt)` swap sequences and an independent model proves, after every action, that the stored cumulative matches exactly and TWAP ∈ [min, max] observed ticks — plus the original fee/access/buffer invariants.
- `test/shared/MockPoolManager.sol` (new): minimal `extsload` slot0 mock so the hook's **real** `getSlot0` read path is executed under unit + invariant fuzzing.

### Verification (acceptance gate)
```text
forge build     -> exit 0, 0 errors
forge test      -> 134 passed; 0 failed; 0 skipped
forge coverage  -> AetherHook.sol 100% (144/144 stmts, 163/163 branches, 28/28 fns)
                   project total 90.84% stmts / 92.42% lines (target >90%)
```

> Not merged — for review only. Deployment/contract immutability work (fee setter removal, Sepolia validation) belongs to later phases.

* **New Features**
  * Reworked TWAP calculations to use time-weighted pool ticks for more accurate price tracking.
  * Added tick-based observation queries and average tick retrieval.
  * Added direct and inverted TWAP price views.
  * Added clearer safeguards when observations or sufficient elapsed time are unavailable.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved handling of same-time observations, interpolation, extrapolation, and circular-buffer history.
  * Ensured TWAP results remain within observed tick ranges.

author: madsnorgaard
body:
## Why

Follow-up to the query-caching work (#548). The production Redis status page showed the two single biggest render-cache consumers were the local-tasks blocks: `saho_primary_local_tasks` (~9,019 variations) and `saho_secondary_local_tasks` (~8,968), varying by `route` + `url.query_args`.

Those blocks render editorial tabs (View / Edit / Delete / Revisions / ...) that are permission-gated - **anonymous visitors see nothing**. But Drupal still cached the empty render per route, and anonymous/bot traffic with endless tracking and facet query strings minted a fresh entry each time, which is what inflated them to ~18k combined variations.

## What

Adds a `user_role` (authenticated) visibility condition to both blocks, so anonymous requests skip rendering and caching them entirely. The ~18k anon variations collapse to a handful of real editorial ones.

## Verification (DDEV)

- Config applied via partial import (only the two block configs touched; `config:status` was clean beforehand).
- **Anonymous**: node pages render zero tab markup and stay HTTP 200 - confirmed no anon-visible tab is lost (there were none: verified before and after).
- **Authenticated**: full tab set intact - View / Edit / Delete / Revisions / Clone / Usage (Playwright, logged in as admin).

Pure config change; no custom code. On deploy this needs a `drush cim` like any config change.

author: guan404ming
body:
## Purpose

- With `--enable-mm-embeds`, loading multi-MB embedding tensors blocks the API server's event loop, stalling all concurrent requests
- Defer the loading to the shared thread pool, the same way every other modality is already handled
- Error semantics and the sync path are unchanged
- Not a duplicate: issue #49317 covers a different stage; no open PR touches this path

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/entrypoints/unit_tests/test_chat_utils.py` (on Modal L4)
- Loop-stall microbenchmark: parse a chat message carrying a base64 image-embeds tensor while a 1ms ticker task measures the longest event-loop stall (median of 5)

## Test Result

- 63 passed, 0 failed

| embeds size | max loop stall (ms) base → fix | parse wall time (ms) base / fix |
|---|---|---|
| 8 MB | 7.1 → 2.0 | 7.2 / 5.0 |
| 32 MB | 23.1 → 13.5 | 23.2 / 22.3 |
| 128 MB | 110.0 → 54.2 | 110.1 / 108.8 |

Baseline stall equals wall time (the loop is fully blocked). The fix removes the blocking except for GIL-bound segments of tensor deserialization inside the worker thread, and lets other requests interleave at await points.

---

AI assistance was used for this change (Claude); every line was reviewed by the submitter.

author: brunoguerios
body:
## What

Adds `NoPathReason::AmountTooSmall` so dust quotes stop being reported as `no_graph_path`.

Bellman-Ford reported every zero routed-output as `NoGraphPath`, conflating "no route exists" with "the amount is too small to route." During SPFA, each successful hop simulation now checks whether the amount entering the hop covers that hop's own gas; if not, the failure is labeled `amount_too_small` instead. Input-side and single-hop, so healthy and too-large orders never trip it (too-large fails via simulation error). PathFrankWolfe inherits the behavior; the reason flows through aggregation into the `quote_failure` log.

Motivation: steady ETH↔USDC `no_graph_path` failures on Base turned out to be dust-sized requests (confirmed by replay), indistinguishable in the logs from real routing gaps.

Scope: Bellman-Ford + PathFrankWolfe. MostLiquid already reports dust as `insufficient_liquidity` and is unchanged.

## Compatibility

Reason label only: order status stays `NoRouteFound`, wire `QuoteStatus` unchanged, no OpenAPI drift.

## Performance

The check is gated on the already-computed `net_candidate <= 0`, keeping it off the hot path. A/B replay benchmark (recorded market, interleaved runs): ungated cost was ~4% per quote; gated is within measurement noise of main. Details in the PR comment.

## Caveats

- Gas-aware `amount_too_small` requires `token_in` to be priced; unpriced dust falls back to `no_graph_path` (under-report, never a mislabel).
- The flag is per-solve: a no-path solve that also contains a dust hop on some branch can be labeled `amount_too_small`. Rare, label-only.

## Testing

608 tests pass (clippy / fmt / doc / OpenAPI drift clean). Key cases: direct + mid-route dust → `amount_too_small`; too-large revert, low-rate pool with healthy input, connector-excluded, unreachable → `no_graph_path`; gas-aware tiny input → `amount_too_small`.

author: ronenmars
body:
The iOS and Android version-bump steps in `deploy.yml` passed `GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}` to `admin-merge-pr.sh`, so `gh pr create` authored the bump PR as `github-actions[bot]`.
GitHub gates workflow runs on bot-authored PRs behind manual maintainer approval, which left every ship with an orphaned "This workflow is awaiting approval from a maintainer" run in the Actions tab.

The merge itself was never blocked — `admin-merge-pr.sh` squash-merges with `--admin` using `GH_PAT` immediately after creating the PR — so this was cosmetic noise rather than a stuck pipeline.

This passes `secrets.GH_PAT` as `GH_TOKEN` in both bump steps so the PR is authored by the repo owner and no approval-gated run is created.
The merge path is unchanged: `MERGE_TOKEN` already resolved to `GH_PUSH_TOKEN` (`GH_PAT`).

author: awlevin
body: ## Problem An "Untitled" conversation with literal id `greeting` (`/assistant/conversations/greeting`) appears in every user's sidebar (reported by Vargas, reproduced by Aaron). ## Root cause The empty-state greeting calls `POST /v1/btw` with `conversationKey: "greeting"`. When the key has no conversation mapping, `btw-routes.ts` uses the key itself as the conversation id and calls `getOrCreateConversation("greeting")`. Since #38291 moved DB row creation into `getOrCreateConversation`, that call unconditionally persists a `standard` (sidebar-visible) `conversations` row — violating the btw side-chain's "no messages are persisted" contract and leaking the row into every sidebar the first time the greeting cache misses. ## Fix - Add a per-call `ephemeral` option to `getOrCreateConversation` that skips row creation (stripped like `taskRunId` so it never merges into stored conversation options). `Conversation.loadFromDb()` already tolerates a missing row. - `btw-routes.ts` passes `{ ephemeral: true }` only on the unmapped-key path; mapped keys keep reusing their real conversation row. - DB migration `342-delete-stray-greeting-conversation` removes the leaked row for existing installs — only when it carries no messages. If a user opened the stray conversation and chatted in it, the row is user data and is left untouched. Safety of the residual edge: a real send to a row-less conversation id can't corrupt state — the explicit-`conversationId` send path 404s when no row exists, and the keyed path creates its row via the conversation-key store before any message insert. ## Testing - New `conversation-store-ephemeral.test.ts`: ephemeral calls create no row; non-ephemeral calls do. - New migration test: stray empty row deleted; row with messages preserved; unrelated conversations untouched; idempotent. - Updated `btw-routes.test.ts` call-signature assertions. - `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean, eslint clean, migration-prefix-guard green. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ---

author: rat0323
body:
## Summary

- compress large uploaded profile avatars before persisting them to `localStorage`
- keep profile updates atomic so a failed quota write does not poison the in-memory profile
- surface a clear quota error in the profile settings UI
- await asynchronous avatar persistence in both intercepted upload paths
- add regression coverage for quota rollback and avatar optimization

## Root cause

The profile upload path mutated the object returned by `localProfilePrefs()` before calling `localStorage.setItem`. When a Base64 avatar exceeded the storage quota, the write threw but the oversized `imageUrl` remained in `state.profilePrefs`. Later edits, including display-name-only changes, retried the oversized payload and failed again.

Uploaded avatars were also stored as their original Base64 data URL, with an allowed length far larger than the practical `localStorage` headroom of the Codex renderer.

## Behavior after this change

Large multipart avatar uploads are resized to at most 512 px and encoded as WebP/JPEG toward a 220,000-character data URL target. Profile mutations use copies and only replace runtime state after persistence succeeds. Quota failures leave the previous profile intact and return a user-facing error.

## Validation

- `node --check scripts/codex-live-token-cost.js`
- `node tests/codex-live-token-cost.test.cjs`
- verified in Codex++ that a previously failing avatar was persisted as a 512x512 WebP data URL and rendered successfully in the sidebar

## Intent Rebuild the real reachable Today and Home screen in native SwiftUI to match the captain-approved Lavish prototype pixel-close on iPhone 16 Pro across full, sleep-only, HRV-only, and no-readings states. Preserve live HealthKit readiness, sleep, HRV, plan, weekly statistics, and heatmap bindings while replacing presentation with shared Baseline design-system tokens and components. Use the approved segmented ring treatment, render only metric cards backed by available readings, and render no reading cards at all in the no-readings state. Include the prototype floating tab bar where shown, keep any shared navigation change additive, avoid the protected agent-tool and Cloud Functions surfaces, and include simulator screenshots for all four states in evidence. Validate behavior with focused render and summary tests, especially the absence of metric cards when no readings exist, then ship a PR against develop. ## What Changed - Rebuilt the Today home screen in native SwiftUI to match the approved prototype: segmented readiness ring, plan/week/sleep/HRV/heart-rate-zone/movement-balance cards rendered only when backed by real readings (no metric cards at all in the no-readings state), plus a new `TodayWeeklySummary` that derives session counts, cardio/training time, HR zone buckets, and a front/back muscle heatmap from completed training data (vector assets generated via `scripts/generate-today-muscle-map-assets.mjs`). - Added the prototype floating tab bar to `MainTabView` on top of the native TabView (preserving tab lifecycle so Train tears down HR capture on leave), with bottom clearance applied across tab roots and pushed destinations, a Train empty-state chat entry, and week-bounded SwiftData queries with corrected completed-log-to-session pairing. - Added `TodayHomeRenderTests` (all four availability states, asserting no reading cards without readings), `MainTabShellRenderTests` (real shell across all tabs, system bar hidden, Train unmount), and `TodayWeeklySummaryTests`, with simulator screenshots for each state committed under `evidence/`; all 7 tests passed, freshly re-capturing the four Today availability-state screenshots and five shell screenshots, which I visually verified: sleep-only and HRV-only render exactly one backed metric card, the no-readings state renders none, the segmented sleep ring and floating tab bar match the approved prototype, and the real live-bound shell shows the new Today home with empty-store data; the diff touches no protected agent-tool or Cloud Functions files and the worktree stayed clean. - Evidence: Today - full state (sleep + HRV cards) (local file: /var/folders/m3/qgj4gq85293_kqsxz93qlp3m0000gn/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01KY5DEZMDB6WPA50JK5W12B51/today-full.png) - Evidence: Today - sleep-only state (local file: /var/folders/m3/qgj4gq85293_kqsxz93qlp3m0000gn/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01KY5DEZMDB6WPA50JK5W12B51/today-sleep.png) - Evidence: Today - HRV-only state (local file: /var/folders/m3/qgj4gq85293_kqsxz93qlp3m0000gn/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01KY5DEZMDB6WPA50JK5W12B51/today-hrv.png) - Evidence: Today - no-readings state (zero reading cards) (local file: /var/folders/m3/qgj4gq85293_kqsxz93qlp3m0000gn/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01KY5DEZMDB6WPA50JK5W12B51/today-none.png) - Evidence: Real shell - Today tab with live bindings and floating tab bar (local file: /var/folders/m3/qgj4gq85293_kqsxz93qlp3m0000gn/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01KY5DEZMDB6WPA50JK5W12B51/shell-today.png) - Evidence: Real shell - Plan tab (floating bar, no system bar) (local file: /var/folders/m3/qgj4gq85293_kqsxz93qlp3m0000gn/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01KY5DEZMDB6WPA50JK5W12B51/shell-plan.png) - Evidence: Real shell - Train tab empty state (local file: /var/folders/m3/qgj4gq85293_kqsxz93qlp3m0000gn/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01KY5DEZMDB6WPA50JK5W12B51/shell-train.png) - Evidence: Real shell - Profile tab (local file: /var/folders/m3/qgj4gq85293_kqsxz93qlp3m0000gn/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01KY5DEZMDB6WPA50JK5W12B51/shell-profile.png) - Evidence: Real shell - pushed Heart Rate Zones destination clear of bar (local file: /var/folders/m3/qgj4gq85293_kqsxz93qlp3m0000gn/T/no-mistakes-evidence/01KY5DEZMDB6WPA50JK5W12B51/shell-profile-zones.png) ## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
⚠️ **Review** - 1 info - 🚨 `Baseline/Features/Profile/MainTabView.swift:47` - Intent requires "keep any shared navigation change additive", but MainTabView hides the system tab bar for all tabs (`.toolbar(.hidden, for: .tabBar)`) and overlays the floating bar on top, while only TodayHomeView adds bottom clearance (90pt spacer). PlanView's bottom-pinned chat bar ("Ask about your week…", 8pt bottom padding) is now covered by the floating tab bar and largely un-tappable, its undo bar clips it, and WorkoutView (new Train tab) and ProfileView bottom content lost the tab-bar safe-area inset and render under the always-on-top bar. Conversation is now only reachable from the Plan and Train tabs. When a scheduled workout is restarted, repeated, or has a later discarded session, older completed logs get the newest session's startedAt; the finishedAt > startedAt guard in TodayWeeklySummary.build then silently drops to the exercise-duration fallback, and a re-completed workout can attribute the wrong start time, misstating weekly TRAINING time. author: lonelysun1990
body:
## Summary
- **Legacy harvest**: fixed a chain of real bugs preventing 6 of 7 real monthly-update PDFs from ever downloading — an attachment-link overlay-scoping bug, a batch-date fallback that used today's date instead of the email's own month, a popup-viewer PDF-capture mechanism for attachment links that never fire a native download event, an OS-focus-stealing/tab-leak side effect of that fix, and finally an extraction crash on two real months with no "Financial Overview" section (a mid-month acquisition and a management-company transition).
- **McNeil occupancy**: replaced the only existing occupancy source (a rent-roll attachment covering at most 1 of 22 real months) with a new 3-source pipeline read from every monthly email — a direct "Occupancy: X% vs Y%" statement, a vacant-unit-count narrative, and vision-LLM chart reading — merged by priority with a disagreement-warning safety net. Occupancy coverage went from 3/22 (all stale) to 21/22 real months.
- **Dashboard**: wired up a previously-defined-but-unused CSS flag so months that fail arithmetic reconciliation are visibly marked instead of shown as fully trustworthy.

## Notable finding
The final whole-branch review caught a real integration bug no single task's review would have: occupancy priority (direct statement > vacant-unit narrative > chart) was only enforced *within* a single email's own sources, not across the fold of all archived emails — since each email's chart covers ~12 trailing months, a later email's lower-priority chart reading could silently overwrite an earlier email's higher-priority narrative value for the same month. Fixed by computing occupancy globally across all archived batches before merging once, with a regression test (caught and fixed once more on re-review, when the first version of that test turned out not to actually exercise the conflict).

## Known follow-ups (documented, not fixed here)
- The one-time backfill script only reached 3 of ~19-22 historical McNeil months (no emails-tab pagination, scoped to pre-existing local batch dirs).
- The vacant-unit-narrative regex misses "N vacancies" phrasing (only matches "N vacant units") — degrades gracefully to the chart source.
- Two real Legacy months (2026-03, 2026-05) are flagged `reconciled: false` on the dashboard due to a known, pre-existing vision-LLM cell-misreading issue on a dense trailing P&L table — not caused by this branch.

## Test plan
- [x] 199/199 tests passing (`npm test`)
- [x] Compliance audit clean (no direct CashFlowPortal API access)
- [x] Every task individually reviewed (spec compliance + code quality)
- [x] Whole-branch review performed, findings fixed and re-reviewed
- [x] Live-verified against the real portal: all 7 Legacy months and 21/22 McNeil months confirmed with real, content-verified data
- [x] Dashboard flag visually verified in a browser

body:
## Bug

En la pestaña **Consultar**, al escribir una consulta que ocupa varias líneas (por debajo del alto máximo), aparecía una **línea vertical** en el borde derecho del input, junto al botón de enviar. Es la barra de scroll del `<textarea>`: el campo no fijaba `overflow`, así que heredaba el `overflow: auto` por defecto y, en dispositivos con scrollbar clásico, cualquier desbordamiento subpíxel durante el autoajuste la dibujaba.

## Fix

- `#copilot-chat-input` arranca con `overflow-y: hidden`.
- `copilotChatAutosize` cambia a `overflow-y: auto` **solo** cuando el contenido supera el alto máximo (96px) y el campo queda topado; por debajo, permanece oculto.

Así el input crece sin dibujar scrollbar y solo permite scroll cuando de verdad hay más texto del que cabe. Verificado en Chromium: `overflow-y: hidden` con 2-3 líneas, `auto` al toparse en 96px.

author: acdlite
body:
`partialFallback` is an internal flag in the build output that controls the behavior of ISR. When it's enabled, in a Cache Components app, pages that are not generated at build time are upgraded to a full ISR entry upon the first request.

This is a useful feature but there's a risk it could lead to an explosion in ISR costs, because even a prefetch request is sufficient to trigger an upgrade.

The desired behavior is that we only trigger an upgrade for an actual navigation request, or if a link opts into prefetching with the `prefetch` prop.

Currently there's no way for ISR to differentiate between a shell prefetch request (no prefetch prop on the link) and an actual prefetch (`prefetch={true}`). The plan is to introduce additional configuration to the build output that specifies which headers should trigger which operations.

So by default, this PR turns the `partialFallback` flag back off until the new mechanism is available to us.

However, for apps that opt into Partial Prefetching, we will continue to set `partialFallback` to true. That's because in a Partial Prefetching app, per-link prefetch requests are always opt-in. So even without additional support at the ISR behavior, we avoid an unexpected surge in ISR costs by not sending the prefetching request in the first place. There will still be a single request per distinct route (_not_ per distinct URL!), which we will optimize later.

author: jeroensoeters
body:
## Summary

Two rendering fixes across the interactive table views (`inventory`, `status` watch) and the simulate preview.

- **Header highlight consistency.** The simulate view coloured the selected column header with a Selection background and the sorted column with the blue accent, while the tables used bright white. All three now render the active (sort-by) and selected (cursor) column headers as bright white bold — the sort arrow alone marks the active one — with no background bar and no accent colour. `statuswatch` and `inventory` also brighten the active column when the cursor has moved off it (previously dim).
- **Per-cell sort styling lag.** `sync()` applied the row data before the sort state, so `SetRows` sorted the table by the previous column while the styled cells were ordered by the new one. Since `applyCellStyles` maps styled cells to rendered rows by position, per-cell styling (e.g. the `⚠ unmanaged` warning colour) landed on the wrong rows and rendered plain until the next event re-synced — the "wrong until you press up/down" symptom. Setting the sort state before the rows aligns both orders in the same frame. Includes a regression test.

author: asnowfix
body:
## Summary

Closes #49. `runAgent()` in `cmd/homedrive/main.go` previously only built and ran the Changes-API puller; the watcher, push syncer, bisync ticker, real MQTT publisher, and HTTP control server all existed as tested packages but were never instantiated together. `ctl status/pause/resume/resync` were no-op log lines.

This PR introduces an `Agent` type (`agent.go`, `agent_run.go`, `agent_control.go`) that wires everything together per `PLAN.md` §3.2, and rewires `ctl` (`ctl.go`) to make real HTTP calls against the running agent.

## What changed

- **Watcher → push syncer**: `Agent.pumpWatcherEvents`/`dispatchWatchEvent` convert `watcher.WatchEvent` into the `syncer.Event`/`syncer.DirRename` channels consumed by the push worker pool (`push.workers`, `push.retry.*` from config). `/pause` stops forwarding (drops+logs); `/resume` re-enables it.
- **Pull loop**: owned by `agent_run.go` (`runPullLoop`/`pollOnceGuarded`) rather than calling `Puller.Run` directly, so each Changes-API cycle can take `bisyncMu.RLock()` — `syncer.Puller` had no built-in bisync coordination (see bug fix below).
- **Bisync ticker**: started from `Agent.Run`, sharing `bisyncMu` (`sync.RWMutex`) with the push syncer (`RLock`) and the pull loop (`RLock`), per §7.2.
- **MQTT**: `buildPublisher` constructs a real `mqtt.Client` when `mqtt.enabled: true` (LWT, real `Topic`/`PublishJSON`), instead of always defaulting to `noopPublisher{}`. Added `mqtt.Client.Connected()` for `/healthz`.
- **HTTP control server**: `Agent` implements the `internal/http` `Pausable`/`Resyncable`/`Reloadable`/`StatusProvider`/`HealthChecker` interfaces (`agent_control.go`), started on `http.listen`.
- **`ctl` subcommands**: `ctl.go` makes real `GET /status` / `POST /pause|resume|resync` calls and logs the agent's actual JSON response, resolving the control-endpoint address from `--config`'s `http.listen` (falling back to `127.0.0.1:6090`).
- **Graceful shutdown**: SIGTERM/SIGINT cancel the run context; `Agent.Run` shuts the HTTP server down first (bounded 10s), then waits for watcher/pump/push-syncer/pull-loop/bisync goroutines to drain (in-flight push jobs finish, they are not aborted), then closes MQTT (LWT `offline`) and the Bolt journal. SIGHUP calls `Reload` (re-reads config; applies log level and the `dry_run` value reported by `/status` live — structural settings like `local_root`/`watcher.exclude`/`push.workers` require a restart, which is logged explicitly) instead of restarting the process.
- **Two pre-existing bugs found and fixed while wiring**:
  - `internal/syncer/bisync_ops.go`: the remote-to-local sync paths (`syncRemoteToLocal`, `resolveRemoteWins`) wrote an **empty placeholder file** instead of calling `RemoteFS.DownloadFile` (the method the Changes-API puller already used). Left as-is, the first real hourly bisync run would silently truncate any remote-only file to 0 bytes. Fixed by calling `DownloadFile`; strengthened `TestBisync_DetectsDrift_RemoteOnlyPulls` and `TestBisync_ConflictRemoteWins` to assert real downloaded content, not just file existence.
  - `syncer.Puller` never coordinated with the bisync mutex described in §7.2. Fixed at the wiring layer (`pollOnceGuarded`) rather than touching the tested `internal/syncer` package.
- **Testability**: added a local `remoteFS` interface in `adapters.go` (the union of what `rcloneSyncerAdapter` and `Agent.Status`/`Healthz` need — `syncer.RemoteFS` lacks `Quota`, `rcloneclient.RemoteFS` lacks `List`/`GetStartPageToken`/`DownloadFile`) so the whole `Agent` wiring layer can be exercised against a fake remote (`fakes_test.go`) instead of real rclone/Drive, per `homedrive-test-mocks`. `*rcloneclient.RcloneFS` satisfies it unchanged.

## Known gaps (not fixed here, explicitly out of scope per the issue)

- **rclone backend count**: `go tool nm` reports **2** backends linked into the binary (`drive` + a transitively-pulled `crypt`), not the required 1. Pre-existing — `internal/rcloneclient` and `go.mod` are untouched by this PR. Tracked by issue #51 per the issue text's explicit instruction not to fix the CI check here.
- **Pull correctness depends on #50**: this PR wires the pull loop to call `Puller.PollOnce` → `RemoteFS.ListChanges` exactly as it already existed. Per the umbrella issue #47's findings, `RcloneFS.ListChanges` is currently a stub that does one full walk and then returns empty forever — i.e. real incremental Changes-API polling isn't implemented yet. This PR does not change that; full "a remote change is reflected in the pull path" correctness lands with #50, as the issue #49 acceptance criteria anticipated. Everything downstream of `ListChanges` (conflict resolution, journal writes, MQTT events, loop prevention) is wired and tested against the interface as it stands today.

## Test plan

- [x] `go test ./homedrive/cmd/homedrive/...` — 47 tests, **80.2%** coverage, `-race` clean.
- [x] `go test ./homedrive/internal/syncer/...` — bisync tests updated to assert real downloaded content (regression guard for the placeholder-file bug).
- [x] `make test` (macOS, all packages) — green.
- [x] `orb run -m dev -- go test -race -count=1 ./homedrive/...` (OrbStack Ubuntu 24.04, real inotify) — green, including `internal/watcher` (confirms the one `TestWatcher_DirRenameLarge` flake seen once on macOS during this work is FSEvents-only, not a regression — passes both in isolation on macOS and on Linux).
- [x] `GOOS=linux GOARCH=arm64 go build -trimpath -ldflags="-s -w" ...` → **20 MB** stripped binary (< 25 MB budget).
- [x] Integration tests exercise the real wiring end-to-end with a fake remote (never rclone/Drive in tests): local file write → watcher → pump → push syncer → remote (`TestAgent_LocalEditPushesToRemote`), and graceful shutdown draining an in-flight job before returning (`TestAgent_GracefulShutdown_DrainsInFlightJob`).
- [x] Real embedded-broker (`mochi-mqtt`) tests prove `buildPublisher` connects a real `mqtt.Client` when enabled (`TestBuildPublisher_MQTTEnabled_ConnectsRealClient`) and wires it into `/healthz`.

## References

- `homedrive/PLAN.md` §3.2 (runtime topology), §7.2 (bisync mutex), §12 (HTTP control endpoint) — Phase 14 entry added documenting this work.
- Issue #49, part of umbrella #47. Not deployed to the NAS (out of scope for this PR).

author: pi0x
body: ### 🔗 Linked issue resolves #4252, resolves TanStack/router#7403 (related: #4234, #4241, #4266, #4270, #4272, #4274) ### 📚 Description Routes owned by an **opaque catch-all** — a custom `server.ts` server entry (an H3 app with its own routes) or the SSR renderer (framework routers like TanStack Start) — are invisible to `nitro.routing.routes`. The dev middleware classifier therefore treated asset-tagged requests to them (`sec-fetch-dest: image`, asset extensions, …) as Vite assets and marked them `_nitroHandled`, so the user's handler could never run: `` served by a `server.ts` route, or a TanStack Start API route serving a thumbnail, died in a connect `finalhandler` 404. The two cases (`/image.png` is a real opaque route vs. a genuinely missing asset a naive SSR `/**` would render as a 200 page) cannot be told apart *before* dispatching — but they can from the **response**: - The pre-pass now splits non-explicit matches into **transparent** catch-alls (user route files, e.g. `routes/[...path].ts` — Nitro sees everything they can handle, so the existing `_nitroHandled` divert stays and they still never swallow Vite asset misses) and **opaque** ones (renderer / `serverEntry` `/**`, identified by their registered handler paths — or no match at all). - Opaque/no-match asset requests are stamped `_nitroAssetCheck` instead: Vite keeps first shot, and on a Vite miss the post catch-all dispatches to nitro and inspects the response. A 2xx **`text/html`** response means the catch-all rendered a page for a missing asset (#4234) → discarded via `next()` (same `finalhandler` 404 as before). Anything else — real asset types, JSON (deliberate API responses, TanStack/router#7403; sourcemaps), `text/plain` (bridge default for bare string returns), no content-type, non-2xx framework 404 pages, redirects — passes through verbatim. - Only `GET`/`HEAD` requests can be classified as asset loads at all (a `POST /upload.png` is never a browser asset load). Zero config, host-side only: no runtime/bundle changes and no production behavior change. All #4234/#4241/#4266/#4270/#4272 regression contracts stay covered by the existing tests. Verified against a real `@tanstack/react-start` app: API routes under `sec-fetch-dest: image` (extensionless, `.png`-param, and `?filename=x.png` shapes from #7403 / #4274) now return their JSON 200s, while genuinely missing assets and unmatched routes still 404. New regression tests (fail before, pass after, both builders): - `test/vite/server-entry.test.ts` + fixture — custom `server.ts` H3 app: asset-extensioned routes reachable under `image`/absent/`script` fetch dests (including a no-content-type string return and a JSON sourcemap), `POST` to an asset-extensioned route, missing assets still 404, navigations work. - `test/vite/app.test.ts` — the SSR catch-all can deliberately serve `/dynamic-asset.png` (`image/png`) and JSON API routes under `sec-fetch-dest: image` (#7403 shapes), while the missing-asset swallow contracts still hold against an HTML-rendering fixture. Known limitation (documented): opaque semantics require registration via `renderer`/`serverEntry` — a `/**` catch-all added through `routes:`/`handlers:` config or a module is still classified transparent and pre-empted for asset-tagged requests. Also includes `.agents/vite-dev.md` documenting the routing design, its issue lineage, and the invariants to preserve. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Summary
- add an exact loopback-only supervisor health route protected by a per-child 256-bit capability
- preserve `/api/health/deep` as an authenticated personal route while sharing one DB/pool health producer
- keep the wrapper's pool escalation and heartbeat-plus-stdout kill predicates unchanged
- remove healthy 15-second probes from response-body logs, wedge request tracking, and API performance samples

## Evidence
Live Environment #12 showed unauthenticated `GET /api/health/deep` returning `401` every 15 seconds. The wrapper deferred every kill because stdout and heartbeat remained healthy, proving the probe authority contract was broken while the multi-signal predicate worked.

## Security
The exact GET route reaches route-owned validation, then requires both loopback transport and a constant-time comparison against a per-child capability. Missing or invalid authority returns 404 before any DB probe. The capability is consumed from and deleted from the child environment at module load. No personal data route or principal scope is weakened.

## Verification
- `npm run build` passed
- no tests or standalone typecheck run under current policy
- full diff reviewed
- rollback: revert this PR or restore the prior wrapper probe path, with no schema changes

## Residual validation
Production proof requires publishing merged `main` to live Environment #12, then observing successful quiet supervisor polls and absence of recurring 401/API-policy warnings.

author: sausin
body:
## Summary

This PR adds a comprehensive offline test suite for the installer script and hardens the audio prompts download to be truly best-effort, ensuring a fresh install always succeeds even when sound mirrors are unreachable.

## Key Changes

- **New installer test** (`scripts/install_test.sh`): 177-line bash test that exercises the installer offline with a fake `commosd` binary and `file://` sound mirrors. Validates:
  - Fresh install writes valid `pbx.yaml` and admin password even when both sound mirrors 404
  - Auto-generated password never aborts the installer (SIGPIPE trap in `tr|head`)
  - Sounds download tries fallback mirror, extracts correctly, and cleans up temp files
  - `--no-admin-password`, explicit `--admin-password`, and `--force` flags work as documented
  - Existing config protection (refuses overwrite without `--force`)

- **Hardened sounds download** (`install.sh`):
  - Two-step download (fetch to temp file, then extract) so 404s and truncated transfers are caught cleanly
  - Primary mirror + fallback mirror support (`SOUNDS_URL_FALLBACK`)
  - Switched from FreePBX to Asterisk Project mirrors (official source)
  - Every failure path is a `warn` + `return 0`: the sounds step is now truly best-effort and cannot abort the installer
  - Temp tarball cleanup guaranteed even on extraction failure
  - Improved error messages distinguish between unreachable mirrors, invalid archives, and missing sentinel files

- **Password generation robustness**:
  - Explicit `return 0` in `gen_password()` to prevent SIGPIPE from `tr|head` aborting under `set -e`
  - Redirects stderr to `/dev/null` to suppress spurious warnings

- **Documentation updates**:
  - Updated all references from FreePBX to Asterisk Project / Sangoma
  - Clarified that sounds download is best-effort and voicemail falls back to a beep
  - Added comments explaining the SIGPIPE trap and two-step download strategy

- **CI integration** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`):
  - Installer test runs first (seconds, no toolchain needed) before Rust build/test

## Implementation Details

The installer test uses a temporary directory with:
- A fake `commosd` binary that just prints a version string
- A valid Asterisk sound pack (tar.gz with `vm-intro.ulaw` sentinel)
- A corrupt archive to test extraction-failure handling
- `file://` URLs to avoid network dependencies

The sounds download now uses a temporary file (`mktemp`) to avoid feeding partial/404 responses into tar. Both mirrors are tried in sequence; the first successful extraction wins. The temp file is always cleaned up, even on failure.

All changes maintain backward compatibility: existing `SOUNDS_URL` overrides still work, and the installer behavior is unchanged for successful downloads.

author: fuma-ops
body:
Fixes everything you flagged — the cropped switch clip, un-followable chrono, and the audio mix.

### ✂️ No audio ever cropped (the yoga rule)
Every step's timer is now `ceil-to-5( max(rep-time, clip-length + tail) )`. I measured each clip and baked the lengths in. The **switch step went 6 s → 15 s** (the switch clip is **11.3 s** — that's why it was cut) so it plays in full and gives a real moment to reposition. Verified across glutes sessions: **0 cropped clips, every duration a clean multiple of 5**.

### 🔢 Rep-driven, followable timing
Work time = **reps × tempo** (tonify 3 s/rep, strengthen 5 s/rep), and rep counts are chosen so the product is a whole 5 s number → an **exact beat per rep**. So a 15-rep move lasts exactly long enough to do 15 controlled reps:
- Beginner 10 / Intermediate 15 / Advanced 20 reps (tonify); 8 / 10 / 12 (strengthen).
- Each side of a one-sided move gets its **own full paced window** → `Side 1 (full) → Switch 15 s → Side 2 (full)`.

### ⏱️ A rep pacer you can actually follow

author: carauz1905
body:
Closes #40.

## What
Starting a VM under an active Windows hypervisor (Hyper-V/VBS) can intermittently fail with a host-platform error that clears on a quick retry:
```
VBoxManage.exe: error: Unresolved (unknown) host platform error. (VERR_UNRESOLVED_ERROR)
VBoxManage.exe: error: Details: code E_FAIL (0x80004005), component ConsoleWrap, interface IConsole
```
This was observed live: a TabVM start failed with `VERR_UNRESOLVED_ERROR`, and an immediate direct `VBoxManage startvm` succeeded — confirming it is transient. TabVM correctly surfaced the real error (the #21 diagnosability fix), but the user can only "fix" it by clicking start again.

## Change
The existing bounded start/resume retry (`runControlWithLockRetry`, added for session-lock contention in #21) already retries `isLockContention`. This broadens the retry predicate to `isRetryableStartError = isLockContention || isUnresolvedHostError`, so a transient host-platform init failure is retried the same bounded way (3 attempts, 400ms backoff, context-aware). A genuinely permanent error still surfaces after the retries are exhausted (~0.8s max added latency), so nothing permanent is masked.

## Tests
- `TestStartVM_RetriesOnUnresolvedHostError` (TDD: written first, confirmed RED, then GREEN) — first `startvm` returns `VERR_UNRESOLVED_ERROR`, retry succeeds. Existing lock-contention retry/exhaust tests still pass. `go build`, `go vet -unsafeptr=false`, `go test ./...` green.

Patch release material (v0.3.1).

author: sanjeevrg89
body:
## What this adds

Materials for the July 23 guest session (**AI training, tuning, inference and RL on Kubernetes**, Sanjeev Ganjihal) plus its companion assignment, built to the FDE track's conventions and scaffolded on Moment Search per our discussion.

**`FDE/Assignment_3_AI_Infra_K8s/`**

- **README.md**: the assignment. Students extend Moment Search toward RAG at scale by replacing the hosted LLM with an open-source vision model they serve themselves, in two rungs. Rung A: their first time serving, one box on RunPod with vLLM (framing updated per your note that students have only consumed models through OpenAI-style APIs so far). Rung B, graded: the same model as a two-replica vLLM fleet on GKE behind a LoadBalancer, the app rewired via its three `LLM_BASE_URL` env lines, then three break-and-fix experiments observed through the running app: the lying readiness probe, timing the capacity chain when scale-up buys a node, and a zero-drop rollout under a streaming answer. Quota request framed as real FDE work; teardown graded; ~$5 inside the GCP free credit; kind-cluster fallback if quota stalls.
- **demo/**: the live-demo runbook for the session, five minutes scripted minute by minute (Moment Search answering with citations from the fleet, a pod killed mid-question while the answer keeps streaming, a live Spot GPU node purchase on scale-out), with `provision.sh` / `teardown.sh` so an engineer can reproduce everything end to end in ~45 minutes and ~$3 before class.
- **SESSION_NOTES.md**: the session recap students keep (four workload shapes and their K8s patterns, the 5-layer AI infra stack, the parallelism toolbox, the field guide, July 2026 receipts with sources).
- **AGENTS.md** non-negotiables, **manifests/vllm.yaml** (every field commented), **eval/** rubric + automated scorecard script run against the live cluster before teardown.

Also adds the Assignment 3 row to the FDE track table.

## Two implementation notes worth knowing

- Moment Search shows the LLM actual video frames, so the served model must be **vision-capable**: the manifests use `Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct` with `--limit-mm-per-prompt image=8`. A text-only model fails at the first question.
- The GPU node pool is created with `--enable-autoscaling --max-nodes 3`; without it, the "watch the cluster buy a node" experiment hangs in Pending forever.

Happy to iterate on any of it so the demo and assignment fit the rest of the course.

author: griffin-goepper
body:
Categorization resolution was paying O(transactions × rules) regex/LIKE work on every `transactions_with_category` scan (~0.7s of one core per scan at 9k txns × 247 rules; /goals scanned once per cap). Migration 0013 adds `category_match_cache` (transaction_id → matched rule's category) and rewrites the view to LEFT JOIN it.

**This is not a write-time category column.** Overrides still resolve read-time in the view; the retroactivity contract holds because every mutation of the matching inputs maintains the cache inside the same store call: `upsert_transactions` refreshes the upserted ids, `delete_stale_pending` deletes theirs, `add_rule`/`remove_rule` rebuild in the same transaction (the rebuild IS the retroactive application), and `init()` rebuilds after applying migrations. The match SQL has one home (`_match_cache_insert_sql`); CLAUDE.md documents the invariant that any new write path touching transactions/rules must maintain the cache.

Also in this slice, riding the same read-path work:
- Net-worth series now seeds every account at the window boundary (an account with no snapshot at window start carries its earliest known balance there), so charts start at the window edge and connecting an existing account doesn't render as a new gain. `/api/v1/net-worth` gains `complete_from` (first date with full snapshot coverage) so clients can disclose estimated history.
- `spending_by_category` gets a monthly bucket helper to batch cap-history reads.

## Summary

This PR introduces a complete cart and order workflow, including cart management, order confirmation, order history, and order cancellation. It also refactors the order domain, migrates all price values to `BigDecimal`, and improves data consistency and transactional safety.


---

## ✨ Cart

### Added

- Introduced `Cart` and `CartItem` entities (one cart per user)
- `CartItem` now references `Product` directly
- Added `CartRepository` with `@EntityGraph` for eager loading
- Added `CartItemRepository`
- Implemented `CartService`
  - Get-or-create cart
  - Add item
  - Update quantity
  - Remove item
  - Stock validation
  - Upsert behavior for existing items
- Added `CartController`
  - `GET /v1/cart`
  - `POST /v1/cart/items`
  - `PUT /v1/cart/items`
  - `DELETE /v1/cart/items/{productId}`
- Added request/response DTOs
- Added mapper extension functions
- Added Swagger documentation with examples
- Added dedicated cart error codes (`CART_001`–`CART_005`)

---

## 🛒 Orders

### Reworked order flow

- Orders are now created directly from the user's cart
- Cart items are grouped by store during checkout
- Cart is cleared after successful confirmation

### Added

- `OrderStatus`
  - `PROCESSING`
  - `COMPLETED`
  - `CANCELLED`
- `OrderRepository`
  - user/status queries
  - pessimistic locking support
- `OrderItemRepository`
  - optimized `JOIN FETCH` queries
- Expanded `OrderService`
  - confirm order
  - order history
  - completed order items
  - order cancellation
- Added cancellation endpoint
- Added complete Swagger documentation
- Added dedicated order error codes (`ORDER_001`–`ORDER_002`)

### New endpoints

- `GET /v1/orders/completed`
- `POST /v1/orders/confirm`
- `GET /v1/orders/history`
- `PUT /v1/orders/{orderId}/cancel`

---

## 🔄 Data model changes

### Cart

- `CartItem`
  - `product_item_id` → `product_id`
  - quantity is now mutable
  - references `Product`

### Orders

- `OrderItem`
  - `product_item_id` → `product_id`
  - removed item status
  - references `Product`
- `Orders.totalPrice`
  - `Double` → `BigDecimal`
- `Orders.status`
  - now mutable
- Added deterministic ordering using `@OrderBy`

### Prices

Migrated all price fields from `Double` to `BigDecimal` across order, cart, discount, product, and response models.

---

## 🔗 Cross-domain updates

### Product

- Added trending products query based on completed orders
- Added product locking query

### Product service

- Trending products now use completed orders only

### Product item service

- Prevent deleting products that exist in orders

### Product rating

- Ratings now verify completed purchases through order history

author: princejonaa
body:
## What This Fixes

This PR removes friction points for first-time users by replacing confusing ValueError exceptions with clear, actionable error messages formatted as `<expected> + <found> + <user action>`. Additionally, it lowers video generation defaults to prevent immediate Out-of-Memory (OOM) failures on standard consumer hardware (like 16GB unified memory Macs), adds helpful tooltips to technical parameters, and syncs the documentation to reflect recently added capabilities.

## Error Message Changes

```python
# Before
raise ValueError("Draft model path cannot be empty.")
# After
raise ValueError("Expected a valid draft model path string but found an empty string. Please provide a valid Hugging Face repository ID or local directory path for the draft model.")

# Before
raise ValueError(f"Unsupported draft model type: {model_type}")
# After
raise ValueError(f"Expected a supported draft model type ('mlx-lm' or 'mlx-vlm') but found '{model_type}'. Please ensure your draft model type is set correctly in the node.")

# Before
raise ValueError(
    f"Expected a known resolved model type (e.g. 'mlx-lm', 'mlx-vlm', 'sam3') + Found '{resolved_type}' + Check the model path or force the model type manually"
)
# After
raise ValueError(
    f"Expected a known resolved model type (e.g., 'mlx-lm', 'mlx-vlm', 'sam3') but found '{resolved_type}'. Check the model path or try manually selecting the model type instead of 'auto'."
)

# Before
raise ValueError("Kokoro TTS generated no audio for the given text.")
# After
raise ValueError("Expected Kokoro TTS to generate an audio waveform but found none. This usually means the input text was empty or contained unprocessable characters. Try simplifying your text prompt.")

# Before
raise ValueError(
    "Expected a valid MLX conditioning dictionary from an MLX Load Flux Model node + Invalid or missing conditioning input + Ensure the MLX Load Flux Model node is properly connected"
)
# After
raise ValueError(
    "Expected a valid MLX conditioning dictionary from an MLX Load Flux Model node but found an invalid or missing conditioning input. Ensure the MLX Load Flux Model node is properly connected."
)
```

## Default Changes

- `num_frames` in `MLXVideoGenerator`: **16 -> 8**. Generating 16 frames of video via CLI subprocess is highly likely to trigger an OS-level hard-swap or crash on machines with 16GB unified memory if the user is unaware of the cost. Lowering to 8 ensures a higher likelihood of first-run success.

## Documentation Updates

- Updated the Core Capabilities table in `README.md` to explicitly mention `Kokoro` TTS integration under Audio, and added a new row for `Embeddings`.
- Updated the Architecture Map mermaid diagram to include previously omitted frontend nodes: `MLX Load Draft Model`, `MLX Batch Understand Image`, `MLX Generate Audio (Kokoro)`, and `MLX Generate Text Embedding`.

## Explicitly Out of Scope

- Refactoring the underlying string parsing or generation logic causing the missing audio / unexpected model type errors is out of scope. These are strictly UI and UX debt optimizations.

## Verification

- Verified all parameter keys remain unchanged (only defaults and `tooltip` metadata dictionaries were updated) to ensure backward compatibility with saved user workflows.
- Diff confirms no execution logic or tensor math was altered.
- All unit tests passed via `python3 -m unittest discover tests` and static verification passed via `make verify`.

---

author: amxx
body:
## Summary

Give ERC-7579 modules full control over their own uninstallation, reverting two previously merged behaviors that stripped that control away. In both cases the account is not stuck: a module that blocks its own removal can still be force-removed through a delegate call via `execute`.

### Revert #6390 — hook modules (`AccountERC7579Hooked`)

#6390 special-cased hook-module uninstallation so a bugged or malicious hook could not block its own removal by reverting in `preCheck`/`postCheck`. This reverts that: `_uninstallModule` goes back to the plain `withHook`-modified override (removing the inlined precheck/postcheck handling, the in-place `abi.decode` helper, and the `Bytes`/`LowLevelCall` imports it required), so a hook can prevent its own uninstallation by reverting.

#6390 was never released, so its pending changeset is dropped and it needs no new changeset.

### Revert #6142 — base modules (`AccountERC7579`)

#6142 (released in 5.6.0) swallowed reverts from a module's `onUninstall` hook so a buggy or malicious module could not block its own removal. This reverts that: `onUninstall` is called without catching reverts, so a module can now prevent its own uninstallation by reverting.

The `_uninstallModule` NatSpec now documents that a forced uninstallation bypassing the `onUninstall` hook can still be performed through a delegate call (`CALLTYPE_DELEGATECALL`) via `execute`.

#6142 shipped in 5.6.0, so this reversal carries a `patch` changeset.

## Notes

- Mock helpers `revertOnPreCheck`/`revertOnPostCheck` (from #6390) and `ERC7579ModuleMaliciousMock` (from #6142) are kept — still used by the updated tests.
- Dropped the now-unused `setCode` test import left over from #6390.
- All `AccountERC7579` / `AccountERC7579Hooked` tests pass; lint clean.

## Summary

- Bump the malbeclabs/doublezero SDK-family pins (`doublezero-cli-core`, `doublezero-config`, `doublezero-program-common`, `doublezero-record`, `doublezero_sdk`, `doublezero-serviceability`, `doublezero-telemetry`) from the interim #4030 merge-commit rev (`8b795a3c`) to the released tag `client/v0.31.0` (`25ae6ee7`) — the swap the pin comment planned for "the next v3-containing client/* tag once one is cut".
- This unblocks the do-tn-rewards1 incident: contributor-rewards v0.6.1 crash-loops with `memory allocation of 52264173600 bytes failed` because its `client/v0.27.1`-pinned SDK cannot decode the EdgeSeat access pass created on testnet 2026-07-22T14:46:30Z (`5x9DTsWCrAQtYKH4W7trEjoaCRHnzywsZp2oFX3sg5Zg`, `EdgeSeat(Vec<FeedSeat>)` schema from malbeclabs/doublezero#3954). The pre-FeedSeat decoder misreads an allowlist length from mid-FeedSeat bytes and `deserialize_vec_with_capacity` preallocates (1,633,255,424 + 1) × 32 bytes. A contributor-rewards release cut from this pin decodes the account correctly.
- No code changes needed — the workspace compiles unchanged against v0.31.0. Diff is `Cargo.toml` + `Cargo.lock` only, same shape as #399.

Follow-ups tracked separately (not in this PR): cap the unbounded `Vec::with_capacity` in the serviceability SDK helper, and make `serviceability::fetch` warn+skip undecodable accounts like `telemetry::fetch` does.

- `cargo test -p doublezero-contributor-rewards`: 145 tests pass (100 unit + 45 integration), 0 failures.

body:
Manual accounts previously had exactly one balance-update surface: CLI `account set-balance`. This slice extracts that write path into `transfers.true_up_manual_balance` — update `accounts.balance`/`balance_date`, record the snapshot, re-anchor the account's transfer links at `as_of` — and adds an MCP `set_account_balance` tool on the same function, so the CLI and MCP surfaces cannot drift (the validators/set_goal precedent).

Re-anchor semantics worth knowing: a backdated true-up releases ledger rows posted after the new anchor so those transfers legitimately re-apply against the declared base (each at most once ever, enforced by the applications ledger) — the returned balance is honest in both directions. Pinned by tests through the shared helper.

Decisions:
- The shared function lives in `transfers.py` because the operation's distinguishing behavior IS the link re-anchor/re-apply; return type is a NamedTuple (`TrueUpResult`) carrying the snapshot + reanchor info the MCP shape needs.
- New refusal the CLI previously lacked: non-finite balances (NaN/inf) get a friendly error instead of a DuckDB crash. Hidden accounts remain unaddressable on both surfaces (pre-existing behavior, kept deliberately).
- Tool resolves account by id OR case-insensitive name with a difflib did-you-mean; description cross-references transfer links as the automatic roll-forward path (this tool is for drift/interest true-ups).

body:
Folds the strengths of the approved free-form boards into the discover skill's template pipeline while keeping the shell's guarantees. The two user-approved "marriage" boards are the design spec and ship as committed references.

## What changed

**Board-theme overlay + semantic ramps** (`discovery.css`, `templates/src/page/page.html`)

- `{{PRODUCT_NAME}}` in the docbrand; docmark logo removed; docbar `position: static` below 54rem so a wrapped title no longer collides with the masthead.
- The builder extracts the overlay and re-emits it **after** the injected `discovery.css` in both full-document and `--artifact` fragment builds (fragment mode previously dropped head styles), making cascade precedence order-explicit.

**Free-form-first policy + capture floor** (`SKILL.md`, `references/presentation.md`, `references/presentation/components.md`, new `references/features.md`)
- Hard floor: shell, annotatable sections, **per-card response capture** (option sets with reasons + badged recommendation where real alternatives exist — never a bare accept; accept toggle otherwise; note per card; live counters; single generated-reply prompt rebuilding from all inputs), tokens-only color, dual-theme parity, a11y, self-containment.
- Above the floor the generator designs freely; the component catalog is a reference shelf, action recipes are starting points, and a free-pattern escape hatch guarantees ledger content is never dropped.
- `references/features.md`: the Floor-vs-Menu inventory with a validation-mapping table, wired into workflow steps 7/8 as the pre-build and pre-ship checklist.

**Decision-first device recipes** (`components.md`): editorial masthead position line, stat rails, decision-first card, option card set, readiness meter, landing-map row, critical-path strip, filter chips, pip index + keyboard card-stage, data-driven card sets with the `esc()` idiom.

**Validator hardening** (`scripts/build_artifact.py`, `scripts/test_html_templates.py`)
- Overlay validation: token whitelist (hyphenated ramp names accepted), light **and** dark completeness required.
- Raw-hex leak detection scans mixed style blocks rule-by-rule; only `[data-specimen]`-scoped rules keep the hex exemption.
- Un-interpolated `${…}` literals in rendered text fail the build (the free-form defect this pipeline prevents).
- Fragment structure checks strip `<script>` bodies first so data-driven renderers holding markup strings can't false-positive.

**Reference boards** (`examples/reference/`): the two approved boards (readiness verdict dashboard, blind-spots decision browser) with a README; deliberately outside the validated suite, the recipes and features.md point at them.
