author: girnarholdings
body:
## Summary Three evidence-based reliability fixes for Telegram delivery, one commit each. All signatures below are from `~/.hermes/logs/errors.log` on **2026-07-19 04:04–04:05** (a single flood-control window). ### 1. Budget-aware flood-control retries (was: fixed 3-attempt cap) On flood control Telegram dictates a server `retry_after`. Observed: ``` 04:04:44 [Telegram] flood control on send (attempt 1/3), retrying in 255.0s: Flood control exceeded. Retry in 255 seconds 04:05:50 tools.send_message_tool: Transient Telegram send failure (attempt 1/3), retrying in 249.0s: Flood control exceeded. Retry in 249 seconds ``` With a fixed 3-attempt cap, a 249–255s `retry_after` runs out the attempts and the message is dropped. Now RetryAfter/flood errors keep honoring the server `retry_after` (plus small jitter) until a **wall-clock budget** is spent (default **600s**, `TELEGRAM_SEND_FLOOD_BUDGET_SECONDS`; jitter `TELEGRAM_SEND_FLOOD_JITTER_SECONDS`). Non-flood transient/network errors keep the classic 3-attempt behavior — flood and network retries now use independent counters so a long flood wait never eats a network retry. Budget exhaustion fails loudly (ERROR) and returns a failure result instead of a silent drop. Applied to **both** send paths (gateway adapter loop + standalone `_send_telegram_message_with_retry`). ### 2. MarkdownV2 pre-escape to kill parse-fallback double-sends Same window logged **~40** identical fallbacks: ``` 04:04:58–04:05:50 tools.send_message_tool: Parse mode MarkdownV2 failed in _send_telegram, falling back to plain text: Can't parse entities: character '(' is reserved and must be escaped with the preceding '\' ``` Each MarkdownV2 parse failure is a rejected send + a plain-text re-send — doubling per-chat volume into the very flood control above. `format_message` already does **entity-aware escaping** (it escapes the MarkdownV2 reserved set — including `(` — outside code/link/entity spans, via its step-12 safety net), so its output is valid MarkdownV2 and never trips the fallback. The remaining doubling source was the *"formatting unavailable"* branch in `_send_telegram`, which fell back to sending the **raw, unescaped** text under `parse_mode=MarkdownV2` — guaranteed to parse-fail on the first reserved char and force the plain re-send. Fix: that branch now sends the raw text as **plain text** (`parse_mode=None`), which cannot parse-fail, so there is no doubled send. The last-resort parse-error fallback (now rare) is demoted `WARNING → DEBUG` and is a single re-send with no retry-counter recursion, so a stray fallback no longer spams 40 warnings that mask the real cause. **Why this choice:** the task's recommended entity-aware escaper already exists (`format_message`); re-escaping would double-escape. The minimal change closes the one path that bypassed it. The gateway adapter's own MarkdownV2 fallback is left untouched — its chunks are `format_message` output and it is not implicated in the evidence (all 40 fallbacks are `tools.send_message_tool`). ### 3. Loud operator alert on dead-target marking A send failing with forbidden/not_found marks the chat dead; future deliveries are then **silently skipped** until a later success. The mark was logged at INFO, which never reaches `errors.log` (the operator-visible alert surface). Now: - `mark_dead` emits a grep-able **WARNING** on the transition to dead: `DEAD-TARGET: profile=

platform= chat= reason= — deliveries will be skipped until a send to this target succeeds` - self-heal logs `DEAD-TARGET RECOVERED: …` at **INFO** on clear. No new delivery channel (explicitly out of scope, and unsafe — could itself target a dead chat). There is no dedicated operator-notify API in the gateway; the shared logger → `errors.log` is the existing alert mechanism, so the WARNING rides that path. Profile is best-effort, degrading to `"default"`. ## Tests - `tests/tools/test_send_message_flood_budget.py` (new): flood honors retry_after within budget; gives up after budget; non-flood keeps 3-attempt cap; flood-error classification. - `tests/gateway/test_telegram_thread_fallback.py`: adapter-level flood retries past 3 attempts within budget; gives up (returns failure) when budget exhausted. - `tests/tools/test_send_message_parse_fallback.py` (new): `format_message` escapes the observed `(`; raw-fallback is a single plain-text send (no double). - `tests/gateway/test_dead_targets.py`: `mark_dead` emits the grep-able WARNING (once, idempotent); self-heal emits the INFO recovery line. Local (venv py3.11): touched modules all green — flood-budget 4, parse-fallback 2, existing send_message_tool 152, dead_targets 28, thread_fallback 52. `ruff check` clean; `scripts/check-windows-footguns.py` clean (no POSIX-only symbols added). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: louislp
body:
Closes #20. First slice of the v1 build — implementation against [ADR 0004](https://github.com/LouisLP/colour-combos/blob/main/docs/adr/0004-routing-and-url-state.md) and [ADR 0005](https://github.com/LouisLP/colour-combos/blob/main/docs/adr/0005-app-state-architecture.md) §6–8. No new decisions.

## What's here

- **TanStack Router, code-based tree.** `/` and `/favorites` under one `HubLayout` (ADR 0004 §2). No file-based routing, no generated route tree.
- **The root owns the search params** — `c` (int 1–348), `q`, `size` (2|3|4) — so both routes inherit one contract and nothing is dropped moving between them (§3–4).
- **`c` resolves in the validator** (§8), synchronously during route matching. Valid passes through; absent or invalid falls back to a random combo, pinned via `replaceState`.
- **The fallback is a per-document one-shot** (ADR 0005 §6). Validators are re-invoked constantly — StrictMode doubles them, TanStack re-runs them on any param change — so a bare `Math.random()` would re-theme the site as the user typed.
- **The rejected `c` rides in typed location state** (ADR 0005 §7), ready for the notice in #25. It survives the replace, not a reload.
- `useSelectedCombo()` — one line over the router, per the ADR 0005 §8 rule that a hook holds no logic.
- Vite starter (`App.tsx`, `App.css`, the logo assets) removed.

## A deviation worth flagging

The ADR doesn't specify *how* links carry params. I used an explicit `carryHubSearch` reducer on each `<Link>` rather than `retainSearchParams` middleware. Reason: `c` is required in the schema, so TypeScript refuses a `<Link>` that omits `search` — carrying the params becomes the explicit act and a future link cannot silently drop them. The middleware would have made forgetting invisible. Easy to swap if you'd rather have the middleware.

## Verification

`pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test` (21 tests) all green. Behaviour checked in a real browser, not just asserted:

| URL | Resolves to | History |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/` | `?c=317` (random, pinned) | no entry added |
| `/?c=153` | `?c=153` | no entry added |
| `/?c=999` | `?c=333` + `state.notFoundCombo = "999"` | no entry added |
| `/?c=abc` | `?c=227` + `state.notFoundCombo = "abc"` | no entry added |
| `/favorites?c=153&q=blue&size=3` | unchanged | — |

Changing `q` left the resolved combo stable (`301` → `301`). Navigating `/` → `/favorites` preserved `?c=301&q=blue&size=3`.

## Not here

Theming, the palette, the grid, favourites, the not-found notice UI. This ends with two routable, param-typed placeholder pages and exactly one combo always resolved. Next: #21.

author: buleegasy
body:
💡 **What**: Optimized the `cosineSimilarity` function in `src/app/api/translate/route.ts` by unrolling its inner loop 4 times.

🎯 **Why**: The application computes cosine similarity for hundreds/thousands of 1024-dimension vector embeddings per RAG request. In Node.js/Edge environments, the overhead of branching and incrementing a tight `for` loop thousands of times becomes noticeable. Unrolling the loop reduces instruction counts and branching, making numeric array traversal faster.

📊 **Impact**: Reduces execution time of dot products by ~20-25% in V8 (verified via local benchmarks dropping time from ~940ms to ~730ms per 100 runs of 5,000 similarity calculations).

🔬 **Measurement**: You can observe faster RAG similarity matching times in the Cloudflare/Edge runtime logs. The `[4] 向量匹配完成，耗时: Xms` step should show a measurable drop in milliseconds on large corpuses.

author: techsavvyash
body:
## Summary

This branch grew from an RFC-012 design bundle into the full post-rebuild platform arc: **114 commits** spanning five RFCs, the Studio web app, and a set of indexer-correctness fixes found by the new verification machinery itself.

### RFC-010 — Tree-sitter structure extraction
- `internal/ingest/structure`: official CGO tree-sitter bindings, 7 non-Go grammars; body ranges for non-Go languages now come from real parse trees (declaration-order inference deleted).
- Declarator-bound arrows/function expressions promoted to Function/Method (`kind_promotion.go`) so they participate in the call graph; provenance stamped (`rangeSource`, `kindSource`).

### RFC-011 — Doc-to-code linking
- `codegraph index docs`: markdown ingestion with hash-diff sync, deterministic Layer-D miners (docmine, 0.96 precision on khaata), pluggable LLM provider contract, semantic summarize-then-match layer (semlink, OpenAI text-embedding-3-small), provenance-badged edges surfaced through MCP find/expand/source.

### RFC-001 — Polymorphic call resolution (closed for Go + TS)
- Go Layer 3: in-repo structural resolver (`internal/ingest/resolve`, go/packages + types.Implements) as a drift guarantee over scip-go's IMPLEMENTS emission.
- TS Layer 3: `tools/ts-resolver` runs the *target project's own* TypeScript compiler (`isTypeAssignableTo`); required-function-member filter kills option-bag noise (khaata: 767 → 23 edges, all genuine).
- Tier-2 entry points fixed (method-level IMPLEMENTS edge shape); NestJS-style decorator routes detected via tree-sitter (khaata: 424 routes vs 107 before).

### RFC-013 — Graph correctness (the trust layer)
- `codegraph verify {integrity|oracle|census|drift}` + non-blocking post-index hooks.
- **Integrity**: 8 Cypher invariants, schema expectations derived from the schema package, LOOKUP-index self-healing.
- **Oracles**: Go sandwich (`static ⊆ CALLS ⊆ CHA` over x/tools SSA) — **100% recall on codegraph**; sampled TS compiler oracle — 98.9% on khaata; tree-sitter census — 0 dropouts on khaata.
- **Telemetry**: per-run IndexRun nodes, counters computed from the graph, ±25% drift detection.
- **Labeled fixtures**: 39 hand-verified must-have/must-not-have edge assertions.
- Oracle-found indexer bugs fixed: same-name method range clobbering (CALLS misattribution) and deliberate self-loop drop (recursion was a language-wide recall gap; degrees now asymmetric by design — inDegree excludes self-loops, outDegree keeps them). codegraph CALLS 2,465 → 2,924.

### RFC-012 — CodeGraph Studio (`web/studio`)
- SvelteKit app over a pooled stdio bridge to `bin/codegraph-mcp` (crash-loop cooldown): Dashboard (service health incl. drift/telemetry flags), Graph explorer (search → canvas → expand → inspect, edge-stitch deep links), Flows screen (tiered entry rail, stepped call spine, inspector).
- Full design bundle under `design/studio/` (20 cards, synced to claude.ai/design).

### Platform hardening along the way
- Service subgraph isolation (`scope_id`/`serviceName` on every write path), `Service.rootPath` stamping + cwd-independent source resolution, fulltext+RRF searcher replacing the OpenSearch stack, single-traversal flow spines, LOOKUP-index preservation in schema management, cross-package Neo4j test lock, integration-test scope-leak fixes.

## Test plan
- `make test` (unit) and `make test-integration` (Neo4j-backed, incl. labeled truth fixtures + golden harness) green.
- `web/studio`: 222 vitest unit tests + Playwright e2e green.
- Live verification on the dev graph: integrity 13/13 clean; Go oracle 100% recall (2 explained precision suspects, recorded as known limitations); khaata census 0 dropouts.

author: tedeuxx
body:
Begins reverse-engineering the product's architecture into ADRs, so the library — taken together — documents the **whole current stack and vision** (the exhaustive backlog we agreed). Product ADRs live here; methodology ADRs (the dev-loop machine) live in the plugin.

## The keystone
**ADR-0001 — lean by design, calibrated to the strategic priority.** The site's job today is *presence through content and portfolio*, so the architecture is deliberately minimal — optimized for **cost + simplicity, evolving gradually**. This is the driver the backend and much else were cut *toward*, and the lens every other ADR is read through. Its considered-options weigh keeping the full backend-ful platform (rejected: cost/complexity/attack-surface the strategy doesn't need) and going even leaner (rejected: gives up the SPA/agent-built engineering argument that *is* the proof).

## This slice
- **0001** — lean by design (keystone / driver)
- **0002** — fully static SPA, no backend (the largest application of 0001; supersedes the backend era)
- **0003** — trunk-based, single environment (adopts the plugin's trunk-single-env model; supersedes GitFlow two-env)
- **README** — the full catalog: **21 live** decisions + **5 superseded** (backend era), 0001–0003 authored, the rest pending. Includes **ADR-0021** — the CV cross-surface coherence decision (profile.ts to LinkedIn to Canva) you flagged as missing (public captures the coherence obligation; the private sync mechanics stay in the .brand layer).

## Format to react to
Each ADR is MADR with real considered-options (chosen + strongest rejected, each with its trade-off) and a non-empty consequences section (the bad costs too). If this granularity/format is right, the next slices author the remaining layers — frontend (0004–0011), infra (0012–0016), SDLC (0017–0020), the CV-sync (0021), and the superseded history (0022–0026) — each its own PR.

Docs only.

author: kingnazz
body:
## What & why

On Windows some networks have a transparent router/proxy that answers TCP (e.g. port 53) for **every** address in the subnet. The old "TCP-open ⇒ host is up" rule then counted all 254 phantom addresses as live — the reported "254/254 found, ~196 unknown" bug. Angry IP / Advanced IP Scanner avoid this because a genuine LAN device must answer ARP, and a middlebox can't forge a distinct MAC per address.

## Change

In `src-tauri/src/scanner.rs`, liveness is now decided by segment:

- **Local segment** (target falls inside one of our own interface subnets, or any host in range produced a real ARP MAC): require a **real, non-proxy ARP MAC**. ARP is ground truth — any real ICMP/TCP responder necessarily has an ARP entry, and proxy-ARP (one MAC shared across many IPs) is filtered out via a frequency threshold.
- **Remote targets**: unchanged, still probe-based (`p.up` from ICMP/TCP/RST).
- Our own interface IPs are always kept.

Also added the `ip_in_ranges` helper and an `ip_range_containment` unit test.

## Version

Bumped to **1.5.2** across `package.json`, `src-tauri/Cargo.toml`, `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`, and `APP_VERSION` in `src/App.tsx` so the release pipeline ships this fix.

## Summary

R6, second milestone (PLAN.md §GUI feature roadmap → R6, M72). **Stacked on #159 (M71)** — base
is `feat/m71-two-tier-toolbar`; only the M72 commit is new here.

The markup bar's two Redact slots become **one armed tool** with Preview-style gesture detect:

* `ArmedTool.REDACT` resolves **at press** on the existing text-hit path
  (`TextSelection.has_word_at` — exact containment, never nearest-snap): a drag starting on a
  word runs the text-flow redaction; a drag starting in margin/image space rubber-bands a
  block. Resolution swaps in the concrete tool (`REDACT_TEXT` / `REDACT_REGION`), so the
  armed-selection tint, the release path and the one-shot disarm are exactly the explicit
  tools' — nothing downstream knows the combined slot exists.
* A press off any page stays armed and **unresolved** (a mis-click neither wastes the arm nor
  locks in a gesture); a no-commit click on text **restores** the combined arm, so a stray
  click can't leave the text gesture locked in for the next press. A rotated view resolves to
  the block gesture (text selection is disabled there).
* The bar's one Redact button **lights for the whole redact family** (combined or menu-armed
  explicit) and clicking the lit button always disarms. A live text selection applies the
  text-flow redaction immediately — the M46 select-then-click contract, same as Redact Text.
* **Menus unchanged** (the complete-catalog budget): Tools ▸ Redact Text (Ctrl+Shift+R) and
  Redact Block keep arming their own tools; the combined slot is toolbar sugar, not a third
  verb, so it deliberately has no menu row.

author: magodelaweb-dev
body:
## Por qué

El panel de operaciones mostraba atributos crudos con el mismo peso visual (PID, versiones, entradas de caché) y sin interpretación, y le faltaban las dos señales más elocuentes de un servicio vivo: tasa de errores y tráfico. Se reestructura siguiendo las cuatro señales doradas del SRE (latencia, tráfico, errores, saturación) para que el panel cuente una evaluación de salud, no un volcado de datos.

## Qué cambia

- **Cuatro tarjetas de señales doradas** al frente, cada una con badge de salud, umbrales documentados en el microcopy y, en latencia, un sparkline SVG inline con las últimas duraciones.
- **Errores**: % de 5xx y conteos 4xx/5xx — el buffer ya capturaba los status pero nadie los agregaba.
- **Tráfico**: peticiones/min sobre la ventana de muestreo (el propio panel sigue excluido del muestreo).
- **Saturación**: memoria RSS del proceso vía `/proc` (cumple lo que el README ya prometía) y backlog de la cola.
- Identidad del proceso y tamaños de BD degradados a una fila compacta de inventario; Solid Queue conserva su sección con una línea de contexto.
- **Fix de bug latente**: la telemetría guardaba `event.end` (Float monotónico) como timestamp; ahora usa `Time.current`, necesario para comparaciones de reloj de pared.

## Plan de pruebas

- [x] `bin/ci` completo en verde (incluye rubocop, erblint, brakeman, 52 tests)
- [x] 4 tests nuevos de telemetría (tasa de errores, rpm, history, estados cero)

author: nickmisasi
body: #### Summary Final PR in the MCP Apps stack (base: #912). Renders MCP Apps inline in conversations and ships a built-in demo app plus e2e coverage. With this PR, tool calls from MCP servers that declare `_meta.ui.resourceUri` display as interactive sandboxed apps instead of plain JSON tool cards. - Adds `@mcp-ui/client` and a new `MCPAppView` (`webapp/src/components/mcp_apps/`) mounted from `ToolCard` when a tool call carries UI metadata, the tool reached Success/AutoApproved (apps never execute before user consent), and apps are enabled. A single epoch-guarded loader fetches the resource via `GET /mcp/app-resource` and passes pre-fetched HTML to `AppRenderer` (typed boundary, no casts). - Error taxonomy → UX: `401 mcp_auth_required` renders a **Connect to view** button (OAuth window + websocket/refocus-driven retry; repeated 401 after a connect attempt becomes the no-access notice); `403` renders the onlooker notice naming the invoking user; `404/502` degrade gracefully to the plain tool card with a subtle note. Onlookers who can access the origin server render the app under their own credentials. - Sizing: full-width iframe, height driven by `ui/notifications/size-changed` clamped to 160px–70vh with viewport-resize re-clamp; theme (light/dark + palette) derived from Mattermost CSS variables and passed via `hostContext`. Display-only V1: app-initiated `tools/call`/`ui/message` return explicit protocol errors; `ui/open-link` opens with `noopener`. author: andste82
body:
## WP-03 — Non-minimal varint sweep axis (blocking, agreement-only)

Implements `docs/improvements.md` **WP-03**. A varint admits **non-minimal** forms — redundant `0x80` continuation bytes that add only zero high bits (`5` = `05` = `85 00` = `85 80 00` …). `gen.varint` emits only minimal encodings, so no corpus reached this class; F-0016 covered only the **>64-bit overflow**. Whether the 13 decoders agree on a non-minimal-but-≤64-bit varint — accept-and-normalize, or reject — was untested, exactly the class where streaming decoders silently differ.

### What changed
- **New axis `engine/structured/sweep_varint.py`** places a non-minimal varint at every varint **role**: field-id header, fixlen length word, array element-count, array element value, and inside a skipped (unknown-id) field — padded +1/+3 bytes and up to the 10-byte ≤64-bit maximum, with minimal-accept controls and an 11-byte >64-bit overflow-reject contrast. **23 vectors.** `gen.varint` is left untouched (it is the canonical reference encoder; the non-minimal forms are hand-built).
- Registered in `sweep_run.py` `AXES`; blocking in `scripts/sweep.sh`; gated by `replay.yml` (which runs `sweep.sh`). **Sweep gate is now seven axes.**

### Result — green
All 13 drivers **accept every non-minimal varint and re-encode to the identical minimal canonical form** (the round-trip normalizes it away), and all 13 **reject** the overflow. 0 divergences, 0 conformance failures. **No finding.**

```
[sweep_varint] 23 vectors — 0 divergence(s), 0 conformance failure(s)  [OK]
```

### Spec is silent → agreement-only + spec proposal
CORELIB_PLAN §4.1 guards only overflow; MESSAGE_SPEC §2 constrains the *encoder*, not the decoder. Per ground rule 6 the axis is **blocking but agreement-only**: the 18 non-minimal vectors carry `expect="agree"` — the runner asserts only that all 13 agree (and, for free, that the round-trip normalizes them to the one canonical form), **not** accept-vs-reject conformance — until a clause lands. The minimal-accept controls and the overflow-reject contrast **are** spec-defined and asserted.

Filed **[documentation#24](https://github.com/sofa-buffers/documentation/issues/24)** (`docs/spec-proposals.md` Proposal 5) proposing the observed consensus (accept + normalize; reject overflow) as the rule. On adoption the vectors tighten from `expect="agree"` to `expect="accept"` and the axis becomes a conformance gate — the F-0015 arc (hole → clause → conformance).

### Verification
- `./scripts/sweep.sh` → exit 0; **seven** blocking axes, all green.
- No `results/FINDINGS.md` / `SOFABGEN.md` change (green, no finding, no codegen defect).

### Notes for merge sequencing
- Independent of WP-01 (PR #88); branched from `main`.
- `docs/improvements.md` isn't on this branch (it lands on main via WP-01), so the WP-03 roadmap tick is deferred until then. WP-03's as-built record is in STATUS.md (change entry) + ARCHITECTURE.md (Deviation 2026-07-22d).
- The STATUS.md changelog ordinal ("Twenty-eighth") parallels WP-01's — trivially reconciled whichever merges second.

author: jleechan2015
body:
## Background

r4 (PR #455) was closed without merging after codex-bot posted 4 P2 review threads. Three of them pointed at real bugs the r4 work left unfixed; the fourth (rate-limit-doesn't-abort-dispatch) was already addressed in r4 itself and codex was reviewing a stale diff. r5 cherry-picks the r4 commit on top of current main (3d906a8) and then closes the three real items.

The original 2026-07-22 problem (slow-tier re-probing every factory-labeled PR every ~60s, exhausting the 5000/hr core gh bucket) is fixed by the r4 work this branch carries; r5 only tightens three loose ends in that work.

## Goals

- Restore the r4 fix's cache-short-circuit behavior on the REST fallback path (the r4 deserializer was reading a non-existent field, so REST-fallback PRs all came back with head_sha=None and the cache treated them as uncacheable).
- Stop silently serving stale `AuthorPermission` decisions across ticks when the cache key is incomplete (head_sha or updated_at_epoch is None).
- Make the slow-tier `INTAKE_GH_CALL_WARN_THRESHOLD` warning actually fire when the daemon burns O(N) gh calls via the REST fallback (r4 only counted the list query as 1).

## Tenets

1. **TDD red to green for every fix** — every r5 change has a test that fails on the r4 code and passes on r5.
2. **Pure-function deserializer** — the REST /pulls/{n} parsing is now in a public `parse_rest_pull_payload` so unit tests can drive it with fixture payloads (no fake-`gh` shell-out required).
3. **Trait-uniform metric plumbing** — `Scm::labeled_prs` now takes `&mut gh_calls` so every impl can record its own subprocess invocations; no leaky `as_any` downcasting.
4. **Cache-strict on key completeness** — only decisions under a fully-populated `(external_ref, head_sha, updated_at_epoch)` triple get cached; incomplete keys are uncacheable (probed fresh every tick), preserving pre-r4 behavior on schema-drifted upstream payloads.
5. **No silent substitution of methods** — r5 inherits the r4 "degrade, don't abort" rate-limit path verbatim and adds a stronger test pinning it; the r3 `return Ok(())` does not return.

## High-level description of changes

- **`daemon/src/adapters.rs`** — Extract `CliScm::parse_rest_pull_payload(repo, json)` as the canonical deserializer for a single GitHub `/pulls/{n}` REST payload. Reads `head.sha`, `head.ref`, `head.repo.full_name`, `head.repo.owner.login`, and `updated_at` (matching GitHub's actual REST shape — the r4 `RestPullExt` looked for a non-existent top-level `head_sha`). `labeled_prs_via_rest` is refactored to delegate here. `labeled_prs` and `labeled_prs_via_rest` now thread `&mut gh_calls` so the slow-tier metric counts every `gh` subprocess (list query + per-PR `pulls/{n}`).
- **`daemon/src/tools.rs`** — `Scm::labeled_prs` trait signature gains `&mut gh_calls` so every impl records its own subprocess invocations into the slow-tier `IntakeProbeMetrics.gh_call_count`.
- **`daemon/src/intake.rs`** — `ProbeCacheKey::is_complete()` predicate gates `AdoptionProbeCache::insert` (returns `false`, no-op on incomplete keys). Both `normalize_labeled_prs_outcome` and `normalize_labeled_prs` pass `&mut gh_calls` through to `scm.labeled_prs` so the metric reflects real subprocess invocations on both intake paths.
- **`daemon/src/{main.rs,er_runner.rs,verifier.rs}`** — `Scm` impls updated for the new `labeled_prs` signature.
- **`daemon/tests/{common/mod.rs,er_runner_integration.rs,tick_integration.rs}`** — Test fakes updated for the new signature; FakeScm counts its single list-query increment toward `gh_call_count` (matches the primary `gh pr list` path, since the fake short-circuits the fallback).
- **`daemon/tests/intake.rs`** — 3 new r5 tests (TDD red→green against r4):
  - `adoption_probe_cache_refuses_incomplete_keys` (P2 #2 API contract)
  - `incomplete_key_pr_is_reprobed_every_tick` (P2 #2 end-to-end)
  - `intake_metrics_gh_call_count_counts_real_subprocesses` (P2 #3)
- **`daemon/src/adapters.rs` unit tests** — 3 new `parse_rest_pull_payload` tests:
  - `parse_rest_pull_payload_extracts_head_sha_from_head_dot_sha` (P2 #1 happy path)
  - `parse_rest_pull_payload_detects_cross_repo_pr` (P2 #1 fork shape)
  - `parse_rest_pull_payload_tolerates_missing_updated_at` (P2 #1 backward-compat)

## Testing

```
$ cd daemon && cargo test --quiet 2>&1 | grep "test result"
... 15 suites, 602 passed, 0 failed, 11 ignored
```

```
$ cd daemon && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 2.05s
```

**602 tests pass** (was 596 on r4 baseline; +6 from r5 — 3 `parse_rest_pull_payload` unit tests in adapters.rs + 3 integration tests in intake.rs). Clippy clean with `-D warnings`.

## Low-level details

### Codex P2 review thread mapping

| Thread | Status in r5 |
|--------|-------------|
| P2 #1: Populate REST fallback SHA from head.sha | **FIXED** — new `parse_rest_pull_payload` reads `head.sha` directly; 3 unit tests pin same-repo, fork, and missing-updated_at shapes |
| P2 #2: Avoid caching PRs without complete cache keys | **FIXED** — `ProbeCacheKey::is_complete()` gates `cache.insert`; 2 tests pin API contract + end-to-end re-probe behavior |
| P2 #3: Count REST fallback subprocesses in gh metrics | **FIXED** — `Scm::labeled_prs` takes `&mut gh_calls`; `labeled_prs_via_rest` increments per `pulls/{n}` call; 1 integration test with scripted fake that mirrors the real fallback (1 list + N pulls, asserts metric = N+1) |
| P2 #4: Don't abort slow-tier dispatch on intake rate limits | Already fixed in r4 (see `daemon/src/tick.rs` lines 1350-1365, where the if-else `(Vec::new(), Vec::new())` branch logs a skip and continues past PR intake into routing + dispatch). r5 inherits this verbatim. |

### Acceptance criteria mapping (cumulative r4+r5)

| # | Criterion | Where satisfied |
|---|-----------|-----------------|
| 1 | Cached across ticks, keyed on head SHA + updated_at | r4 — `AdoptionProbeCache` keyed on `(external_ref, head_sha, updated_at_epoch)` |
| 2 | Steady-state = O(1) list calls per repo | r4 — second_tick_over_unchanged_prs_makes_zero_per_pr_probes test |
| 3 | Per-tick gh call count metric, warn > threshold | r4 metric + **r5 plumbing** (P2 #3 fix makes the warning actually fire under fallback) |
| 4 | Two ticks over unchanged PR set, second makes 0 per-PR probes | r4 — same test as #2 |
| 5 | Rate-limit degrades intake, dispatch continues | r4 — `run_slow_tier` if-else branch, verified by intake_rate_limit_during_labeled_prs_does_not_abort_dispatch |

**Evidence**: https://gist.github.com/jleechan2015/4940c7a37944090ed45a772585dfdd1d (head 448c50c)

author: githubrobbi
body:
## What

The targeted per-candidate MFT re-read (`resolve_frs_to_lcn`) already reads every requested record's full bytes off the volume — then parses out a single LCN and discards them. Downstream consumers need those bytes (resident `$DATA` content, reparse targets, forensic attributes) and were paying for the read anyway. This exposes them, streaming and bounded.

## API

- **New: `uffs_mft::for_each_record(volume, frs_list, visit)`** — reads each **distinct** FRS in ascending order, applies the NTFS Update-Sequence-Array fixup, and hands the fixed-up record to the callback as a **borrow from one reused scratch buffer**: no per-record allocation, retention impossible by construction. Per-record failures (outside `$MFT`, transient I/O, torn write) fold to `None` without aborting the pass; `Err` only when `$MFT`'s extents can't be determined at all. Works on live volumes and VSS snapshot devices — the same `VolumeHandle` contract as `resolve_frs_to_lcn`. `MftRecordReader` stays `pub(crate)`.
- **`resolve_frs_to_lcn` now delegates to it** (identical output contract). Side effect: the LCN parse now runs on **fixup-verified** bytes — previously it parsed raw record bytes, so a runlist straddling a sector boundary (offset 510–511) could read the USA sentinel instead of data.
- **`first_data_lcn` is now public** — callers derive the LCN from the callback bytes with the exact parser `resolve_frs_to_lcn` uses, so one pass yields LCN ordering *and* record contents with no second call and no duplicated runlist parsing.

## Hot-path impact: none

Purely additive. The bulk-ingest readers and the search path never touch this module; the only in-repo caller of `resolve_frs_to_lcn` is the opt-in `resolve_lcn_order` post-processing pass in the daemon, which is unchanged in behavior and gains only a ~1 KiB memcpy + fixup per candidate — noise against the disk-bound read it wraps. No index schema, wire, or memory-footprint changes.

## Tests

- USA fixup round-trip; torn-write and bad-magic rejection.
- End-to-end fixture proving fixup is load-bearing: a resident `$DATA` value straddling the sector-1 boundary parses to real content only after fixup (raw bytes hold the sentinel).
- Sort/dedup ordering of the want-list.
- Ignored live-volume parity test (`--ignored`, elevated Windows): `for_each_record` + `first_data_lcn` must reproduce `resolve_frs_to_lcn` exactly, callbacks ascending + deduplicated, out-of-MFT FRS folds to `None`.

Gates: full workspace suite (2498), lint-prod, lint-tests, xwin Windows clippy, rustdoc (`--document-private-items --locked`), doc-tests — all green; full pre-push bundle passed on push.

body:
## MCP Phase 2 PR1 — door-contract grammar hardening (hub #765 findings 1/3/4)

Hub-first hardening of the composed account-scope grammar in `packages/door-contract/src/scopes.ts` (Phase 1, merged #764), published as **0.6.1**. Cloud's Phase 2 PRs import these builders/parsers, so the grammar is made airtight + fail-closed FIRST. **Purely additive** — every currently-valid parse stays byte-identical; only newly-malformed inputs are rejected.

### The three fixes
- **Finding 1 — builders throw on malformed slots.** `composedWildcardVaultsScope`, `composedVaultScope`, `composedVaultCreateScope`, and `composedModuleScope` now validate every interpolated `id` / `vault` / `module` slot via a shared `assertComposedSlot` guard and **throw a clear `Error`** when a slot is empty, the wildcard sentinel `*`, or contains a `:`. Either would inject extra scope segments (separator injection) or forge a wildcard grant a user never consented to. Wildcard authority is expressed ONLY by the dedicated `composedWildcardVaultsScope` builder. Fail-closed at construction time → a malformed grant can never be minted.
- **Finding 4 — parser rejects `*` as a module name.** `parseComposedAccountScope` now returns `null` for `account:<id>:mod:*:<verb>` (previously parsed as a literal `*` module), mirroring the vault slot's existing `*`-fails-closed rule. Denied downstream, consistent with fail-closed.
- **Finding 3 — doc fix.** Corrected the §1.4 guardrail comment that mislabeled the cross-account mint gate as "the hub's" — it is the **CLOUD door's** mint gate (`parachute-cloud workers/identity/src/oauth-token.ts`, `denyForeignAccountMint`). Swept the file: lines referencing the self-host hub / hub exact-string gate are accurate and left as-is.

### Invariants held
- **Existing parse fixtures byte-identical.** A new regression table re-locks all 9 currently-valid composed/legacy forms. The ONLY existing assertion that changed is `account:<id>:mod:*:<verb> → null` — which IS Finding 4.
- **Fail-closed preserved** — unrecognized → `null` (deny), never a permissive fallback.
- **`isRequestableAccountScope` unchanged** — composed forms stay non-requestable; consent is their sole author.

### Version + gates (`packages/door-contract`)
- `package.json` 0.6.0 → **0.6.1** + CHANGELOG entry.
- `bun test src` → **85 pass / 0 fail / 338 expect() calls** (baseline was 83/0/289; +2 tests: builder-throws + valid-form regression table).
- `bun run typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit`, TypeScript 5.9.3) → **exit 0**.
- `bunx biome check` on changed files → **clean**.

Do NOT publish/tag — the tag → CI publish happens after review + merge.

## Summary

This pull request introduces a `MazeGenerator` class that generates perfect mazes using the Depth-First Search (DFS) algorithm with recursive backtracking.

## Changes

* Added the `MazeGenerator` class.
* Implemented recursive DFS for maze generation.
* Added randomized neighbor traversal using an optional seed for reproducible mazes.
* Implemented neighbor discovery within maze boundaries.
* Added wall removal logic between adjacent cells.
* Initialized grid and visited matrices for maze construction.
* Added inline documentation and comments to improve code readability and maintainability.

## Notes

* The generated maze is a **perfect maze**, meaning there is exactly one path between any two cells.
* Passing a seed produces deterministic maze generation, which is useful for testing and debugging.

The install commands the README already advertises now actually work:
  ```
  /plugin marketplace add Paramchoudhary/ResumeSkills
  /plugin install resume-skills@resume-skills-marketplace
  ```

- **AGENTS.md** (agents.md standard) at the repo root: layout, skill format, install paths, and the contributor workflow for AI agents.
- **Docs**: README (stale "20 skills" → 22, two newest skills added to categories, repository-layout section, Windows symlink caveat) and CONTRIBUTING (skill location, required frontmatter, sync script, plugin version-bump rule). Minimal `.gitignore`.

## Why

The repo had three skill locations drifting apart, and the plugin install path was broken — `config.json` is not a filename Claude Code reads, and its schema errors would fail the load even if it were. This PR makes `skills/` the single source of truth, keeps every tool's discovery directory automatically in sync, and makes all four README install options genuinely work.

## Testing

All run locally on this branch:

- `scripts/sync-skills.sh --check` → "All skill symlinks in sync"; `find . -type l ! -exec test -e {} \; -print` → no broken links; all 176 mirror entries are git mode `120000`.

- `npx skills add <repo>` in a scratch project → all 22 discovered and installed (no double-counting from the symlink mirrors).

Note: the commands referencing the `Paramchoudhary/ResumeSkills` slug only resolve after this merges; the local-path equivalents above prove the mechanics.

author: jeferson0306
body:
## Summary
- New `gateway` (8th microservice): single entry point fronting every backend, path-prefix routing (no rewriting) to whichever service owns a path's first segment after `/api/v1/`.
- Generic reverse-proxy route (`quarkus-reactive-routes` + Vert.x Mutiny `WebClient`) forwards method/headers/query/body verbatim and streams the upstream response back verbatim - not N typed REST clients, one handler.
- Redis-backed fixed-window rate limiting (429 once exceeded, per client IP).
- JWT fast-fail (`TokenValidator`): a present-but-invalid/expired token is rejected with 401 before reaching any backend; a missing token passes through untouched. Deliberately does **not** duplicate RBAC - every backend still independently enforces its own `@RolesAllowed`, defense in depth (see ADR 0013 for the reasoning).
- CORS via native Quarkus config, no custom code.
- No MongoDB, no Kafka, no hexagonal domain/application/infrastructure split - genuinely infrastructure-only, documented as a deliberate deviation in ADR 0013 rather than a shortcut.
- Docs: ADR 0013, `docs/c4/container.md`, ARCHITECTURE.md, ROADMAP.md, CHANGELOG.md, `docs/development/testing.md`. `ci.yml`'s matrix now covers all eight services. `.gitignore`/`.gitleaks.toml` extended to allowlist the gateway's dev/test JWT keypair (same non-secret fixture every other service already uses).

## Test plan
- [x] `mvn -f backend/pom.xml clean test` - all 8 services pass, BUILD SUCCESS
- [x] `gateway` test suite (14 tests): `ProxyRoutesTest` (forwarding correctness, upstream status passthrough, unmapped-prefix 404, CORS preflight, Authorization header pass-through/rejection) against a stub upstream HTTP server; `RateLimiterTest` (limit enforcement, per-client isolation) against real Redis via Dev Services; `TokenValidatorTest` (valid/expired/malformed/missing tokens) using real RS256-signed tokens
- [x] JaCoCo gate: gateway has its own measured floor (0.01, documented in ADR 0013 - JaCoCo cannot instrument `@Route`-generated invokers, not an undertested module); every other service unchanged
- [x] `spotless:check` clean, gitleaks clean

author: ipv1337
body:
Resolves the naming half of the tabula cutover blocker from #1062, following James's steer to **err toward Google's best practice**.

## The best-practice answer

A Cloud Run revision name must be **unique per configuration**. Cloud Run *rejects* a name reused with different config — the `409 Revision … with different configuration already exists` error. So:

- `<service>-<digest>` (the archetype's current scheme, used by oauth) collides the moment one promoted image is deployed with different env. It's a latent bug that just hasn't fired for oauth.
- `<service>-<digest>-<configHash>` (tabula's app stack, from the #1018 409 fix) encodes image **and** config, so it's always unique. **This is the correct scheme.**

(Google's strongest guidance is actually to let Cloud Run auto-name revisions and do blue-green via *tags* — a bigger change to both apps + the archetype, noted as a long-term follow-up, not this PR.)

## What changed, and where

The bu2 leaves now compute the suffix `<shortDigest>-<configHash>`, so the archetype produces `tabula-api-<env>-<digest>-<hash>`. The hash is over the **deployed** env (app env + the `SECRET_PREFIX` the archetype injects), sorted keys, NUL-separated — **byte-identical to tabula's app stack**, so the archetype names revisions exactly as the live service does. That also means the eventual cutover lands on the existing revision name instead of forcing a rename.

**Kept entirely in the leaf, not the shared archetype.** `serverless_space` already appends whatever suffix the leaf gives it, so tabula's revision strategy lives in tabula's lane. This does **not** touch `serverless_space` (the oauth bu1 cutover is mid-flight — verified the active PR #1063 only edits the oauth app stack) and does **not** change oauth. Centralizing the config-hash in the archetype — which would fix oauth's latent 409 too — is a clean follow-up once bu1 settles.

## Tests

The naming rule (stable across map order, sensitive to a changed value and an added key, 6-hex shape, NUL-separator boundary), that `deployedEnv` includes `SECRET_PREFIX`, and a **golden value** pinning the dev hash to tabula's (`1b062f`) so any drift between the two implementations fails CI. They run in the `gcp-app-infra-bu2-development` preview leg added in #1061.

Conformance clean.

author: hartsock
body:
Closes #292. Part of newt-agent #1354 (the "web-authz triangle", from the PR #1353 security audit). Discharges epic items 3–5 as one cohesive contract.

## What this PR does

Adds `agent-bridle-core::operator` — the shared operator-authz schema that newt-web (and future agents) key on. bridle owns the contract; newt implements the first store behind it (locked-decision #8).

- **`HumanPrincipal`** — an authenticated human keyed by OIDC `(issuer, subject)`, **never** email; carries display email + IdP groups.
- **`PrincipalBinding`** — a signed binding of a `HumanPrincipal` to a mesh `AgentKey` fingerprint (the who ↔ which-agent edge). Verified through the existing `policy::ApproveVerifier` seam.
- **`RequestedCapability`** — the unified 6-valued vocab (`exec`/`fs_read`/`fs_write`/`net`/`remote_tool`/`git_write`) reconciling newt's `DenialKind` with bridle's 3-valued `policy::CapabilityClass` (`to_capability_class()` maps; the name-based leashes → `None`).
- **`PermissionChallenge`** — a signed, expiring, digest-bearing request for a decision, issued by the agent. **Wall-clock-free**: `is_expired(now)` takes the clock as a parameter.
- **`DecisionVerdict` + `OperatorDecision`** — the LIVE decision vocab (`deny`/`allow_once`/`allow_session`/`approve_durable`), distinct from the durable policy `Verdict`, and a decision that binds to exactly one challenge (`request_id` + payload digest, so it can't be lifted). `ApproveDurable` is terminal-only — the **web channel is strictly ephemeral**.

**Design fidelity to house doctrine:**
- **Reuse, don't reinvent crypto** — no new signer/verifier trait; verification is `policy::ApproveVerifier`, the fingerprint is `agent_mesh_protocol::Fingerprint`, and `hex_decode` was promoted to `pub(crate)` rather than forked.
- **Wall-clock-free** — the expiry predicate takes `now` (the `step_up` causal-freshness posture).
- **Field-boundary safety** — multi-field `signing_payload`s are length-delimited, so a value can't forge a field boundary (unlike the single-field `policy` entries, a newline join would be unsafe here).
- **Composition root stays a manifest** — one `pub mod operator;` line; no definitions added to `lib.rs`.

## Test plan

Inline tests (bridle convention), exhaustive enumeration + adversarial tamper: identity-keyed-not-by-email, the 6→3 capability map, field-boundary distinctness, fail-closed expiry at the boundary, decision↔challenge binding (tampered target ⇒ not answered), ephemeral-vs-durable verdict, step-up opt-in. Ed25519 sign/verify round-trips (genuine verifies; unsigned/tampered-field/wrong-key all rejected) gated behind `verifier-ed25519`.

Green on the full dual matrix: `cargo fmt --check`, `clippy --workspace --all-targets` on both `--all-features` and `--no-default-features` (`-D warnings`), and `cargo test --workspace` on both feature sets.

## Out of scope

The full pairing/transcript/SAS ceremony + WebAuthn browser-possession signature (newt-agent #1354 LATER / steps 7–9), and newt's adoption of these types (a follow-on in newt-core).

author: kerimcetinbas
body:
## Description

The agreed executor architecture: dispatch goes through pipelines **closed over the message's runtime type**, built once per (message type, result type, group set) and cached process-wide.

- **Executor core** — `IPipelineExecutor` / `IPipelineExecutor<TResult>` (Core.Abstractions) + internal executors wrapping the mediation strategies; `IMessageMediator.DispatchAsync(...)` entries; facades resolve executors by dictionary lookup. No per-call `MediateOptions`, no erased strategy, no boxed `ValueTask`.
- **Independent sync/async handler contracts** — `IHandler` is an empty marker (object-typed `Handle(object, ...)` root removed); `IHandler<TMessage, TResult>` is pure sync returning `TResult` directly; `IAsyncHandler<TMessage>[,TResult]` are standalone `ValueTask` contracts. All handler DIMs deleted; strategies invoke through typed members only.
- **Events & streams** — per-type invokers (`EventBroadcastInvokerCache`, `QueryStreamInvokerCache`) carry per-call state (settings / cancellation token); even `PublishAsync((IEvent)e)` dispatches typed.
- **Breaking**: interface-erased dispatch (`Mediate` with `TMessage = ICommand<T>` against concrete handlers) now throws `NotSupportedException` with guidance; `CommandMediator`/`QueryMediator` constructors slimmed.
- The reflective executor construction (one `MakeGenericType` per message type) is the JIT fallback the source generator will emit concretely — completing the Native AOT story.

## Benchmark (100k no-op dispatches, 7800X3D / .NET 9)

| Scenario | Before | After | MediatR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Public `SendAsync` | 7.89 ms / 14.5 MB | **7.19 ms / 5.34 MB** | 6.24 ms / 18.31 MB |
| Raw mediator | 6.47 ms / 5.34 MB | 6.33 ms / 5.34 MB | — |
| ScopePerDispatch | 19.25 ms / 55.7 MB | **18.42 ms / 41.96 MB** | 11.26 ms / 33.57 MB |

Facade allocation is byte-identical to the raw path; handler-side allocation is zero for sync-completing handlers.

## Type of Change
- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature — executor dispatch seam (`IPipelineExecutor`, `DispatchAsync`)
- [x] Other — v2 breaking change (severed handler contracts, erased dispatch removed)

## Related Issue
Follow-up to #83; the design was agreed as the step before source-gen Phase 1.

## Testing
- [x] I have added tests that prove my changes work — existing suites now exercise the executor path end-to-end; handler-contract tests rewritten to typed members
- [x] All existing tests pass — 0 warnings / 0 errors (no-incremental, AOT analyzers on), full suite green on net9.0 + net10.0

## Checklist
- [x] My code follows the code style of this project
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [x] I have updated the documentation where necessary (CHANGELOG, README benchmarks + architecture notes)

Not: Interceptor katmanının object kökleri bilinçli olarak bu PR dışında bırakıldı (sonraki temizlik: interceptor typed-invocation + `Task*InvocationStrategy` yeniden adlandırma).

author: bghgary
body:
[Created by Copilot on behalf of @bghgary]

## Context

This continues #16994 by @matanui159 (Jasmine Minter), which implemented AMD **FSR 1** (EASU upscale + RCAS sharpen) as fragment post-processes (a `PostProcessRenderPipeline`) in WGSL. That PR was **WebGPU-only** because the EASU pass uses `textureGather`, which Babylon's GLSL target doesn't expose — so it did not run on WebGL2 or Babylon Native.

Full credit for the original FSR 1 pipeline and shaders goes to Jasmine; her commit is preserved as the first commit here and this PR builds directly on it.

## Change

- Adds **GLSL (`Shaders/`) variants** of the EASU / RCAS shaders and the `ffxFunctions` include, so the pipeline runs on **WebGL2 and Babylon Native** in addition to WebGPU. The EASU `textureGather` calls are rewritten as 4 explicit `texelFetch`es (in gather order) — the approach the original author suggested; RCAS uses plain texel loads and ports unchanged.
- The thin post-processes select WGSL vs GLSL via `_gatherImports`, the same pattern as FXAA / TAA.
- Switches the effects to **plain uniforms** (`con0..con3` / `con`) set from `onApplyObservable` instead of a uniform buffer, so they work on backends that disable uniform buffers (Babylon Native). Shaders are simplified accordingly (dropped the `uint`→`float` bit-casts and the UBO/struct declarations).
- `isSupported` is `isWebGPU || engine.version >= 2` (WebGPU / WebGL2 / Native → true; WebGL1 → false).
- Fixes an FSR shader crash on the D3D11 / Babylon Native swapchain.

## Behavior

Purely additive: a new opt-in `FSR1RenderingPipeline`. No existing behavior changes — WebGPU output is unchanged, and the WebGL2 + Native paths are newly enabled.

## Validation

- Shaders compile to SPIR-V via glslang (Native's toolchain) and validate as GLSL ES 3.00 (WebGL2).
- Rendered a scene through the FSR 1 pipeline on Babylon Native's D3D11 backend — correct upscaled output, clean exit.
- Visualization test `FSR1 render pipeline` runs a photographic source through the pipeline. It moves 12.21% of pixels against a naive upscale of the same half-resolution source, versus the harness's 1.1% gate.

## Try it

[FSR1 A/B toggle playground](https://playground.babylonjs.com/?snapshot=refs/pull/18723/merge#GB98SV#0) — cycles FSR1, a naive bilinear upscale of the same half-resolution source, and a native full-resolution render. Tap, space, or 1-3 to switch; drag to orbit and wheel to zoom in on the reconstruction.

Judge FSR against the naive upscale rather than the native render: the pipeline renders at half resolution, so switching it off is always sharper and that is not a defect.

Credit: @matanui159 (Jasmine Minter) for the original FSR 1 pipeline, #16994.

## Épico 6 - Retirada
A tela **Retirada** já existia e cobria o épico quase por completo:
- Pesquisa por nome, telefone ou número do pedido (`GET /pickup`).
- Mostra produtos, pagamento e status do pedido selecionado.
- Botão grande "Entregar pedido", que já chama `PATCH /orders/:id/status` — o mesmo endpoint do Épico 4, então entregar um pedido já: atualiza o status (o dashboard reflete na próxima consulta), grava no histórico (`order_status_history` com usuário/data/hora) e envia notificação automática ao cliente.
- Único ajuste feito: reforcei o botão como call-to-action (uppercase/tracking) para deixá-lo mais próximo do "ENTREGAR PEDIDO" do briefing.

## Épico 7 - Dashboard
- **Indicadores**: todos os 11 pedidos já existiam na tela (Pedidos Hoje/Amanhã, Receita Hoje/do período, Produtos Vendidos, Ticket Médio, Produto Mais Vendido, Cliente que Mais Comprou, Pedidos Pendentes, Entregues, Estoque Baixo). Reorganizei em duas seções: um grupo "agora" sempre fixo em hoje/amanhã (Pedidos hoje, Pedidos amanhã, Receita hoje, Pendentes, Entregues hoje, Entregues total, Estoque baixo) e um grupo "Resumo do período" que reage ao filtro escolhido.
- **Filtros**: novo seletor Hoje / Semana / Mês / Ano / Personalizado (com dois `<input type="date">` para o período customizado). O backend (`GET /dashboard?period=...&from=...&to=...`) recalcula receita, produtos vendidos, ticket médio, produto mais vendido, cliente que mais comprou, distribuição de pagamento e a série do gráfico de receita para o período selecionado, comparando com o período equivalente anterior para a tendência (%).

Nenhuma migration nova. Só reescrevi a query do endpoint `/dashboard` na Edge Function (redeployada como v13) para aceitar filtro de período.

author: darkdante9
body:
## Summary

Every fee-gated entrypoint (`create_token`, `create_tokens_batch`, `mint_tokens`, `set_metadata`) validated `fee_payment >= required_fee` but then transferred `fee_payment` itself, not the required fee. A UI bug, unit confusion (XLM vs. stroops — a 10⁷ factor), a stale cached fee, or the conventional practice of padding `fee_payment` above the displayed fee so a transaction survives an in-flight admin fee update, would all result in the contract keeping the full overpayment with no refund — direct loss of user funds on mainnet.

This PR treats `fee_payment` as the caller's authorized upper bound only (the same `amount`/`max_amount` pattern DEX contracts use), and charges the currently required fee exactly.

## Changes

- `create_token` / `mint_tokens` now call `distribute_fee(..., state.base_fee)` instead of `distribute_fee(..., fee_payment)`.
- `create_tokens_batch` charges the already-computed `total_fee` (`base_fee * tokens.len()`) instead of `fee_payment`.
- `set_metadata` charges `state.metadata_fee` instead of `fee_payment`.
- `fee_payment` remains the `InsufficientFee` gate's lower bound in all four entrypoints — a `fee_payment` below the required fee is still rejected before any transfer, including the fee-update race (admin raises the fee after the caller signed with headroom for the old fee): the call now fails cleanly with `Error::InsufficientFee` and no partial transfer at either rate.
- **Tests** (`mint_tokens`/`set_metadata`, which don't require a real token WASM to deploy — see below):
  - `test_mint_tokens_overpayment_charges_exact_fee_only` / `test_set_metadata_overpayment_charges_exact_fee_only`: passing `fee_payment = 2 * required_fee` results in exactly `required_fee` leaving the caller's balance.
  - `test_mint_tokens_fee_split_sums_to_charged_fee_not_payment`: a configured fee split still sums exactly to the charged fee, not the passed `fee_payment`.
  - `test_fee_update_race_rejects_with_no_partial_transfer`: submitting with `fee_payment` sized for the old fee after the admin raises it fails with `InsufficientFee` and leaves every balance untouched.
- **Fuzzing**: extended `fuzz_fee_arithmetic` with a charged-amount == required-fee invariant across all three required-fee values (`base_fee`, batch `total_fee`, `metadata_fee`) — for any `fee_payment >= required_fee`, the amount handed to `distribute_fee` must equal `required_fee` exactly and never exceed `fee_payment`, and the existing conservation invariant is re-checked against the charged amount.
- **Docs**: added a "Fee semantics" section to `docs/contract-abi.md` explaining the `fee_payment`-as-upper-bound model and the fee-update-race behavior, plus per-entrypoint notes on the exact amount charged.

## Not changed

- **Frontend**: checked `FeeDisplay`, `MintForm`, `MetadataForm`, and `CreateToken` — they already pass the current `base_fee`/`metadata_fee` verbatim as `feePayment` with no padding or multiplier. No frontend change was needed to satisfy the new semantics; a `fee_payment` sent this way is already exactly what gets charged.
- **`create_token`/`create_tokens_batch` balance tests**: these share the identical `distribute_fee` call site fixed here, but a successful deploy needs a real, externally-audited SEP-41 token WASM that isn't part of this repo (this is an existing, already-documented limitation — see the "error paths only — deploy requires real wasm" comment in `test.rs`). `mint_tokens`/`set_metadata` exercise the identical charging logic without that limitation.

## Dependency

This branch is stacked on #1034 (`fix/1007-persistent-storage`), which fixes an unrelated pre-existing merge-conflict bug that otherwise prevents the crate from compiling at all. This PR's diff against `main` will include that PR's changes until #1034 merges; the diff against `fix/1007-persistent-storage` is the actual scope of this change.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p token-factory` — 124/124 pass (120 from the stacked branch + 4 new)
- [x] `cargo clippy -p token-factory --all-targets` — clean (only a pre-existing, unrelated warning)
- [x] `cargo build -p token-factory --release --target wasm32v1-none` — release WASM builds successfully
- [x] `cargo check` on the fuzz crate (`fuzz_fee_arithmetic`) — compiles cleanly with the new invariant
- [x] `npm test` (frontend, 585 tests) — untouched by this PR, ran clean via the pre-push hook

Closes #1008

author: vtothep
body:
## Was & Warum

Systemischer Fix für den Fabrik-Deadlock aus #100. Ursache: Beim Anlegen der Design-Kette #95–#99 wurden **alle** Issues pauschal `status:blocked` gelabelt — auch die Wurzel #95, die laut Body **keine** `#N`-Blocker hat („## Blocked by: Keine"). Ergebnis: null `status:ready`-Issues → `/implement-next` lief leer → Nacht-Fabrik verhungert.

Option 2 (systemisch) aus dem Issue. Der wörtliche „anlegende Pfad" (`grill-me-with-docs` / `/to-issues`) ist ein externes Plugin bzw. existiert nicht als Repo-Datei, ist also hier nicht versionierbar. Deshalb umgesetzt in den zwei **repo-kontrollierten** Hebeln:

### 1. `CLAUDE.md` — Regel geschärft
Neue, explizite Guardrail: Die **Wurzel** einer Blocker-Kette ist **nie** `status:blocked`. Pro Issue gilt die Label-Regel; nur Issues mit mindestens einem offenen `#N`-Blocker sind blockiert.

### 2. `.github/workflows/unblock-ready.yml` — Sicherheitsnetz gehärtet
- **Trigger** jetzt auch `opened` + `labeled` (bisher nur `closed`). Bei null ready-Issues feuert nie ein `closed`-Event → das Netz hätte den Deadlock sonst nie brechen können.
- Ein `status:blocked`-Issue, dessen „## Blocked by"-Abschnitt **keine** `#N`-Referenz enthält (z.B. „Keine"), wird **aktiv** auf `status:ready` gehoben statt übersprungen.
- **Sicher by default:** Fehlt der Abschnitt ganz, bleibt es blockiert. Der `triage`-Guard bleibt unberührt — autonom erstellte Issues werden weiter nicht auto-ready.

## Test
- Parsing-Logik für alle drei Zweige (Wurzel/„Keine", echter `#N`-Blocker, kein Abschnitt) lokal verifiziert.
- `npm run lint`, `npm test` (78 grün), `npm run build` — alle grün.

## Hinweis — kein Auto-Merge
Ändert CI-Config (`.github/workflows/`) → per CLAUDE.md „Never-auto-merge": manueller Review + Merge durch Vincent.

## Nicht Teil dieser Slice
- Sofort-Fix, #95 selbst zu entblocken (Option 1) — separat/manuell, falls gewünscht.
- Umsetzung der Design-Issues #95–#99.

Closes #100

author: luckypipewrench
body:
## What changed

Three per-agent denial-of-wallet budget fields (a concurrent-tool-call limit, a per-endpoint retry limit, and fan-out limits) were accepted by config and described as enforced, but no runtime path consulted them, so an operator could set them and believe agent traffic was constrained when it was not. This removes the per-endpoint retry and fan-out fields entirely, because the mediated MCP layer cannot observe the per-endpoint signals they would need to be enforced honestly, and it rejects a nonzero concurrent-tool-call limit at config validation and startup with a clear message that the field is reserved for a future control and should be unset. The budgets that are actually enforced (per-session tool count, wall-clock, per-tool retry, and loop detection) are unchanged and keep enforcing.

## Why it is safe

The rejection runs at every configuration admission boundary (file load, direct reload, and the policy-bundle apply path) and before license resolution can remove a profile, so a reserved limit cannot slip in through any load path, a hot reload, a signed bundle, or a YAML anchor. A configuration that still sets one of the removed fields fails to load with an explicit message naming the field. Documentation no longer claims these limits are enforced. The change is fail-closed: it can only reject configuration that previously produced a false sense of protection, and the honestly-enforced budgets keep working, proven by a real mediated round-trip that still blocks an over-budget request.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Documentation**
  * Updated Denial-of-Wallet guidance to reflect current budgets for tool calls, retries, loop detection, and wall-clock duration.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Configurations using unsupported or reserved budget limits are now rejected with actionable errors.
  * Policy bundles authenticate signatures and verify payload integrity before configuration validation.
  * Invalid reloads fail safely without altering the active configuration.

* **Behavior Changes**

author: contip
body:
Patch release for a **production 500** on `GET /api/socials/pinterest/boards`.

## Root cause
The plugin's logger wrapper invoked Pino's level methods with the wrong `this`. Pino's methods require the logger instance as their receiver, so a **successful** token refresh threw a `TypeError` from inside Pino — which propagated out of `saveCredentials` and turned board discovery into a 500. The existing tests used `vi.fn()`, which ignores `this`, so the defect was concealed.

## Fixes
- **`fix(logging)`** — bind each resolved level method to the host logger instance, and wrap the actual log call in try/catch so a host logging backend can never convert a successful business operation (credential persist, publish, scheduler, retry, error-response) into an application failure.
- **`fix(pinterest)`** — split outbound scope serialization (comma) from inbound token-response parsing (whitespace/comma-tolerant) and use the shared parser in **both** the code exchange **and** the refresh path (refresh previously split on commas only, mis-reading Pinterest's space-delimited response). Also stop clobbering stored scopes when a response omits `scope` (persist `undefined`, not `[]`).

## Tests (the ones that would have caught it)
- Receiver-sensitive fake asserting `this === logger`, plus a **real Pino 9.x** `not.toThrow()` regression; connection-service success path now runs through real Pino and a throwing logger.
- Integration regression replaying the production sequence: refresh → encrypted persist → real-Pino log → boards returned, called twice to prove token caching (no re-refresh).
- Pino is a **devDependency only** (not shipped at runtime).

## Scope / safety

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
### Why these changes are necessary
The mathematical engine previously executed an unverified trial-division and probabilistic check for primality, bypassing mathematically proven trial-division algorithms. This introduced a significant risk of false-positive prime classifications during ray-casting operations. 

To address this without degrading performance for large candidate numbers, we have introduced a tiered execution path. Small inputs (under $2^{64}$) are now routed through proven trial-division logic, while larger inputs fall back to the existing recursive factorization path. Additionally, to prevent accidental code changes or malicious interference in production, we have enforced strict proof-to-code alignment checks at startup and automated trust boundary verification at build-time.

---

### Key Decisions & Rationale
* **The $2^{64}$ Performance Boundary:** Inputs under $2^{64}$ can be exhaustively and mathematically verified using Verus-proven trial-division without introducing any latency overhead to the ray-casting pipeline. Larger numbers bypass this pathway to maintain baseline factorization performance.
* **Fail-Fast Startup Security:** To guarantee deployment integrity, the system immediately panics if there is any mismatch between active code and the cryptographically signed proof manifest.
* **Automated Trust Documentation Audits:** Rather than relying on manual reviews, we updated the build-time auditor to dynamically parse and validate that all documentation links and trust boundaries correspond to real, existing files.

---

### What's Changed

#### 1. Tiered Primality Routing (`math_utils.rs`)
* Modified the entry point `verified_is_prime`.
* Added a dynamic check to identify candidates below $2^{64}$ and route them to the verified logic:
  ```rust
  if n < 18446744073709551616 {
      crate::verus_proofs::verified_is_prime(n)
  } else {
      // Fallback to original probabilistic/recursive logic
  }
  ```
* Guaranteed zero incorrect classifications for the verified threshold while preserving execution speeds.

#### 2. Deployment Integrity Assertion
* Verified that the engine validates the cryptographic hashes of `verus_proofs.rs` during startup.
* Confirmed the engine triggers an immediate panic if active logic drifts from the registered proof manifest.

#### 3. Build-Time AST Drift & Path Auditor (`auditor.py`)
* Refactored `auditor.py` to parse and evaluate authoritative and informal documentation paths defined inside `docs_manifest.json` (such as `README.md` and `TCB.md`).
* Confirmed that any broken file references inside the trust boundary correctly trigger a `[DOC CHECK ERROR]` and fail the build.

author: jslok
body:
## What

Two related delegate-lifecycle bugs in `createModel` / `HybridTfliteModel`:

### 1. Null delegates are registered with the interpreter

Delegate factories can legitimately return `nullptr` — e.g. `TfLiteCoreMlDelegateCreate` on devices without a Neural Engine (the default `enabled_devices` is ANE-only). `createModel` passed that `nullptr` straight into `TfLiteInterpreterOptionsAddDelegate`, corrupting/crashing interpreter creation.

**Fix:** skip null delegates so the model falls back to CPU. `getDelegates()` now also reports only the delegates that were *actually* registered, instead of claiming a delegate is active when its creation returned null.

### 2. Delegates are never freed

TFLite's C API does **not** transfer delegate ownership to the interpreter — the caller must keep the delegate alive and delete it itself after the interpreter is destroyed ([TFLite docs](https://ai.google.dev/edge/api/tflite/c/group/c-api)). `~HybridTfliteModel` deleted the interpreter but never the delegates, so every model destruction leaked the delegate's compiled kernels / driver contexts. For the GPU delegate that's a substantial native+driver allocation per model load — very visible in apps that load/unload models across their lifecycle.

**Fix:** capture a per-delegate deleter (`TfLiteGpuDelegateV2Delete` / `TfLiteNnapiDelegateDelete` / `TfLiteCoreMlDelegateDelete`) at creation time and run them in the destructor *after* `TfLiteInterpreterDelete` (delegates must outlive the interpreter), plus on the interpreter-creation failure path.

## Testing

Running in production (React Native scanner app, Android GPU delegate + CoreML) as a patch-package fix — model load/release cycles no longer accumulate native memory, verified with heapprofd before/after.

# Background

Renovate config is a [complex beast](https://docs.renovatebot.com/config-overview/).

We want to mark OpenFeature SDK updates as `feat` commits. https://github.com/OctopusDeploy/openfeature-provider-dotnet/pull/73

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
### Summary
This PR addresses critical issues in the proof verification engine where Lean's compiler optimized out or reordered stateful Depth-First Search (DFS) operations, and manual registration of the validator class caused segmentation faults during interactive/hot-reload environments. 

By forcing stateful FFI calls into the `IO` monad and moving memory class registration to the module load phase, we guarantee deterministic search correctness and crash-free execution in all runtime environments.

---

### Key Changes & Rationale

#### 1. Monadic Sequencing for DFS Stateful Operations
* **The Problem:** Treating state-modifying DFS search steps (`rust_dfs_*`) as pure Lean functions allowed the compiler to aggressively optimize, reorder, or cache dynamic query results. This broke backtracking and search state integrity.
* **The Solution:** 
  * Updated FFI signatures in `lean4-proofs/UALBF/FFI.lean` to wrap `rust_dfs_*` operations inside the `IO` monad. This forces sequential evaluation and prevents compiler caching.
  * Updated the Python exporter script (`scripts/export_lean_specs.py`) to correctly output C signatures expected by Lean `IO` operations, which require a world parameter (`lean_object* w`) and return a `lean_obj_res`.
  * Adapted the Rust core (`dfs_tree.rs`) to extract pure mathematical logic into nested `_rust_dfs_*` routines while exposing standard FFI handlers that package outputs using the newly defined `rs_lean_io_result_mk_ok` macros.

#### 2. Load-Time Validator Class Registration
* **The Problem:** Lazy or manual registration of the certificate external memory class caused interactive editors (which frequently reload modules) to trigger duplicate registration crashes and segfaults.
* **The Solution:**
  * Modified `Validator.lean` to leverage `builtin_initialize initCertClass` eagerly during module load rather than lazily during runtime execution.
  * Added defensive guards inside `ffi.c` (`if (g_cert_class == NULL)`) to ensure the external class registration operates as a strict singleton, safely ignoring repeated execution requests from hot-reloads.

#### 3. Automatic Resource Management
* Verified certificate lifecycles are now backed by standard `OpaqueCertificate` (`CertHandle`) allocations utilizing `lean_alloc_external`. External resources are automatically reclaimed by Lean's garbage collector when reference counts are exhausted.

---

### Verification & Testing
* **No Regression in Pure Functions:** Pure mathematical mappings remain non-monadic to ensure maximum computational performance.
* **Interactive Stability:** Verified that reloading the verification module inside interactive environments no longer produces segmentation faults.
* **Search Correctness:** Confirmed that state updates and backtracking evaluations maintain absolute parity with the baseline mathematical models.

author: baileyrd
body:
## What
Adds a raw `process::prctl` escape hatch plus `set_pdeathsig`/`get_pdeathsig` (`PR_SET_PDEATHSIG`/`PR_GET_PDEATHSIG`).

## Why
Closes #29. No `prctl` at all, so there was no path even for an opt-in caller to ask the kernel to signal a child if its parent dies first — the standard fix for orphaned children surviving a crashed/killed job-control shell.

## Test plan
- [x] `set_and_get_pdeathsig_roundtrip` and, more importantly, `set_pdeathsig_kills_child_when_parent_exits`: a three-generation fork dance (test process → intermediate → grandchild) where the grandchild arms `pdeathsig` against the intermediate, the intermediate exits immediately, and the test asserts — via a pipe held open only by the intermediate and grandchild — that the grandchild actually dies within milliseconds, rather than surviving as an orphan. Tests real kernel behavior, not just that the syscall doesn't error. A bounded fallback sleep in the grandchild keeps a future regression from hanging the suite instead of surfacing as a timeout.
- [x] `PRCTL` syscall number (157 x86_64, 167 aarch64) and `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG`/`PR_GET_PDEATHSIG` verified against real kernel headers.
- [x] Verified on both x86_64 and aarch64 (native + qemu-user cross) **and** as an unprivileged user (`setpriv --reuid=nobody`) on both — after #48 needed a same-day fix for exactly this gap, every subsequent test in this round gets checked unprivileged before it ships, not just as root.
- [x] `no_std`/`std` builds, `cargo fmt`/`clippy -D warnings`/`cargo doc -D warnings` clean.

Closes #29.

author: joswayski
body:
## What changed

- adds platform-neutral recording and media crates plus a macOS 13+ ScreenCaptureKit backend with hardware H.264/AAC writing, system audio, and selected CPAL microphone capture
- replaces separate video and GIF entry points with one Record Screen action for region, window, or full-display selection
- creates the recording selector only when requested, wakes its transparent click-through WebView from native code, and destroys it after Escape, Cancel, or recording start so every selection mounts a fresh event bridge
- adds deadline-based native and frontend wake paths, and makes a repeated Record Screen command reopen an already-prepared selector instead of reporting a capture in progress
- resets frontend and native selector state so reopening always accepts clicks and region drags without flashing cached window highlights
- records one recoverable video master with countdown, excluded controls, pause/resume, restart, microphone mute, discard, and crash-safe segments
- adds a non-destructive editor where the user chooses MP4 or GIF and can trim, crop, resize, remix audio, compress, or enforce a strict maximum file size
- adds unified screenshot/video/GIF history, including interrupted recording recovery in Capture History instead of a separate tray or Preferences destination
- dismisses a screenshot preview after a successful native file drop, while preserving the capture and leaving cancelled drags visible
- replaces native recorder checkboxes with compact switches and modernizes checkbox styling across recording preferences and the editor
- documents planned opt-in product-health diagnostics, reviewed feedback bundles, and AI-assisted draft-fix triage without changing today’s local-only behavior
- bundles pinned LGPL-only FFmpeg/ffprobe sidecars with release compliance assets and updated user and maintainer documentation
- includes the cross-platform desktop fixes from #26, preserving Windows linker, process, protocol-origin, updater, and packaging behavior

## Why

The old recorder exposed a large Preparing recorder overlay and split the choice between video and GIF before capture. The hidden, reused selector could suspend before its event bridge or fallback timers ran, remain click-through after Escape, briefly show a cached blue window highlight, or stay invisible while still reserving the backend session. Clicking Record Screen again then produced a misleading capture-in-progress error.

Recording should open directly into a ready, recoverable target selector, create one durable master, and defer the output decision to editing. A selector is cheap enough to recreate per selection; keeping a stale hidden WebView alive was both slower in practice and unreliable.

A successfully dragged screenshot has already reached its destination, so its floating quick preview should get out of the way just as if the user clicked Close. Dismissing the preview must not delete the saved capture or its history entry.

## Impact

On macOS 13+, users start from one Record Screen command, select a region, window, or display, and then export the result as MP4 or GIF. Clicking Record Screen prepares selection only; recording begins after the user presses Record and the countdown completes.

The selector is now created on demand with a transparent initial surface. A native wake path does not depend on suspended JavaScript timers, and Cancel/Escape destroys the selector so the next attempt gets a fresh interactive window. Repeating the command while preparation is pending reopens that selector instead of failing. Existing screenshot and drag-to-upload behavior from main remains intact, and all media stays local.

Finished captures and interrupted recording drafts now share one Capture History surface. Draft segments remain separate on disk only so a crash cannot corrupt or erase a recoverable recording.

After a successful screenshot file drop, Captures removes only the floating runtime preview with its normal dismiss animation. The saved file and Capture History record remain available. A cancelled or rejected drag leaves the preview open.

## Validation

- `npm run check`: 12 release tests, 77 desktop UI tests, and the production website build
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo test --workspace`: 71 Rust tests
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- Windows-target check for the platform-neutral recording and media crates
- clean app and DMG build with pinned FFmpeg/ffprobe sidecar validation
- strict deep code-sign verification of the packaged app
- regression test for Escape followed by a new interactive region drag
- regression test for a suspended selector WebView that never supplies an animation frame
- packaged-app lifecycle test: cold start, first selector page load/reveal, cancellation and destruction, then a distinct second selector page load/reveal
- regression tests for successful and cancelled native screenshot file drags
- native macOS selector visually verified for region, window, and full-screen modes
- real four-second ScreenCaptureKit recording smoke test, discarded after capture

## Follow-up before public release

- run the ten-minute real-hardware acceptance pass for A/V drift, frame loss, memory growth, control exclusion, device loss, and crash recovery
- add low-disk and hot-plug polish, editable click and keystroke overlays, and a pre-record microphone level meter
- implement Windows and Linux recording backends in focused follow-up PRs
- build and notarize with production Apple credentials; this local validation build is ad-hoc signed

author: jluterek
body:
Fixes #48 — reproduced, diagnosed to the mechanism, and verified against a clean Node 24 host.

## Root cause (confirmed by reproduction, not just the stack)

Vite **SSR-externalizes** bare node_modules imports and loads them with **Node's native ESM loader**. Our published `@astro-slides/client` pointed its runtime entries at raw `src/index.ts` — and Node refuses to type-strip anything under `node_modules`. So in any published install, the first deck-route SSR render failed on the client import, Vite retried per request, the open pages reload-looped (the "errors with no request lines" in the issue — plus a flood when pages *were* open), and the dev server eventually wedged. The workspace never sees this because the client resolves outside `node_modules` there — which is exactly why it survived CI.

Identified the consumer empirically with a logging shim: the import fires in the **main astro dev process** right after the first deck-route render — matching the SSR-external mechanism, not a background job.

## The fix

1. **Published entrypoints ship compiled JS + declarations** (`.` and `./fit-text` → `dist/`). The composite tsc build already emitted dist — it just wasn't packed or mapped. Styles/themes/components/layouts stay as source (Vite owns those). One module graph for every consumer: an intermediate attempt (`node` condition → dist, browsers → src) made Vite's optimizer disagree with itself about CJS interop and broke the deck runtime — rejected.
2. **Interop-tolerant CJS imports**: the repro exposed a second latent bug — `lz-string` (eager, Magic Move), `recordrtc` and `@fix-webm-duration/fix` (lazy, recorder) have their callable surface on the namespace, `default`, or `default.default` depending on the serving pipeline. A wrong guess crashed the deck runtime and put the presenter into a reload loop (measured 142 navigations/15s). All three now probe for the actual functions.

## Verification (clean npm host, Node 24, `prefix` + `scopedReact`, 2 decks — the issue's shape)

| Check | Published 0.3.0 | This branch |
|---|---|---|
| `Stripping types` errors | **311** in one session | **0** |
| Page reload loops | dashboard/read flood; presenter 142 navs/15s | **0 reloads** in 12s soak |
| ArrowRight navigation | broken | `/slides/talk/2` ✓ |
| Console/page errors | interop crash | **none** |
| Server after soak | wedges (per issue) | HTTP 200 in 10ms |

Workspace unaffected: 359 unit + 42 e2e green, all examples build.

Changeset: patch for `@astro-slides/client` → 0.3.1.
